HEADQUARTERS
CRIME BRANCH
JUNE 29, 39.
S.

In accordance with the instructions of the
D. C. (Crime) the 1st accused Ts Vung Hyou was
handed over to Det. Con. Mansfield of the C.M. Customs
River Police at 11.30 a.m. on 27.6.39. Receipt for
prisoner attached.

The 2nd accused Kau Ming Woo has been given
every opportunity to find a guarantor, but up to the
present has been unable to do so.

The only person he knew in Shanghai was
Loh Ta liau (陸士標) of the Loh Lai Tai (老瑞泰)
Rice Shop, 728 Newchang Road, but this man is absent
from Shanghai at present, and it is uncertain when he
will return. The other employees of this rice shop
state they do not know this accused, so they are
therefore, unwilling to guarantee him.

6

FURTHER TO A DISTANCE TO THE JAPANESE MILITARY
WATER POLICE.

In accordance with the instructions of
the D.C. (Crime), the Japanese Military Water
Police were informed by telephone referred to
TSU VUNG NYEU (朱文元) and KAO MING WOO (高夢特)
at 11 a.m. 26.6.39. Upon investigation, Tsu Vung
Nyeu is not requested to be handed over on un-
recognition of his being concerned directly with
the guerilla, but according to the information,
Tsu is wanted on the Circular order of arrest
by River Police.
        It is understood that the River Police
will make direct arrangements with the S.M.Police
regarding the handing over of the said person.
        Kao Ming Woo is seen to be a member of
guerrillas, but in the absence of any material
evidence it is similarly not required to be handed
over.
        In view of the foregoing, the Japanese
Military Water Police request that the case be
concluded herewith and the S.M.P. deal with these
two men as they see fit.

D. C. ( CRIME )                      D. I.

6

关于进一步致日本海军水上警察事宜。

遵照刑事科副总监（D.C. (Crime)）的指示，已于1939年6月26日上午11时通过电话通知日本海军水上警察，涉及朱文元（TSU VUNG NYEU）和高梦特（KAO MING WOO）。经调查，因无法认定其直接参与游击队活动，故不要求移交朱文元；但据情报显示，水上警察局已对其发布通缉令。
据悉，水上警察局将就移交该人一事与工部局警务处（S.M.Police）直接安排。
高梦特被视为游击队成员，但因缺乏任何实质证据，同样不要求移交。
鉴于上述情况，日本海军水上警察要求就此结案，并由工部局警务处酌情处理这两人。

刑事科副总监（D. C. ( CRIME )）                      督察（D. I.）

of the Japanese Military Water Police stationed at

C.l Misc.92/39
June 25, 39
4

A statement has been taken from the 2nd.
accused, Kao Ming Woo, and a copy of same is attached.
In this statement the 2nd. accused claims
that he works in his father's rice hong at Iyee Ka Jao,
Wusih and that he arrived in Shanghai at about 6 p.m.
on 16.6.39. That he came to Shanghai for recreation.
That he intended to stay with a friend of his father,
who is the master of the Leh Zai Tai (陸瑞泰) Rice
Shop, on Newchang Road. On disembarking from the boat
at the Customs Jetty he hired a ricksha to proceed to this
shop but whilst passing along Foochow Road he met a
fellow countryman, who was well known to him named Ts
Nyi Pau (周二宝). That Ts Nyi Pau borrowed money
from him and told him he (Ts Nyi Pau) was living in Room
433 of the Grand Hotel. That he went to this room and
the only person present was Ts Vung Nyeu (1st. accused).
That Ts Vung Nyeu handed him a note that had been left
by Ts Nyi Pau. That he remained in this room for about
20 minutes, when the police arrived and placed him under
arrest.

S.C.
Cg-/ 28/6/39.
hd
24/6

The note referred to above was found in
possession of the 2nd. accused at the time of arrest
and a translation of same follows:-
"No.13 Si Meng Li, Rue Porte de L'Ouest.
Newchang Road. Leh Zai Tai Rice Hong.
Room 446, 3rd. floor, Tung Fung Hotel."

1939年6月25日
4

已对第二被告高梦特（Kao Ming Woo）进行讯问并记录供词，副本附后。
在该供词中，第二被告声称他在无锡伊家桥（Iyee Ka Jao）父亲的米行工作，并于1939年6月16日下午6点左右抵达上海。他来上海是为了娱乐。他打算住在他父亲的一位朋友那里，这位朋友是新昌路陆瑞泰（Leh Zai Tai）米行的老板。他在海关码头下船后，雇了一辆人力车前往该米行，但在经过福州路时，遇到了一位名叫周二宝（Ts Nyi Pau）的同乡，此人是他熟识的。周二宝向他借钱，并告诉他（周二宝）住在大华饭店433号房间。他去了那个房间，当时在场只有朱文元（第一被告）。朱文元递给他一张周二宝留下的纸条。他在那个房间待了大约20分钟，随后警察到达并将他逮捕。

S.C.
Cg-/ 1939年6月28日。
hd
24/6

上述提到的纸条是在逮捕第二被告时从其身上搜出的，译文如下：
“西门路13号思孟里。新昌路。陆瑞泰米行。东方饭店三楼446号房间。”

page_data.en:
4/2

The statement of the 2nd. accused differs from
that of the 1st. accused, in that the 1st. accused states
that Ts Nyi Pan, three other males and one female Chinese
were in the room when the 2nd. accused arrived. The
1st. accused denies having handed the note to the 2nd.
accused, and maintains he did not know of its existence.

Both accused have been confronted with these
conflicting statements but both maintain they are telling
the truth.

Judging by the fact, that when the police
visited this room, it was obvious that a number of
people had been to dinner there and the food was still
warm, also some of the cloths belonging to the other
persons were found in the room, it would appear that
the statement of the 1st. accused is correct.

Enquiries at the Loh Zai Tai Rice Hong, 793
Newchang Road show that Loh Sa Piou (陸士標); the
person whom the 2nd. accused states he came to Shanghai
to visit, is not in Shanghai at present. The 2nd.
accused is not known to the other persons in this rice
hong.

On the morning of 21.6.39 Inspector Dyrbv,
Sgt. Kanchaga and Det. Constable Mansfield of the
page_data.zh:
4/2

第二被告的供词与第一被告不同，第一被告称当第二被告到达时，房间内还有周二宝（Ts Nyi Pan）、另外三名男性和一名中国女性。第一被告否认曾将纸条递给第二被告，并坚称他不知道这张纸条的存在。

两名被告已就这些相互矛盾的供词当面对质，但两人都坚持说的是真话。

根据事实判断，当警察进入该房间时，显然有多人在那里吃过饭，食物还是热的，而且在房间里还发现了属于其他人的衣物，看来第一被告的供词是正确的。

对新昌路793号陆瑞泰（Loh Zai Tai）米行的查询显示，第二被告声称来上海拜访的人陆士标（Loh Sa Piou）目前不在上海。该米行的其他人也不认识第二被告。

1939年6月21日上午，德比（Dyrby）巡官、坎查加（Kanchaga）警长和

page_data.en:
4/3

River Police came to C.B.H.Q. and requested permission
to question the 1st. accused. The River Police state
that on May 15th. they arrested 10 men for the larceny
of $14,000.00 worth of cotton from cargo boats in the
river, and these men had implicated the 1st. accused,
Ta Vung Nycu, as the receiver of this stolen property.
Whilst admitting that he knows the 10 men arrested
by the River Police he denies being the receiver of the
stolen property. Inspector Dyrby requests that if this
accused is not handed over to the Japanese Gendarmerie,
he be handed over to the River Police for further
enquiries.

（批：23/6）

（签名：G. B. Dyrol）
D.S.I.
page_data.zh:
4/3

水上警察局的曼斯菲尔德（Mansfield）警佐来到刑事科总部（C.B.H.Q.），请求允许讯问第一被告。水上警察局表示，他们于5月15日逮捕了10名男子，罪名是从河上的货船上盗窃价值14,000.00美元的棉花，这些人供认第一被告朱文元（Ta Vung Nycu）是赃物的接收者。虽然他承认认识被水上警察局逮捕的那10个人，但他否认是赃物接收者。德比（Dyrby）巡官请求，如果该被告不移交给日本宪兵队，则应移交给水上警察局以作进一步调查。

（批：23/6）

（签名：G. B. Dyrol）
副督察长（D.S.I.）

page_data.en:
KAO MING TOO (馬劳格)

WUSH
// D.S.I. Zia an Fong.
translated
C.1                20.6.39        .///////      Clerk Hsu.

My name is Kao Ming Too, age 32, native of Nyee Ka
Jaog Wusih, M/Rice merchant.

I was born and brought up at Nyee Ka Jao, Wusih.
At the age of 8 I attended a primary school in my native
place. I left the school at the age of 15. When I was
16 years of age I was employed as an apprentice at the
Zee Van Hang Rice Goods Shop, Nyee Ka Jao, Wusih. I was
thus employed for 3 years and then went to work as a shop
assistant in the An Tseong Piece Goods Shop, Nyee Ka Jao,
with a monthly pay of $3.00, when I was 20 years old.
In the latter shop I worked for four years. At the age
of 24 I quitted employment in the second mentioned piece
goods shop and remained at home assisting my father in rice
deal for my father owned a rice shop in our native place,
known as the "Kao Wan Yae" Rice Hong. This job I have retained
till present time.

At the age of 8 I came to Shanghai with my parents
and stayed in Shanghai for one week.

The object of my present visit to Shanghai is that
firstly for recreation and secondly I was instructed by my
father to enquire the price of wheat in Shanghai. I left
my home at 1 p.m. 14.6.39 and proceeded to Yang Chi Tsung
where I took a Chinese launch to Tsangsoh, where I passed
that night (14.6.39 to 15.6.39). At 7 a.m. 15.6.39 I left
Tsangsoh and walked to Hau-poo whence I took a foreign
(exact country unknown) steamer, S.S. "Kastenfjy)" to
Shanghai, the ticket fee being $2.40. Altogether I spent
page_data.zh:
高梦特（KAO MING TOO）（马劳格）

无锡
// 副督察长 夏安芳（Zia an Fong）。
翻译
C.1                1939年6月20日        .///////      书记员徐。

我叫高梦特，32岁，籍贯无锡伊家桥（Nyee Ka Jaog），职业：米商。

我在无锡伊家桥出生并长大。8岁时，我在家乡读小学。15岁时离校。16岁时，我在无锡伊家桥的济万恒（Zee Van Hang）米货店当学徒。我在那里工作了3年，然后去无锡伊家桥的安总（An Tseong）布店做店员，月薪3.00美元，当时我20岁。在后一家店里我工作了四年。24岁时，我辞去了上述第二家布店的工作，留在家中协助父亲做米生意，因为我父亲在家乡拥有一家名为“高万亚”（Kao Wan Yae）的米行。这份工作我一直做到现在。

8岁时，我曾随父母来过上海，在上海停留了一周。

我此次来上海的目的，首先是为了娱乐，其次是受父亲指示来上海询问小麦价格。我于1939年6月14日下午1时离开家，前往杨其宗（Yang Chi Tsung），在那里乘坐一艘中式小轮船前往常熟（Tsangsoh），并在那里过夜（1939年6月14日至15日）。1939年6月15日上午7时，我离开常熟，步行至黄埔（Hau-poo），在那里乘坐一艘外国（具体国籍不详）轮船“Kastenfjy”号前往上海，船票费用为2.40美元。总共花费

page_data.en:
- 2 -
about $13.00 on my way to Shanghai. I arrived at Shanghai
at about 6 p.m. on the 16.6.39, and landed at the jetty
infront of the big building with a very large clock on its
top, (Customs Jetty). I then hired a ricsha and told the
coolie to take me to Loh Zai Tai Rice Shop, Newchang Road,
the ricsha coolie charging me 20 cents which I agreed to pay.
Instead of taking me to the above address the ricsha coolie
pulled me to Foochow Road where he stopped and told me that
he could not locate Newchang Road. On hearing this I did
not argue with him, but paid him 20 cents and then walked
along the road. I passed about 20 houses when I observed
one of my fellow-countrymen named Ts Hyi Pau (周一二), who
owns a piece goods shop in Wusih. I accosted him and he
in turn asked me when I arrived in Shanghai. In reply I
told him that I just reached here. He later asked me for
a loan of money which he said he needed to meet some urgent
use. Accordingly I lent him $20.00, which he promised to
refund me the following day. I further told him that I did
not bring with me much money, but I would buy some cloth
for my wife. Ts said he would do the shopping for me. I,
therefore, gave him another sum of $17.00 in order to purchase
some cloth for my wife. On taking over the money he told me
he would return me the money that I had lent him together with
the cloth that he would buy for me in a few hours. He further
told me that he was living in Room 435 (4th floor) The Grand
Hotel, and asked me to go to his room for recreation. After
the above conversation we departed. Later I went to purchase
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
约13.00美元在来上海的途中。我于1939年6月16日下午6点左右抵达上海，在一个顶部有巨大时钟的大建筑物前的码头（海关码头）上岸。随后我雇了一辆人力车，告诉车夫带我去新昌路的陆瑞泰米行，车夫收费20美分，我同意支付。车夫没有带我去上述地址，而是把我拉到了福州路，停下来说他找不到新昌路。听到这话，我没有与他争辩，付了他20美分，然后沿路步行。我经过了大约20户人家，这时我看到了一位同乡，名叫周一二（Ts Hyi Pau），他在无锡拥有一家布店。我上前与他搭话，他反过来问我何时到达上海。我回答说刚到。后来他向我借钱，说急需使用。于是我借给他20.00美元，他承诺第二天归还。我还告诉他我没带多少钱，但我想给妻子买些布料。周说他可以帮我买。于是我又给了他17.00美元用于给妻子买布。接过钱后，他告诉我几小时内会把借的钱连同买的布一起还给我。他还告诉我他住在大华饭店435号房间（四楼），并请我去他房间娱乐。上述谈话后我们分开。后来我去购买

page_data.en:
- 3 -
a straw hat for $3.60 in a certain shop. After making this
shopping I hired a public ricksha which took me to the Grand
Hotel, Yu Ya Ching - Canton Roads corner. On entering the
Hotel I took a lift to 4th floor and went into Room 433
where I met Ts Vung Nyeu (1st accused) standing by the door.
I approached Ts Vung Nyeu and asked him if Ts Nyi Pau was
in the room. In reply he told me that Ts Nyi Pau had not
yet returned. He then asked me what connection I had with
Ts Nyi Pau, to which I replied that I was a fellow-countryman
of Ts Nyi Pau. I entered the room proper and found nobody
was in. I further asked Ts Vung Nyeu when Ts Nyi Pau would
return to the room. He said he did not know, but told me
that Ts Nyi Pau had left a chit to me on a table. I then
went to the table and took possession of a piece of paper
which I immediately placed in my pocket. I had some congee
in the room. About 20 minutes afterwards a party of police
suddenly raided the room and arrested me. The real object
of my visit to this room was to wait for Ts Nyi Pau from
whom I intended to collect the money that I had lent him and
also to have the cloth that he promised to buy for me. I
do not know why I was arrested. Since the outbreak of the
hostilities I have been living in my native place, but have
not gone to elsewhere. When I left my home my father gave
me a piece of paper on which was written the following address:-
"Luk Zui Tai (陸瑞泰) Rice Shop, Newchang Road". I however,
do not know when or where I lost this chit.
The above is my true statement. Signed:Kao Ming Woo.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
一顶草帽，花了3.60美元。买完东西后，我雇了一辆公共人力车，把我带到虞洽卿路与广东路转角的大华饭店。进入饭店后，我乘电梯到四楼，走进433号房间，遇见朱文元（第一被告）站在门口。我走近朱文元，问他周二宝是否在房间里。他回答说周二宝还没回来。然后他问我和周二宝有什么关系，我回答说是同乡。我走进房间内部，发现没人在里面。我又问朱文元周二宝什么时候回房间。他说不知道，但告诉我周二宝在桌上给我留了一张便条。于是我走到桌前，拿起一张纸，立刻放进口袋。我在房间里喝了一些粥。大约20分钟后，一群警察突然突袭房间并将我逮捕。我去这个房间的真正目的是等待周二宝，打算从他那里收回借出的钱，并拿到他答应为我买的布。我不知道为什么被捕。自战事爆发以来，我一直住在家乡，没有去别处。离家时，父亲给了我一张纸，上面写着以下地址：“新昌路陆瑞泰（Luk Zui Tai）米行”。然而，我不知道是何时何地丢失了这张便条。
以上是我的真实供词。签名：高梦特。

The finger print record of the 1st accused
shows that he has four previous convictions, namely:-
21.4.13 - Attempted Extortion. Released on security.
17.6.20 - Armed Robbery - 4 years & expelled.
24.12.24- Returning - 6 months.
28.12.26- Armed Robbery - 5 years & expelled.
The 2nd accused has no previous convictions.
On the morning of 17.6.39 Sgt. Major SAKAMOTO
of the Japanese Gendarmerie came to C.D.H.Q. accompanied
by an interpreter and requested permission to question
the two accused. This was granted and the two accused
questioned in the presence of D.S.I.s Pryde and Zia
Wan Fong.
The two accused were further questioned by
D.S.I.s Pryde and Zia Wan Fong on the morning and
afternoon of 19.6.39 and a statement taken from the
1st accused, a copy of which is attached.
In this statement the 1st accused admits
his previous convictions. Since 1932 he states
he operated a food shop on Route des Soeurs,
French Concession. That he sold his share in this
concern about a month ago and invested the proceeds
in another food shop on Boul. Montigny. That he is
also a partner in a factory at Zikawei which makes

3.

第一名被告的指纹记录显示其有四次前科，即：-
1913年4月21日 - 企图勒索。取保释放。
1920年6月17日 - 持械抢劫 - 判刑4年并驱逐出境。
1924年12月24日 - 被驱逐后返回 - 判刑6个月。
1926年12月28日 - 持械抢劫 - 判刑5年并驱逐出境。
第二名被告无前科。
1939年6月17日上午，日本宪兵队的坂本（Sakamoto）警曹长在一位翻译的陪同下来到中央巡捕房总部（C.D.H.Q.），请求许可讯问两名被告。该请求获准，两名被告在副督察普赖德（Pryde）和谢万芳（Zia Wan Fong）在场的情况下接受了讯问。
1939年6月19日上午和下午，副督察普赖德和谢万芳再次对两名被告进行了讯问，并从第一名被告处取得了一份供词，副本附后。
在这份供词中，第一名被告承认了其前科。他称自1932年以来，他在法租界姐妹路（Route des Soeurs）经营一家食品店。大约一个月前，他出售了在该商号中的股份，并将所得款项投资于蒙塔尼路（Boul. Montigny）的另一家食品店。他还是徐家汇一家工厂的合伙人，该厂生产

page_data.en:
3/2.

joints for leather belts used on cotton spinning
machines. Through this business he knows one
named Zee Chi Ming (徐启明) who is cotton
broker with offices situated on Fukien Road near
Foochow Road. Together with Zee Chi Ming he en-
gaged Room 443 Grand Hotel, Foochow Road to discuss
business. That at 4 p.m. on 16.6.39 one of the
tea boys at the Grand Hotel informed him that Zee
Chi Ming had telephoned to Room 433, so he went
to this room and answered the phone and Zee Chi
Ming informed him that one named Ts Hyi Pau (周义保),
(a piece goods shop master from Wusih, who was a
mutual friend) had arrived in Shanghai and was
occupying Room 433 and suggested that he (1st accused)
should visit him. The 1st accused went to Room 433
at 8 p.m. and found Ts Hyi Pau there together with
three other male and one female Chinese. All were
having dinner at the time and Ts Hyi Pau invited
him to join them. Shortly afterwards Kao Ming Woo
(2nd accused) arrived and almost immediately Ts Hyi
Pau and the others left the room. A few minutes
afterwards the police arrived.
The 1st accused states he does not know for
what reason these men left the room. He maintains
that he has never been concerned in guerrilla or
page_data.zh:
3/2.

用于棉纺机上的皮带接头。通过这项业务，他认识了一位名叫徐启明（Zee Chi Ming）的人，此人是棉花经纪人，办事处位于福州路附近的福建路。他与徐启明一起在福州路的大华饭店（Grand Hotel）开了443号房间以商讨业务。1939年6月16日下午4时，大华饭店的一名茶房告知他，徐启明打电话到433号房间，于是他前往该房间接听电话，徐启明告诉他，一位名叫周义保（Ts Hyi Pau）的人（无锡的一位绸缎庄老板，是他们的共同朋友）已抵达上海并住在433号房间，建议他（第一名被告）去拜访。第一名被告于晚上8点前往433号房间，发现周义保在那里，另有三名中国男性和一名中国女性。当时众人正在用餐，周义保邀请他加入。不久后，高茂梧（Kao Ming Woo，第二名被告）到达，几乎与此同时，周义保和其他人离开了房间。几分钟后，警察到达。
第一名被告称不知道这些人离开房间的原因。他坚称自己从未参与游击队或

page_data.en:
3/3.

other anti-Japanese activities, and except for one
occasion, shortly after the fall of Nanking, when he
went to Wusih to see if his house was intact, he has
never left Shanghai, since the beginning of hostilities.
The 2nd accused has been questioned but up to
the present no reliable statement can be obtained from
him. He claims he arrived in Shanghai from Wusih on
16.6.39 (the day of arrest). This man is very nervous,
but whether his nervousness is caused by a guilty
conscience or the shock of having been arrested, cannot
be definitely decided at present.
The man will be further interrogated.

H.E.S
20/6

G. B. Suple
D. S. I.

其他反日活动，并且除了南京沦陷后不久曾去无锡查看房屋是否完好这一例外情况外，自战事开始以来他从未离开过上海。
第二名被告已接受讯问，但截至目前未能从他那里获得可靠的供词。他声称自己于1939年6月16日（被捕当天）从无锡抵达上海。此人非常紧张，但其紧张是由于良心不安还是因被捕而受惊，目前尚无法确定。
将对此人进行进一步讯问。

H.E.S

G. B. Suple

TS VUNG NYLU (〔此处转录不清〕), 50,
Zang-zoh,                                     D. A. I. Pryde,
C.l                  19.6.39

My name is Ts Vung Nyou, age 50, native of Zangzoh,
and I am a partner in the Kwei Jeu Factory, manufacturing
leather belts and other accessories for weaving machinery at
Zikawei, French Concession.
    I was born at Zangchow, near Zangzch, and was educated
in my native place until I was 13 years of age. I then came
to Shanghai and was employed as an apprentice in the Zang Ding
Food Shop on Seward Road. I remained in this employment for
four years. I then returned to my native place and married,
and remained there for about three years. About 1910, I
returned to Shanghai and was employed as an assistant in the
Zoong Nyeu Lieu Restaurant on Foochow Road.. I then became
unemployed for approximately two years. During this time, I
was arrested by West Hongkew Station on two occasions. The
first time on a charge of attempted extortion and I was
released on security, the second time on a charge of larceny and
I was sentenced to one month imprisonment. I then became a
second to a Chinese detective/sergeant at West Hongkew and
continued to make a living in this manner until about June 1920
when I was concerned in the robbery of a cargo of opium on
Peking Road. After the robbery, I left Shanghai for Hankow, but
was later arrested by detectives from Central Station and
brought back to Shanghai and sentenced to 4 years imprisonment
and expelled. I was released from gaol in July 1923. About
one year later, I was again arrested by Central Station detec-
tives for "Returning after a Sentence of Expulsion" and
sentenced to six months imprisonment and in addition, had to
page_data.zh:
朱文元（TS VUNG NYLU，〔此处转录不清〕），50岁，
常州，                                     副督察 普赖德，
C.l                  1939年6月19日

我叫朱文元（Ts Vung Nyou），50岁，常州人，我是法租界徐家汇桂记工厂（Kwei Jeu Factory）的合伙人，该厂生产织布机用的皮带及其他配件。
我出生在常州附近的张渚（Zangchow, near Zangzch），在家乡受教育至13岁。随后我来到上海，在西华德路（Seward Road）的张鼎食品店（Zang Ding Food Shop）当学徒。我在此工作了四年。之后我返回家乡结婚，并在那里待了大约三年。约1910年，我回到上海，在福州路的宗纽留餐馆（Zoong Nyeu Lieu Restaurant）当助手。随后我失业了大约两年。在此期间，我曾两次被西虹口捕房逮捕。第一次是因企图勒索罪，我取保释放；第二次是因盗窃罪，我被判监禁一个月。之后我成为西虹口捕房一名华籍侦探/巡长的助手，并以这种方式谋生，直到1920年6月左右，我参与了在北京路抢劫一批鸦片的事件。抢劫发生后，我离开上海前往汉口，但后来被中央捕房的侦探逮捕并带回上海，被判刑4年并驱逐出境。我于1923年7月出狱。大约一年后，我再次因“被驱逐后返回”罪被中央捕房侦探逮捕，被判监禁六个月，此外，还须

page_data.en:
- 2 -

serve an extra year (Remission of previous sentence). About
6 months after being released from gaol on this occasion, I was
arrested by Louza Station on a Charge of Armed Robbery and
sentenced to 5 years imprisonment. I was released on this
occasion in October, 1930.
I then was employed as an assistant in a gambling house
on Rue du Consulat, French Concession for 1½ years. With money,
I had saved, I then together with another man opened a small food
shop on Rte. des Soeurs, French Concession and operated this
until one month ago, when I sold my share in this establishment
for $2,150.00 and invested the money in a share in the Tsung
Tsoong Food Shop on Boul.Montigny. About one year ago, I invested
$3,000.00 in this Kwei Jeu Factory ( in Zikawei) and still own
a partnership in this concern.
A business friend of mine named Zee Chi King, who is a
cotton broker with an office on Fukien Road, near Foochow Road,
suggested that I should open a room in the Grand Hotel, where we
could discuss business. Zee, being a cotton broker, knows all
the cotton factories and as I manufacture leather belts etc. for
cotton machines, we intended doing business together. I there-
fore opened Room 443 of the Grand Hotel. I also know a man named
Ts Nyi Pau who is a piece goods shop master in Wusieh, and also
an acquaintance of Zee Chi King.
At about 4 p.m. on 16.6.39 one of the tea boys at the
Grand Hotel informed me that Zee Chi Ming had telephoned to Room
443 asking for Ts Nyi Pau and as Ts Nyi Pau was not in, would I
answer the phone. I then went from my own room (443) to Room 4:
and spoke to Zee Chi Ming on the telephone. He informed me tha
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

额外服刑一年（撤销之前的减刑）。在这次出狱约6个月后，我因持械抢劫罪被老闸捕房逮捕，被判刑5年。我于1930年10月此次获释。
随后我在法租界领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）的一家赌场当了1年半的助手。用我积攒的钱，我与另一人在法租界姐妹路（Rte. des Soeurs）开了一家小食品店，一直经营到一个月前，我以2,150.00美元的价格出售了在该店中的股份，并将这笔钱投资于蒙塔尼路（Boul.Montigny）的宗总食品店（Tsung Tsoong Food Shop）的股份。大约一年前，我在这家桂记工厂（位于徐家汇）投资了3,000.00美元，至今仍拥有该商号的合伙权。
我的一位商界朋友徐启金（Zee Chi King，音译，原文为Zee Chi King，下文供词中又称Zee Chi Ming），他是棉花经纪人，在福州路附近的福建路设有办事处，建议我在大华饭店开一个房间，以便我们商讨业务。徐作为棉花经纪人，熟悉所有棉纺厂，而我为棉纺机器生产皮带等，因此我们打算合作做生意。所以我开了大华饭店的443号房间。我还认识一位名叫周义保（Ts Nyi Pau）的人，他是无锡的一家绸缎庄老板，也是徐启金的熟人。
1939年6月16日下午4点左右，大华饭店的一名茶房告诉我，徐启明（Zee Chi Ming）打电话到443号房间找周义保（Ts Nyi Pau），因周义保不在，问我是否愿意接电话。于是我从自己的房间（443号）走到4:
并在电话中与徐启明交谈。他告诉我那

page_data.en:
- 3 -

Ts Nyi Pau had arrived in Shanghai and was living in Room 433
and suggested I should call on him. Therefore I visited Room
433 at about 8 p.m. 16.6.39 and met Ts Nyi Pau there together
with 3 other male and one female Chinese. I do not know the
names of these others and have not met them before. They
were having dinner at the time and Ts Nyi Pau invited me to
join them. A few minutes later Kao Ming ..oo (2nd. accused)
entered the room. Almost immediately after Kao's arrival Ts
Nyi Pau and the other three men and one woman left the room
and immediately afterwards the police arrived and placed Kao
Ming ..oo and myself under arrest. I do not know why these
others left the room, but at the time I thought they wished
to talk together outside.
    I have no idea why I have been arrested. I have never
been a soldier neither have I ever been concerned in guerrilla
or other anti-Japanese activities. With the exception of one
occasion just after the fall of Nanking, when I obtained a
pass and visited Wusih for 10 days to see if my house was
intact, I have never left the French Concession and International
Settlement since the beginning of hostilities.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

周义保已抵达上海并住在433号房间，建议我去拜访他。因此，我在1939年6月16日晚上8点左右访问了433号房间，在那里见到了周义保以及另外三名中国男性和一名中国女性。我不知道这些人的名字，以前也未见过他们。当时他们正在吃晚饭，周义保邀请我加入。几分钟后，高茂..oo（第二名被告）进入房间。高到达后几乎立即，周义保和其他三名男子及一名女子离开了房间，随即警察到达并将高茂..oo和我逮捕。我不知道其他人为什么离开房间，但当时我认为他们想在外面一起谈话。
我不知道自己为何被捕。我从未当过兵，也从未参与游击队或其他反日活动。除了南京沦陷后不久的一次例外，当时我弄到通行证去无锡呆了10天以查看房屋是否完好外，自战事开始以来，我从未离开过法租界和公共租界。

D. C. (Special Branch).

S. 1. Misc. 92/39.
JUNE 17, 39.

2.

At 3.40 p.m. on 16.6.39 Sgt. Major **〔此处转录不清〕** of the Japanese Gendarmerie stationed at the Floating Restaurant, Peking Road Jetty, telephoned C.B.H.Q., and requested assistance to arrest six male Chinese at a certain place in the French Concession, on a charge of having been concerned in guerrilla activities. At about 4 p.m. Sgt. Major Sakamoto again telephoned and stated that the men they required to arrest were moving into the International Settlement and he would apply for assistance later. At 8 p.m. Sgt. Major Sakamoto and one other member of the Japanese Gendarmerie came to C.B.H.Q. and requested assistance to visit Room 435 Grand Hotel to arrest six male Chinese, two of whom were named Wong Siau Doo (黄小大) and Pao Chi Ming (包啟明), the remainder names unknown, and alleged that these six men had been concerned in guerrilla activities in the Wusih Area.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.Is Pryde, Sia Wan Fong, D.P.S. Yamahara, C.D.S. 40, 272, C.D.C. 184 and 212, and the stated address

S. 1. Misc. 92/39.
1939年6月17日。

2.

〔此处转录不清〕

1939年6月16日下午3时40分，驻扎在北京路码头浮包餐厅的日本宪兵队警曹长**〔此处转录不清〕**致电罪案科总部（C.B.H.Q.），请求协助在法租界某地逮捕六名中国男子，指控他们参与游击活动。下午4点左右，坂本（Sakamoto）警曹长再次致电，称他们需要逮捕的人正进入公共租界，他将稍后申请协助。晚上8点，坂本警曹长和另一名日本宪兵队成员来到罪案科总部，请求协助前往大华饭店435号房间逮捕六名中国男子，其中两人名为黄小大（Wong Siau Doo）和包启明（Pao Chi Ming），其余姓名不详，并称这六人曾参与无锡地区的游击活动。

副督察普赖德、谢万芳（Sia Wan Fong）、副巡长山原（Yamahara）、华捕40号、272号，以及印捕184号和212号提供了协助，并前往所述地址

page_data.en:
2/2.

visited. Two male Chinese were found in the
room, namely:-
1st accused : Ts Vung Nyeu (朱文元), 50, Zangzoh,
M/Factory master, Sik wei.
2nd accused : Kao Ming Woo (高茂梧), 32, Wusih,
M/Rice merch nt. Wusih.

It was apparent that there had been a number
of persons to dinner in this room and that the others
had left just prior to the arrival of the police.
The following was found in possession of
the 1st accused : -
5 name cards (one of which bore the characters
Zee Chi Ming (徐啟明) the last
two characters being the same as
the characters of Pao Chi Ming
(包啟明) whom the Gendarmerie
wished to arrest.)

3 20-cent pieces.
1 5 " piece.
2 1-cent piece.
1 Key.

In possession of the 2nd accused was
$6.20 in notes.
1 10-cent piece.
4 coppers.
page_data.zh:
2/2.

进行搜查。在房间内发现两名中国男子，即：-
第一名被告：朱文元（Ts Vung Nyeu），50岁，常州人，
男/工厂主，徐家汇。
第二名被告：高茂梧（Kao Ming Woo），32岁，无锡人，
男/米商，无锡。

显然此前有多人在此房间用餐，其他人在警察到达前刚刚离开。
在第一名被告身上搜出以下物品：-
5张名片（其中一张印有徐启明（Zee Chi Ming）字样，最后两个字与宪兵队希望逮捕的包启明（Pao Chi Ming）的名字相同。）

3枚2角银币。
1枚5分银币。
2枚1分铜币。
1把钥匙。

在第二名被告身上搜出
纸币6.20美元。
1枚1角银币。
4枚铜板。

page_data.en:
2/3.

7 stamps.
2 keys.
4 papers.

The following was also seized in the room
and must have been left there by the persons who
**〔此处转录不清〕** : -

One flannel jacket containing : -
1 brown paper
1 20-cent note.
1 pair sun glasses
1 paper

One white jacket containing : -
$150 in notes.
1 20-cent piece
5 stamps
1 cigarette holder

The two arrested men were conveyed to C.B.H.Q.
and detectives left in the room to arrest anyone who
visited there.

On return to C.B.H.Q. Sgt. Major Sakamoto
of the Japanese Gendarmerie stated that he was in
possession of information that Wong Siau Doo (黄小杜)
(not arrested) was a leader of guerrillas in the
Wusih area and had amassed between $30,000 - $50,000
by robbery. That he had brought this money to Shanghai

2/3.

7张邮票。
2把钥匙。
4张纸。

房间内还查获以下物品，必定是那些
**〔此处转录不清〕** 的人遗留在那里的：-

一件法兰绒夹克，内含：-
1张棕色纸
1张2角纸币

一件白色夹克，内含：-
纸币150美元。

两名被捕男子被押送至罪案科总部，侦探留在房间内以逮捕任何来访者。

返回罪案科总部后，日本宪兵队的坂本警曹长称，他掌握情报显示黄小杜（Wong Siau Doo，未被捕）是无锡地区游击队的头目，并通过抢劫积累了30,000至50,000美元。他将这笔钱带到上海

page_data.en:
2/4.

to further guerrilla activities, and had handed
some to a girl in a massage establishment situated
on the ground floor of the Chun Nan (春南) Hotel,
Avenue Edward VII, for safe keeping. Sgt. Major
Sakamoto requested assistance to search this place
and seize the money. To substantiate his information
Sgt. Major Sakamoto then brought his informer to
C.B.H.Q. This man was disguised by having a cloth
bag over his head. When questioned he stated he
had obtained this information from an old friend
of his named Wong K ei Nyeu (王桂元) who was also
an associate of Wong Siau Doo. He stated that he
did not know the name of the female who had possession
of this money, but described her as being of stout
build and cross-eyed.
    Assistance was rendered at 10 p.m. accordingly
and the massage establishment, which proved to be
situated at 548 Ave. Edward 7th, visited. No female
answering the given description was found there.
All the rooms and the boxes therein were searched,
but nothing found.
    The two arrested persons were placed in an
identification parade at C.B.H.Q., but the Gendarmerie
informer was unable to identify them.
    Both men have been detained in Central Cells
pending further enquiries being made.

E. R. Suyde

以资助游击活动，并将部分款项交给爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）春南酒店（Chun Nan Hotel）底楼一家按摩院的一名女子保管。坂本警曹长请求协助搜查该地点并没收款项。为了证实其情报，坂本警曹长随后将其线人带到罪案科总部。此人头上套着一个布袋以作伪装。经讯问，他称此情报来自他的老朋友王桂元（Wong K ei Nyeu），此人也是黄小杜的同伙。他称不知道持有这笔款项的女子的姓名，但描述她体型肥胖且斜视。
于是当晚10点提供了协助，并走访了该按摩院，经查实位于爱多亚路548号。在那里未发现符合上述描述的女子。搜查了所有房间及其中的箱子，但未发现任何物品。
两名被捕人员在罪案科总部参加了列队辨认，但宪兵队的线人未能认出他们。
两人均被关押在中央拘留所，以待进一步调查。

E. R. Suyde

Hsu Nyoch Yieh (許玉葉), age 23, married,
residing in Frenchtown,
xx D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung
translated      Tsaung Zung Pau

I am a second-hand clock & watch dealer by profession.
I was arrested by the Police on the 18-6-39 and
detained there until 12 noon on the 13-7-39, when I was
taken by a party of Japanese to the Japanese Military Police
Headquarters, The Bund. I was questioned by two Japanese and
a Chinese if I had visited the Yangtse Hotel for the purpose
of purchasing pistols. I replied that I went there to buy
opium, but not pistols. A Japanese soldier then came into the
room and by showing his pistol to me, threatening that I had
better confessed to the purchase of pistols. On my refusing
to admit this, the soldier went away. The other two Japanese
told me that they could release me if I only admitted that
I went to the hotel to purchase pistols. They further stated
that if I did not wish to tell them so, I should, on my
return to the Police Station, inform the foreign detectives
that I did go to the Yangtse Hotel to purchase pistols and
that during my presence in the room the man who was going to
sell me the pistols showed me a sample of his. The two
Japanese added that should I refuse to talk in this manner,
I should never be released.

Sgd., Crossmarked & Thumbprinted by HSU NYOEH YIEH.

我是一名二手钟表商。

并被拘留至1939年7月13日中午12时，当时我被一群日本人带到外滩的日本宪兵司令部。两名日本人和一名中国人讯问我是否曾为了购买手枪而去过扬子饭店。我回答说我去那里是为了买鸦片，而不是手枪。随后一名日本士兵走进房间，向我展示他的手枪，威胁说我最好承认购买了手枪。在我拒绝承认后，那名士兵离开了。另外两名日本人告诉我，只要我承认去饭店是为了购买手枪，他们就可以释放我。他们进一步表示，如果我不愿这样告诉他们，我在回到警察局后，应告知外国侦探，我确实去了扬子饭店购买手枪，并且在我在场期间，那个要卖给我手枪的人向我展示了样品。那两名日本人补充说，如果我拒绝按这种方式说法，我将永远无法获释。

HSU NYOEH YIEH (許若葉), 23, M/Unemployed,
Swatow, C.D.S. 272,
C.1 19. 6. 39. Clerk Yao Dinsin.

My name is Hsu Nyoeh Yieh, aged 23 years, native of Swatow, M/
formerly employed as pawnshop assistant and at present without
employment, N.F.A.

I have been unemployed since October, last year. I live
in hotels and lodging houses all the time in Shanghai. Hsu Nyih
Ding (1st. arrested man) is a native friend of mine .

At about 4 or 5 p.m. 11.6.39 when walking along Rue du
Consulat, F.C. I happened to encounter Hsu Nyih Ding, who was on
his way visiting a friend. He informed me that he had just
arrived from Tungchow and that he intended opening a room in
either the Chungnan or Dah Woo Hotels ~~for temporary quartering~~
during his brief stay in Shanghai, where he would purchase
certain provisions. At about 8 p.m. even date, Hsu Nyih Ding
and myself met again at the entrance of the Chungnan Hotel, Ave.
Edward VII, where I was informed that Room No.610, Dah Woo Hotel
had been engaged, and that he would like me accompanying him to
his room for a tete-a-tete. I did not go with him at once, but
went there alone some minutes later.

During my presence in his room, he informed me that he
intended going into the opium business, saying that the profit
therefrom was so good that he would risk carrying a quantity
on his own person and make a trip to the outskirts of Tungchow
for sale. As he was soliciting my advice in this matter, I
told him that I had a friend named "Zung", and that the latter
being an opium dealer, I would arrange an interview and talk
the matter over with him.

During the forenoon of the 13 or 14.6.39, I proceeded to
page_data.zh:
许若叶（HSU NYOEH YIEH），23岁，男/无业，
汕头，C.D.S. 272号，
C.1 1939年6月19日. 书记员 Yao Dinsin.

我叫许若叶，23岁，汕头人，男/前当铺助手，现无业，非上海籍居民（N.F.A.）。

自去年十月起我一直失业。在上海期间，我一直居住在旅馆和客栈中。许业廷（第一名被捕者）是我的同乡朋友。

1939年6月11日下午4或5时许，当我沿法租界领事馆路（Rue du Consulat, F.C.）行走时，偶遇正去拜访朋友的许业廷。他告诉我他刚从通州抵达，打算在短暂停留上海期间，在中南旅馆或大沪旅馆开一个房间~~作为临时住所~~，并在那里购买某些物资。当晚8时许，我与许业廷再次在南京东路（Ave. Edward VII）中南旅馆门口相遇，得知他已在大沪旅馆预订了610号房间，并希望我陪他去房间私下交谈。我没有立刻跟他去，而是几分钟后独自前往。

在他房间里，他告诉我打算从事鸦片生意，说利润丰厚，他甚至愿意随身携带一定数量的鸦片前往通州郊区销售。由于他就此事征求我的建议，我告诉他我有个朋友叫“郑”（Zung），此人是个鸦片贩子，我可以安排见面并与他商谈此事。

1939年6月13日或14日上午，我前去

page_data.en:
- 2 -

see "Zung" at his residence at the upstairs room of a shop on
the intersection of Rue Hou and Avenue Edward VII. On the
purpose of my visit being revealed to him, Zung stated that he
would introduce me to his friend's son, who worked in an opium
wholesale establishment and would arrange an interview with him
in the near future for negotiations.

As no reply was forthcoming, I went to see Zung again
at 10 a.m. 18.6.39. In his room, I was introduced to another
whose name was also Zung. The latter enquired if I actually
intended purchasing a quantity of opium. I replied in the
affirmative, whereby he revealed that he had a friend living
in the Nanyang Lodging House, North Chekiang Road, who had in
store a large consignment of Persian or Red Opium as well as
morphine and other narcotics. He added that the red opium,
which had proved a popular demand in and around Shanghai, would
usually cost approx. $120.00 or more per unit, but owing to his
relations with that person, he could purchase any quantity at
a much lower rate, i.e. approx. $110.00 per unit. (The second
named "Zung" was the person arrested at Yangtsze Hotel at the
same time). I assured Zung that I was actually eager to
purchase a quantity of red opium, whereby he instructed me to
proceed to the entrance of the Yangtsze Hotel, 387 Yunnan Road,
together with my friend, Hsu Ding Hyih, and await their arrival
at 8 p.m. same date. We should carry the money to this appointment too.

At about 5 p.m. that day, I proceeded to the Dah Faung
Hotel (Room 439) looking for Hsu Ding Hyih, to whom I intended
reporting the foregoing. However, on arrival, I was informed by :
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

在侯家路（Rue Hou）与南京东路（Avenue Edward VII）交叉口一家店铺的楼上房间见“郑”。当我向他说明来意后，郑表示会将我介绍给他的一位在鸦片批发行工作的朋友之子，并在近期安排我与该人见面洽谈。

因未获回复，我于1939年6月18日上午10时再次去见郑。在他的房间里，我被介绍给另一位同样姓郑的人。后者询问我是否真的打算购买一定数量的鸦片。我给予了肯定回答，于是他透露他在北浙江路南阳旅舍有一位朋友，那里存有大批波斯鸦片或红土鸦片，以及吗啡和其他麻醉品。他补充说，红土鸦片在上海及周边地区需求旺盛，通常每单位价格约为120美元或更高，但由于他与那人的关系，他可以以更低的价格购买任意数量，即每单位约110美元。（第二位被称为“郑”的人，是当时在扬子饭店同时被捕的人。）我向郑保证我确实急于购买一定数量的红土鸦片，于是他指示我与我的朋友许定希（Hsu Ding Hyih，音译）一同前往云南路387号扬子饭店门口，并于当晚8时等候他们的到来。我们也应携带资金赴约。

当天下午5时许，我前往大丰旅馆（439号房间）寻找许定希，打算向他报告上述情况。然而，到达后，我从以下人员处得知：

page_data.en:
- 3 -

one of the room boys that Hsu had just left the hotel. As I
walked out of Dah Faung Lodging House, I was lucky to meet Hsu
on Rue Hue. I reported to him of what had happened and was told
that he would like to buy 10 or 15 units of red opium if the
price was cheap, and, in case, the price was quite dear, he
still intended buying one or two.

At about 8 p.m. as previously arranged, Hsu and myself
proceeded to the entrance of the Yangtsze Hotel awaiting to
see the man Zung, who came 20 minutes afterwards, accompanied
by a Japanese. (Hsu and I came separately and I arrived first.
The Japanese then took me to Room No.704, where he enquired if
my 'master' was coming too (Hsu). I replied that Hsu would come
later. Zung then ordered me to go downstairs and await at the
entrance for Hsu, saying that he had the samples with him already
and that if Hsu had brought with him the money for opium, he
was sure that the transaction could be concluded right away.
I at once proceeded downstairs and came back to Room 704 with
Hsu. The Japanese gave Hsu and I each a cigarette and left the
room saying that he was hungry and would show us the samples
after having some refreshments outside. Soon Police arrived
and placed us under arrest.

This is the truth.

Signed : HSU NYOEH YIH.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

一名茶房说许刚离开旅馆。当我走出大丰客栈时，幸运地在霞飞路（Rue Hue，今淮海中路）遇到了许。我向他汇报了发生的情况，他告诉我如果价格便宜，他想买10到15单位红土鸦片，如果价格相当昂贵，他仍打算买一两单位。

晚上8时许，按先前约定，我和许前往扬子饭店门口等候见郑姓男子，二十分钟后他 accompanied by a Japanese（陪同一名日本人）到来。（许和我分开前来，我先到达。随后那名日本人带我到704号房间，询问我的“主人”（指许）是否也来。我回答说许稍后会来。郑随即命令我下楼在门口等候许，说他已带了样品，如果许带来了买鸦片的钱，他确信交易可以立即达成。我立即下楼，并与许一起回到704号房间。日本人给了我和许每人一支香烟，然后离开房间，说他饿了，去外面吃点东西后再给我们看样品。不久警察赶到并将我们逮捕。

以上属实。

签名：许若叶（HSU NYOEH YIH）。

page_data.en:
HSU MYIH DING (許華庭), age 24, married,

Tungchow                                      xx             C.D.C.-211
                                               translated
H. Q. C. B.           19-6-39      --------      Tsaung Zung Pau

I was formerly a cotton dealer in Tungchow, but
lost the job in April 1938 when the city was occupied by
Japanese troops.

On 11-6-39 I arrived in Shanghai from Tungchow
and put up in Room 330 at the Dah Fong (大方) Hotel, Avenue
Edward VII, French Concession. I brought $350.00 with me
for the purpose of trafficking in opium.

At 6 p.m. on the day of my arrival, I encountered
my intimate friend, Hsu Nyoch Yieh (許玉英), at the entrance
to Poh Ling Li (卜慶弄里) alleyway, Rue du Consulat, French
Concession. He then accompanied me to the Dah Fong Hotel
and while he waited on the ground floor, I went upstairs to
Room 330, but rejoined him a few minutes later to proceed
together to Room 610 of the Dah Woo Lodging House, which was
engaged by my friends. There I asked Hsu Nyoch Yieh about
the price of opium in the local market, and he stated that
the approximate price was $130.00 per lb. I left the lodging
house after requesting him to purchase some opium for me.
I removed to Dah Tsoong (大中) Hotel on the 12-6-39.

At about 5 p.m. 18-6-39 whilst passing outside the
Chung Nan (中南) Hotel, Avenue Edward VII, I met Hsu Nyoch
Yieh who happened to come out of the Billiards Room of this
hotel. He told me that he had a friend named Sung (鄭),
native of Fukien, who was desirous of selling one lb. of opium
for the sum of approximately $120.00 and who had also in
his possession some morphine and pistols for sale at a cheap
price. I informed him that I did not require any morphine or
page_data.zh:
许华庭（HSU MYIH DING），24岁，已婚，

通州                                      xx             C.D.C.-211
                                               翻译
总部 刑事科           1939年6月19日      --------      Tsaung Zung Pau

我原是通州的棉花商人，但在1938年4月该城被日军占领时失业。

1939年6月11日，我从通州抵达上海，入住法租界南京东路（Ave. Edward VII）大丰（Dah Fong，大方）旅馆330号房间。我随身携带350.00美元，目的是从事鸦片贸易。

抵达当天傍晚6时，我在法租界领事馆路卜庆里（Poh Ling Li）巷口遇到了密友许玉英（Hsu Nyoch Yieh）。随后他陪我到大丰旅馆，他在一楼等候时，我上楼去了330号房间，但几分钟后我又下楼与他汇合，一同前往由我朋友预订的大沪客栈（Dah Woo Lodging House）610号房间。在那里，我向许玉英询问当地市场的鸦片价格，他说大约每磅130.00美元。我请求他为我购买一些鸦片后离开了客栈。1939年6月12日，我搬至大中（Dah Tsoong）旅馆。

1939年6月18日下午5时许，当我经过南京东路中南（Chung Nan）旅馆外时，遇到了碰巧从该旅馆台球室出来的许玉英。他告诉我他有个福建籍朋友姓宋（Sung，注：原文拼音为Sung，但上下文对应之前的Zheng/Zung，此处依原文译作宋，或可能为同一人不同拼写），想以约120.00美元的价格出售1磅鸦片，并且他手中还有一些吗啡和手枪低价出售。我告诉他我不需要任何吗啡或

page_data.en:
- 2 -

pistols, as I was requested by someone only to purchase opium.
He stated that he had arranged with Zung to talk over the
matter again at the Yangtse Hotel, Yunnan Road, at 7 or 8 p.m.,
and requested me to meet him at the entrance to the hotel at
that hour. At about 8 p.m. that night I proceeded to the
entrance of the Yangtse Hotel and found that Hsu Nyoch Yieh
was already there with his friend named Zung. They
immediately took me to Room 704 of this hotel, the only
occupant of which was a Japanese. Zung spoke to the latter in
Japanese for a while. I then asked Zung regarding the price
of his opium, and he stated that the price would be
approximately $120.00. He asked me whether I had brought the
money, to which I replied in the negative. At this juncture
a Police party arrived and placed me under arrest.

Since my arrival in Shanghai I have, apart from
losing about $50.00 in gambling, purchased a number of
articles including two gold finger rings, wrist watch, cloth,
socks etc. for the total sum of $180.00. All these articles
had been sent to my native place by some friends at my request.
The remaining sum of $110.00 was temporarily kept at an office
in the former "China Merchants Steam Navigation Co." Building,
Foochow Road, through a friend of Zung's (name unknown), on
the understanding that Zung should accompany me whenever I
wish to take this money.

Sgd., Cross-marked & Thumbprinted by : HSU NYIH MING.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

手枪，因为有人只要求我购买鸦片。
他说他已经与Zung（音译）安排好，于晚上7点或8点在云南路扬子饭店再次商谈此事，并请求我在那时到饭店门口与他见面。当晚约8点，我前往扬子饭店门口，发现Hsu Nyoch Yieh（音译）已经在那里，同行的还有他的朋友Zung（音译）。他们立即将我带到该饭店的704房间，房内唯一的住客是一名日本人。Zung（音译）用日语与该日本人交谈了一会儿。随后我向Zung（音译）询问鸦片的价格，他说价格大约是120.00元。他问我是否带了钱，我回答没有。就在此时，一队警察赶到并将我逮捕。

自从我抵达上海以来，除了赌博输掉约50.00元外，我还购买了一些物品，包括两枚金戒指、一只手表、布料、袜子等，总金额为180.00元。应我的要求，所有这些物品已由一些朋友寄回我的老家。剩余的110.00元通过Zung（音译）的一位朋友（姓名不详）暂时存放在福州路原“招商局”大楼的一间办公室里，约定是只要我想取这笔钱，Zung（音译）应陪同前往。

签署人，画十字并按手印：HSU NYIH MING（许业明，音译）。

page_data.en:
D. C. (Special Branch).

**〔此处转录不清〕**

Headquarters
C.l. Misc. 93/39    Crime Branch
                     June 19,    39.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY WATER POLICE.

At 8 p.m. June 18, 1939, Sgt. Major
Sakamoto of the Japanese Military Water Police
requested assistance to arrest two alleged guerillas,
names etc. unknown.

Sgt. Major Sakamoto had informed D.P.S.
Yamahara that an informer Sung Hoo Hwei (宋与辉),
Taiwan, had contacted the two males who had expressed
a wish to purchase two or three dozen pistols.
A Mauser pistol had been shown to them as a sample
and they were satisfied. They had told the informer
they would meet him at the entrance to the Far Eastern
Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m.
June 18, 1939.

At 8.30 p.m. D.P.S. Yamahara was informed
that the two alleged guerillas had informed the informer
per telephone that they would meet him in room 4 of the
Nanyang Hotel, 304 North Chekiang Road.

It was arranged that Sgt. Major Sakamoto
would be in the room as the dealer and the informer to
pose as the go-between. On the arrival of the two males
Sgt. Major Sakamoto would inform Crime Branch Headquarters
who would then attend with a party.

（左侧手写批注：）
OK
Lut 19/6
S1
D.B.Q.
19/6
page_data.zh:
D. C. (特务科)。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

总部
C.l. Misc. 93/39    刑事科
                     1939年6月19日。

协助日本军方水上警察。

1939年6月18日晚上8点，日本军方水上警察的坂本（Sakamoto）警曹长请求协助逮捕两名涉嫌游击队员，姓名等信息不详。

坂本警曹长曾告知警务处副巡官（D.P.S.）山原（Yamahara），一名来自台湾的线人宋与辉（Sung Hoo Hwei）已联系上这两名男子，他们表示希望购买两到三打手枪。向他们展示了一支毛瑟手枪作为样品，他们表示满意。他们告诉线人，将于1939年6月18日晚上8点至9点之间在虞洽卿路远东酒店门口与他见面。

晚上8点30分，警务处副巡官山原获悉，这两名涉嫌游击队员通过电话通知线人，他们将改在浙江北路304号南洋酒店的4号房间与他见面。

经安排，坂本警曹长将在房间内扮演卖家，线人则扮演中间人。当这两名男子到达时，坂本警曹长将通知刑事科总部，届时总部将派员前往。

（左侧手写批注：）
同意
Lut 6月19日
S1
D.B.Q.
6月19日

page_data.en:
- 2 -

The British Military were informed of the
intended visit at 8.45 p.m. No objection was raised.
At 9.15 p.m. D.P.S. Yamahara informed the
undersigned that the wanted males had again telephoned
the Military Water Police informer stating they had
changed the venue to room 704 of the Yangtse Hotel,
Yunnan Road.
At 9.45 p.m. a telephone message was
received from Sgt. Major Sakamoto to the effect that
the two males were then in room 704 of the Yangtse
Hotel.
A party consisting of D.P.S. Yamahara,
D.I. Chu, C.D.S. 40, 272 and C.D.C. 211 and the
undersigned attended the room at 9.50 p.m.
In the room was Sgt. Major Sakamoto and
the informer and a number of other Japanese as also
two others who gave their names as :-
(1) HSU NYIH DING (許業廷), 24, Tungchow,
H/Cotton yarn dealer,
residing Chiang Tsao Kong
(姜灶港), Tungchow.
(2) HSU WYCEH YINH (許玉英), 23, Swatow,
ex-pawnshop assistant, N.F.A.
A search of their persons in the room
revealed nothing of an incriminating nature. A search
of the room proved fruitless also.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

英军当局于晚上8点45分获知此次行动意向。未提出异议。
晚上9点15分，警务处副巡官山原告知本人，被通缉的两名男子再次致电军方水上警察线人，称已将地点改为云南路扬子饭店的704房间。
晚上9点45分，收到坂本警曹长的电话消息，称这两名男子当时已在扬子饭店的704房间内。
由警务处副巡官山原、督察朱（Chu）、刑事侦探警士（C.D.S.）40号和272号、刑事侦探警员（C.D.C.）211号以及本人组成的小队于晚上9点50分到达该房间。
房间内已有坂本警曹长、线人以及其他几名日本人，还有另外两人，他们报出的姓名如下：
(1) HSU NYIH DING（許業廷），24岁，通州人，职业：棉纱商，住址：通州姜灶港。
(2) HSU WYCEH YINH（許玉英，音译），23岁，汕头人，前当铺助手，无固定住所（N.F.A.）。
对他们在房间内的人身搜查未发现任何罪证。对房间的搜查也一无所获。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

Questioned in the room as to the reason of
their visit they stated they had wished to purchase
opium and the Water Police informer had told them he
could procure some for them and had told them to go to
the room.

Louza Station was informed of the visit.

On return to Crime Branch Headquarters, Sgt.
Major Sakamoto and informer left, saying they would
return on the morning of the 19th June.

The 1st named suspect stated he arrived in
Shanghai from Tungchow on the 12th inst. and stayed
in room 328 of the Dah Fong (大力) Hotel, Route
Touraine, French Concession. He met the 2nd suspect
whom he has known for some years and spoke of having
come to Shanghai to purchase goods etc. together with
a friend named Zung (陳). Goods to the value of
$180.00 were purchased by him and Zung was leaving
Shanghai on the morning of June 19th to take them to
Tungchow.

He had left about $180.00 and of this he
gave $110.00 to keep for him.

He intended buying opium with the $110.00
and mentioned this to the 2nd suspect who stated he
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

在房间内受询问及来访原因时，他们声称希望购买鸦片，且水上警察线人告诉他们可以弄到一些，并让他们去该房间。

老闸捕房已获知此次行动。

返回刑事科总部后，坂本警曹长和线人离开，称将于6月19日上午返回。

第一名嫌疑人称，他于本月12日从通州抵达上海，住在法租界陶尔斐司路大力饭店（Dah Fong Hotel）的328房间。他遇到了第二名嫌疑人，他认识此人已有数年，并谈到与一位名叫Zung（陳，音译）的朋友一起来上海采购货物等事宜。他和Zung（音译）购买了价值180.00元的货物，Zung（音译）将于6月19日上午离开上海，将这些货物带回通州。

他留下了约180.00元，其中交给他人代为保管110.00元。

他打算用这110.00元购买鸦片，并向第二名嫌疑人提及此事，后者称

page_data.en:
- 4 -

could get in touch with a Chinese who, in turn, could
get in touch with some Japanese.

At about 7 p.m. June 18th, the 2nd suspect
told the 1st suspect to go to the Yangtse Hotel and
wait in the vestibule. He did this and was met by the
2nd suspect and the Water Police informer. The two
conducted him to room 704 where, already in the room
was a Japanese male (Sgt. Major Sakamoto). No
conversation had transpired when the Police party
arrived.

The 2nd suspect Hsu Myoh Yieh stated he
met the 1st suspect who mentioned he wanted about 10
pieces of opium. The 2nd suspect thought he might make
a profit on the deal and got in touch with one named
Zung residing Rue Hue, French Concession, who in turn
got in touch with the Water Police informer. During
the morning of June 18th, Zung met him (2nd suspect)
and accompanied him to the Nanyang Hotel, 394 North
Chekiang Road, where they met the Water Police informer
who told him he could purchase any type of drug and in
any amount if he went to room 704 of the Yangtse Hotel.
He was told to visit room 704 of the Yangtse Hotel
between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m. June 18th.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

他能联系上一名中国人，而该中国人又能联系上一些日本人。

6月18日晚上7点左右，第二名嫌疑人让第一名嫌疑人去扬子饭店并在门厅等候。他照做了，随后遇到第二名嫌疑人和水上警察线人。两人将他带到704房间，当时房间内已有一名日本男子（坂本警曹长）。警察小队到达时，双方尚未进行交谈。

第二名嫌疑人Hsu Myoh Yieh（音译）称，他遇见了第一名嫌疑人，后者提到他想买大约10件鸦片。第二名嫌疑人认为这笔交易可能有利可图，便联系了一位住在法租界霞飞路的名为Zung（音译）的人，后者又联系上了水上警察线人。6月18日上午，Zung（音译）与他（第二名嫌疑人）见面，并陪他前往浙江北路394号南洋酒店，在那里他们见到了水上警察线人，线人告诉他，如果去扬子饭店的704房间，他可以购买任何种类和数量的毒品。他被告知于6月18日晚上7点至8点之间前往扬子饭店的704房间。

page_data.en:
- 5 -

He left and met the 1st suspect and told him
of the arrangements. The 1st suspect told him he had
only money for one piece (about 12 ozs. or so). Both
arrived at the Yangtse Hotel at about 8.50 p.m. The
2nd suspect went upstairs to room 704 whilst the 1st
suspect stayed in the vestibule. On the 2nd suspect
entering the room he met the Water Police informer and
the Japanese (Sgt. Major Sakamoto). The Japanese asked
him if he was going to take responsibility for the sale.
He said "no" and would call the real buyer who was then
downstairs together with the Water Police informer and
met the 1st suspect. All three returned to room 704.
The Japanese asked them to wait whilst he had food
before talking business. A few minutes later the
Municipal Police party arrived.

Both suspects strenuously deny having met
the informer for the purpose of purchasing pistols etc.
They deny having had any military training as also
having met the informer on any previous occasion.

They are being temporarily detained in the
cells at Central Station pending further evidence being
produced by the Japanese Military Water Police.

Statements are being taken from them.

m-c-s
13/6/39

（签名）
D. S. 389
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

他离开后遇见了第一名嫌疑人，并告知了上述安排。第一名嫌疑人告诉他，他的钱只够买一件（约12盎司左右）。两人于晚上8点50分左右到达扬子饭店。第二名嫌疑人上楼进入704房间，而第一名嫌疑人留在门厅。第二名嫌疑人进入房间后，见到了水上警察线人和那名日本人（坂本警曹长）。日本人问他是否愿意为这次销售承担责任。他说“不”，并称要叫真正的买家上来，当时真正的买家正与水上警察线人在楼下，随后他们与第一名嫌疑人会合。三人一同返回704房间。日本人让他们等待，说他在吃饭后再谈生意。几分钟后，工部局警察小队到达。

两名嫌疑人都极力否认曾为了购买手枪等目的而与线人会面。他们否认受过任何军事训练，也否认此前曾与线人会面。

在日本军方水上警察提供更多证据之前，他们被暂时拘押在中央捕房的牢房内。

正在对他们进行笔录。

m-c-s
1939年6月13日

（签名）
D. S. 389

D. C. (Special Branch).

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. D. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 299/73
Date ____ / ____ / ____

Prior to entering the teashop, Sgt.Yoshimitsu

协助日本当局。
（军方水上警察。）
 ____ 

1939年6月21日上午10点45分，隶属于日本军方水上警察宪兵队的坂本（SAKAMOTO）警曹长、吉光（YOSHIMITSU，音译）警士和小牧（KOMAKI，音译）下士来到刑事科总部C.1处，请求协助在浙江路的一家茶馆逮捕一名中国男子，该人因替游击队购买武器而被通缉。

在请求获准后，英军当局获知此事，上午11点，由渡边（Watanabe）副督察、翁宗伟（Weng Zung We，音译）副督察、刑事侦探警士（C.D.S.）172号、刑事侦探警员（C.D.C.）206号以及本人组成的小队，在坂本警曹长的一名线人带领下：

H. E. YEATES - 英国籍 - 前工部局警务处成员，住址：静安寺路1025号37室，
前往浙江路662号“羅春閣”茶馆，线人在那里指认了一名中国男子并将其拘留，该人姓名如下：

周阿贵（TSEU AH KWEI），39岁，摩托车行老板，籍贯桑哈（Sanghah，音译），住址：法租界霞飞路180号。

在进入茶馆之前，吉光警士

（左侧手写批注：归档）
（左下角手写批注：95-216 / Ind 6月23日）

page_data.en:
- 2 -

requested that the foreign informer be allowed to enter
the teashop alone and make the arrest, this, however, was
refused, and the party entered together. On arriving
inside, H.E. Yeates walked around a table at which two
persons were sitting and pointed out one of them as the
person to be arrested. I, the undersigned, then took
hold of the accused's left arm and brought him to his
feet, this then left Yeates on the accused's right hand
side. Just as the accused got to his feet, C.D.S. 172
who was standing in front, called out to Yeates not to
touch the accused and at the same time caught hold of
Yeates' hand. I immediately pulled the accused towards
me and saw that Yeates had been about to put a folded
piece of paper in the accused's right hand-side outer
jacket pocket. Yeates at first refused to hand the
paper over, but on being requested by me, handed same over,
mumbling, "Alright, but it was given to me by the accused".
On returning to Police Headquarters, D.I. Glover
was informed of the incident in the teashop and took all
concerned before Supt. Grubb, where the facts were again
related.
Supt. Grubb questioned all concerned, and was
informed by Sgt. Major Sammete that as Yeates had got
the paper from the accused some weeks ago, he was quite
justified in taking this method of returning it to him.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

请求允许外籍线人单独进入茶馆实施逮捕，但此请求被拒绝，小队一同进入。进入店内后，H.E. Yeates走到一张坐着两人的桌子旁，指出其中一人为待逮捕对象。本人随即抓住嫌疑人的左臂并将其扶起，这使得Yeates位于嫌疑人的右侧。就在嫌疑人站起时，站在前面的刑事侦探警士（C.D.S.）172号大声喝止Yeates不要触碰嫌疑人，同时抓住了Yeates的手。我立即将嫌疑人拉向我这边，并看到Yeates正试图将一张折叠的纸放入嫌疑人右侧的外套口袋中。Yeates起初拒绝交出这张纸，但在我的要求下，他交出了纸张，嘴里嘟囔着：“好吧，但这是嫌疑人给我的。”
回到警察总部后，格洛弗（Glover）督察获悉了茶馆内发生的事件，并将所有相关人员带到格鲁布（Grubb）巡官面前，再次陈述了事实经过。
格鲁布巡官讯问了所有相关人员，并从萨梅特（Sammete，音译）警曹长处得知，由于Yeates在几周前从嫌疑人那里拿到了这张纸，他采取这种方式将其归还给嫌疑人是完全合理的。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

He, Sgt. Major Sakamoto then complained of the lack of
cooperation on the part of the foreign detective rendering
assistance, intimating that had Yeates been allowed to
make the arrest, the paper would have been in the accused's
possession before the arrival of the Settlement Police.

The accused, on being questioned by Supt.Grubb,
stated that during 1938, a friend of his, named KOO SIAO
SOONG (顧小松), frequently visited his home and during
November, took along two other persons, named Loh Zung
Ling (陸仁林) and Wu (吳). During a subsequent
conversation, Loh Zung Ling stated that he had a large
consignment of arms arriving in Shanghai and requested him
the accused, to try and find a buyer.

About one week later, the accused met another
friend, named : -
LI YING (李英), 29, M/Ex-P.S.B. Constable,
Hupei, residing, 257 Rue des
Seux Republiques, F.C,
and informed him of the arrival of the arms. Li Ying
then promised to find a buyer and was later introduced to
Koo Siao Soong, Loh Zung Ling and Wu.

After the aforementioned introduction had taken
place, nothing further was done about the matter till the
middle of May, this year, when Koo, Loh and Wu again
visited the accused and requested him to find Li Ying as
the arms had arrived.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

坂本警佐随后抱怨负责协助的外国侦探缺乏合作，暗示如果允许耶茨（Yeates）实施逮捕，该文件本应在租界警察到达之前就被查获并处于被告控制之下。

被告在受到格鲁布（Grubb）督察讯问时陈述，1938年间，他的一位名叫顾小松（KOO SIAO SOONG）的朋友经常造访其住所，并于同年11月带去了另外两人，分别名为陆仁林（Loh Zung Ling）和吴（Wu）。在随后的谈话中，陆仁林称有一大批军火即将运抵上海，并请被告设法寻找买家。

约一周后，被告会见了另一位朋友，名为：
李英（LI YING），29岁，男/前上海市警察局巡捕，湖北籍，居住于法租界双共和国路（Rue des Seux Republiques）257号，
并向其通报了军火抵达的消息。李英随即答应寻找买家，随后被介绍给顾小松、陆仁林和吴。

在上述介绍完成后，此事直至今年5月中旬再无进展，当时顾、陆和吴再次拜访被告，请其寻找李英，因为军火已经抵达。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

(The accused located Li and arranged a meeting in the
Loo Tsung Koh Teashop, No.462 Chekiang Road, where Li
handed a guerilla pass (seized from Yeates) to Loh Zung
Ling to prove that he had guerilla connections, about 12
meetings in all were then held after which, Li Ying stated
that he had no further interest in the deal owing to his
having no funds and as Loh refused to hand back the pass.
This a.m. Li Ying was requested to visit the tea-
shop to inform all concerned that he had no further
interest, but sent the accused in his stead.
On Yeates being questioned by Supt. Grubb, he
stated that he was an informer of Sgt. Major Sakamoto
and about 3 weeks ago, had received information from two
of his own informers, named Leh and Wu, that the accused
was trying to purchase arms for guerillas and alleged that
the pass had been given to his informer by the accused.
He then admitted that he had endeavoured to get the pass
back into the accused's possession by placing it in his
pocket.
In view of the accused's admission, Sgt.Major
Sakamoto requested assistance to arrest Li Ying, Supt.
Valentine of the French Police (Political Section) was
therefore informed and stated that assistance could be
given.
The aforestated detectives together with C.D.I.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

（被告找到了李英，并安排在浙江路462号鲁宗科茶馆会面，会上李英将一张游击队通行证（从耶茨处缴获）交给陆仁林，以证明其拥有游击队关系。此后共举行了约12次会面，之后李英表示因无资金且陆拒绝归还通行证，他对这笔交易不再感兴趣。今天上午，李英被要求前往茶馆告知各方他不再感兴趣，但他派被告代为前往。
在受到格鲁布督察讯问时，耶茨称他是坂本警佐的线人，约三周前，他从自己的两名线人勒（Leh）和吴处获得情报，称被告正试图为游击队购买军火，并声称该通行证是被告交给他的线人的。他随后承认，他试图通过将通行证放入被告口袋的方式，使其重新回到被告手中。
鉴于被告的供认，坂本警佐请求协助逮捕李英，因此通知了法国警察（政治科）的瓦伦丁（Valentine）督察，后者表示可以提供协助。
上述侦探以及法国警察的

page_data.en:
- 5 -

Dalorme and D.S.I. Yankovsky of the French Police were
then led by the accused to No.287 Rue des deux Republiques,
where the 2nd. accused, Li Ying, was located in a front
attic, a search of the attic failed to produce anything of
an incriminating nature, 16 group photographs and snaps,
however, were taken at the request of Sgt. Yoshimitsu.
The 1st. accused's home was then searched, but with
abortive results.

The 2nd. accused was handed over by the French
Police at 4:45 p.m. and on being questioned by D.S.I.Wong
and C.D.S.172 and the undersigned, admitted having tried
to purchase one pistol for a loafer friend, named Nyeu
Ching Pieh (牛劍標), and it was the latter friend who had
supplied the pass, same being a counterfeit made by
another friend and was given to Loh who alleged that he
wished to transport some arms through the guerilla lines.

The 2nd. accused proved to have one previous
conviction for possession of arms, he having been arrested
by detectives of Chengtu Road Station during April,1938,
and was sentenced to 4 months imprisonment, suspended.

On being questioned regarding this, the accused
first stated that the charge was for "Assault" and later,
stated that it was for possession of opium.

Both accused are now being detained in Central
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

达洛姆（Dalorme）首席侦探督察和杨科夫斯基（Yankovsky）副侦探督察，随后由被告带领至双共和国路287号，在那里发现了第二名被告李英，他住在一间前阁楼内。对阁楼的搜查未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品，但应吉光（Yoshimitsu）警佐的要求，拍摄了16张集体照和快照。
随后搜查了第一名被告的住所，但一无所获。

第二名被告于下午4时45分由法国警察移交，在接受副侦探督察黄（Wong）、刑事侦缉处172号及本人的讯问时，承认曾试图为一位名叫牛剑标（Nyeu Ching Pieh）的无业游民朋友购买一支手枪，并称该通行证是由这位朋友提供的，系由另一位朋友伪造，并交给了陆，陆声称希望透过游击队防线运输一些军火。

经查，第二名被告有一次持有军火的前科，他曾在1938年4月被成都路捕房的侦探逮捕，并被判处四个月监禁，缓刑执行。

当就此问题接受讯问时，被告起初称指控罪名为“袭击”，随后又称罪名为持有鸦片。

两名被告现均被拘留在中央

page_data.en:
TSEU AH KWEI (周阿貴), 30, M/Shop Proprietor,
Zangzoh, --- C.D.S. 172,
C.1 21.6.39 Clerk Yao.

I am a bicycle hong proprietor, residing at House 150
Rue Lafayette, Fr. Con. I was born in Zangzoh, Kiangsu, where
my aged mother, wife and children are still living. I own four
mows of land and a few straw huts in Zangzoh (Si Wo Deu Village,
East Lai Tsung, Zangzoh, Kiangsu.) I have never gone to
school, and at the age of 10 (1919) my father died, leaving
nothing for my mother and myself to live on. My mother then
came to Shanghai with me, she succeeding in obtaining the job
of a maid-servant, whilst I being sent to Mr. Wong Kying Loong's
workshop (copper-smith) at Yang Kying Village, off Shanghai,
to be an apprentice. There I stayed for 3 years, finishing
the course of apprenticeship at the age of 19, whereby I came to
Shanghai, looking for a job. As efforts at seeking jobs prove
abortive, I eked out a living as a second hand goods dealer,
keeping a stall in French Concession. This profession last three
years, after which, in about January, 1931, I succeeded in renti:
a house (No.150) on Rue Lafayette, wherein I set up a bicycle
hong, which exists to the present day.

I have been always a peaceful resident in the French
Concession. I have few friends.

Some time ago, my friend, Koo Siao Seeng, a boatman from
Pootung, began frequenting my house, and, once in about November,
1938, when Koo was again at my house together with two of his
friends, Loh Sung Ling et al, I was informed by Loh Sung Ling
that he had in possession of a large consignment of arms which
he was eager to sell. He requested my assistance to find a suit-
able buyer for him, if possible, and I consented to do my best.
page_data.zh:
周阿贵（TSEU AH KWEI），30岁，男/店主，江苏张家港（Zangzoh），--- 刑事侦缉处172号，
C.1 1939年6月21日 书记员姚。

我是一名自行车行店主，居住在法租界拉斐特路（Rue Lafayette）150号。我出生于江苏张家港，我的老母、妻子和孩子仍住在那里。我在张家港（江苏张家港东莱宗西沃德村）拥有四亩土地和几间草屋。我从未上过学，10岁时（1919年）父亲去世，未留下任何生计给母亲和我。母亲随后带我来到上海，她成功找到了一份女佣的工作，而我则被送到上海郊外杨泾村的黄庆龙先生作坊（铜匠铺）当学徒。我在那里待了三年，19岁时出师，随后来到上海找工作。由于求职努力均告失败，我以贩卖二手货物为生，在法租界摆了一个摊位。这一职业持续了三年，之后在1931年1月左右，我成功租下了拉斐特路150号的房屋，在此开设了一家自行车行，至今仍在经营。

我在法租界一直是一名安分守己的居民。我的朋友很少。

不久前，我的朋友顾小松（Koo Siao Seeng），一名来自浦东的船夫，开始频繁造访我家。大约在1938年11月的一次，当顾小松再次与他的两个朋友陆松林（Loh Sung Ling）等人来到我家时，陆松林告诉我，他拥有一大批急于出售的军火。他请求我协助为他寻找合适的买家，如果可能的话，我同意尽力而为。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

About a week after that, I met my friend, Li Ying, a Northerner
(former employee of the Nantao Police Bureau) in the vicinity
of my shop. During the course of our conversation, I requested
Li Ying to assist me in trying to find a buyer for the consign-
ment of arms in Loh's possession, as previously mentioned. Li
stated that he was sure that he could find a suitable buyer
amongst his friends, suggesting a meeting be held to talk it
over.

Subsequently, date forgotten, a meeting was held and
everyone, i.e. Loh Zung Ling, Koo Siao Soong, Li Ying, one
certain Wu and myself, put in an appearance. Despite my
presence, however, owing to my little or no experience in tradi
arms, I did not actually participate in the conversation at the
meeting. It was when the meeting came to an end, when one of
them informed me that they were going to meet again for further
discussions.

Nothing was heard of the matter until about May, 1938,
when Loh Zung Ling, Wu, and Koo Siao Soong again came to my home
seeking my assistance in trying to locate Li Ying. When I
enquired why they wanted to see Li, they replied that the
consignment of arms had already arrived in Shanghai and that
they were eager to sell it at a profitable price. Then they left
saying that they could be found daily from 9 - 10 a.m. at "Loo
Tsung Kah" Tea Shop, Chekiang Road, and from 5 p.m. onwards at
the New World Amusement Park, Yu Ya Ching Road.

In the middle of May, 1938, Li Ying came to my house
again, whereby I informed him of the arrival of the arms as well
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

大约一周后，我在店铺附近遇到了我的朋友李英，一名北方人（前南市警察局雇员）。在谈话过程中，我请求李英协助我为前述陆某持有的那批军火寻找买家。李英表示他确信能在朋友中找到合适的买家，建议举行一次会议商讨此事。

随后，日期已忘，举行了一次会议，所有人，即陆仁林、顾小松、李英、某位吴姓人士以及我本人，均出席了会议。然而，尽管我在场，但由于我对传统军火几乎没有或完全没有经验，我实际上并未参与会议上的谈话。会议结束时，其中一人通知我，他们将再次会面进行进一步讨论。

直到1938年5月左右，此事再无音讯，当时陆仁林、吴和顾小松再次来到我家，寻求我的协助以找到李英。当我询问他们为何想见李时，他们回答说那批军火已经运抵上海，他们急于以有利可图的价格将其售出。随后他们离开，并称每天上午9点至10点可在浙江路“鲁宗卡”茶馆找到他们，下午5点后可在虞洽卿路的新世界游乐场找到他们。

1938年5月中旬，李英再次来到我家，我便将军火抵达的情况以及

page_data.en:
- 3 -

as the fact that the others were anxious to see him. At once,
I accompanied Li to the Loo Tsung Zoh Tea Shop, 462 Chekiang
Road, and interviewed Loh Zuag Ling, Wu and Keo Siao Seong
therein. A brief discussion was held, but no definite results
obtained. After that occasion, Li Ying and myself visited
this teashop continuously for about a dozen times, and on each
occasion, they talked about the arms deal . On some occasions
I heard that Li Ying insisted that no payment would be made
prior to delivery of arms, whilst Loh and others maintained
that they could not deliver the arms unless Li Ying could
produce a certificate in proof of his identity etc. Subsequently
after many interviews, Li produced a "travelling certificate"
and handed same to Loh et al. However, at this juncture, Li
all of a sudden, suggested cancelling the whole affair on the
grounds of insufficient funds. As nothing further could be
done, Li requested Loh et al to return to him his travelling
certificate. This caused an argument between them. (Travelling
certificate at present seized by Police). After that a number
of meetings were held at the teashop and on each occasion, Li
demanded the return of his certificate.

At 8 a.m. 20.6.39, Loh Zung Ling, Wu, et al came to my
shop appointing me to meet at the tea shop again at 10 a.m. next
day. At the appointed hour, I went to the teashop and was
arrested by police.

At the time when the police were effecting our arrest,
a foreigner, who had come with the others, attempted to drop a
piece of paper into my coat pocket, but he was caught in the act
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

其他人急于见他的事实告诉了他。我立即陪同李英前往浙江路462号的鲁宗佐茶馆，并在那里会见了陆仁林、吴和顾小松。双方进行了简短讨论，但未取得确切结果。在那次之后，李英和我连续访问该茶馆约十几次，每次他们都谈论军火交易。有几次我听到李英坚持要求在交付军火前不付款，而陆等人则坚持除非李英能出示身份证明等证书，否则无法交付军火。随后经过多次面谈，李英拿出了一张“旅行证”并交给了陆等人。然而，就在此时，李英突然以资金不足为由建议取消整个交易。由于无法再做其他事情，李英要求陆等人归还他的旅行证。这引发了他们之间的争论。（旅行证目前已被警方扣押）。此后在茶馆又举行了多次会议，每次李英都要求归还他的证件。

1939年6月20日上午8时，陆仁林、吴等人来到我的店铺，约定我于次日上午10时在茶馆再次会面。在约定时间，我前往茶馆并被警察逮捕。

在警察实施逮捕时，一名随同前来的外国人试图将一张纸片塞进我的上衣口袋，但被一名注意到这一行为的中国警员当场抓获。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

by a Chinese member of the police, who noticed it. On being
examined, it was the travelling certificate belonging to Li Yi
but had left in the hands of Loh Zung Li et al as previously
mentioned.

During my detention at Crime Branch Hdqrs, I led a
police party to 287 Rue du Republie, Fr. Con. wherein, they
effected the arrest of Li Ying.

This is the truth.

Signed : TSEU AN KWEI.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

经检查，那是属于李英的旅行证，如前所述，该证件此前留在了陆仁林等人手中。

在刑事侦缉处总部拘留期间，我带领一队警察前往法租界共和国路287号，在那里他们逮捕了李英。

以上属实。

签名：周阿贵（TSEU AN KWEI）。

page_data.en:
LI YING (李英), alias LI KYIEN NGAUN (
Tientsin, aged 29 years, -- C.D.S. 172,
C.1 21. 6. 39 Clerk Yao Dinsin.

My name is Li Ying, alias Li Kyien Ngaun, native of Tientsin,
aged 29 years, Married, hawker, at present living in an attic,
at House 287 Rue de Seux Republique.

I was born in Nan Ts District, Southern Tientsin, where
my father, mother, brother, sister and wife are still residing.
To be a hawker has been the profession of Li Family for generations
During October, 1934, I came to Shanghai and became employed
as Constable No.1923 at the Old South Gate Sub-Station, Nantao
P.S.B. which position I held for over 3 years. During June,
1937, owing to the meagre income from the police job, I resigned
and became a hawker. However, after the outbreak of hostilities
the hawker business proved so poor that I had to quit again,
whereby I succeeded in becoming a police constable under Chief
Tsang An Dien of Tung Chong Road Sub-Station, Da Dao Police
Bureau, Pootung. However, owing to insufficient means to live
on, I resigned and became a police constable (No.1114) with the
French Police. It was during September, last year, when I was
undergoing a course of training at the French Police Depot, that
I was arrested together with a friend, Yang Ngoh Sai, by detectives
of Chengtu Road Station on a charge of "trafficking in and
possession of opium", which brought about a 4 month suspended
sentence on me. I was thus compelled to resign from the French
Police, and this resumed my hawker profession.

In about November, last year, when visiting the Kwai Li
Bicycle Hong at 186 Rue Lafayette, my friend, Tsou Ah Kwei, the
proprietor, informed me that his friend, one Loh by name, had in
store a large consignment of arms and was eager to dispose of it
through sale.
page_data.zh:
李英（LI YING），别名李健元（LI KYIEN NGAUN），
天津籍，29岁，-- 刑事侦缉处172号，
C.1 1939年6月21日 书记员姚丁新。

我叫李英，别名李健元，天津人，现年29岁，已婚，小贩，现居住在双共和国路287号的一间阁楼内。

我出生于天津南部的南区，我的父母、兄弟姐妹和妻子仍居住在那里。李家世代以小贩为业。1934年10月，我来到上海，受雇于南市警察局老北门分署，担任第1923号巡捕，该职位我担任了三年多。1937年6月，由于警察工作收入微薄，我辞职成为小贩。然而，战事爆发后，小贩生意惨淡，我不得不再次离职，随后成功在浦东大道警察局潼钟路分署曾安典巡长手下担任巡捕。然而，由于生计困难，我再次辞职，成为法国警察的一名巡捕（编号1114）。去年9月，当我在法国警察训练所受训期间，我与朋友杨五世（Yang Ngoh Sai）一起被成都路捕房的侦探以“贩卖及持有鸦片”的罪名逮捕，导致我被判处四个月监禁，缓刑执行。因此我被迫从法国警察辞职，并重操小贩旧业。

去年11月左右，当我在拉斐特路186号拜访桂利自行车行时，店主我的朋友周阿贵告诉我，他的一个姓陆的朋友库存有一大批军火，急于通过销售处理掉。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

As he asked me if I could help him by looking for a suitable
buyer, I consented to try, stating that my friend, one Nyisu
Kyien Piau, a loafer, might be able to find a buyer for him or
purchase a pistol himself.

Subsequently, on date forgotten, I accompanied Nyisu to
Tseu's bicycle shop, when we were introduced to Tseu's friends
or owners of the consignment, Loh and Koo Siao Soong. Nyisu
enquired if he could purchase a pistol for himself, but received
a negative reply from Loh and Koo, who stated that the consign-
ment of arms would not be sold in small lots. As no definite
results were forthcoming from this interview, the party left.

During the middle of May, when I was again at Tseu's
place, the latter informed me that Loh and Koo had again visited
Tseu, bringing him the news that the consignment had already
arrived, and that they were finally willing to sell one pistol
to Nyau. Several days later, I met Nyeiu on Rhe Rue, where he
was informed of the foregoing. Nyeiu stated that he actually
wanted to buy a piece and that should negotiations prove a
success, he would give me a commission of $5. Tseu subsequently
took me to the Leo Tsung Koh Teashop, where we interviewed Loh,
and Koo for a number of occasions. During the negotiations, Koo
insisted that the goods would not be delivered unless Nyau, the
prospective buyer, could produce a travelling pass. Several days
later, when Nyieu and I met again, Nyieu stated that he could
counterfeit the pass required by the other party. Consequently,
two or three days later, Nyieu and I met again in French Town,
when I was introduced by the former to his friend, one Li Hwo
Chiu, the latter informing me that the necessary pass had been
counterfeited already.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

由于他问我能否通过寻找合适的买家来帮助他，我同意试一试，并声明我的朋友 Nyisu Kyien Piau（音译），一个游手好闲的人，或许能替他找到买家，或者自己购买一支手枪。

随后，在日期遗忘的一天，我陪同 Nyisu 前往 Tseu 的自行车店，当时我们被介绍给 Tseu 的朋友或这批货物的货主 Loh 和 Koo Siao Soong（音译）。Nyisu 询问他是否可以为自己购买一支手枪，但遭到 Loh 和 Koo 的拒绝，他们声称这批军火不会零星出售。由于此次会面未得出任何确切结果，众人随即离开。

五月中旬，当我再次来到 Tseu 处时，后者告知我 Loh 和 Koo 再次拜访了 Tseu，带来消息说这批货物已经抵达，并且他们最终愿意向 Nyau 出售一支手枪。几天后，我在法租界（Rhe Rue，原文疑为 Rue de France 或类似街道名之误）遇见 Nyeiu，并将上述情况告知了他。Nyeiu 表示他确实想购买一支，如果谈判成功，他将给我 5 美元的佣金。随后 Tseu 带我去了 Leo Tsung Koh 茶馆，我们在那里多次会见了 Loh 和 Koo。在谈判期间，Koo 坚持除非潜在买家 Nyau 能出示通行证，否则不会交货。几天后，当 Nyieu 和我再次见面时，Nyieu 表示他可以伪造对方所需的通行证。因此，两三天后，Nyieu 和我在法租界再次见面，当时前者将我介绍给他的朋友 Li Hwo Chiu（音译），后者通知我所需的通行证已经伪造完毕。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

Li produced the counterfeit pass and handed over same to me,
whereby the three of us proceeded to the Loo Tsung Koh Teashop
and interviewed Loh and Koo, showing to the latter men the pass
in question. Loh and Koo then appointed another date to show
us a sample of the pistols for sale and left.

One day in the latter part of May, Nyieu came to me
with the news that he no longer wish to purchase the pistol
as he had insufficient funds. He and I together with Tseu Ah
Kwei then proceeded to the teashop in an effort to cancell the
whole affair and get back the counterfeit pass which had been
handed over to the other party during one of the previous
meetings. However, some argument arose between the two, Koo
and myself before we left. To our surprise, at about noon
on June 21, 1939, Tseu led a party of police to the teashop and
placed me under arrest. I do not know why.

This is the truth.

Signed : LI YING.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

Li 拿出伪造的通行证并交给我，于是我们三人前往 Loo Tsung Koh 茶馆，会见了 Loh 和 Koo，并向后者展示了该通行证。Loh 和 Koo 随后另约日期向我们展示待售手枪的样品，然后离开。

五月下旬的一天，Nyieu 来找我，带来消息说他因资金不足不再希望购买手枪。他和我和 Tseu Ah Kwei 一起前往茶馆，试图取消整件事，并收回在前几次会面中交给对方的伪造通行证。然而，在我们离开之前，Koo 和我之间发生了一些争执。令我们惊讶的是，1939 年 6 月 21 日中午左右，Tseu 带领一队警察来到茶馆并将我逮捕。我不知道原因。

这就是事实。

签名：LI YING。

Lieu Tsung Yoong(劉心榮).
Yangchow                                      x D.S.I. Lieu Kyling Ching
                                              translated
C.B.H.Q.                8-11-39               XXXXXX      Kuh Mei Han

    I am named Lieu Tsung Yoong(劉心榮), aged 24, a
native of Yangchow, residing at the Sing Hung Yoong Gifts
Shop, 57 Rue du Marche, F.C. and was employed there.
    On the 6-7-39, I was arrested by the S.M.P. Head-
quarters. On 20th, October, 1939, I was handed over to
the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters. On the 3rd day of
my being handed over, a Japanese questioned me of my age,
native place, profession, and connections with the Shanghai
Commercial anti-Japanese Corps. In reply, I confessed that
through one named Sung Poe Zau's(沈伯兆) introduction I
entered the corps and acted as vice i/c undertaking the
work of propaganda with a view of reminding the merchants
to boycott the Japanese goods. The corps consists of more
than ten members. The first meeting of the corps was called
in my shop discussing the general regulations of the corps.
The 2nd meeting was held for the purpose of encouraging the
members to be assiduous in each one's work. The 3rd meeting
was for the purpose of printing pamphlets and collecting fees.
We decided to collect $1.20 off each member for the expendi-
ture of the corps. But the decision has not been carried out.
    On th 8th, inst. I was returned to the S.M.Police
whilst Sung Kuang Yau(沈光耀) who was handed over with me
on the same day, was still in the custody of the Japanese
Gendarmerie.

    我叫 Lieu Tsung Yoong (劉心榮)，24 岁，扬州人，居住在法租界 Marche 路 57 号 Sing Hung Yoong 礼品店，并受雇于此。
    1939 年 7 月 6 日，我被上海公共租界警务处（S.M.P.）总部逮捕。1939 年 10 月 20 日，我被移交给日本宪兵队总部。在我被移交后的第三天，一名日本人讯问了我的年龄、籍贯、职业以及与上海商业抗日团体的联系。作为回答，我供认经一名叫 Sung Poe Zau (沈伯兆) 的人介绍加入该团体，并担任副总指挥，从事宣传工作，旨在提醒商人抵制日货。该团体由十多名成员组成。团体的第一次会议在我的店里召开，讨论了团体的总章程。第二次会议的目的是鼓励成员勤勉工作。第三次会议的目的是印刷小册子和收取费用。我们决定向每名成员收取 1.20 美元作为团体的开支。但该决定尚未执行。
    本月 8 日，我被归还给上海公共租界警务处，而与我同一天被移交的 Sung Kuang Yau (沈光耀) 仍由日本宪兵队拘留。
    以上是我的真实陈述。

On instructions of the D.C. (Crime) dated
July 17, 1939, the Japanese Gendarmerie were informed
that SUNG KWANG YAU (沈廣耀) would be handed over
to them against receipt. The other male LIEU TSENG

would not be handed over to them.

Since that date until the present date
the Gendarmerie have not taken custody of SUNG KWANG
YAU (沈廣耀) because, they stated, they required
the handing over of both males.

They have been repeatedly informed that no
evidence against the 2nd. named LIEU TSENG YOONG has
been unearthed by the Municipal Police neither have
the Gendarmerie produced any evidence of any kind to
substantiate their statements that he was concerned
in anti-Japanese activities.

On July 30th. Sgt.Major Kuhasawa attended
Crime Branch Headquarters and, through the interpretation
of D.P.S. Yamahara, stated the Gendarmerie had arrested
a male Chinese some days previously who admitted being a
member of the "Shanghai Professional Corps for the

4/1

续：协助日本宪兵队。

遵照 1939 年 7 月 17 日刑事处副总监（D.C. (Crime)）的指令，已通知日本宪兵队，SUNG KWANG YAU (沈廣耀) 将在出具收据后移交给他们。另一名男性 LIEU TSENG YOONG (劉正榮) 因无证据指控，将不会移交给他们。

自该日起至本日，宪兵队尚未接管 SUNG KWANG YAU (沈廣耀)，因为他们声称需要同时移交这两名男性。

已反复告知他们，公共租界警务处未发现针对第二名列名者 LIEU TSENG YOONG 的任何证据，宪兵队也未提供任何类型的证据来证实他们关于其参与反日活动的说法。

7 月 30 日，Kuhasawa 警长莅临刑事处总部，并通过 D.P.S. Yamahara 的翻译，陈述宪兵队日前逮捕了一名中国男性，该男子承认是“上海职业肃奸抗敌团”的成员。

（左侧手写批注：S.G. C¹⁄₈）

page_data.en:
4/2

In reply to a request by the undersigned to
produce the man, Sgt. Major Kabasawa stated that he
had been arrested by a different section of the
Gendarmerie who were at that time interrogating him
and therefore it was not possible to bring him over.
Sgt. Major Kabasawa however stated that the arrested
man definitely implicated the second named as being
a member of the above Corps.

It was explained to Sgt. Major Kabasawa
that all members of the Corps (numbering only 13 at
the time of the raid) were required to append their
signatures, thumbprint and photograph in the membership
book. In a number of instances however, the photographs
had not been appended due to members only having just
joined and the fact the Corps was newly-formed.

A check of the fingerprints of the 2nd. named
had been made by the Finger-print Bureau with prints
in the membership book but no identification was made.

It was further explained to Sgt. Major Kabasawa
that if the man in custody of the Gendarmerie was a
genuine member of the Corps, his name and thumbprint
would also be in the membership book and that was
the reason the undersigned requested the man be produced
in order that those points might be checked upon.
page_data.zh:
4/2

针对本人要求带出该人的请求，Kabasawa 警长陈述称，该人是由宪兵队的另一部门逮捕的，该部门当时正在对其进行审讯，因此无法将其带出。然而，Kabasawa 警长表示，被捕者明确牵连第二名列名者是上述团体的成员。

已向 Kabasawa 警长解释，该团体所有成员（突袭时仅有 13 人）均需在会员名册上附上签名、指纹和照片。然而在若干情况下，由于成员刚加入且团体新成立，照片尚未附上。

指纹局已将第二名列名者的指纹与名册中的指纹进行了核对，但未发现匹配。

进一步向 Kabasawa 警长解释，如果宪兵队拘留的人确实是该团体的成员，他的名字和拇指印也会出现在会员名册中，这就是本人要求带出该人以核查这些要点的原因。

page_data.en:
4/3

Since that date, no communication of any
kind has been received from the Gendarmerie regarding
either of the two men detained by the Municipal Police.
In view of the foregoing, this file is
submitted for further instructions regarding action
to be taken.

H.H.S
11/8

Shun Pao, Sin Wen Pao, Eastern Times    7. 7. 33

TWO ANTI-JAPANESE SUSPECTS ARRESTED BY FRENCH POLICE

At about 8 p.m. yesterday, 2 Japanese
detectives in plain clothes called at the Lu-Ka-Wei Police
Station in the French Concession reporting that a large
quantity of handbills of an anti-Japanese nature were in
the possession of anti-Japanese elements living in the
Shin Han Yung (新亨永) Shop, 57 Rue de Marche. Acting
on this information, foreign and Chinese detectives of
the Station, in company with the Japanese detectives,
went to the place and carried out a search. However,
nothing objectionable was found. Later, they arrested
Sung Kwang-yao (孫光耀), age, native of Sungkiang (松江),
and Liu Tsung-ying (刘振英), age 25, native of
Chinkiang (鎮江), two employees of the shop, and they
are now detained by the French Police.
It is learned that the French Police
are making enquiries into the case.

SUNG KWANG YAU (沈廣耀 alias SUNG KWA G DAU
(沈光涛 ), age 21, residing 57 Rue du Marche,
Sungkiang                                      C.D.S. 172
H. . C. B.             8-7-39          translated
                                       Tsoung Sung au

I am not married. I was born in Dah Kah (大街),
outside West Gate, Sungkiang, where my parents, brothers and
sisters live at present. We own 4 mow of fields in that
locality. At the age of 7 I was sent to a school, and
remained there until I was 11 years old, when I assisted my
father in taking care of a small store which he owned, at
Rue du Consulate, French Concession. At the age of 15 I
became an apprentice at Zung Tsong Yoong (仁昌永) Gift Shop,
Kiukiang Road, from which I was discharged in January last
year. I was then introduced by my friend, Sung Kyah Nyl
(沈家義), to work as an assistant at Sing Hang Yung (新亨永)
Gift Shop, 57 Rue du Marche, where I am now still employed.
There I receive a pay of $8.00 per mensem.

During the middle of June 1939, Sung Fah Zu
(沈百如), the young master of Sung Faung Tsai Cake Shop
situated in the vicinity of my shop, approached me with a
request to solicit my enrolment in the Shanghai Professional
Corps for the Extermination of Traitors and Resistance to
Enemies which he had organized, and at the same time showed me
a book containing names of persons connected with this organ.
It impressed me so much that I readily agreed to join the
Corps. However, this organisation has not yet been formally
inaugurated, hence no work of any sort has been accomplished.
The aforesaid book was generally placed on the shelf in my
shop. Another book seized by the Police is really an
exercise book wherein I practiced my rough hand-writing.

The above is my true statement.

Signed, Cross-marked X Thumb-printed by SUNG KWANG YAU.
page_data.zh:
沈廣耀 (SUNG KWANG YAU，别名 沈光涛 SUNG KWA G DAU)，21岁，住马浪路57号，
松江                                      C.D.S. 172
H. . C. B.             1939年7月8日          翻译
                                       Tsoung Sung au

我未婚。我出生在松江西门外的大街（Dah Kah），我的父母、兄弟姐妹目前都住在那里。我们在当地拥有4亩田地。7岁时我被送进学校读书，一直读到11岁，之后我便协助父亲打理他在法租界领事馆路（Rue du Consulate）拥有的一家小店。15岁时，我成为九江路仁昌永（Zung Tsong Yoong）礼品店的学徒，去年一月被解雇。随后，经朋友沈家義（Sung Kyah Nyl）介绍，我在马浪路57号新亨永（Sing Hang Yung）礼品店担任店员，至今仍在此任职。我每月的薪水是8.00元。

1939年6月中旬，我家店铺附近的沈丰泰（Sung Faung Tsai）糕饼店少东家沈百如（Sung Fah Zu）找我，请求我加入他组织的“上海职业锄奸抗敌团”，同时给我看了一本记载与该组织有关人员姓名的名册。这给我留下了深刻印象，于是我欣然同意加入该团。然而，该组织尚未正式成立，因此尚未开展任何工作。上述名册通常放在我店铺的架子上。警方查获的另一本书实际上是我练习毛笔字的习字本。

以上是我的真实陈述。

沈廣耀 签字，画十字，按手印。

My name is Lieu Tseng Yoong, age 24, native of
Kiangtu, Single, and residing at No. 57 Rue de Marche,
French Concession.

I was born in Chi Tsu Chow, 3rd District, Kiangtu.
There are eight members in my family, consisting of my
parents, brothers, sisters and myself.

In 1930 I came to Shanghai and through the intro-
duction of my friend, I procured employment in "Tau Yoong
Sie" Fan shop, Han-kow Road, as an apprentice. I was thus
employed for three years, then resigned from that shop and
went to Tanyang. I was employed in "Tai Chong" Oil
Factory, Tung Meng Li, Tanyang, for three years. I came
back to Shanghai in 1937 and again went to work in the
"Tau Yoong Sie" Fan Shop,

Owing to the current hostilities which broke out
on 13.8.37, I quitted my position in the fan shop and evacuated
to my native place. In October 1938 I returned to Shanghai,
and was unable to find a job. Later, a friend of mine, named
Sung, introduced me to work in "Ta Hwa" Iron Factory, East
Yuhang Road near Alcock Road, Hongkew, manufacturing horse-
equipment for Japanese Military use. I retained this position
until the end of November 1938 when the factory ceased business
I then went to live in **〔此处转录不清〕** "Hung Wen Kao" Printing Shop,
268 Hankew Road. Sometime in December, proprietor of
"Hung Wen Kao" inaugurated a temporary Chinese handwriting
and scroll of picture exhibition, and I was employed there
as an entertainer. The exhibition was concluded at the end

C.l. 1939年7月8日. //////// 徐。

我叫刘正荣，24岁，江都人，未婚，住法租界马浪路57号。

我出生在江都第三区的季子周（Chi Tsu Chow，音译）。我家共有八口人，包括父母、兄弟姐妹和我自己。

1930年我来到上海，经朋友介绍，我在汉口路“陶永 Sie”扇店当学徒。我在那里工作了三年，然后辞去该店工作去了丹阳。我在丹阳同德里（Tung Meng Li）的“泰昌”油厂工作了三年。1937年我回到上海，再次去“陶永 Sie”扇店工作，

由于1937年8月13日爆发的当前战事，我离开了扇店的工作，撤离回老家。1938年10月我回到上海，但找不到工作。后来，一位姓沈的朋友介绍我去虹口阿尔科克路（Alcock Road）附近的东余杭路“大华”铁工厂工作，制造供日军使用的马具。我一直保留该职位直到1938年11月底工厂停业。
随后我住在**〔此处转录不清〕**汉口路268号“鸿文阁”印刷店。12月间，“鸿文阁”店主举办了一次临时中文书法和画卷展览，我被聘为招待员。展览于月底结束

On 6.7.39 a party of foreign and Chinese detectives
