Translation of our latent book
of the Shanghai Professional Corps
for the extermination of Traitors
and Resistance to spies, inaugurated
in June 1939.

Rules of the Corps

(1) Those wishing to join this Corps should first supply
a list of antecedents together with a 3" photograph.
(2) Each member should apply his fingerprints on the
enrolment Book so as to show his loyalty for the nation,
and is not allowed to withdraw from the Corps or apply
for leave at his own discretion, otherwise supreme penalty
will be inflicted on such offenders.
(3) Members of this Corps should preserve the spirit of
faith and mutual aid, and should refrain from accepting
unlawful profits.
(4) Once becoming a member of this Corps, one should
always obey the instructions of their leader.
(5) Those who are assigned to propaganda work and other
duties should face them with courage, and should on no
account make an excuse to absent themselves from such
missions.
(6) Members of this Corps should, if necessary, take any
risks and be contented to sacrifice their lives for our
country.
(7) All members are strictly forbidden to extort money
from merchants etc. by using the name of this Corps. Such
offenders, if found guilty of the charges, will be severely
dealt with.
(8) All expenses to be incurred for the dissemination of
pamphlets etc. should in the meantime be advanced by each
member in equal sums. This will discontinue as soon as
the Central Government sanctions the operation of our Corps
and appropriate the necessary funds.

1939年6月成立的上海职业锄奸防谍团潜伏名册译文

团规

(1) 凡欲加入本团者，应先提供履历表及3寸照片一张。
(2) 每位成员应在名册上按捺指纹，以示对国家的忠诚，不得随意退出本团或请假，否则将对违规者处以极刑。
(3) 本团成员应保持信义互助的精神，不得接受非法利益。
(4) 一旦成为本团成员，应始终服从领导人的指示。
(5) 被指派从事宣传工作和其他任务者，应勇敢面对，绝不得以任何借口缺席此类任务。
(6) 本团成员如有必要，应承担任何风险，并乐于为国家牺牲生命。
(7) 严禁所有成员以本团名义向商人等勒索钱财。此类违规者，若罪名成立，将受到严厉惩处。
(8) 散发传单等所需的一切费用，暂时由每位成员均摊垫付。一旦中央政府批准本团运作并拨付必要资金，此规定即行停止。

DOORO KYUU KON (童玉巧)
S.-SHUN, SHENI // D.S.I. Wong Aung Noo.
translated
C.1. 11.7.39. /////// liou.

My name is Seong Byuh Koh, age 36, native of Sochow,
Anhui, M/Unemployed, and residing at No. 136 Rue Porte de
L'Quest, French Concession (in a room on 2nd floor bove the
kitchen of the Loh Fong (洛芳) Photographers).

I was born and brought up in Sochow, Anhui.
When I grew up I assisted my parents in farming. I have
three brothers who are all farmers. Owing to financial
difficulties in Sochow, I came to Shanghai on 10.2.27,
together with friend, named Tou Zang An (朱長安) and
went to do business in Haimen. Eight years afterwards
Tou Zang An and I left Shanghai on 18.4.35 for Haimen where
we later established a cigarette shop which existed for
three years, being subsequently closed down on 24.12.38 due
to business depression. I then on 26.12.38 came to Shanghai
with my wife and rented a room above the kitchen of No. 65
Sie Sung Li, Rue Brenier de Montmorand, F.C. I stayed in
Shanghai only for three days, and then alone returned to
Haimen on 29.12.38. My wife after living at the above address
for one month removed to No.136 Rue Porte de L'quest.

On arrival at Haimen I went to look for a friend,
one named Sung Mah Sing (沈月超), whom I consequently located.
This friend then enlisted me as a member of the guerilla units.
I was appointed the adjutant of the 1st company of the Haimen
Guerillas under the command of one named Ding Tseng Sing
(丁象堂). I served in the guerilla unit for seven months,
but owing to ill health I finally resigned my post on 30.6.39,
and came to Shanghai on 1.7.39 to seek medical treatment.
page_data.zh:
DOORO KYUU KON (童玉巧)
S.-SHUN, SHENI // 副督察 Wong Aung Noo.
翻译
C.1. 1939年7月11日。 /////// liou.

我叫 Seong Byuh Koh（音译，对应中文名可能为宋伯高或类似，但结合下文及档案语境，此人即为童玉珂/董若古，此处拼音可能有误或为别名），36岁，籍贯安徽苏州（注：苏州属江苏，原文写 Anhui 可能有误或指祖籍），男/无业，居住在法租界西爱咸斯路 (Rue Porte de L'Quest，即今永嘉路附近或旧称) 136号（洛芳照相馆厨房楼上的二楼房间）。

我出生在安徽苏州并在那里长大。
成年后，我协助父母务农。我有三个兄弟，都是农民。由于苏州经济困难，我于1927年2月10日与一位名叫朱長安 (Tou Zang An) 的朋友一起来到上海，前往海门做生意。八年后，朱長安和我于1935年4月18日离开上海前往海门，在那里我们后来开了一家香烟店，经营了三年，后因生意萧条于1938年12月24日关闭。随后，我于1938年12月26日携妻子来到上海，在法租界蒙马兰路 (Rue Brenier de Montmorand，即今吉安路) 65号 Sie Sung Li（音译）租了一间厨房楼上的房间。我在上海只待了三天，然后独自于1938年12月29日返回海门。我的妻子在上述地址居住一个月后，搬至西爱咸斯路 (Rue Porte de L'quest) 136号。

到达海门后，我去寻找一位名叫沈月超 (Sung Mah Sing) 的朋友，并成功找到了他。这位朋友随后招募我加入游击队。我被任命为丁象堂 (Ding Tseng Sing) 指挥的海门游击队第一连的副官。我在游击队服役七个月，但因健康原因，最终于1939年6月30日辞职，并于1939年7月1日来上海求医。

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

CHIANG KAI SHEK'S TYRANNY CAUSES ASSASSINATION OF
NEWSPAPER MAN; MURDERERS OF SZE LIANG ZAI
IDENTIFIED

Among anti-Japanese terrorist
gangs which had been dispatched to various places by
the Chungking Government the gang in the Shanghai
area headed by Ling Chiu Yuin was very active in
assassinating Japanese and pro-Japanese Chinese, but
the gang was destroyed on July 12, 1939 when the
Japanese Consular Police arrested Wang Ts Ming and Liu
Ping Hang. As a result it has been proved that
Sze Liang Zai, President of the Sun Pao, was assassinated
by the two prisoners in Hangchow about 5 years ago in
accordance with instructions from Ling Chiu Yuin to
whom Chiang Kai Shek had issued an order to assassinate
Sze Liang Zai because the latter had published an article
in his paper against the National Government.

The late President of the Shun Pao, S Liang-zai, was
assassinated on November 13, 1934, on the Shanghai-Hangchow
Highway.

on 12/7/39 at 70/444 Rue Tenant de la Tour at the request of the

蒋介石的暴政导致报人被暗杀；施良才（Sze Liang Zai）的凶手已被确认

在重庆政府派遣至各地的抗日恐怖团伙中，由凌秋园（Ling Chiu Yuin，音译）领导的上海地区团伙在暗杀日本人及亲华日本人方面非常活跃，但该团伙于1939年7月12日被日本领事警察逮捕王志明（Wang Ts Ming，音译）和刘平航（Liu Ping Hang，音译）后遭到摧毁。结果证实，《申报》社长施良才（Sze Liang Zai）是约5年前在杭州被这两名囚犯暗杀的，他们是按照凌秋园的指令行事，而蒋介石曾下令凌秋园暗杀施良才，因为后者在其报纸上发表了一篇反对国民政府的文章。

已故《申报》社长施良才（S Liang-zai）于1934年11月13日在沪杭公路上被暗杀。
王志明（Wong Ts Ming）：34岁，浙江人，男，无业，于1939年7月12日在唐恩路（Rue Tenant de la Tour）70/444号应日本领事警察的要求被捕（D.3299/78 - 1939年7月12日）。

CCI 7 1939
〔右上角手写批注：25501 809/79 12 39〕

Terrorist Round-Up Here,
Described In Tokyo

Mr. Shiya Saka, Former Police Chief Of Japanese
Consulate Tells Japan Police Board Of Many
Raids In Settlement And Concession

TOKYO, Oct. 6.—A first hand ac-
count of the round-up of anti-
Japanese terrorists in Shanghai,
especially a raid carried out on
July 12, was given by Mr. Shiya
Saka, Chief of the Secretariat of
the Metropolitan Police Board, in a
press interview during a party
given in his honour by General
Gunzo Kayaba, Superintendent of
the Metropolitan Police Board.

Mr. Saka recently was transferred
to the Metropolitan Police Board
from the position of Chief of Police
attached to the Japanese Consulate-
General in Shanghai, which post he
held for many years.

"Shanghai terrorist organizations,
whose leaders were arrested in raids
conducted by men under my super-
vision, were especially active last
year and early this year, threaten-
ing the lives of officials of the new
Government at Nanking," Mr. Saka
said.

"We concluded that as long as such
terrorist organizations continued in
existence it would be impossible to
accomplish the task of constructing
a new order in East Asia.

"In September of last year we re-
organized the consular police so that
we might cope effectively with the
murderous activities of members of
the organizations.

Arrested Four Or Five A Day

"We arrested Chinese terrorists at
the rate of four to five a day. These
men were found to be underlings.
Nothing about the location of the
headquarters of the organizations
was known until a man who hap-
pened to know details of the or-
ganizations came our way.

"We ascertained the location of
the headquarters of the terrorist
group on July 10.

"We made raids at three places
at the same time in the Interna-
tion Settlement and at eight places
in the French Concession and
rounded up 17 ringleaders of the
organizations.

Against Great Odds

"I was deeply impressed by the
men who conducted the raids. They
knew the men sought by them had
a large number of revolvers and
thousands of bullets. Yet they went
into action armed with only one
revolver.

"About 50 foreign policemen who
co-operated with us in the round-
up of the terrorists joined the raids
only after they had put on bullet-
proof vests.

"From one of the arrested ter-
rorists we learned the whereabouts
of the membership lists of the or-
ganizations and of the revolvers and
bullets they had. On July 14 we
confiscated all this evidence. None
of the Japanese who participated in
the raids were injured."—Domei.

东京描述上海恐怖分子大搜捕

日本前领事馆警察局长向日本警视厅汇报租界内的多次突袭行动

东京，10月6日电。——在加屋军藏（Gunzo Kayaba，音译）警视总监为酒井志也（Shiya Saka，音译）先生举行的欢迎宴会上，警视厅秘书课长酒井志也先生在记者采访中， firsthand 讲述了上海反日恐怖分子的搜捕情况，特别是7月12日进行的一次突袭行动。

酒井先生最近从上海日本总领事馆附属警察局局长的职位调任至警视厅，他担任该职多年。

“去年和今年年初，在我监督下的人员进行的突袭行动中逮捕了其领导人的上海恐怖组织特别活跃，威胁着南京新政府官员的生命安全，”酒井先生说。

“我们得出结论，只要此类恐怖组织继续存在，就不可能完成构建东亚新秩序的任务。

“去年9月，我们重组了领事警察，以便有效应对组织成员的谋杀活动。

每天逮捕四到五人

“我们以每天四到五人的速度逮捕中国恐怖分子。这些人被发现是下属人员。直到一个碰巧了解组织细节的人出现，我们才知道组织总部的位置。

“我们在7月10日确定了恐怖团体总部的位置。

“我们在公共租界的三个地点和法租界的八个地点同时进行了突袭，抓获了该组织的17名头目。

面对巨大劣势

“我对执行突袭的人员印象深刻。他们知道被搜捕的人拥有大量左轮手枪和数千发子弹。然而，他们仅携带一支左轮手枪就采取了行动。

“协助我们搜捕恐怖分子的约50名外国警察是在穿上防弹背心后才加入突袭行动的。

“从一名被捕的恐怖分子那里，我们得知了组织成员名单以及他们拥有的左轮手枪和子弹的下落。7月14日，我们没收了所有这些证据。参与突袭的日本人均未受伤。”——同盟社。

On the 4th. October, 1939, I was conveyed to the
Japanese Consulate where I was interrogated by them regarding
my past activities. I told them the whole truth. I returned
to the Hongkew Police Station on the 12th. October, 1939.
On the 19th. October, 1939, D.S. Fowler and D.S.I.
Soong visited me in Hongkew Police Station and questioned
me whether I had spoken truth to the Japanese. I replied
that I had told the truth. They further asked me why I
prevaricated to the S.M.Police on my initial arrest. I
replied that as I was treated in a civilized manner and
there being a lack of evidence, I therefore did not admit
anything. Later, I was forced to tell the whole truth
by the Japanese.
I served under the Kiangsu Provincial Government
only for one year and received $30.00 per mensem.
This is a true statement.

( Sd.) Lan Yuen Sung.

1939年10月4日，我被带往日本领事馆，他们就我过去的活动对我进行了讯问。我向他们讲了全部实情。我于1939年10月12日回到虹口捕房。1939年10月19日，福勒侦探长（D.S. Fowler）和宋高级督察在虹口捕房看望了我，并问我是否对日本人说了实话。我回答说我说了实话。他们进一步问我为什么在初次被捕时对上海公共租界警务处支吾其词。我回答说，因为我受到文明对待，且缺乏证据，所以我没有承认任何事情。后来，我被日本人强迫说出了全部实情。
我仅在江苏省政府服役一年，月薪30.00元。
此陈述属实。

x D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung.
translated
19-10-39 x xxxxx Kuh Nei Han

On 4-10-39, I was handed over to the Japanese Con-
sulate and on 12-10-39, I was returned to S.M.P. from there.
Whilst in the custody of the Japanese Consulate I was not
questioned. On 19-10-39 detectives of the S.M.P. questioned
me re the statement of Tsoong Foh Zai (童福財) as to whether
or not it was true. I then pointed out the following re my
connections with Tsoong Foh Zai.

I became acquainted with Tsoong Foh Zai in the 4th
International Refugee Camp, Ferry Road, in november, 1937.
At that time I was in charge of the Supervisory Section of the
Camp whilst Tsoong was a supervisor of the Camp.

In June, 1938 I entered the Shanghai Labour Union
under Tsu Sse. The Union was organized for the purpose of
joining workmen so as to supervise the whole work of the Union.
In August, 1938, I recommended Tsoong Foh Zai to enter the
Union, and in november Tsu Sse instructed me to set fire in a
Japanese factory. I then passed the instructions to Tsoong Foh
Zai but I myself refused to undertake such a task as it would
cause a serious result. I then resigned from the Union. Later,
Tsu Sse appointed one named Tsu Tsung Tai (朱宗泰) to accept my
position, but I don't know to what extent he had got in contact
with Tsoong Foh Zai.

Whilst I was employed in the Union I used to get in
contact with Tsu Sse in a certain temple at No. 101, Handley
Road.

This is my true statement.

Signed: Chaung Cheng.

翻译
1939年10月19日 x xxxxx 顾内汉（Kuh Nei Han，音译）

1939年10月4日，我被移交给日本领事馆，1939年10月12日，我从那里被退回上海公共租界警务处。
在日本领事馆羁押期间，我没有受到讯问。1939年10月19日，上海公共租界警务处的侦探就童福财（Tsoong Foh Zai）的供词是否属实对我进行了讯问。随后，我就我与童福财的关系指出了以下情况。

我于1937年11月在渡船路第四国际难民收容所结识了童福财。当时我负责收容所的监管科，而童是收容所的监管员。

1938年6月，我加入了朱四（Tsu Sse，音译）领导下的上海劳工工会。该工会的组织目的是吸纳工人，以便监督工会的全部工作。1938年8月，我推荐童福财加入工会，11月，朱四指示我在一家日本工厂放火。随后我将指令传达给童福财，但我自己拒绝承担此项任务，因为这会造成严重后果。随后我辞去了工会职务。后来，朱四任命一名叫朱宗泰（Tsu Tsung Tai）的人接替我的职位，但我不知道他与童福财接触到了什么程度。

我在工会任职期间，曾在汉密路（Handley Road）101号的一座寺庙里与朱四联系。

这是我的真实陈述。

签名：龚诚。

in politics in any way.
Lieu Ching Ho's statement has been
corroborated as far as it has been possible to do so.
The 16th arrest, Lan Yuen Sung, has likewise
continued in his denials of being concerned in anti-
Japanese activities. A statement, (No. 19 in
amplification of a previous one, No. 13), was taken
from him at Hongkew Station on September 26, 1939.
Again, the points in his statement have,
as far as is possible, been checked upon and found to
corroborate. The only point not possible to check upon
was the period between August 1937 and August 1938,
during which he removed with his family to Quinsan
because of local hostilities.
However, in view of the fact the allegation
of Ying Wei S (應渭水) (statement No. 16) is that he
joined an anti-Japanese organisation in April or May
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

蕭鐘麟 (Siao Zung Ling) 提到，刘靖華是梅約 (May Yoh) 的姻亲；
梅約系恐吓信登记处的文书助理。
就此接受讯问时，梅約表示，刘靖華的姑母是他的妻子（即梅約之妻）。
他认识刘靖華约14年，可以担保其品行端正，且未参与反日活动，事实上也未以任何方式参与政治。
就力所能及的范围而言，刘靖華的供词已得到证实。
第16号被捕者藍永生同样继续否认参与反日活动。
1939年9月26日，在虹口捕房对其录取得一份供词（作为此前第13号供词的补充，编号为第19号）。
同样，其供词中的要点已在力所能及的范围内进行了核查，并发现予以佐证。唯一无法核实的要点是1937年8月至1938年8月期间，在此期间，因当地战事，他携家人搬往昆山 (Quinsan)。
然而，鉴于應渭水 (Ying Wei S)（第16号供词）的指控是他于1939年4月或5月

page_data.en:
- 3 -

1939 in Shanghai and not during the period between
August 1937 and August 1938, this point was left in
abeyance.

The 19th arrest, Chaung Cheng, has made a
statement (No. 20), in which he admits having been a
member of the Military Affairs Committee in Shanghai
between June and November 1938 and receiving $30.00
per month. During this period he recruited one other
who was subsequently arrested by the Japanese Consular
Police and gave information leading to his (Chaung
Cheng's) arrest. He states that he began to realize
the dangerousness of his situation in November 1938 and
therefore withdrew from the organisation and has since
had no connection with any group whatever.

To sum up; against the :-
13th arrest Lieu Ching Ho (刘靖華)✓
and
16th arrest Lan Yuen Sung (蓝永生)✓

no definite proof has been submitted by the Japanese
Consular Police that these two men have been concerned
in any way in anti-Japanese activities. No documents
of any kind were found in the house (No. 6 Shanghai
Terrace, Route Vallon) where the 13th arrest is the
chief tenant and the 16th arrest a sub-tenant in spite
of the fact Ying Wei S in a brief statement (No. 16)
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

在上海加入了一个反日组织，而非在1937年8月至1938年8月期间，因此这一点被暂时搁置。

第19号被捕者熊誠 (Chaung Cheng) 作出了一份供词（第20号），其中承认他在1938年6月至11月期间曾是上海军事委员会的成员，每月领取30.00美元。在此期间，他招募了另一人，该人随后被日本领事馆警察逮捕，并提供情报导致了他（熊誠）的被捕。他表示，他在1938年11月开始意识到处境的危险，因此退出了该组织，此后未与任何团体有任何联系。

综上所述；针对：
第13号被捕者 刘靖華 (Lieu Ching Ho)✓
以及
第16号被捕者 蓝永生 (Lan Yuen Sung)✓

日本领事馆警察未能提交确凿证据证明这两人以任何方式参与了反日活动。尽管應渭水在一份简短的供词（第16号）中声称

page_data.en:
- 4 -

avers that the house was used as a headquarters in which
he was a Captain of the 3rd detachment.

It must also be remembered that Ying Wei S
et al were arrested at practically the same time as the
13th and 16th arrest due to simultaneous raids carried
out, therefore previous knowledge by the 13th and 16th
arrest of the arrest of Ying Wei S and the chance to
destroy evidence was not possible.

Against the 19th arrest, Maung Cheng, there
is evidence to hand to show that he was formerly
engaged in anti-Japanese activities.

〔此处转录不清〕

D. S. 329
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

该房屋被用作总部，且他是第三分队队长，但在第13号被捕者作为主要租户、第16号被捕者作为分租户居住的房屋（万隆路 [Route Vallon] 上海里6号）内，未发现任何类型的文件。

还必须记住，由于同时进行的突击搜查，應渭水等人几乎与第13号和第16号被捕者同时被捕，因此第13号和第16号被捕者不可能预先知晓應渭水被捕并有时间销毁证据。

针对第19号被捕者 Maung Cheng，现有证据表明他以前曾从事反日活动。

〔此处转录不清〕

D. S. 329

page_data.en:
further Lieu Ching Ho (劉靖華) 18
xx D.S. Fowler
Hongkew Stn. 26-9-39 D.S.I. Soong

Further to my previous statement (No. 12), the
following is what transpired between November 1935 and June
1939.

Whilst working for the Zoong Yoong Ching (陳永青)
Exchange Shop, Kiukiang Road, the Stabilisation scheme by
the Nationalist Government came into force in November 1935
and therefore there was very little business to be done
because of small fluctuations.

In November 1935 or 1936, I took over chief
tenant of No. 6 Shanghai Terrains, Route Vallon and paid
$70.00 per month rent.

Owing to there being very little business in the
money exchange in 1936, I began to speculate in the cotton
business. I had about $3,000.00 at that time. I used to
frequent the Zoong Yoong Ching Exchange Shop only infrequently
as I had worked for some time on a commission basis.

Finally, in August 1937, due to the Sino-Japanese
hostilities, the cotton exchange closed. I had made about
$500.00 to $1,000.00 profit. The money exchange shop where
I had worked had changed hands and, due to that and very
poor business, I decided to live on the profit from the
sub-letting of my house which was bringing me in about
$100.00 per month profit.

I continued to do this until June 1939. I did
not go out very much for recreation as I wished to save the
little money which I had. Even then I had to borrow
$1,000.00 from my mother-in-law Chung Wong Sz (程黃氏), who
page_data.zh:
续前 刘靖華 (LIU CHING HO) 18
xx 福勒副督察 (D.S. Fowler)
虹口捕房 1939年9月26日 宋督察长 (D.S.I. Soong)

继我之前的供词（第12号）之后，以下是1935年11月至1939年6月期间发生的事宜。

当我在九江路陈永青 (Zoong Yoong Ching) 兑换店工作时，国民政府的法币稳定方案于1935年11月生效，因此由于波动很小，生意寥寥无几。

1935年或1936年11月，我接手了万隆路 (Route Vallon) 上海里 (Shanghai Terrains) 6号的主要租户身份，每月支付租金70.00美元。

由于1936年兑换店生意清淡，我开始涉足棉花生意。当时我约有3,000.00美元。因为我已按佣金 basis 工作了一段时间，所以我很少去陈永青兑换店。

最终，在1937年8月，由于中日敌对行动，棉花交易所关闭。我获利约500.00至1,000.00美元。我曾工作的兑换店易主，加之生意极差，我决定依靠出租房屋的分租利润生活，这每月给我带来约100.00美元的利润。

我一直这样做直到1939年6月。我不常外出娱乐，因为我想节省手头仅有的一点钱。即便如此，我还不得不向与我同住的岳母程黃氏 (Chung Wong Sz) 借款1,000.00美元，她

page_data.en:
- 28

was also living in the house.

I made attempts to find work but this proved
fruitless.

In January 1939 I assisted my brother-in-law Siao
Yue Ling (蕭玉麟), who was formerly the sub-manager of the
National Commercial Bank, in collecting rents for houses he
had on Route Dolfuss, French Concession.

For that service he used to give me about $10.00
per month.

In June 1939 my friend Ts Seu Mai (朱瘦梅) opened
the Dong Yih Foreign Exchange Hong (同益票行) at No. 50
Ching Yue Li (清遠里), Peking Road (near Honan Road). He
gave me a job at $50.00 per month plus commission which
averaged about $150.00 per month. I worked there until my
arrest.

During the time I had no regular employment I was
not, and never have been, concerned in any anti-Japanese
activities whatsoever, neither have I had any position with
the Chinese Government.

At about 3.30 a.m. July 12, 1939, Settlement and
French Police, together with Japanese, entered my home and
asked for one named Ling (林) who could drive a motor car.
I told the parties that no person by the name of Ling lived
in my house, neither could anyone in the house drive a motor
car.

The Japanese insisted that the house be searched.
This was done, but nothing was found. The Japanese then
page_data.zh:
- 28

也住在这所房子里。

我试图寻找工作，但毫无结果。

1939年1月，我协助我的妹夫蕭玉麟 (Siao Yue Ling) 收取他在法租界杜美路 (Route Dolfuss) 拥有的房屋的租金。他以前是国家商业银行的副经理。

作为这项服务的报酬，他每月给我约10.00美元。

1939年6月，我的朋友朱瘦梅 (Ts Seu Mai) 在北京路（近河南路）清遠里50号开设了同益票行 (Dong Yih Foreign Exchange Hong)。他给了我一份工作，月薪50.00美元，外加平均每月约150.00美元的佣金。我在那里工作直到被捕。

在我没有固定工作期间，我从未，也从来没有，参与任何反日活动，我也未曾在中国政府担任任何职务。

1939年7月12日凌晨3点30分左右，公共租界和法国警察会同日本人进入我家，询问一名姓林 (Ling) 且会开汽车的人。我告诉各方，我家中没有姓林的人居住，家中也没有人会开汽车。

日本人坚持要搜查房屋。搜查进行了，但未发现任何东西。日本人随后

page_data.en:
- 3 -

insisted that the men in the house be taken for identification.
The men consisted of myself, Lan Yuen Sung (藍永生), Hsia
Hwo Ching (謝華卿) and Hsia Lih Hyung (謝立勳).

Lan Yuen Sung came to live in the upstairs front
rooms in May 1939. I don't know what business he did as I
was concerned in my own affairs. I never had any trouble
with him during the time he lived in my house.

Hsia Hwo Ching and Hsia Lih Hyung came to live at
my house in November 1938, together with their families.
I understood them to be refugees from around Yangchow or
somewhere near there. They did not appear to have a lot of
money, but they were respectable. The two men appeared to be
always sick.

To corroborate my statement re money and cotton
exchange business done by myself, the following persons can
be questioned :-

Siao Yue Ling        (蕭鈺麟),
                     Residing No. 4, Lane
                     217, Route Delastre,
                     F.C. Tel : 71391.

Ts Seu Mai           (朱瘦梅),
                     at Tung Yih Foreign
                     Exchange Shop, Peking
                     Road. Tel : 18392.

Siao Zung Ling       (蕭鍾麟),
                     sub-assistant to Mr.
                     Rosenfeld, Continental
                     Bank Building, Kiukiang
                     and Szechmen Roads.
                     Tel : 18150.

The foregoing is true.

Sgd. & Thumbprinted by : LIHU CHING HO.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

坚持要将屋内的男子带走进行辨认。这些男子包括我自己、藍永生 (Lan Yuen Sung)、謝華卿 (Hsia Hwo Ching) 和謝立勳 (Hsia Lih Hyung)。

藍永生于1939年5月搬来住在楼上的前间。我不知道他做什么生意，因为我忙于自己的事务。在他住在我家期间，我与他从未发生过任何纠纷。

謝華卿和謝立勳于1938年11月携家人搬来住在我家。据我了解，他们是扬州附近某地的难民。他们似乎没有很多钱，但为人正派。这两人看起来总是生病。

为了佐证我关于自己从事兑换和棉花生意的陈述，可以讯问以下人员：

蕭鈺麟 (Siao Yue Ling)，
住址：法租界德拉司德路 (Route Delastre) 217弄4号。
电话：71391。

朱瘦梅 (Ts Seu Mai)，
地址：北京路同益兑换店。
电话：18392。

蕭鍾麟 (Siao Zung Ling)，
罗森菲尔德先生 (Mr. Rosenfeld) 的助理，
大陆银行大楼，九江路与四川路路口。
电话：18150。

以上属实。

签署并按指印：LIHU CHING HO (刘靖華)。

page_data.en:
19
LAN YUEN SUNG (盛永昌)
Quinsen -- J.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung
translated
H'kew Stn. 26.9.39 Hsu S. P.

My name is Lan Yuen Sung, age 25 years, native of
Quinsen.

I was born at House No. 10 Mei Ka Loong (梅家弄),
Nantao, Shanghai. My father is named Lan Zung Ts (盛润志),
employed at The Chung Hwa (中華) Confectionery Co.

At the age of 7 I attended the Ning Lou Yih (銀樓義)
Primary School, situated at Dah Tung Meng (大東門), Nantao,
where I left at the age of 15 when I went to study in the
Shanghai Middle School.

At the age of 17 I quitted study and became an
apprentice in the Yeong Tai Ziang (永泰祥) Haberdashery,
Rue de Consulat.

At the age of 19 I was transferred to the Yoong
Hwa (永華) Haberdashery, Rue Palikao, which was operated
by the same owner of Yoong Tai Ziang.

The last mentioned shop was eventually closed down
when I was 21 years old and, therefore, became unemployed
during which period I was supplied food etc by my parents.

At the age of 22 I procured another job in the
Brothers Haberdashery (兄弟), at Lao Si Meng, Nantao,
where I remained employed till the age of 23 (year 1937)
when war broke out in Shanghai, which brought destruction
to our shop.

With my whole family I evacuated to Quinsen where
I stayed until some time in Aug. 1938 when I returned to
Shanghai seeking for employment. At that time I made my
residence at my aunt's home, situated at 2nd house, 2nd lane,
page_data.zh:
19
盛永昌 (LAN YUEN SUNG)
昆山 -- 宋秉宗督察长 (J.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung)
翻译
虹口捕房 1939年9月26日 徐 S. P. (Hsu S. P.)

我叫藍永生，25岁，昆山人。

我出生于上海南市梅家弄10号。父亲名叫盛润志 (Lan Zung Ts)，在中华糖果公司 (The Chung Hwa Confectionery Co.) 任职。

7岁时，我就读于位于南市大东门的银楼义 (Ning Lou Yih) 小学，15岁时离校，进入上海中学学习。

17岁时，我辍学，成为领事馆路 (Rue de Consulat) 永泰祥 (Yeong Tai Ziang) 百货店的学徒。

19岁时，我被调到白尔部路 (Rue Palikao) 的永華 (Yoong Hwa) 百货店，该店由永泰祥的同一老板经营。

当我21岁时，最后提到的这家店最终关闭，因此我失业，在此期间由父母提供食物等生活所需。

22岁时，我在南市老西门的兄弟百货店 (Brothers Haberdashery) 找到了另一份工作，一直受雇到23岁（1937年），当时上海爆发战争，导致我们的店铺被毁。

我全家撤离到昆山，一直待到1938年8月的某个时候，我回到上海寻找工作。当时我住在阿姨家，地址位于贝当路 (Route Pere Robert) 旁的松松里 (Sung Sung Li) 2弄2号，

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Sung Sung Li, off Route Pere Robert.

In May 1939 through the recommendation of my
uncle Lan Vee Sung (藍維松), residing at No. 6 Ting Ziang
Li, Boul. de Kontigny, I obtained a job in the Bah Seh (八仙)
Emporium, off Rue Kreetzer with pay at $25 per mensem.

In the night time I slept in the provisional
office of the Bah Seh Emporium, located at House No.
6, Shanghai Terrace, Route Vallon.

At about 3 a.m. on the 12.7.39 I was arrested
by Police. The reason for my arrest is unknown to me.

I have never been in the Military or Police
organisations, nor have I any interest in the political
affairs.

The owner of the Bah Seh Emporium is one named
Yu Tsung Hwei (俞宗輝) whose address is unknown.

Signed & cross marked by :

Lan Yuen Sung (alias
Lan Ka Sung ).
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

1939年5月，通过居住在孔提尼路 (Boul. de Kontigny) 鼎祥里6号的叔叔藍維松 (Lan Vee Sung) 的介绍，我在克里泽路 (Rue Kreetzer) 旁的八仙 (Bah Seh) 商场找到了一份工作，月薪25美元。

晚上，我睡在位于万隆路 (Route Vallon) 上海里6号的八仙商场临时办公室。

1939年7月12日凌晨3点左右，我被警察逮捕。我被捕的原因我不清楚。

我从未在军队或警察机构服役，也对政治事务没有任何兴趣。

八仙商场的老板名叫俞宗輝 (Yu Tsung Hwei)，地址不详。

签署并画十字标记：

藍永生 (别名
藍嘉松 Lan Ka Sung)。

page_data.en:
A.U.S. & A.I 龔誠 19
-- . . . 184
.P.R. . 26.9.39 translated Hsu . P.

Chang Cheng further states:-
In June 1938 through the introduction of Mr.
Wong Yih Ming (王一民) also a member of the No. 4
Refugee Camp staff, located on Perry Road, I became
acquainted with one named Tsu S (朱祥), who later
requested me to contact labourers of various factories
and instigate them to participate in anti-Japanese work.
In July same year I got in touch with one named
Tsoong Foh Zai (鐘福才) whom I asked to assist me in
doing the above mentioned work.
In November 1938 Tsoong Foh Zai in turn approached
two others namely Tsu An Loong (朱安龍) and Wong Yih Chu
(王一柱) who were requested by Tsoong to join us.
I received every month from Tsu S $30.00 as my wage.
In December I discovered that Tsu S was a member
of the Military Affairs Committee of Central Government,
and his duty was to destroy every factory. On discovery
of the above I resigned my position since I was afraid
of being caught and getting into trouble.
I then started my career as a hand cart merchant.
The above is my true statement.

Signed, cross marked and thumb
printed by Chang Cheng.
page_data.zh:
A.U.S. & A.I 龔誠 19
-- . . . 184
.P.R. . 1939年9月26日 翻译 徐 . P. (Hsu . P.)

张成 (Chang Cheng) 进一步陈述：
1938年6月，通过同在佩里路 (Perry Road) 第四难民收容所工作人员王一民 (Wong Yih Ming) 先生的介绍，我结识了一位名叫朱祥 (Tsu S) 的人，他后来要求我联系各工厂的工人，煽动他们参与反日工作。
同年7月，我联系上了一位名叫鐘福才 (Tsoong Foh Zai) 的人，我请他协助我进行上述工作。
1938年11月，鐘福才又接触了另外两人，即朱安龍 (Tsu An Loong) 和王一柱 (Wong Yih Chu)，鐘请求他们加入我们。
我每月从朱祥那里领取30.00美元作为工资。
12月，我发现朱祥是中央政府军事委员会的成员，他的任务是破坏每一家工厂。发现上述情况后，因害怕被抓并惹上麻烦，我辞去了职位。
随后，我开始从事手推车小贩的职业。
以上是我的真实陈述。

张成签署、画十字标记并按指印。

FURTHER TO: ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE
CONSULAR POLICE.

At 11 a.m. 20.9.39, Mr. Hashidzume of the
Japanese Consular Police called at C.1, Crime Branch
Headquarters, and produced documental evidence against
Chaung Cheng (龔誠) and Tsoeng Foh Zai (鐘福財)
together with the statements of these two persons.

In their statements, Chaung Cheng admits
having concerned in anti-Japanese activities as a
special service member of the Military Affairs Committee
of the Nationalist Government, while Tsoeng Foh Zai
admits having committed arson on the Hsih Woo Mill
(喜和紗廠) in accordance with the instructions of
Chaung Cheng.

The evidence produced shows that Chaung
Cheng has connection with Ying Wei S (應渭水) et al
and also concerned in the arson on the Hsih Woo Mill.

Translation attached.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 21 9 39）
（批：C.D.S. Sal / Rush / 21/9.）

Mackenzie
C.D.I.

8299/78
1939年9月21日

C.1，刑事调查总部。
C.1 杂项 105/39
1939年9月20日。
42

续：协助日本领事警察。

1939年9月20日上午11时，日本领事警察的桥爪（Hashidzume）先生到访 C.1 刑事调查总部，出示了针对 Chaung Cheng（龔誠）和 Tsoeng Foh Zai（鐘福財）的书面证据，以及此二人的供词。

在他们的供词中，Chaung Cheng 承认作为国民政府军事委员会特别工作人员参与了反日活动，而 Tsoeng Foh Zai 承认按照 Chaung Cheng 的指示对喜和纱厂（Hsih Woo Mill）实施了纵火。

所出示的证据显示，Chaung Cheng 与 Ying Wei S（應渭水）等人有联系，并参与了喜和纱厂的纵火案。

附译文。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科 1939年9月21日）
（批：C.D.S. Sal / 急件 / 9月21日。）

TRANSLATION

Japanese Consulate-General.
September 19, 1939.

Statement of Cheung Cheng (龔诚)

I was engaged in the special service during the period between June and November 1939 with fund $30.00 per month which was supplied by Tsu S (朱師), a special service member in Shanghai of the Military Affairs Committee of the Nationalist Government.

During this time I succeeded in obtaining three persons namely Tsoong Foh Zai (鐘福財), Tsu Su Loong (朱安龍) and Wong Yih Jeu (王一權) as my followers.

Statement of Tsoong Foh Zai (鐘福財)

I enrolled myself in the anti-Japanese Association through the canvass of Chaung Cheng in November 1938, and have since been active under his direction.

In accordance with instructions from Chaung Cheng I together with other two members namely Tsu Su Loong and Wong Yih Jeu set fire to Hsih Woo Mill (喜和紗廠) of the Japan and China Cotton Mill on December 28, 1938.

....................

As per statements mentioned, it is quite apparent that Chaung Cheng had concerned in the anti-Japanese operation of the Military Affairs Committee and Tsoong Foh Zai and two others had committed an arson as a part of anti-Japanese operation in accordance with the instructions of Chaung Cheng.

Moreover, judging from the fact that a report in connection with performance of arson found in the documents seized at No. 17 Huh Chuin Faang (合羣坊), Route Tenant de la Tour, French Concession, which was photographed and attached herewith, there is no room for argument that Cheung Cheng had connection with Ying Wei S and his group and having concerned in the arson on the Hsih Woo Cotton Mill.

S. Masa. (Inspector)
page_data.zh:
译文

日本总领事馆。
1939年9月19日。

Cheung Cheng（龔诚）的供词

在1939年6月至11月期间，我从事特别服务工作，每月由国民政府军事委员会驻上海特别工作人员 Tsu S（朱師）提供资金30.00美元。

在此期间，我成功招募了三个人，即 Tsoong Foh Zai（鐘福財）、Tsu Su Loong（朱安龍）和 Wong Yih Jeu（王一權）作为我的追随者。

Tsoong Foh Zai（鐘福財）的供词

我于1938年11月经 Chaung Cheng 游说加入反日协会，此后一直在他指挥下活动。

按照 Chaung Cheng 的指示，我与另外两名成员，即 Tsu Su Loong 和 Wong Yih Jeu，于1938年12月28日放火烧毁了日华纱厂旗下的喜和纱厂（Hsih Woo Mill）____

根据上述供词，很明显 Chaung Cheng 参与了军事委员会的反日行动，而 Tsoong Foh Zai 等两人则按照 Chaung Cheng 的指示，作为反日行动的一部分实施了纵火。

此外，从法租界陶尔斐司路（Route Tenant de la Tour）合羣坊（Huh Chuin Faang）17号查获的文件中发现了一份关于实施纵火的报告（已拍照并附后），据此可以毫无疑问地认定 Cheung Cheng 与 Ying Wei S 及其团伙有联系，并参与了喜和纱厂的纵火案。

S. Masa.（警探）

他仅陈述 Lieu Ching Ho、Lan Yuen Sung 和 Feng Ming Tseng 是“上海反日特别服务团”的成员。在他之前的第5号和第7号供词中，他并不清楚这三人的具体角色。

针对 11) Loh Kwoh S（女）；12) Kwoh Yung Tsong；14) Hsia Hwo Ching；15) Hsia Lih Hyung，没有任何针对他们的证据提出，且在1939年8月3日将他们移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处羁押时，日本领事警察要求予以拘留，因为当时他们手中没有针对这些人的证据，但预计几天内会有证据出现（见第2页第24号日志）。自那以来已过去六周，但毫无结果。

Chaung Cheng ( 龔誠 ).
Yen Chen, Kompo.                                D.S.I. Wong Zung Wo
                                                 translated
H.Q.B.B.            August 30, 39.    XXXXXXXX   Kuh Nei Han

    My name is Chaung Cheng alias Chaung Chien Cheng
( 龔謙臣 ), aged 31, a native of Yen Chen, Kompo, married,
handcart master, residing at No. 1764 Ying Woo Li, Robison
Road.
    During my youth, I lived together with my parents
in the country. In 3rd year of the Chinese Republic, when
at the age of 6, I studied in Po I Primary School and when
at the age of 12, I stopped my study owing to the death of
my parents. In January 1922 I had been an apprentice in
Wu Tuh Woo Grocery. In 1927, after having completed my
apprentice period I stayed at home and was unemployed for
a year. In February 1928, my elder brother brought me to
Shanghai and in May, my elder brother recommended me to
Sun Sin No.7 Cotton Mill where I was employed as a laborer
for 9 years.
    At the outbreak of hostilities on August 13, 1937,
I went to my mother-in-law's home at No. 1764 Ying Woo Li,
Robison Road, and boarded there. On September 25, 1937,
one of my friends, named Cheng Tsu Yeon ( 陳祖榮 ), Head
of the 4th International Refugee Camp, recommended me to be
in charge of the Supervisory Section of the Camp. On March
12, 1938, I returned to my native country and sold all my
land property which is valued at more than 500 dollars.
On August 22, 1938, I came to Shanghai and still resided at
my mother-in-law's home. As I intended to resume the hand-
cart business, in October 1938, I purchased two handcarts
by spending about $400, and then made a living by hiring
page_data.zh:
Chaung Cheng ( 龔誠 )。
籍贯：Kompo 之 Yen Chen。                                警司一級 Wong Zung Wo
                                                 翻译
总部 BB            1939 年 8 月 30 日    XXXXXXXX   Kuh Nei Han

    我叫 Chaung Cheng，别名 Chaung Chien Cheng
( 龔謙臣 )，31 岁，籍贯 Kompo 之 Yen Chen，已婚，
人力车夫，居住于罗便臣道英华里 1764 号。
    年少时，我与父母在乡下共同生活。民国三年，
我 6 岁时，在博一小学读书，12 岁时因父母去世而
辍学。1922 年 1 月，我在 Wu Tuh Woo 杂货店当学徒。
1927 年，学徒期满后，我在家待业一年。1928 年 2
月，兄长带我来到上海，5 月，兄长推荐我进入申新
第七棉纺织厂，我在那里当了 9 年工人。
    1937 年 8 月 13 日战事爆发后，我搬到岳母家，
即罗便臣道英华里 1764 号，并寄宿于此。1937 年 9
月 25 日，我的一位朋友，第四国际难民收容所所长
Cheng Tsu Yeon ( 陳祖榮 )，推荐我负责该收容所的
监管部。1938 年 3 月 12 日，我返回家乡，卖掉了所有
土地财产，价值超过 500 美元。1938 年 8 月 22 日，
我来到上海，仍居住在岳母家。由于我打算重操人力
车行业，1938 年 10 月，我花费约 400 美元购买了两辆
人力车，然后通过每天出租

page_data.en:
- 2 -

the handbills to others every day. On August 29, 1939, I
was arrested by officers of Central Police Station together
with several Japanese, but I don't know why I should be ar-
rested.

The seized map, books etc, belong to one of my
friends, named Hong Woo Chi (洪雨池), who handed same to
me for safe keeping.

This is my true statement.

Signed and thumbprinted by Chaung Cheng.
page_data.zh:

人力车谋生。1939 年 8 月 29 日，我被中央巡捕房的
警官连同几名日本人逮捕，但我不知道为何被捕。

查获的地图、书籍等属于我的一位朋友，名
叫 Hong Woo Chi (洪雨池)，是他交给我代为保管的。

这是我的真实供词。

FURTHER REPORT TO JUDGE OF CONSULAR POLICE

At 6 p.m. August 30th, 1939, Mr. Hashizume
of the Japanese Consular Police requested assistance
to raid an address in the French Concession at 11 p.m.
30-8-39, where it was hoped to arrest another
accomplice of Ying Wei Sz (應渭水):

At 11 p.m. 30-8-39, a party of S.M. Police
consisting of D.S.I. Crighton, D.S. Yamahara, D.S.I.
Lieu Kyung Ching, C.D.S. 40 and C.D.C. 212, accompanied
by J.D.S.'s Ninomiya and Noda of the Japanese Consular
Police, proceeded to Lokawei Station, where after
necessary assistance had been given by D.S. Moron,
the party visited No. 12 Rue du Marne, French
Concession, where it was hoped to arrest one named
Chuen Yeu Ding (龔雨亭); however on arrival there it
was ascertained that the person in question had left
two days ago and so had had failed to return.

D.S. Ninomiya next requested assistance
to visit Lane 58, House 58, Boulevard de Montigny,
where he alleged this man might still be located.
D.S. Moron agreed to raid this address, however once
again same proved abortive.

致领事警察法官的进一步报告

1939年8月30日下午6时，日本领事警察桥爪先生（Hashizume）请求协助，拟于当晚11时突袭法租界内的一处地址，希望能在那里逮捕应渭水（Ying Wei Sz）的另一名同伙：

1939年8月30日晚上11时，由警佐克里顿（Crighton）、警佐山原（Yamahara）、警佐刘景清（Lieu Kyung Ching）、华籍高级巡长40号及华籍巡长212号组成的工部局警务处小队，在日本领事警察二等巡佐二宫（Ninomiya）和野田（Noda）的陪同下，前往卢家湾捕房。在得到莫伦警佐（Moron）的必要协助后，该队前往法租界马浪路12号，希望在那里逮捕一名叫龚雨亭（Chuen Yeu Ding）的人；然而到达后发现，此人已于两天前离开，且尚未返回。

随后，二宫警佐请求协助前往蒙梯尼大道58弄58号，他声称此人可能仍藏匿于此。莫伦警佐同意对该地址进行突袭，但再次无功而返。

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

Before rendering the assistance as requested
in diary 31, it was learned from Inspt. Yuasa of
the Japanese Consular Police, that from documents
seized in the French Concession, one Chaung Cheng
(龔 誠), 31, M/Hand cart master, native of Kompo,
residing No. 1764 Ying Woo Li, Robison Road, was
implicated as a member of a guerilla unit, and it
was believed that documents and a large amount of
money could be seized at his home. It was also
believed that documents could be seized from an
upstairs room of No. 1710 Ying Woo Li, and No.
53 Mei Fong Li, Robison Road.

At 10.10 p.m. the U.S.M.C. Headquarters,
and Italian Marine Headquarters and Footoo Road
Station were informed of the impending raid, after
which, a party consisting of D.S. Krader, P.S.
MacAuley attached to Footoo Road Station, D.S.
Sugimoto, D.P.S. Yamahara, D.S.I. Wong Sang Woo,
C.D.S. 2, C.D.G.s 184, 211 and the undersigned,
proceeded to an upstairs front room of No. 1764
Ying Woo Li, Robison Road where the suspect afore-
mentioned was arrested.

关于协助日本领事警察的后续报告

在执行日记第31条所请求的协助之前，从日本领事警察的汤浅督察（Inspt. Yuasa）处获悉，根据在法租界缴获的文件，一名叫龚诚（Chaung Cheng），31岁，男，手推车夫，江苏高邮人，居住在罗宾森路（Robison Road，即今延安中路）应武里1764号的男子，被牵涉为游击队成员，据信在其家中可搜获文件和大量现金。另据信，在罗宾森路应武里1710号的楼上房间以及罗宾森路梅芳里53号也可搜获文件。

晚上10点10分，美国海军陆战队总部、意大利海军陆战队总部和福州路捕房接到了即将进行突袭的通知。随后，由克拉德警佐（Krader）、隶属福州路捕房的麦考利巡佐（MacAuley）、杉本警佐、山原副巡佐、黄生武警佐、华籍高级巡长2号、华籍巡捕184号和211号以及本人组成的小队，前往罗宾森路应武里1764号的楼上前面房间，逮捕了上述嫌疑人。

29

关于：涉及日本领事警察的后续报告

1939年8月17日下午2时30分，桥本警佐（Hashimoto）、宋秉宗督察（Soong Ping Tsung）和本人前往日本领事警察办公室，并在领事警察官员和一名翻译在场的情况下，获准讯问应渭水（YING WEI S）。
在讯问开始时，应渭水承认参与了1939年1月29日在新新旅馆605室刺杀一名叫画斋航（Hoa Nyoh Hong）的案件（凶杀案初步调查报告 414/39的主题）。他牵连出骆意（Loh Yien）及其他几人。
在此阶段，桥本先生要求调查和讯问仅限于以下三人的活动：1) 刘清华（Lieu Ching Ho）；2) 盛永生（Ian Yuen Sung）；3) 冯明政（Teng Ming Tseng）。
对应渭水进行了关于这三人的陈述记录（副本附后）。
从他的举止以及他对关于这三人活动的问题所作的含糊回答来看，他似乎并不掌握任何

page_data.en:
29/2.

definite facts whatsoever and merely averred
they were members of the same assassination
group as himself, namely; the "Shanghai Anti-
Japanese Special Service Corps".

It is worthy of note that Ying ei
is the type who, to curry favour with anyone,
would have no compunction whatever in implicating
persons in trumped-up charges.

In a statement (No.5) taken from him
by the undersigned and interpreted by Clerk
Asio at C.M.H.Q (C.1) on July 21 when no one
else was present, he denied being a member of
an assassination group as admitted by him in
a statement (No.7) taken by the Japanese Consular
Police and stated he had no knowledge of the
contents of the statement and only appended
his thumbprint because he was struck several times.

In statement No. 7 he states he does not
know the part actually played by Lieu Ching Ho
(刘靖华), but he was believed to be on the
intelligence staff of the corps. He mentioned
Lan Yuen Sung (蓝永生) as said to be one of
the Headquarters staff and concurrently purchasing
officer". With regard to Feng Ming Tseng 冯明政
he stated he was ..."not of the personnel of the
page_data.zh:
29/2.

确切事实，只是声称他们是与他同一暗杀团体的成员，即“上海抗日特别服务队”。

值得注意的是，应渭水（Ying ei）这类人为了讨好任何人，会毫无顾忌地通过捏造罪名来牵连他人。

在7月21日由本人在中央捕房总部（华务科）单独对其进行的陈述记录（第5号）中，由职员Asio翻译，他否认自己是暗杀团成员，这与他在日本领事警察所做的陈述（第7号）中的供述相矛盾，并称他对陈述内容不知情，只是因为遭到多次殴打才按下了指印。

在第7号陈述中，他表示不知道刘靖华（Lieu Ching Ho）实际扮演的角色，但据信他是该团的情报人员。他提到蓝永生（Lan Yuen Sung）据说是总部工作人员兼采购员。关于冯明政（Feng Ming Tseng），他表示他……“不是该团的人员，但经常提供重要情报，因此他作为非成员与成员之间没有区别”。

page_data.en:
29/3.

corps but used to give important information so
there is no difference between him being a non-
member and a member of the corps".

In view of the admissions and denials
by Ying Mei 5 according to the environments
when the statements were taken there is still
a reasonable doubt as to the veracity of his
statements.

Questioning of Lieu Ching Ho, Lin Yuen
Sung and Feng Ming Tseng whilst detained in
Hongkew Station Cells shows that per their
statements to S.M.Police No. 12, 13, and 14
they neither made or signed any statement
whilst temporarily detained by the Japanese
Consular Police.

19/2

对拘押在虹口捕房牢房内的刘清华、林永生（Lin Yuen Sung，原文与前文Lan/Ian不一致，依原文译）和冯明政的讯问显示，根据他们向工部局警务处所做的第12、13和14号陈述，他们在被日本领事警察临时拘留期间，未曾制作或签署任何陈述。

Ying Wei S. (應渭水)
Sou Shing                                D.S.I. Soong
1-8-39                                   translated by Mei Han

I am named Ying Wei S alias Kiang Pei Tuh, alias
Bing Sen, aged 45, a native of Sou Shing, married, un-
employed, residing at No. 291, Park Road. I was arrested
at my home by the Settlement Police at 1.50 a.m. on July
12, 1939.

After a short stay with the Settlement Police, I
was brought to the Japanese Gendarmerie for investigation.

I confessed that in August, 1938, I entered the
Active Service Corps of the Central Government with the
purpose of assassinating traitors. Shortly after, I was
promoted to the rank of Captain of the 3rd Detachment with
Headquarters established at No. 6, Route Vallon, F.C.

In January, 1939, I was communicated with by Ling
Tseu Yang (凌秋雲); Commander-in-Chief of the Corps,
that one named Lieu Ching Ho (劉清華) would enter our
service and in April and May, I was again informed that

绍兴                                宋秉宗警佐
1939年8月1日                       梅汉翻译

我叫应渭水，别名江北土（Kiang Pei Tuh），别名炳森（Bing Sen），45岁，绍兴人，已婚，无业，居住在公园路291号。我于1939年7月12日凌晨1时50分在家中被捕，由租界警察执行。

在租界警察处短暂停留后，我被带到日本宪兵队接受调查。

我供认，1938年8月，我以刺杀汉奸为目的加入了国民政府现役服务队。不久后，我被晋升为第三分队队长，总部设在法租界瓦隆路6号。

1939年1月，该队总指挥凌秋云（Ling Tseu Yang）通知我，刘清华（Lieu Ching Ho）将加入我们的队伍；4月和5月，我又被告知冯明政和蓝永生（Lan Yuen Sung）也将加入我们的队伍。除了这三人外，还有一些人未被捕，我无法记住所有人的名字。

此为真实陈述。

应渭水签字并按指印。

FURTHER TO : ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

With reference to comment of D.C. (Crime)
dated August 10, 1939, re 27 pistols etc. not being
included in the summary of the case against Lieu Ping
Hoong (刘炳恒) and 6 others, the following is
forwarded in explanation :-

The arms etc. were not, as far as is known
to the Municipal Police, discovered at Lane 316,
House 17, Route Prelupt, F. C., through information
divulged by any of the arrests made by the Municipal
Police whilst rendering assistance to the Japanese
Consular Police.

Reference diary 7, page 1; it was a
Consular Police interpreter named Yamamoto who
"discovered" the cache of arms. No prisoner
accompanied the party. The Consular Police did not
inform the Municipal Police that the discovery of the
arms was the result of interrogation of persons
temporarily loaned to them, therefore, in the absence
of definite proof against the 7 males this was not
included as evidence.

据工部局警务处所知，上述武器等物并非由工部局警务处在协助日本领事馆警察期间逮捕的任何人员所泄露的情报，而在法租界普鲁路（Route Prelupt）316弄17号被发现。

查阅日记第7册第1页；是一名名为山本（Yamamoto）的领事馆警察翻译“发现”了这批藏匿的武器。当时并无囚犯陪同前往。日本领事馆警察并未告知工部局警务处，武器的发现是审讯临时借给他们的人员的结果，因此，由于缺乏针对这7名男子的确凿证据，此事未被列为证据。

One other case has been admitted by :-
(7) Lieu Ping Hoong
(8) Wong Ts Ming
(9) Bien Shang San

arrested was because one named Kou Tsung Tsing (過正鼎)

法国警察局发布的通缉令上还有另一名男子，王竹轩（Wang Tso Chi），又名约瑟夫·王（Joseph Wang）。然而，这四名被捕男子声称对此人一无所知。
另有一起案件由以下人员承认：
(7) 刘炳恒
(8) 王子明
(9) 边兴山
(10) 骆意
即：1938年3月底，在法租界市场附近的克腊策尔路（Route Kraetzer）一家湖南餐馆内，刺杀一名姓王（王）的男子。他们牵连出，
戈宗公（Kou Tsung Kung）
相强伟（Siang Jan Wei）
曹立俊（Zau Lih Tsing）
并称戈宗公是实际开枪射击受害者的人。
据这四人称，他们已向日本领事馆警察作出供词，承认这两起刺杀案，但截至目前，这些供词尚未作为针对他们的证据通报给工部局警务处。
他们还声称，他们被捕的原因是，一名叫过正鼎（Kou Tsung Tsing）的人

page_data.en:
- 4 -

who was also concerned with them in the assassination
of Wong, had gone over to the Japanese side and given
the necessary information. Loh Yien in his statement
(No. 11) states he has seen Kou Tsung Tsing whilst
detained by the Japanese Consular Police.

With reference to the :-
(13) Lieu Ching Ho
(16) Lan Yuen Sung
(18) Feng Ming Tseng

there is nothing of a definite nature to hand against
them to show anti-Japanese activities. They deny
complicity in the two aforementioned assassinations
and are not implicated by those admitting having taken
part.

The only evidence produced against them by
the Japanese Consular Police is a brief statement
(No. 6) taken by them from Loh Yien and one (No. 7)
from Ying Wei S (應渭水), in which they state Lieu
Ching " has been concerned in collecting information
for the Special Service Section Headquarters. Lan Yuen
Sung is supposed to be a purchasing officer for the
Special Service Section Headquarters. Against Feng
Ming Tseng there does not appear to be anything of a
definite nature put forward by the Consular Police,
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

也参与了王的刺杀案，此人已投奔日方并提供了必要情报。骆意在其供词（第11号）中称，他在被日本领事馆警察拘留期间见过过正鼎。

关于：
(13) 刘靖华
(16) 蓝永生
(18) 冯明政

目前没有任何确凿证据表明他们有反日活动。他们否认参与上述两起刺杀案，且那些承认参与作案的人也未牵连他们。

日本领事馆警察提出的针对他们的唯一证据是一份简短的供词（第6号），系从骆意处取得，以及另一份（第7号）系从应渭水（Ying Wei S）处取得，其中称刘靖“曾参与为特务部总部收集情报”。蓝永生被认为是特务部总部的采购员。针对冯明政，领事馆警察似乎没有提出任何性质确凿的证据，

Tsung Kun (戈震根)(surrendered to Japanese), Wong Ta Ming
(王子明),(arrested), and one named Chien (錢) under the
direction of Zao Li Tsing (曹立俊), shot Sze Liang Zai (史良才
)to death in the vicinity of Oung Kai Street, in the
country of Hangchow. I also confessed that towards the end
of March, 1938, I, together with Kou Tsung Kun, Loh Yien
(駱意), Siang Jan Wei, Wong Ta Ming, Mien Shang San (邊興山),
and Zau Li Tsing murdered a traitor named Wang (王) in a
certain Hunan restaurant on Rue Krastner near the market.
During Sept. 1938, Hsia Ta Ming (夏子明), Zau Li Tsing
and Siang Jan Wei entered Tang Jhao Tse's (唐紹儀) residence
on Route Ferguson, F.C. and assassinated Tang whilst Loh Yee,
Wong Ta Ming, Kou Tsung Kun, Loh Tsung (駱宏), Zoo Ming
Zou (徐明義), Kou Zun Sung (戈潤臣), Mien Shang San and
I guarded the entrance of the house.

With reference to these three cases, I have signed and
finger-printed statements when in the custody of the Japanese
Consular Police, but I am not concerned with any other cases.
page_data.zh:
刘炳宏（Lieo Ping Hoong）：

四川                                    xx 宋副督察长（Soong，隶属刑事科）
                                            由顾内汉（Kuh Nei Han）翻译。
虹口捕房          1939年8月6日                xxxxxx

我叫刘炳宏，35岁，四川人，未婚，无业，居住在法租界陶尔斐司路（Route Tenant de la Tour）444弄贺乐坊（Ho Le Faung）70号。

我于1939年7月12日凌晨4时被法国警察逮捕，并于7月14日移交给租界警察羁押。7月15日，我被移交给日本领事馆警察，并接受了十多次审讯。我供述，1933年，我和曹南俊（Zau Kan Tsing）、吕国华（Luo Kwo Hwa）、相强伟（Siang Jan Wei）、戈震根（Kou Tsung Kun，已向日方自首）、王子明（Wong Ta Ming，已逮捕），以及一名姓钱（Chien）的人，在曹立俊（Zao Li Tsing）的指挥下，在杭州乡下的翁家街（Oung Kai Street）附近枪杀了史良才（Sze Liang Zai）。我还供述，1938年3月底，我与戈震根、骆意（Loh Yien）、相强伟、王子明、边兴山（Mien Shang San）和曹立俊一起，在市场附近的克腊斯特纳路（Rue Krastner）某湖南餐馆内谋杀了一名名叫王（王）的汉奸。1938年9月间，夏子明（Hsia Ta Ming）、曹立俊和相强伟进入法租界费格森路（Route Ferguson）唐绍仪（Tang Jhao Tse）的住所并刺杀了唐，而骆意（Loh Yee）、王子明、戈震根、骆宏（Loh Tsung）、徐明义（Zoo Ming Zou）、戈润臣（Kou Zun Sung）、边兴山和我则在屋外把守入口。

关于这三起案件，我在被日本领事馆警察羁押期间签署了按有指纹的供词，但我与其他案件无关。

page_data.en:
Liau Ying Hoeng

- 2 -

In spite of strict questioning by the Japanese Consular Police, I never confessed that I had been concerned in crimes within the Settlement. On the 3rd of August, I was brought by the Japanese to the Hongkew Police Stn.

I had been a grocer in Swatow during my youth and acted as a soldier in the Twenty First Division of the Republican army in 1925. I then came to Shanghai in March 1931 and trafficked in opium. I was employed as a servant of Sun Li Tsing in 1936. During the hostilities in August 1937, I served as a chaffeur in the Chinese Army and after the retirement of the army from around Shanghai, I served as a cook to Sun Li Tsing until the time of my arrest.

This is the true statement.
page_data.zh:
廖英恒（Liau Ying Hoeng）

- 2 -

尽管日本领事馆警察严加审讯，我从未承认参与过租界内的犯罪活动。8月3日，我被日本人带到虹口捕房。

我年轻时曾在汕头做过杂货商，并于1925年在国民革命军第二十一师当过兵。随后我于1931年3月来到上海，从事鸦片交易。1936年，我受雇于孙立清（Sun Li Tsing）做仆人。1937年8月战事爆发期间，我在中国军队中担任司机，军队撤出上海周边地区后，我继续为孙立清担任厨师，直至我被捕。

以上陈述属实。

page_data.en:
WONG TS MING (王子明), age 34, M/Unemployed,
residing at 70, Wu Loh Fong, Rte. Tenant de la Tou:
xx D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung (C.1)
translated Tsang Zung Pau
Zaushing
Hongkew. Stn. 6-8-39

At about 4 a.m. 12-7-39, I was arrested and brought
to the French Police Station, where a statement was taken
from me. At about 4 p.m. 14-7-39, I was handed over to the
Settlement Police and detained in their custody until the
following day, when I was taken to the Japanese Consulate.
During the period of my detention I have confessed
to the Japanese authorities the following two cases of
assassination :-
(1) Murder of a traitor named Wong (王 ) at a
certain Hunan Restaurant, Rue Kractzer Market,
towards the end of March 1938.
(2) Murder of a traitor named Tang Shao Yi (唐紹儀)
at Route Ferguson, F.C., during September 1938.
Actually I have admitted participation in 7 or 8
cases of assassination, but apart from the above two real
cases, the remainder I was coerced to confess after they had
subjected me to a severe punishment.
The leader of our Corps is named Tsang Yih Jing
(張葉勤), who had seven others under his supervision :-
Bien Shing San (边兴山) (arrested)
Lieu Ping Heong (刘炳恒) ( " )
Loh Yien (駱意) ( " )
Siang Jang Wei (相湯偉) (not in custody)
Loh Tsung (駱應) ( - " - )
Koo Tsung Kung (戈亞根) ( - " - )
and myself.
Koo Tsung Kung was the one who slew the aforementioned
page_data.zh:
王子明（WONG TS MING），34岁，男/无业，
居住在陶尔斐司路（Rte. Tenant de la Tou）吴乐坊（Wu Loh Fong）70号：
xx 宋秉忠副督察长（D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung，隶属C.1）
由曾宗保（Tsang Zung Pau）翻译
造信（Zaushing，音译）
虹口捕房。1939年8月6日

1939年7月12日凌晨4时许，我被逮捕并带到法国警察局，在那里对我进行了录供。1939年7月14日下午4时许，我被移交给租界警察，并由他们羁押至次日，随后我被带往日本领事馆。
在被羁押期间，我向日本当局供认了以下两起刺杀案：
(1) 1938年3月底，在市场附近的克拉克策尔路（Rue Kractzer）某湖南餐馆谋杀一名名叫王（王）的汉奸。
(2) 1938年9月间，在法租界费格森路谋杀一名名叫唐绍仪（Tang Shao Yi）的汉奸。
实际上，我承认参与了7或8起刺杀案，但除了上述两起真实案件外，其余案件是在他们对我施以严刑拷打后被迫供认的。
我们团体的头目名叫张叶勤（Tsang Yih Jing），他手下还有七个人：
边兴山（Bien Shing San）（已逮捕）
刘炳恒（Lieu Ping Heong）（ " ）
骆意（Loh Yien）（ " ）
相汤伟（Siang Jang Wei）（未在押）
骆应（Loh Tsung）（ - " - ）
戈亚根（Koo Tsung Kung）（ - " - ）
以及我自己。
戈亚根是杀害上述

page_data.en:
- 2 -

ong, whilst Tang Shao Yi was killed by Siang Jeng Wei.
With reference to the above cases, a statement
was taken from me at the Japanese Consulate on the 28th
July 1939. On the 3rd August 1939, I was removed to Hongkew
Police Station.
During my early years I took up the career of a
mason in my native place. Later I joined the Wei Yung (偉成)
Co. in Hangchow to learn the art of weaving. At the age of
24 I came to Shanghai, where I was employed as an engineer
at the Mayar (美亞) Filature in Nantao. I lost this job
after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
On March 17, 1938, I joined an Anti-Japanese
Association through the introduction of Lieu Ping Hoong.
I have never committed any crime in the International
Settlement, neither have I served with the Military or Police
authorities before.

Sgd. & Thumbprinted by :-        WONG TS MING
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

王某的人，而唐绍仪是由相正伟（Siang Jeng Wei）杀害的。
关于上述案件，1939年7月28日在日本领事馆对我进行了录供。1939年8月3日，我被转移至虹口捕房。
早年我在家乡从事泥瓦匠职业。后来加入杭州的伟成（Wei Yung）公司学习织造技艺。24岁时来到上海，在南市的美亚（Mayar）丝厂担任工程师。中日战事爆发后，我失去了这份工作。
1938年3月17日，经刘炳恒介绍，我加入了一个抗日协会。
我从未在国际租界内犯下任何罪行，此前也未曾服役于军方或警方机构。

签名并按指印：        王子明

page_data.en:
BIEN SHANG SAN (边兴山)
Kaushing, Chekiang // D. I. Sieu Ching Tsing
(C.1.) at H'kew Stn. 6.8.39 translated
------ Hsu C.F.

My name is Bien Shang San, aged 30 years, native
of Kaushing, Chekiang, married and residing at No. 77
Lich Loh Bung, Lane No. 444 Route Tenant de la Tour, F.C.
During my childhood I studied 3 or 4 years at
home and entered business at the age of 15 or 16.
In 1923 I was enrolled as a soldier in the 2nd
Division of the Chekiang Army, where I remained for 9
years and then I left the army of my own accord.
Later I came to Shanghai; after the outbreak
of current hostilities and through the introduction
of Shang Chiang Wei (相強偉) and Wong Ts Ming (王子明),
both fellow-country men of mine, I joined the Homicide
Squad with purpose of assassinating traitors, our leader
being one named Chang Yih Zung (張業勤). The Squad
consisted of 7 members, namely :-
Chang Yih Zung (張業勤).
Loh Yien (駱意), arrested
Loh Tsung (駱振).
Wong Ts Ming (王子明), Arrested.
Shang Chiang Wei (相強偉).
Koh Tsung Ting (過宗鼎), and
myself.
In March or April of last year I and three others,
led by Koh Tsung Ting, went to Rue Kretzer Market and
murdered one named Wong (王) in the Hunnan (湖南)
Restaurant, Rue Kretzer, F.C. I, however, did not actually
participate in the shooting of Wong, as I was at that time,
page_data.zh:
边兴山 (BIEN SHANG SAN)
浙江嘉兴 // 虹口捕房督察员萧清静 (D. I. Sieu Ching Tsing)
(C.1.) 于1939年8月6日翻译
------ 徐C.F.

本人名为边兴山，现年30岁，籍贯浙江嘉兴，已婚，居住于法租界陶尔斐司路444弄77号（李罗邦）。
幼年时在家读书三四年，十五六岁时开始经商。
1923年，我入伍加入浙军第二师，服役九年后自愿退伍。
后来我来到上海；在当前战事爆发后，经同乡相强伟 (Shang Chiang Wei) 和王子明 (Wong Ts Ming) 介绍，我加入了以刺杀汉奸为目的的暗杀队，队长名为张业勤 (Chang Yih Zung)。该队共有7名成员，即：
张业勤 (Chang Yih Zung)。
骆意 (Loh Yien)，已被捕
骆振 (Loh Tsung)。
王子明 (Wong Ts Ming)，已被捕。
相强伟 (Shang Chiang Wei)。
过宗鼎 (Koh Tsung Ting)，以及
本人。
去年三月或四月间，我与另外三人由过宗鼎带领，前往法租界克雷赛尔路市场，在克雷赛尔路的湖南餐馆谋杀了一名姓王 (Wong) 的人。然而，我并未实际参与枪击王某，因为当时我

page_data.en:
unarmed, but only stood on the roadway, acting as a look-out.
Loh Tsung Ting opened fire on Wong and killed the latter on
the spot. This crime was perpetrated by Wong Ts Ming,
Loh Yien (arrested), Chang Chi-ng Wei, Loh Tsung Ting
(not yet in police custody), and myself.
Unexpectedly Loh Tsung Ting surrendered to the
Japanese, which, I think, resulted in the arrest of us.
In July or August of last year I also participated
in the murder of Tung Shao Yi (唐紹儀), in which case I
again acted as a look-out (unarmed) on Route Ferguson.
I went to the scene of this crime with Loh Yien,
Wong Ts Ming, Chang Chi-ng Wei, and several unknown persons.
I did not see who actually entered the premises
and killed Tung.
After completion of the above assassination I
received from a female named Siau Chi (羅小姐), $100.00
reward. In addition I received $10.00 from the same female
as reward for the murder of Wong in Hunan Restaurant.
The above is my true statement.

Signed:
page_data.zh:
未携带武器，只是站在马路上放风。
骆宗亭 (Loh Tsung Ting) 向王某开枪并当场将其击毙。此罪行由王子明、骆意（已被捕）、张继伟 (Chang Chi-ng Wei)、骆宗亭（尚未被警方拘留）以及本人实施。
不料骆宗亭向日本人自首，我认为这导致了我们被捕。
去年七月或八月间，我还参与了唐绍仪 (Tung Shao Yi) 的谋杀案，在该案中我再次在费格生路担任放风任务（未携带武器）。
我是与骆意、王子明、张继伟及几名身份不明者一同前往犯罪现场的。
我没有看到是谁实际进入屋内杀害了唐绍仪。
在完成上述暗杀行动后，我从一名名为罗小姐 (Siau Chi) 的女子那里收到了100.00美元的酬金。此外，我还从同一女子那里收到了10.00美元，作为在湖南餐馆谋杀王某的酬金。
以上是我的真实供词。

签名：

page_data.en:
LOH YIEN (駱意), age 49, residing at
No. 142 Route Vallon,
Zaushing xx D.S.I. Lieu Kyung Ching
( attached to H.C.S.-C.l. )
Hongkew 6-8-39 translated Tsaung Zung Pau

On the morning of 12-7-39 I was arrested and taken
to Lokawei Police Station for enquiries. On 13-7-39 I was
removed to Headquarters Crime Branch (C. l.), S.M.P., from
where I was handed over to the custody of the Japanese
Consulate on the following day.

On being interrogated by the Japanese Consular
Police, I admitted that I joined an assassination corps
through the introduction of my cousin named Loh Tsung (駱振).
Revealing the leader of this corps as one named Zau Lih Tsing
(曹立俊), I described the part which I had taken in the
assassination of Tang Shao Yi (唐紹儀) on Route Ferguson,
F. C., between July and August 1938, as follows :-

I was instructed by Zau Lih Tsing to participate
in this murder. The party accompanying me composed of
Loh Tsung, Siang Jang Wei (相淺偉), Wong Ts Ming (王子明),
Bien Shing San (边兴山), Lieu Ping Hoong (刘炳恒) and
Zau Lih Tsing himself. Zau and others entered the house
occupied by Tang Shao Yi, and chopped him to death with an axe,
whilst I maintained a watch on the roadway, posing as a
carpenter. I subsequently received a reward of $100.00.

I further related the assassination of one named
Wong at a Hunan Restaurant, Rue Kraetser Market, F.C., between
March and April 1938, in which I also took part. The other
persons who participated in this murder were Zau Lih Tsing,
Koo Tsung Ting (过正鼎), Wong Ts Ming, Bien Shing San, and
Siang Jang Wei. Koo Tsung Ting was the one who actually
entered the restaurant and shot the victim to death with a
page_data.zh:
骆意 (LOH YIEN)，49岁，居住于
华隆路142号，
浙江 xx 副督察员刘景清 (D.S.I. Lieu Kyung Ching)
(附属于重案组-C.l.)
虹口 1939年8月6日翻译 庄宗宝 (Tsaung Zung Pau)

1939年7月12日上午，我被捕并被带往老闸捕房接受讯问。1939年7月13日，我被移送至工部局警务处总部重案组 (C. l.)，次日从那里被移交给日本领事馆拘留。

在接受日本领事警察讯问时，我承认经我的表亲骆振 (Loh Tsung) 介绍加入了一个暗杀团。我揭露该团首领名为曹立俊 (Zau Lih Tsing)，并描述了我在1938年7月至8月间于法租界费格生路参与刺杀唐绍仪 (Tang Shao Yi) 的情况如下：

我受曹立俊指示参与此次谋杀。随我同行的成员包括骆振、相浅伟 (Siang Jang Wei)、王子明 (Wong Ts Ming)、边兴山 (Bien Shing San)、刘炳恒 (Lieu Ping Hoong) 以及曹立俊本人。曹等人进入唐绍仪居住的寓所，用斧头将其砍死，而我则伪装成木匠在马路上放风。事后我收到了100.00美元的酬金。

我还供述了1938年3月至4月间在法租界克雷赛尔路市场一家湖南餐馆谋杀一名姓王者的案件，我也参与了此案。其他参与谋杀的人员有曹立俊、过正鼎 (Koo Tsung Ting)、王子明、边兴山和相浅伟。过正鼎是实际进入餐馆并用

page_data.en:
- 2 -
pistol. On this occasion I remained outside again as a
look-out.
Our arrest was brought about at the instigation of
Koo Tsung Ting, who had surrendered to the Japanese, as I have
seen him whilst being detained at the Japanese Consulate.
As regards to the various cases of assassination
which I confessed to the Japanese Consulate, I was only
concerned in two of them as aforementioned, the remainder
being falsely admitted under pressure of their punishment.

Sgd., crossmarked & thumbprinted by: LOH YEN.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
手枪将受害者射杀的人。在此事件中，我再次在外面放风。
我们的被捕是由过正鼎投奔日本人所促成的，因为我在被拘留于日本领事馆期间见到了他。
关于我向日本领事馆供认的各起暗杀案件，我仅如前所述参与了两起，其余均是在其刑罚压力下虚假承认的。

签名、画押并按指印：骆意 (LOH YEN)。

page_data.en:
LIU CHING HO (刘清豪)
Mukiang // P.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung.
Hongkew Stn. 5.8.39 translated (C.M.H. J.O.L)
Hsu U. F.
12

My name is Lieu Ching Ho, aged 32, native of Mukiang,
married clerk, employed at the Dong Yih (同益) Foreign Exchange
Hong, No. 60 Ching Yue Li, Peking Road and residing at No.6
Shanghai Terrace, Route Vallon, F.C.

At 4 a.m. on the 12.7.39 I was arrested and taken
to French Police Station where a statement was taken from
me by French Police detectives.

At 4 p.m. 13.7.39 I was removed from French Police
Station to the Municipal Police Headquarters, whence I was
subsequently handed over to Japanese Consular Police, who,
on my arrival at their offices, took down my particulars.

At 3 p.m. 19.7.39 a Japanese Consular Police Officer,
after taking down my name etc., asked me through the inter-
pretation of a Chinese interpreter, who was the man living
in the downstairs room of my house. In reply I told them
that I only knew the man as one named Wong. I was then taken
back to cells.

At 11 a.m. 27.7.39 I was once more removed from
cells and escorted in a motor car to the Police Department
of the Japanese Consulate, where I was questioned by a
Japanese Officer who finally said that I was not the man
and was, therefore, sent back to cells again.

At 5 p.m. on the 5.8.39 I was taken from the Japanese
Police Dept. cells and conveyed to Hongkew Station where I
have since been lodging.

Up to date I have made no confession to any one,
nor signed a statement whilst in the custody of the Japanese.
page_data.zh:
刘清豪 (LIU CHING HO)
无锡 // 虹口捕房巡官宋秉忠 (P.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung)。
1939年8月5日翻译 (C.M.H. J.O.L)
徐U. F.
12

本人名为刘清豪，现年32岁，籍贯无锡，已婚，职员，受雇于北京路庆余里60号的同益 (Dong Yih) 外汇庄，居住于法租界华隆路6号上海别墅 (Shanghai Terrace)。

1939年7月12日凌晨4时，我被捕并被带往法国捕房，法国警探对我进行了录供。

1939年7月13日下午4时，我从法国捕房被移送至工部局警务处总部，随后被移交给日本领事警察，他们在我到达其办公处后记录了我的个人资料。

1939年7月19日下午3时，一名日本领事警官在记录了我的姓名等信息后，通过一名中文翻译问我，住在我家楼下房间的人是谁。我回答说我只知道那人姓王。随后我被带回牢房。

1939年7月27日上午11时，我再次从牢房被提出，乘汽车被护送至日本领事馆警务部，一名日本官员对我进行了讯问，最后说我不是他们要找的人，因此我又被送回牢房。

1939年8月5日下午5时，我从日本警务部牢房被提出，并被送往虹口捕房，此后一直羁押于此。

截至目前，我在日本拘留期间未向任何人认罪，也未签署任何供词。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

I was born and brought up in Kiukiang. I attended
the St. John's Middle School in Kiukiang and transferred
to study in the Kwang Hwa Middle School (also in Kiukiang)
when I was 19 years of age.

At the age of 20 I came to Shanghai and through
the recommendation of my brother-in-law, one named Siao
Yue Ling (蕭麟), sub-manager of the King Yih (兴業)
Bank, I procured a job in a foreign exchange shop, operated
by Lung Yoong Ching (許永吉), and located on Kiukiang Road.

I retained the above employment until 13.8.37 when
Sino-Japanese hostilities broke out in Shanghai and I
was thrown out of job.

Some time in June 1939 I secured another employment
in the Dong Yih Foreign Exchange Hong, where I have been
working till present.

I have never been employed in Military or Police
organisations.

I am a law-abiding citizen in the Settlement and
have committed no crime.

我出生并成长于九江。我就读于九江圣约翰中学，19岁时转学至九江的光华中学 (Kwang Hwa Middle School)。

20岁时我来到上海，通过我的姐夫萧麟 (Siao Yue Ling)（兴业银行副经理）的介绍，我在许永吉 (Lung Yoong Ching) 经营的一家位于九江路的外汇店找到了一份工作。

我一直从事上述工作，直到1937年8月13日上海中日战事爆发，我因此失业。

1939年6月的某个时候，我在同益外汇庄找到了另一份工作，并一直工作至今。

我从未在军队或警察机构任职。

我是租界内的守法公民，未曾犯罪。

我不认识应渭水 (Ying Wei S) 及其他同时被捕的人。

以上是我的真实供词。

Route Vallon, French Concession.
    On 13th. July, 1939, I was arrested and detained
at the Lokawei Station, French police for investigation.
On 13th. July, 1939, I was conveyed to the Police Headquarters
(G.I), S.M.Police, and on the 17th. inst. I was taken to the
Japanese consular police.

I had been employed by any military or police organizations.

Yien ( 駱憲 ). I told them that I had studied in boyhood
and later I became an apprentice. I did not know Ying and
Loh. They then questioned me if I have another name besides
Lan Yuen Sung. I replied in the negative. On the 3rd.
August, 1939, I was brought to the Hongkew Police Station
and detained there.
    This is a true statement.

and conveyed to the Police Headquarters, C.l, S.M.Police.

C.l, Crime Branch Headquarters for the purpose of taking
a statement. On 20th. July, I was again conveyed to the
Japanese Consular Police and on the 3rd. August, I was
removed to the Hongkew Police Station Cells.

TRANSLATION

Police Department,
Japanese Consular Police.

July 26, 1939.

Major K.M. Bourne,
Commissioner of Police,
S.M.P./S.M.C.

Sir,

I have the pleasure to inform you in regard to
the Shanghai Anti-Japanese Special Service Corps which
had been under enquiries with the co-operation of the
Municipal Police in the International Settlement and
French Concession. It is entirely evident that all
the properties in the houses of Ying Wei Sz, No.2 Park
Road, International Settlement and of Ling Chu Yung, No.
17 Hah Chuen Foung off Route Tenant de la Tour, French
Concession were purchased with the fund issued from the
Chungking Government to the anti-Japanese Special Service
Corps in this city for the purpose of furthering anti-
Japanese terrorism, and some of them were even proved to
be the direct or indirect material for furthering anti-
Japanese terrorism.

It is quite obvious thorough the confession of Lieu
Ping Hung (the Chauffeur employed by Ling) who was arrested in
the French Concession on the 12th. inst., that the motor car
(Stream-lined, new form, Plymouth, Blue-dark coloured) kept
in the garage of Eastern Motor-cars Co., Rue Amiral Bayle,
French Concession, being owned by the general leader of the
Anti-Japanese Special Service Corps. The motor car had been
used in carrying out various anti-Japanese terroristic
activities.

Therefore I should be greatly obliged if you would
kindly consider about the matter re handing over of the
properties in the abovementioned houses together with the
motor car to our authorities.

I am, Sir,
Yours faithfully,
Sealed: Nobuya Saka
Director.
page_data.zh:
译文

警察局，
日本领事馆警察。

1939年7月26日。

K.M. Bourne 少校，
警务处处长，
上海公共租界工部局/上海公共租界工部局董事会。

先生：

兹荣幸告知阁下关于上海抗日特别服务队一事，该队此前在国际公共租界及法租界巡捕房的配合下接受了调查。现有确凿证据表明，位于国际公共租界公园路2号应渭水（Ying Wei Sz）寓所内，以及位于法租界陶尔斐司路（Route Tenant de la Tour）哈春坊（Hah Chuen Foung）17号凌楚永（Ling Chu Yung）寓所内的所有财产，均系使用重庆政府拨发给本市抗日特别服务队用于推进抗日恐怖活动的资金购买，其中部分物品甚至被证实为直接或间接用于推进抗日恐怖活动的物资。

通过本月12日在法租界被捕的凌氏司机刘平洪（Lieu Ping Hung，音译）的供词，情况已十分清楚：停放在法租界贝勒路（Rue Amiral Bayle）东方汽车公司车库内的一辆汽车（流线型、新款、普利茅斯牌、深蓝色），其所有者即为抗日特别服务队的总头目。该汽车曾被用于实施各种抗日恐怖活动。

因此，如蒙阁下考虑将上述寓所内的财产连同该汽车一并移交给我方当局，本人将不胜感激。

此致，
敬礼
盖章：坂信哉（Nobuya Saka）
主任。

3rd.- House 6, Shanghai Terrace. Route Vallon,

The necessary assistance having been obtained
from the French Police, the party first visited the
Tung Faung (東方) Garage, not Dah Tung (大東),
located at 439 to 443 Route Amiral Bayle, where
enquiries regarding a chauffeur named Ah Kai proved
fruitless. Whilst making these enquiries were in
progress Inspt. Mayhate of the Japanese Consular
Police, observed a large "Plymouth" Limousine standing
in this garage without licence plates and immediately
laid claim to same stating that it was the property
of Ling(林). As he could produce no evidence to
substantiate this, his request to remove the car
was refused by D.S. Moren of the French Police,
who, however, warned the garage people not to remove
same pending further enquiries, etc.

The party next proceeded to Avenue Joffre,
and after experiencing some difficulty eventually
succeeded in locating the Joffre Apartments, Apt.
"K", however, on enquiries being made therein it
was ascertained that the present occupant named
Vai Sun Ching (樊文卿) age 48, native of Hunan,
M/Merchant, had bought this apartment over from one
page_data.zh:
19/2.

第三 - 凡尔登路（Route Vallon）上海别墅6号，此前曾访问并实施逮捕，此次仅为搜查。

在获得法国警察的必要协助后，一行人首先访问了位于贝勒路439至443号的东方（Tung Faung）车行，而非大东（Dah Tung）车行，在那里关于一名名叫阿凯（Ah Kai）的司机的查询毫无结果。在进行这些查询期间，日本领事馆警察的 Mayhate 督察观察到该车库内停着一辆没有牌照的大型“普利茅斯”豪华轿车，并立即声称该车为林（Ling）所有。由于他无法提供证据证实这一点，法国警察的 Moren 警佐（D.S. Moren）拒绝了他移除该车的请求，但警告车行人员在进一步调查等期间不得移动该车。

随后，一行人前往霞飞路，经过一番周折，最终找到了霞飞公寓“K”座。然而，经查询得知，现住户樊文卿（Vai Sun Ching），48岁，湖南籍，男/商人，约一个月前以1,100.00美元的价格从一名叫林（Ling）的人手中买下了这套公寓。

page_data.en:
19 /3.

named Ling (林) about one month ago for the
sum of $1,100.00. In substantiation of this fact
he produced a newspaper cutting from the Sing Yung
Pau (新涌報) showing where Ling had advertised the
apartment for sale.

A search of a photograph album revealed
nothing of an incriminating nature, and the party
withdrew without making any arrests or seizures.

Finally the party visited House 6, Shanghai
Terrace, where one named Lieu Ching Ho (劉清何) and
three others were arrested on July 12th 1939, (See
Diary No. 2 page 5), but although these premises
were searched from top to bottom nothing of an
incriminating was found.

The party first returned to French Police
Headquarters and then to Crime Branch Headquarters
arriving at the latter place at 7.45 a.m. 21st July
1939.

John Coghlan
D. S. I.
page_data.zh:
19 /3.

为了证实这一事实，他出示了一份《新涌报》（Sing Yung Pau）的剪报，显示林曾刊登广告出售该公寓。

对相册的搜查未发现任何具有指控性质的内容，一行人未实施任何逮捕或扣押便撤离了。

最后，一行人访问了上海别墅6号，1939年7月12日，一名叫刘清何（Lieu Ching Ho）的人和其他三人在此被捕（见日记第2卷第5页），尽管对该处所进行了彻底搜查，但未发现任何具有指控性质的物品。

一行人先返回法国警察总部，然后返回刑事侦缉处总部，于1939年7月21日上午7时45分抵达后者。

John Coghlan
高级警佐（D. S. I.）

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

At 4 a/m. 16-7-39, in compliance with request
made by Japanese Consular Police, as contained in Diary
No. 11, the undersigned, D.S. Sugimoto, D.S. Yamahara,
A/D.S.I. Zia Vai Faung and C.D.S. 115, accompanied by
D.S.'s Noda and Yamaguchi of the Japanese Consular
Police, proceeded to French Police Headquarters and
after having obtained the necessary assistance, visited
the Great Shanghai (大滬) Hotel, 345 Avenue Edward
VII, French Concession, where in room 203 it was hoped
to arrest one named Hou Tien Foong (何天風) alias Hou
Ying Kyi (何行健), an accomplice of Ying Wei S (應渭水).
Inquiries at the room in question revealed
same to have been engaged since the 13-7-39 by one named
Yang Sz Soong (楊如松), age 45, native of Shanghai,
M/Shop-master, residing at 35 Saung Yuen Ka (桑園街),
Small South Gate, Nantao.
This man was questioned, also his room was
searched, but there being nothing of an incriminating
nature against him, he was not taken into custody.
Further enquiries at the reception desk
revealed that up until the 12-7-39 this room had been
engaged by one named Loh Yoong Hyorn (陸永源), age 39,
native of Shanghai, whom the Japanese authorities

关于向日本领事馆警务处提供协助的后续报告

1939年7月16日凌晨4时，应日本领事馆警务处在日记第11号中的请求，署名者、杉本警司（D.S. Sugimoto）、山原警司（D.S. Yamahara）、助理警司谢维方（A/D.S.I. Zia Vai Faung）和刑事侦缉警佐（C.D.S.）115号，在日本领事馆警务处的野田警司（D.S. Noda）和山口警司（D.S. Yamaguchi）陪同下，前往法国警务处总部，在获得必要协助后，前往法租界爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）345号大滬酒店（Great Shanghai Hotel），希望在203房间逮捕一名叫何天風（Hou Tien Foong），又名何行健（Hou Ying Kyi）的人，此人是應渭水（Ying Wei S）的同伙。
对该房间的查询显示，该房间自1939年7月13日起由一名叫楊如松（Yang Sz Soong）的人租用，45岁，上海人，职业为店主，居住在南市小南门桑园街35号。
对此人进行了讯问，并搜查了他的房间，但因未发现任何对他不利的罪证，故未将其拘留。
在前台的进一步查询显示，直到1939年7月12日，该房间一直由一名叫陸永源（Loh Yoong Hyorn）的人租用，39岁，上海人，日本当局

Documents seized in Lane 317, House 17 Route Frelupt.
(Misc. 105/39)

1. Three secret radiogram code books in Chinese language.

2. Statement of accounts for February, consisting of (a) ordinary incomes, (b) ordinary expenses, (c) special incomes and (d) special expenses.

3. One record book containing a list of names of the personnel in April, communication agents, group members and section members, together with their rate of pay, date engaged, and district covered by them.

4. Statement of accounts for January.

5. Reports and letters consisting of the following :-
(a) A note addressed to one Ling (凌 ) by Yeu Ho-tsing (許子同者); in which 4 pistols and 14 rounds of ammunition are mentioned.
(b) A report made by Yeu Ho-tsing relating to the murder of Chen Loh (陳絡 ) and the persons participating in the assassination.
(c) Five personal letters and one doctor's chit.

6. Five private letters.

7. A letter from one Sung (声 ) to one Ying (英 ; expressing his intention to leave for Nanking for the purpose of seeking employment.

8. A letter addressed to Ih ng (一声) relating to a certain suit case and the money question.

9. A letter addressed to Wei Ying (慧英 ) by Li Sih (莉雪) encouraging Wei Ying's view in organizing a rear hospital, which the writer states is good for national salvation.

10. A letter addressed to Wei Ying by Han Fung and Poh Chuan (志芬及祐培), containing a recollection on Wei Ying's departure and endorsing her views in organizing a rear hospital.

11. A report from Li Chun (理君) to Han Ching (漢清) requesting an increase in living allowance of eleven section members namely Siang Jung-Wei (相強偉), Hoo Tseng Keng (胡正根), Wong Chi-mai (王其才), Pien Ta-lih (邊之禮), Koo Hang-sung (顧永臣), Xi Hung-shan (徐鴻善), Liu Ping-yung (劉炳榮), Ma Su-huang (馬素黃), Loh Tseng (駱增), Li Hung (李洪 ) and Wu Ping (吳平 ). The report also mentions the distribution of rewards granted in connection with the assassination of Li Zoeng-ying (李宗英 ) and another named Tang (唐 ).

12. A manuscript rough budget made by Ling To Kiang (凌道江) relating to expenses of a group of members.

13. A report bearing on enlisting of new members. Attached to the report are eleven forms containing brief particulars of the new members enlisted.

14. A report made by Ling Tien Hwei (凌天惠) relating to proposed assassination of Wa Sing-wu (華星武) and Chen Yu-tsing (陳玉清), who are accused of being traitors.

15. A report made by Ling Tien Hwei bearing on proposed assassination of Chen Yu-tsing.

(b) 許子同者（Yeu Ho-tsing）关于谋杀陳絡（Chen Loh）及参与暗杀人员的报告。

who is part owner and manager of the concern. No
search of the premises was made.
Dr. Feng was identified by the informer and
the Consular Police also produced a small photograph
of him in support their statement that he was the
right person.

关于日本领事警察要求在租界内进行搜查一事，1939年7月15日上午10时05分，由警佐罗斯辛顿（Rossington）、警佐罗兹（Rhodes）、警佐杉本（Sugimoto）、副警佐山原（Yamahara）、副警佐清水（Shimidzu）、代理副督察谢伟方（Zia Wei Fong）、华捕172号、华捕巡长184号和206号组成的工部局警务处小队，向桥爪先生（Hashidzume）及一队领事警察提供了必要协助，并在一名线人的带领下，前往湖北路514号《东方日报》社办公室，试图逮捕一名名为杜曼松（Doo Man Sung）的男子。然而，屋内居住者均不认识此人，且线人显然无法指认他。未实施逮捕或搜查。
该队随后于上午10时30分左右前往虞洽卿路39号“佛慈”中药店，并在店内逮捕一人：-
冯明政先生，36岁，杭州人，职业医生，
系该商号的合伙人之一兼经理。未对该场所进行搜查。
线人指认了冯医生，领事警察还出示了他的一张小照片，以佐证他们所言确系此人。

page_data.en:
9/2.

According to the Consular Police the arrested
man, and the person Doo Man Sung (not arrested)
and one other named Doo Sung Soo who is also employed
at the Foh S Medicine Shop, but absent at the time
of the raid, were implicated as being members of an
Anti-Japanese Assassination Group, by one Ying Wei
S (色 滑 少) who was arrested 12.7.39 at 291 Park
Road and handed over on loan to them, vide Diary 2
Page 2.

Enquiries regarding Doo Sung Soo ascertained
that he left the medicine Shop early this a.m. for
an unknown destination.

Since the Consular Police believed that he
may possibly return, they requested that a watch be
maintained until 1 p.m. 15.7.39. Japanese and Chinese
members of the S.M.P. were left on the premises, but
since the wanted man failed to return they were with-
drawn at the time stated.

The following property was taken possession
of from the person of Dr. Fang Ming Tseng.

One leather wallet.
One note book.
One curfew pass.
4 visiting cards.
One paper.
page_data.zh:
9/2.

据领事警察称，被捕男子以及杜曼松（未被捕）和另一名同样受雇于佛慈药店但在搜查时外出的杜松寿（Doo Sung Soo），均被一名英伟斯（Ying Wei S，音译：色滑少）牵连为反日暗杀团成员，该英伟斯于1939年7月12日在派克路291号被捕并被借移交给他们，详见日记第2卷第2页。

经查询杜松寿的情况，获悉他于今日清晨离开药店，去向不明。

由于领事警察认为他可能会回来，故要求监视至1939年7月15日下午1时。工部局警务处的日籍和华籍警员留守在该处，但因通缉犯未返回，他们在指定时间撤离。

一个皮夹。

This was communicated to Supt. Grubb and

关于日本领事警察在此案中请求进一步协助一事（参见日记第6号），下述人员：副督察科诺瓦洛夫（Konovaloff）、警佐杉本（Sugimoto）、副警佐山原（Yamahara）、副督察吴承浩（Wo Chen Ho）和副督察黄宗武（Wong Zung Wo），在日本领事警察副督察马畑（Mayehata）、警佐日宫（Hino-miya）及翻译山本（Yamamoto）的陪同下，前往法租界警察局卢家湾分局，在获得必要协助后，前往法租界普鲁帕特路（Route Prelupt）316弄17号，据称一名姓林（Ling）的人居住于此，且可查获大量枪支。

到达该地址并进入后，在楼下前间遇到一名名为陈秀珍（Tung Siau Tsung，原文拼音与中文名不符，依中文名译）的中国女性，28岁，单身女性，广东籍。经询问，她否认有任何名为林的人居住于此，称该房屋的租户姓王，且几天前已下乡。

在审问该女子期间，日本领事警察翻译山本开始搜查房屋的楼下部分，并在片刻之后提请下述人员注意他所称的

the false roof of a lavatory, situated at the rear
of the premises. After some difficulty this was forced
open revealing the following arms, ammunition, documents
etc., as per attached list.

Having removed these arms etc. the Japanese Consular
Police next requested permission to search the remainder
of the premises and on this being agreed too by the
French Police representative, a further search was made
resulting in a further seizure of documents, photographs
etc.

The search having been completed, the seizures,
along with the female found on the premises were taken
to Lokawei Station, where they are now being detained
pending a decision being made regarding the handing
over of same, which has been promised by 11 a.m. this
inst.

移除这些武器等物品后，日本领事警察随即请求允许搜查房屋的其余部分，在得到法国警察代表同意后，进行了进一步搜查，结果又查获了文件、照片等物品。

FRENCH POLICE DENY JAPANESE AID IN RAIDS

"There has never yet been an instance in
which we co-operated with the Japanese Army in
conducting searches or raids in the French Concession,"
declared a spokesman of the French Police yesterday
in denying a report published yesterday afternoon.

The report in question alleged that French
Police co-operated with some 20 Japanese, believed to
be members of the Japanese Army's Special Service
Section, in conducting two raids at 4 a.m. yesterday
in quest of guerillas and other anti-Japanese elements.

The report, according to the spokesman, was
probably erroneously derived from a series of raids in
Frenchtown at that hour, in which members of the
Shanghai Municipal Police, including Japanese detectives,
co-operated with the Frenchtown force.

The raids were not made in quest of guerillas
or other anti-Japanese elements, he said, but of armed robber
and loafers. Several arrests were made, he confirmed,
but the number of suspects taken into custody was not
divulged. Further arrests were expected, he explained.

〔此处转录不清〕

8292/8

法国警察否认在突击搜查中协助日本人

“我们从未有过在法租界进行搜查或突击行动时与日本军队合作的先例，”法国警察发言人在昨天下午否认一篇报道时声明。

该报道声称，法国警察与约20名日本人合作，这些人被认为是日本陆军特务机关成员，于昨天凌晨4时进行了两次突击搜查，旨在寻找游击队和其他反日分子。

发言人称，该报道可能是错误地源自当时在法华界（Frenchtown）进行的一系列突击搜查，在这些行动中，包括日本侦探在内的工部局警务处成员与法华界警力进行了合作。

他说，这些突击搜查并非为了寻找游击队或其他反日分子，而是为了寻找武装抢劫犯和游手好闲者。他证实有几人被捕，但未透露被拘留嫌疑人的数量。他解释说，预计会有更多逮捕行动。

〔此处转录不清〕

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
"1 20 1939
POLICE STAGE SUDDEN RAID IN FRENCHTOWN

Search for guerillas carried out
by detectives

Acting on the request of Japanese military
authorities, detectives of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, co-operating with the French Police, raided
a Chinese residence on Lane 440 Route Tenant de la
Tour about 7 p.m. yesterday.

Reports circulated shortly after the raid
were to the effect that three Chinese, suspected of being
connected with guerilla bands in this area, were taken
into custody and removed from the Concession into the
International Settlement.

This report was subsequently denied by
French Police quarters who maintained that while
the raid had been made, it produced no results in the
way of capturing Chinese guerillas.

French Police quarters also denied that any
Japanese military men had participated in the raid.
They pointed out that some Japanese may have been
in the raiding party, but if so, they were members of
the Shanghai Municipal Police.

（批：C 29/1 16/7 277）

"1939年1月20日
警察在法华界发动突然突击搜查

侦探执行搜寻游击队任务

应日本军方当局的要求，工部局警务处的侦探与法国警察合作，于昨晚约7时突袭了唐乃安路（Route Tenant de la Tour）440弄的一处中国住宅。

突击搜查后不久流传的报告称，三名涉嫌与该地区游击队有联系的中国人被拘留，并从租界转移至公共租界。

此报告随后被法国警察方面否认，他们坚持认为，虽然进行了突击搜查，但在抓捕中国游击队方面没有取得任何成果。

法国警察方面还否认有任何日本军人参与此次突击搜查。他们指出，突击小队中可能有一些日本人，但如果是这样，他们是工部局警务处的成员。

JUL 15 1939
POLICE STAGE MANY RAIDS IN GUERILLA HUNT
Crime Branch Acts On Japanese Requests; No Arrest Made

Acting on requests and informa-
tion furnished by the Japanese
military authorities, detectives of
Crime Branch headquarters, S.M.P.,
went into action in a big way late
yesterday afternoon and carried
out a series of raids designed to
bring about the arrest of alleged
guerilla leaders said to have been
hiding out in various parts of the
Settlement.
The raiding parties left head-
quarters about 5 p.m. and remain-
ed on the job for more than two
hours. All places on the list pro-
vided by the Japanese authorities
were visited by the detectives but,
according to information available
last night, the results were
negative.
No guerillas nor guerilla suspects
were nabbed during the course of
eight raids staged between 5 p.m.
and 7 p.m. It is understood that
other raids were to be carried out
before dawn but no confirmation of
this report was available last night.
Police officials were uncom-
municative concerning the raids
but it was learned from authentic
sources that not a single person,
answering the descriptions provid-
ed the Settlement authorities, could
be found in the establishments
visited.

警察在搜捕游击队行动中发动多次突击搜查
罪案科应日本方面要求行动；无人被捕

根据日本军方当局提供的请求和信息，工部局警务处总部罪案科的侦探于昨天下午晚些时候大规模采取行动，进行了一系列突击搜查，旨在逮捕据称隐藏在租界各处的所谓游击队领导人。
突击小队于下午5时左右离开总部，行动持续了两个多小时。侦探走访了日本当局提供的名单上的所有地点，但根据昨晚获得的信息，结果是否定的。
在下午5时至7时之间进行的八次突击搜查中，没有抓获任何游击队员或游击队嫌疑人。据悉，黎明前还将进行其他突击搜查，但昨晚无法确认此报告。
警方官员对突击搜查一事守口如瓶，但从可靠消息源获悉，在被访问的场所中，找不到任何符合提供给租界当局描述的人。

Assistance to Japanese Military Police

Sir,
At 6.30p.m. on the 15/7/39 Sgt. Major Ishida of
the Special Branch Japanese Military Police Headquarters,
Bridge House, North Szechuan Road, came to the station
and requested assistance to arrest a male Japanese named
K. Hanano, who had whilst being employed on the civilian
staff of the Japanese Military and attached to the
Katayama detachment, misappropriated military stores and
absconded at the end of May, 1939. They had every reason
to believe that this man was boarding at Apt. 315 No.1377
Avenue Road.

Necessary assistance was rendered by the
undersigned and D.S. Nagamune and the wanted Japanese
was located at the above address which is the Avenue Apts.
and placed under arrest. He had been residing at this
address for about 6 weeks, having rented a room from the
occupier, a Mr. Coon, Rumnian at a rental of $300.00
per month who had advertised for a tenant in the North
China Daily News.

He was handed over to Sgt. Major Ishida after
Mr. Yorke, D.C. "B" and D.I. Tabrum, A./D.D.O. "B" had
been informed of the facts pertaining to his arrest.

7

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Reference Shan-ken-ko No. 972, and Nantung-
ken-ko No. 311, the suspect "Zung Ts Ming (陳志敏)"
has been further interrogated regarding the allega-
tions contained in the latter mentioned communica-
tion.

He stoutly maintains that at no time has
he ever been connected with any guerrilla units, or
associated with any Anti-Japanese activities.

He claims that he has never heard of the
supposed relative named Zung Chih Foo (陳志福),
and that none of his known relatives are connected
with guerrillas.

Regarding the information supplied by the
Japanese to the effect that he left New Hong Kong
(牛洪港), Haimen with several thousand dollars,
following being defeated towards the end of June
1938, according to a bank book seized from the person
of the suspect, it shows that he deposited $3000.00
in the Commercial Bank of China on April 5th, 1939.

This money he avers represented the Savings
of his brother Zung Ts Tsoong himself.

续：协助日本宪兵队。

参照申宪告第972号和南宪告第311号，就后者通信中所含指控，对嫌疑人“陈志敏（Zung Ts Ming）”进行了进一步讯问。

他坚决声称，他从未与任何游击队单位有过联系，也从未参与任何反日活动。

他声称从未听说过名为陈志福（Zung Chih Foo）的所谓亲戚，且他所知的亲属中无人参与游击队活动。

关于日方提供的信息，称其在1938年6月底战败后携带数千美元离开海门牛洪港（New Hong Kong），根据从嫌疑人身上搜出的存折显示，他于1939年4月5日在中国商业银行存款3000.00美元。

他声称这笔钱代表其兄弟钟茨松（Zung Ts Tsoong）本人的积蓄。

On May 2 and 6th respectively he withdrew
a total of $500.00 from this account and some was
given to his brother who returned to his work in

On July 18th 1939 he again drew $500.00

Zai Cheng Lumber Yard F.C.

As reported in Diary 5 the statement of

and found to be more or less true.

No evidence has been found by the Police

6.

FURTHER TO : ASSISTANCE TO THE JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

At 10.30 a.m. August 25,1939 a note (Shankenko No.972) appended with Nantung-Ken-Ko No.311 was received at C.l.,Crime Branch Headquarters, from Sergeant Kurouji of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters.

It is to be recalled that the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters had referred this case to the Nantung Gendarmerie for the purpose of obtaining concrete information regarding Zung Ts Ming (陳志敏 ), and the Nantung-Ken-Ko No.311 was received from the Nantung Gendarmerie in response to their reference.

The note Shankenko No.972 requests the immediate handing over of Zung Ts Ming on the basis of the newly submitted evidence which was supplied by the Nantung-Ken-Ko No.311.

Translations of Shankenko No.972 and Nantung-Ken-Ko No.311 are attached herewith.

1939年8月25日上午10时30分，刑事科总部收到来自日本宪兵队总部黑路次（Kurouji）警曹的一份便函（申宪告第972号），附有南宪告第311号。

需回顾的是，日本宪兵队总部将此案转交南通宪兵队，目的是获取关于陈志敏（Zung Ts Ming）的具体信息，而南宪告第311号是南通宪兵队对此查询的回复。

申宪告第972号便函要求基于南宪告第311号提供的新证据，立即移交陈志敏。
