TRANSLATION.

Ref. Shan-ken-Ko No.972.

Shanghai Detachment,
Japanese Gendarmerie.
August 24, 1939.

Major K.N.Bourne,
Commissioner of Police,
S.M.P./I.M.C.

Sir,

With reference to Tung Ts Ming (陳之敏), who
was arrested with assistance of your Police Force on July
21, 1939 and request for whose handing over was made by
us, the attached information to substantiate his being a
guerilla is submitted herewith.

This information was received in response to our
reference from the Japanese Gendarmerie stationed at Nan-
tung under the control of which comes the former address
of Tung Ts Ming.

In view of the newly submitted evidence, I have
the pleasure to request you that Tung Ts Ming be handed over
to us at your earliest convenience.

I am, Sir,
Yours faithfully,

Sealed : Col. K.Kanaya.
Officer-in-Command.

工部局警务处/工部局。

先生，

关于1939年7月21日在贵警队协助下逮捕的陈之敏（Tung Ts Ming），我方曾请求移交此人，现随函附上证明其为游击队员的信息。

此信息是我方查询后，由驻扎在南通的日本宪兵队回复提供的，陈之敏以前的住址属于该队管辖范围。

鉴于新提交的证据，我很荣幸请求您在方便时尽早将陈之敏移交给我方。

此致，

Sir,

With reference to Nanking—No 4001
Dated August 27, 1939, relating to one
Man (陳志敏), I beg to forward the following
report: —

TANG TS MING (陳志敏), aged about
30 years, attached to
the newly organized 1st
Brigade, 1st Route, 5th War Zone,

(1) Carrier.

The person referred to TANG TS MING (陳志敏),
is a relative of Zung Chih Foo (陳瑞福), Chief of the
1st Brigade of the newly organized 1st Route of the 5th
War Zone (formerly the 3rd Detachment, 1st Section, 4th
Guerilla District of the 24th Group), and in the
capacity of the senior officer of this Brigade, he
participated in the active operation in the Siymen
District.

On January 26, 1939 he together with Zung Chih
Foo tendered submission to the Japanese Forces, but
when Zung Chih Foo rebelled against the Japanese Forces
on April 12, 1939 Tang Ts Ming also waged fighting
joining in the rebels and upon these rebels being
inflicted crushing defeat by the forces under the
command of Lee Ming Yang (李明楊) towards the

先生：

关于南京—第 4001 号
1939年8月27日来函，涉及一名
男子（陳志敏），谨呈报如下
报告：—

唐志明（TANG TS MING，即陳志敏），年龄约
30岁，隶属于
新编第五战区第一路
第一旅，

(1) 信使。

上述唐志明（陳志敏）系新编第五战区第一路
第一旅旅长陈瑞福（Zung Chih Foo，音译）之亲属（该部前身为第二十四集团第四游击区第一支队第三大队），并作为该旅高级军官，
参与了在泗门（Siymen，音译）地区的作战行动。

1939年1月26日，他与陈瑞福一同向日军投降，但当陈瑞福于1939年4月12日反抗日军时，唐志明也参与战斗，加入叛军行列。至1939年6月初，这些叛军被李明楊（Lee Ming Yang）指挥的部队彻底击溃后，

page_data.en:
- 2 -

beginning of June 1939, Zung Ts Ming managed to
escape to the vicinity of New Hong Kong, Hainan
Island, with the remnants of rebels following
under him.
(2) Items for information.

The person referred to, Zung Ts Ming,
seems to have been endeavouring to re-organise his
troop by managing those remnants and also secretly
obtaining arms keepin in touch with his men in
Shanghai.

According to the latest information, he
left New Hong Kong (新香港) carrying with him
a sum of money amounting to several thousand dollars
for Shanghai with a view to purchasing firearms there.

I am, Sir,
Yours faithfully,

Sealed: Kitaro Hagiwara.
Officer-in-charge.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

唐志明（Zung Ts Ming，音译）得以率领残部逃往海南岛新香港（New Hong Kong）附近地区。
(2) 供参考事项。

上述人员唐志明（Zung Ts Ming，音译），
似乎正试图通过管理这些残部来重组其部队，并秘密获取武器，同时与他在上海的手下保持联系。

据最新情报，他携带数千美元离开新香港（新香港）前往上海，意图在那里购买枪支。

此致，
敬礼，

盖章：萩原喜太郎（Kitaro Hagiwara）。

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE

In compliance with the instructions of the
D. C. Crime, during the forenoon of August 9th, 1939,
with the assistance of the French Police, enquiries
were conducted at the "Zai Chong" (坊昌) Lumber Yard,
No. 363 Rue du Pere Froc, where it was ascertained
that on July 20th, 1939, Zung Ta Ming's carpenter
named Yuen Zung Lee (袁仁鴻) and one Yeong Hou Ming
(熊厚民) paid $400.00 as part payment for wood
ordered. An entry in the account book is recorded to
this effect.

On July 24th, 1939, all the wood ordered was
transported away by the carpenter and Yeong Hou Ming,
and a balance of $398.30 was paid.

The lumber yard accountant named Lee Peh
Kong (李伯康) identified Zung Ta Ming as one who came
with two or three others to bargain and choose wood
which they finally ordered.

This more or less confirms the statement made
by Zung Ta Ming in regards to his object in being in
Shanghai.

The Japanese Gendarmerie have again been
informed that they must produce evidence against Zung

关于协助日本宪兵队事宜

遵照刑事副主任的指示，1939年8月9日上午，
在法国警察的协助下，对位于拉神父路（Rue du Pere Froc）363号的“坊昌”（Zai Chong，音译）木行进行了调查，经查实，1939年7月20日，唐大明（Zung Ta Ming，音译）的木匠袁仁鴻（Yuen Zung Lee，音译）和熊厚民（Yeong Hou Ming，音译）支付了400.00美元，作为订购木材的部分货款。账簿中有相应记录。

1939年7月24日，所有订购的木材由该木匠和熊厚民运走，并支付了余款398.30美元。

木行会计李伯康（Lee Peh Kong，音译）指认唐大明是当时与两三人一同前来议价并挑选最终所订木材的人之一。

这在很大程度上证实了唐大明关于其在上海目的的陈述。

已再次通知日本宪兵队，他们必须提供针对唐

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Ts Ming before he can be handed over.
A verbal reply has been received from
them to the effect that they have no material evidence
against this suspect at present, but they allege
that he is related to some alleged guerilla leader
who they have not yet arrested.
They have requested that Zung Ts Ming be
further detained until such times they apprehend
the supposed relative, when they then hope to be in
a position to produce evidence against Zung.
There is no indication of when the arrest

志明（Zung Ts Ming，音译）的证据，方可将其移交。
已收到他们的口头答复，大意是目前他们没有针对这名嫌疑人的实质证据，但他们声称他与某位所谓的游击队领导人有关联，而此人他们尚未逮捕。
他们要求继续拘留唐志明（Zung Ts Ming，音译），直到他们抓获那位所谓的亲属为止，届时他们希望能提出针对唐的证据。

C.1, C.B.H.Q.
C.1 Mis.114/39
August 7, 39
4

Further to Assistance to Japanese
Gendarmerie.

In compliance with the instructions of the
D.C. Crime, the Japanese Gendarmerie have been asked
to produce any evidence they have regarding Zung Ts
Ming (陳志銘); but to date no reply has been
received from them.

Zung Ts Ming has been further interrogated
and he still maintains that he is not connected with
any guerilla unit, or interested in any anti-Japanese
activities.

A statement has been taken from him, in which
he relates how on July 11th. 1939 he arrived in Shanghai
from Haimen for the express purpose of buying lumber,
which he intended to transport to Haimen to be used
for coffin making.

On July 18th. he drew $500.00 from his
account in the Commercial Bank of China, $400.00 of
which he paid to the "Zai Chong" (瑞昌) Lumber Yard,
Rue du Pere Proc as part payment for wood bought.

He claims that the money was paid to the
lumber yard by his carpenter Yuen Zung Lee (袁仁禮)
who retained the receipt, and has now returned to the
country. Enquiries could be made at Zai Chong Lumber
Yard if necessary.
page_data.zh:
C.1, C.B.H.Q.
C.1 Mis.114/39
1939年8月7日
4

关于协助日本宪兵队事宜。

遵照刑事副主任的指示，已要求日本宪兵队提供他们所掌握的关于唐志明（Zung Ts Ming，即陳志銘）的任何证据；但截至目前，尚未收到他们的回复。

已对唐志明进行进一步讯问，他仍坚持声称自己与任何游击队单位无关，也不参与任何反日活动。

已取得他的供词，其中叙述了他如何于1939年7月11日从海门抵达上海，专门为了购买木材，打算将其运回海门用于制作棺材。

7月18日，他从中国银行账户提取了500.00美元，其中400.00美元支付给拉普罗克路（Rue du Pere Proc，原文如此，应为Rue du Pere Froc）的“瑞昌”（Zai Chong，音译）木行，作为购买木材的部分货款。

他声称这笔钱是由他的木匠袁仁禮（Yuen Zung Lee，音译）支付给木行的，收据由该木匠保管，且该木匠现已返回内地。如有必要，可向瑞昌木行查询。

page_data.en:
4/2

A perusal of his account book which was
found on his person when arrested shows that he
did withdraw $500.00 from his account on July
18th. 1939.

At present there appears to be no evidence
against Zung Ts Ming that he was concerned in guerilla
activities, unless same can be produced by the Japanese
Gendarmerie. At present they appear to be reluctant
to produce any evidence in support of their allegations

page_data.en:
Zung Ts Ming (陳志敏).
Tungchow                                      C.D.C. 211
C.I, C.B.H...      25-7-39           tribunal: text
                                             ///////   clerk aide

My name is Zung Ts Ming (陳志敏), age 28, native
of Tungchow, married, residing at room 11 of the Kyi Sang Sen
(吉陞棧) lodging house, No.10, Lane 195 Nanking Road.

I lived together with my parents in Tungchow when
I was in boyhood. My father was a farmer. I studied at a
private school when I was 8 years old. I remained there until
17 years of age. I then studied at the Pei Teh (培德) Primary
School in Tungchow for one year. I was apprenticed to the
Ming Jung (民昌) Silk Weaving Factory in Soochow through the
recommendation of one named Ts Yih Sai (朱義才) when I
attained the age of 18.

Three years later, I finished my apprenticeship, but
I still remained in the job and received 40 or 50 dollars
per mensem.

At the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in 1937, our factory closed down, and I then returned to my
native place. Owing to my bad health I stayed at home for
six months.

In February 1938 (I was 27 years old), I obtained
a job as shroff at the Chung Hoo (中和) Steamship Company,
Sz Chi Hong (隆積行), Haimen (海門), through the recommen-
dation of my cousin, Zung Ts Chi (陳志其). I received $24.00
wages per mensem. At that time I used to purchase cigarettes
from Shanghai and sell them in Haimen.

On 25th. April, 1939 (28th. year of the Republic of
China), my wife and I came to Shanghai and lived together with
one named Yeung Hou Ming (楊厚民) at No.1 Nam Ko, Foo Sai
page_data.zh:
唐志明（Zung Ts Ming，即陳志敏）。
通州                                      C.D.C. 211
C.I, C.B.H...      1939年7月25日           法庭：文本
                                             ///////   助理书记员

我叫唐志明（Zung Ts Ming，即陳志敏），28岁，通州人，已婚，居住在南京路195弄10号吉陞棧（Kyi Sang Sen，音译）旅馆11号房间。

我少年时与父母同住通州。父亲是农民。我8岁时进入私塾读书。一直读到17岁。随后我在通州培德（Pei Teh，音译）小学读了一年。18岁时，经朱義才（Ts Yih Sai，音译）推荐，我到苏州民昌（Ming Jung，音译）丝织厂当学徒。

三年后，我出师，但仍留在那裡工作，每月收入四五十美元。

1937年中日战事爆发时，我们工厂倒闭，我便返回家乡。因身体不好，我在家休养了六个月。

1938年2月（我27岁时），经表兄陈志其（Zung Ts Chi，音译）推荐，我在海门（Haimen）隆積行（Sz Chi Hong，音译）中和（Chung Hoo，音译）轮船公司找到一份出纳员的工作。每月工资24.00美元。那时我常从上海购买香烟在海门出售。

1939年4月25日（民国二十八年），我和妻子来到上海，与杨厚民（Yeung Hou Ming，音译）一同住在法租界土山灣（Foo Sai Wei，音译）Route de Zikawei（徐家汇路）南柯1号。

page_data.en:
(2)

Wei (土山灣), Route de Zikawei, French Concession. My
brother, Zung Ts Tsoong (陳志忠) gave me $1,500.00 in
notes when I was in Haimen, and requested me to put the same
into a bank. On 29th. April, 1939, I put $3,000.00 in notes
(including my own money, $1,500.00) into the Commercial Bank
of China. On 2nd. May, 1939, I drew out $200.00 and on the
6th. May, 1939, I again drew $300.00 from the above mentioned
bank. On 20th. May, 1939, my wife and I returned to Haimen.
Owing to the fighting between Chinese and Japanese soldiers,
our steamship company closed down, and I then returned to my
native place in Tungchow, where I operated a potato and peach
business between Shanghai and Tungchow. I usually sent my
assistant to attend to business transactions.

On 7th. July, 1939, I consented with Yoeng Hou Ming
and Yuen Ching Zung (袁近仁), friends of mine in my native
place, to raise $1,200.00 (each paid $400.00) to go to Shanghai
re purchasing a quantity of lumber, and offer it for sale in
Tungchow. This was agreed.

On 11th. July, 1939, I came to Shanghai together with
Yuen Zung Lee (袁仁禮) (carpenter), and Wong Young Ba
(黃鳳心), and visited one named Vai Fah Ding (樊發庭).
(who is in the steamship business) at the office of the Dong
Tai (同泰) Steam Navigation Co., situated at room 602, Dah
Yee (大義) Lodging House, Avenue Edward VII, French Concession.
I was told by Vai that I and Wong could invest $800.00 each to
the Dong Tai Steam Navigation Company as shares. He further
stated that Wong and I would be appointed as supervisors of the
said company. I then stayed in the office. About 4 days later,
page_data.zh:
(2)

我在海门时，兄弟陈志忠（Zung Ts Tsoong，音译）给了我1,500.00元钞票，让我存入银行。1939年4月29日，我将3,000.00元钞票（包括我自己的1,500.00元）存入中国银行。1939年5月2日，我从上述银行取出200.00美元，1939年5月6日，又取出300.00美元。1939年5月20日，我和妻子返回海门。由于中日士兵之间的战斗，我们的轮船公司停业，我便返回通州家乡，在上海和通州之间经营土豆和桃子生意。我通常派助手去处理业务交易。

1939年7月7日，我与家乡的朋友杨厚民（Yoeng Hou Ming，音译）和袁近仁（Yuen Ching Zung，音译）商定，筹集1,200.00美元（每人出资400.00美元）去上海购买一批木材，并在通州出售。此事达成一致。

1939年7月11日，我与木匠袁仁禮（Yuen Zung Lee，音译）和黄鳳心（Wong Young Ba，音译）一同来到上海，拜访了在法租界爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）大義（Dah Yee，音译）旅馆602室的同泰（Dong Tai，音译）轮船航运公司办公室工作的樊發庭（Vai Fah Ding，音译）（从事轮船业务）。樊告诉我，我和黄可以各投资800.00美元入股同泰轮船航运公司。他还说，黄和我将被任命为该公司的监理。于是我留在办公室。大约4天后，

page_data.en:
(3)

Yoong Hou Ming came to Shanghai from Haimen and resided at
room No.11 Kyi Sung Zen Lodging House, No.10 Lane 195 Fokien
Road. I then removed to the above mentioned lodging house.
On 18th. July, 1939, I drew $500.00 from the
Commercial Bank of China, and accompanied Yoong Hou Ming and
Yuen. **〔此处转录不清〕** Lee to the Zai Chong (采昌) Lumber Yard, Rue du Pere
Proe, French Concession to purchase a quantity of lumber. On
arrival, we paid $400.00 to the lumber yard and the remainder we
promised to pay on 21st. July, 1939, when we removed the lumber.
I went to the lumber yard late on that day (July 21st.) therefore
I could not engage any coolies to remove the wood. I then
promised to remove same on the following day, and returned to
the Kyi Sung Zen Lodging House. At 2 p.m. a party of S.M.Police
came to my room and took me into custody. I have never been
a soldier, or a member of guerilla units. I have not worked
in any executive organisations.

This is a true statement.

Signed : Zung To Ming
page_data.zh:
(3)

杨厚民（Yoong Hou Ming，音译）从海门来到上海，住在福建路195弄10号吉陞棧（Kyi Sung Zen，音译）旅馆11号房间。随后我也搬到了上述旅馆。
1939年7月18日，我从中国银行提取了500.00美元，并与杨厚民和袁**〔此处转录不清〕**礼（Yuen. **〔此处转录不清〕** Lee）一同前往法租界拉普罗克路（Rue du Pere Proe，原文如此，应为Rue du Pere Froc）的采昌（Zai Chong，音译）木行购买一批木材。到达后，我们向木行支付了400.00美元，并承诺在1939年7月21日运走木材时支付余款。那天（7月21日）我很晚才去木行，因此无法雇用工入搬运木材。于是我承诺第二天再运，并返回吉陞棧旅馆。下午2点，一队公共租界巡捕房警察来到我的房间，将我逮捕。我从未当过兵，也不是游击队成员。我没有在任何行政机构工作过。

以上陈述属实。

M. C. (Special Branch).

HEADQUARTERS
C.1.Msc.114/39. CRIME BRANCH
JULY 22, 39
2.

ASSISTANCE TO THE JAPANESE GENDARMERIE

At 1.30 p.m. on July 21st 1939 the Japanese
Gendarmerie requested assistance to carry out a raid
in the Settlement for the purpose of arresting two
male Chinese who were alleged to be members of a
Chinese guerrilla unit.

According to later verbal information
supplied by Sgt. Major Kateda, the two persons
whom they wished to arrest were named :
ZUNG TS MING (陳志敏) and
WONG FUNG S (黃鳳池)
and were members of a guerrilla unit which about
five months ago had attacked a small detachment of
Japanese soldiers in the Tungehow Area.

This guerrilla unit was then supposed to have
been commanded by one Tsung Chi Foo (張濟福) cousin
of the person Zung Ts Ming.

The necessary assistance was rendered by
D.S. Rhodes, D.S.I. Kouvaleff, D.S. Sugimoto,
A/D.S.I. **〔此处转录不清〕** Wan Fung, C.D.S. 2 and C.D.C. 211,
and together with Sgt. Major Kateda and an informer,
page_data.zh:
M. C. （特科）。

总部
C.1.Msc.114/39. 刑事科
1939年7月22日
2.

协助日本宪兵队

1939年7月21日下午1时30分，日本
宪兵队请求协助在租界内进行突袭，目的是逮捕两名
据称是中国游击队成员的中国男子。

根据后来由军士长Kateda口头提供的
信息，他们希望逮捕的两人姓名为：
陈志敏（ZUNG TS MING）和
黄凤池（WONG FUNG S）
并且是一个游击队的成员，该游击队在大约
五个月前曾在通州地区袭击了一小队
日本士兵。

当时推测该游击队由一名张济福（Tsung Chi Foo）指挥，
此人是陈志敏的表亲。

罗德兹副督察（D.S. Rhodes）、库瓦列夫副警司（D.S.I. Kouvaleff）、杉本副督察（D.S. Sugimoto）、
代理副警司（A/D.S.I.）**〔此处转录不清〕**、万丰（Wan Fung）、2名华人侦探（C.D.S. 2）和211号华人巡捕（C.D.C. 211）提供了
必要的协助，并与军士长Kateda及一名线人一起，

page_data.en:
2/2.

room No. 11 of the "Kyi Sung Zen" (吉生棧) Lodging
House, situated at No. 10 Lane 159 Fokien Road was
visited.

This room was found to be occupied at
the time by six male Chinese, but the informer
picked out one who eventually gave his name as:-
ZUNG TS MING (陳志敏) alias
ZUNG YING (陳英) 28, native of Tungchow,
M/Unemployed, N. F. A.

A search of the room failed to find any
incriminating evidence.

The following property was seized from
his person : -
1. One wrist watch.
2. One bank book, showing $2000.00, credited
to Zung Ying.
3. One pocket book.
4. One seaman's union badge.
5. 4 $5.00 notes.
6. 3 Photos.
7. 4 Tramway coupons.
8. 2 20-cent notes.
9. 1 10-cent piece.
10. One leather wallet.
11. 16 visiting cards.
page_data.zh:
2/2.

探访了位于福建路159弄10号的“吉生栈”（Kyi Sung Zen）旅馆
11号房间。

发现当时有六名中国男子居住在该房间，但线人
指认了其中一人，此人最终自报姓名为：-
陈志敏（ZUNG TS MING），别名
陈英（ZUNG YING），28岁，通州人，
男/无业，非本地居民协会成员（N. F. A.）。

对房间的搜查未能找到任何罪证。

从其身上搜获以下财物：-
1. 一只手表。
2. 一本存折，显示陈志敏名下存款$2000.00。
3. 一个口袋书（记事本）。
4. 一枚海员工会徽章。
5. 4张5.00美元钞票。
6. 3张照片。
7. 4张电车券。
8. 2张20分钞票。
9. 1枚10分硬币。
10. 一个皮夹。
11. 16张名片。

page_data.en:
2/3.

Zung Ts Ming denied having been concerned
in any guerrilla activities at any time and claimed
that he came to Shanghai to purchase lumber.

He admitted knowing the other wanted man
named Wong Fung S (黃鳳池) and that they came
together from Tungchow to Shanghai on 11.7.39,
since which time they had stayed together.

Wong who was absent at the time of the
raid was, according to the arrested man, visiting
friends at room No. 602 Great Shanghai Hotel, No.
602 Avenue Edward VII.

According to the Gendarmerie information
Wong may have gone to room 502 of the above hotel.

They therefore, requested S.M.P. to follow
up and obtain the assistance of the French Police
to visit the Gt. Shanghai Hotel in search of Wong.

This request was acceded to. Mr. Valentine,
French Police was communicated with, and finally he
agreed to give the necessary assistance.

At 3.45 p.m. 21.7.39 the S.M.P. party accom-
panied by French Police, (the Gendarmes did not
proceed to the Concession) visited No. 502 of the
Great Shanghai Hotel, this room was found to be
vacant, but from enquiries it was learned that the
page_data.zh:
2/3.

陈志敏否认曾参与任何游击活动，并声称
他来上海是为了购买木材。

他承认认识另一名被通缉者黄凤池（WONG FUNG S），并称他们于1939年7月11日一同从通州来到上海，此后一直在一起。

据被捕者称，突袭时不在场的黄凤池正在爱多亚路602号大华饭店602室拜访朋友。

根据宪兵队的情报，黄可能已前往上述饭店的502室。

因此，他们请求工部局警务处跟进，并获得法国警察的协助，前往大华饭店搜寻黄凤池。

此请求获准。已与法国警察Valentine先生取得联系，最终他同意提供必要协助。

On the 7th August 1939 p.m., Sgt. Komaki
of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters informed the
S. M. Police by a note, attached with translation,

have conceded to the instructions of D. C. (Crime),

arrested, Tseu Hai Zion (周海泉) to be released,
whilst the 3rd arrested, Chuin Pah Gee (錢伯琦) could
be handed over to the Japanese authorities.

Gee, Shan-Ken-Ko No. 888 (attached) has already been
received from the Japanese authorities claiming the
permanent custody of the prisoner.

detained pending instructions for their release.

arrested persons with any crime.

General summary of the case against the 3rd
arrested, Chuin Pah Gee, is being prepared.

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO JAPANESE
GENDARMERIE HEADQUARTERS ON BEHALF OF JAPANESE
MILITARY WATER POLICE

At 10.30 a.m. on the 29th July 1939, a further
documentary evidence, as per diary No. 9, was produced
by Sgt. Major Sakamoto of the Japanese Water Police,
against the 3rd arrested, Chauen Fah Zee ( 蔡法仔 ).
According to Sgt. Major Sakamoto's
information the 3rd arrested, Chauen Fah Zee, was
alleged to be a superior officer to the 1st and 2nd
arrested men.
However, on being confronted, the 1st and 2nd
arrested claimed no knowledge of the 3rd arrested,
whilst the latter stated that he had never seen the
1st and 2nd arrested.
In view of the foregoing and the fact that the
produced documentary evidence failed to establish any
connections between the 1st, 2nd and 3rd arrested men,
a request has been made to Sgt. Major Sakamoto to
produce some evidence which would show that the
three arrested men are concerned in one and the same
case.

P. Konovaloff.
D. S. I.

1939年7月29日上午10时30分，日本水上警察坂本军曹长（Sgt. Major Sakamoto）根据日记第9号记录，提交了针对第三名被捕者蔡法仔（Chauen Fah Zee）的进一步书面证据。据坂本军曹长提供的信息，第三名被捕者蔡法仔被指称是第一名和第二名被捕者的上级军官。
然而，在对质时，第一名和第二名被捕者声称不认识第三名被捕者，而后者则声明从未见过第一名和第二名被捕者。
鉴于上述情况，以及所提交的书面证据未能确立第一、第二和第三名被捕者之间的任何联系，已要求坂本军曹长提供能够证明这三名被捕者涉及同一案件的证据。

P. Konovaloff.
副督察长。

H. C. C. B. 25-7-39 ------

I am a hosiery broker and residing at No. 39, Rue
Bluntchli, French Concession.

I was born in Shanghai and lived with my parents
until the age of 16, when I became an apprentice at the Shing
Loong (興隆) Hosiery Factory, No. 144 Kong Chih Li (康吉里),
Rue Bluntchli. I was employed there for three years, after
which I took up the job of a hosiery broker. However, I
became unemployed after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937. I eventually obtained a job as a shop-
assistant at the S Dah (三達) Hosiery Factory on S A Road.
There I received a wage of $30.00 per mensem, but owing to bad
business I was discharged in March 1939 when the Factory
decided to reduce their staff. I then became a hosiery broker
again.

At about 7 or 8 p.m. on the 11th or 12th July 1939,
I was viewing a Peiping theatrical performance at the Wing On
Roof Garden when I encountered my friend, Zee Vung Chung, who
was a professional boxer appearing in this amusement resort.
I requested him to find a job for me, and he stated that
he could get me a position aboard a foreign ship. On being
asked regarding the nature of the work, he said that it was
the position of a boatswain, the monthly profit from whom would
be between $200.00 and $300.00, and that this job could only
be procured by first paying a fee of $1,800.00. I asked him
regarding the identity of the person to whom the payment was
intended, and he revealed to me the captain, interpreter and
account all required a share of this sum, thereby enabling **〔此处转录不清〕**
page_data.zh:
周海泉（TSU HAI ZEE），别名周開龍（TSU KAI LOONG），31岁，已婚，
扬州 xx 副督察长 21a Wei Faung
译员 Tsaung Zung Pau
H. C. C. B. 1939年7月25日 ------

我是一名袜业经纪人，居住在法租界白利南路39号。

我出生于上海，与父母同住直至16岁，当时我在法租界康吉里144号兴隆（Shing Loong）袜厂当学徒。我在那里工作了三年，之后从事袜业经纪人的工作。然而，1937年中日敌对行动爆发后，我失业了。最终，我在萨波托路（S A Road）的三达（S Dah）袜厂找到了一份店员的工作。在那里，我每月工资为30.00美元，但由于生意不佳，工厂决定裁员，我于1939年3月被解雇。随后我又重新做起了袜业经纪人。

1939年7月11日或12日晚上7点或8点左右，我在永安天韵楼观看北平戏曲表演时，遇到了我的朋友徐永忠（Zee Vung Chung），他是在该娱乐场所表演的职业拳击手。我请他帮我找份工作，他说可以帮我在外国船上谋个职位。当问及工作性质时，他说那是水手长的职位，每月收入在200.00到300.00美元之间，但要得到这份工作，首先需支付1,800.00美元的费用。我问他这笔钱是付给谁的，他向我透露船长、翻译和会计都需要分得这笔钱，从而使 **〔此处转录不清〕**

page_data.en:
- 2 -

to obtain the job. After further requesting him to do his
best to help me, I endeavoured to raise this sum of money.
At about 9 a.m. 18-7-39, my friend Fong Ah Zeh (方阿才) came
to my home and told me that he was without a job. On being
asked if I could find him a job, I informed him that a certain
foreign ship required the services of two boatswains, but
these positions would only be given to those who could pay
a sum of more than $1,000.00. He readily consented to
give due consideration in this matter. I also told him that
at least $500.00 to $600.00 should be raised at the earliest
possible moment. It was my intention to get this job by
each of us paying half of the sum. At about 2 p.m. 23-7-39,
Fong Ah Zeh visited my home again when I asked him if he had
procured the money, to which he replied that it could be
done. We two then proceeded to the Great Eastern Tea-Room,
Wing On Co., where I had previously promised to meet Zee Vung
Chung. There we met Zee and two others unknown to me. The
five of us had tea together and Zee Vung Chung introduced the
two strangers to us as the compradore of the boat in question,
(dressed in Chinese clothes) named Tang Yih Ming (唐一鳴)
and the English interpreter named Wong Yih Ming (王一明)
respectively (dressed in foreign clothes). Tang Yih Ming
asked me if I had brought the "negotiation" money with me, and
I replied that same would be ready on the next day. He then
told me to come to this place again between 3 and 4 p.m. the
following day. At about 3 p.m. the next day (24-7-39) Fong Ah
Zeh and I proceeded to the Great Eastern Hotel Room, where we
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

能够获得这份工作。在进一步请求他尽力帮助我之后，我努力筹集这笔钱。
1939年7月18日上午9点左右，我的朋友方阿才（Fong Ah Zeh）来到我家，告诉我他失业了。当被问我能否帮他找工作时，我告诉他某艘外国船需要两名水手长，但这些职位只给予那些能支付1,000.00美元以上款项的人。他欣然同意对此事予以考虑。我还告诉他，应尽快筹集至少500.00到600.00美元。我的打算是我们每人支付一半费用来获得这份工作。1939年7月23日下午2点左右，方阿才再次来到我家，我问他是否筹到了钱，他回答说可以办到。于是我们两人前往永安公司的大东茶室，我之前曾答应在那里与徐永忠见面。在那里，我们见到了徐永忠和另外两个我不认识的人。我们五人一起喝茶，徐永忠向我们介绍那两个陌生人是所谓船只的买办（身穿中式服装），名叫唐一鳴（Tang Yih Ming），以及英文翻译（身穿西式服装），名叫王一明（Wong Yih Ming）。唐一鳴问我是否带来了“洽谈”用的钱，我回答说第二天就能准备好。于是他让我第二天下午3点到4点之间再来这个地方。第二天（7月24日）下午3点左右，方阿才和我前往大东旅馆房间，在那里我们

page_data.en:
- 3 -

met Tung Yih Ming, Wong Yih Ding and Zee Vung Chung. Tung
Yih Ming asked us whether we had the required sum, to which
I replied in the affirmative. He then told me that the
contract would be valid for one year and in the event of our
losing the job within this period the money was to be returned
to us without fail. He further stated that the foreign capital
of this ship was present in room 434 of the Oriental Hotel,
awaiting them to take us there, to meet him. Fong Ah Zah and
I, accompanied by Tung and Wong, immediately visited room 434
at the Oriental Hotel, where we met a foreigner who did not
look like a British, American or French, but had the
resemblance of a Portuguese. This foreigner, through the aid
of the interpreter, asked me if I had the money with me. I
replied in the affirmative. Then he told us to obey his
orders if we wished to take the job. He also asked us whether
we could read characters or not, whereupon we averred that
we were illiterate. He produced a piece of paper from his
pocket and claiming same to be a contract, instructed me to
append my signature thereon. As this was being done, a party
of detectives entered the room and took us into custody. I
am completely ignorant of the reason why I was arrested.
I also do not know why I should be asked to sign my name
below the characters "Vong Yah Cheng" on that paper.

Signed :          TSU HAI ZEE
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

见到了唐一鳴、王一明和徐永忠。唐一鳴问我们要的钱是否准备好了，我给予了肯定的回答。然后他告诉我合同有效期为一年，如果在此期间失去工作，钱款务必退还给我们。他还说，这艘船的外国资方代表就在东方饭店434房间，等着带我们去见他。方阿扎和我在唐和王陪同下，立即前往东方饭店434房间，在那里我们见到了一名外国人，他看起来不像英国人、美国人或法国人，但有点像葡萄牙人。这名外国人在翻译的帮助下，问我是否带了钱。我给予了肯定的回答。然后他告诉我们，如果想得到这份工作，就必须服从他的命令。他还问我们是否识字，我们声称自己是文盲。他从口袋里拿出一张纸，声称是合同，指示我在上面签名。就在此时，一群侦探进入房间并将我们逮捕。我完全不知道被捕的原因。我也不知道为什么要在纸上“Vong Yah Cheng”字样下方签署我的名字。

签名：          周海泉

page_data.en:
FONG AH ZEH (方阿則)
Ningpo                                      D.S.I. Sia Vai Fong.
C. 1                25.7.39        translated      Huu S. F.

My name is Fong Ah Zeh, aged 34 years, native of
Ningpo, s/carton maker, and residing at 7 Rue Conty, F.C.
When I was 12 years old I came to Shanghai with
my elder brother, Fong Kyung Kuen, and lived with him
at 7 Pei'Kun Ling Li, Tung Shing Ming Road, Chapei.
At the age of 14 I obtained employment as an
apprentice at the Now Tai Ziang Carton Factory, Rue Porte
du Nord, F.C. where I remained for 3 years. At the age of
17 I left the above factory and went to work as shop assistant
in the Yuen Tai (元泰) Carton Factory for one year, which
factory was then located in Hungkew.
At the age of 18 I left Shanghai for Sungkiang,
where I secured employment in the Tai Ho (太和) Hosiery
Factory, with pay of over $20.00 per month.
After four years' stay in Sungkiang I returned to
Shanghai and organised a carton factory, known as "Tsung
Tai (宗泰)" Carton Factory, on Rue Frontier de Montauban,
F.C. Four years later my factory was closed down due to
business depression. I again went to work for others in
the Lee Sang Shing (李順興) Carton Shop, 21 Sung Cheng Li,
Dong In Wei, French Concession, where I remained employed
for one year.
On 7.8.36 when I was 32 years old I was arrested
by Louza Station for robbery and was subsequently sentenced
to 3 years & 6 months' imprisonment.
In addition I was arrested by Nanking Station for
larceny and sentenced to 2 days' detention when I was 16 years
page_data.zh:
方阿則（FONG AH ZEH）
宁波                                      副督察长 谢伟芳。
C. 1                1939年7月25日        译员      Huu S. F.

我叫方阿則，34岁，宁波籍，职业纸箱制造工，居住在法租界孔提埃路7号。
12岁时，我和哥哥方庆坤（Fong Kyung Kuen）一起来到上海，与他同住在闸北通圣明路（Tung Shing Ming Road）北昆岭里7号。
14岁时，我在法租界北门路（Rue Porte du Nord）的新泰祥（Now Tai Ziang）纸箱厂当学徒，在那里待了3年。17岁时，我离开了上述工厂，去虹口的元泰（Yuen Tai）纸箱厂做了一年店员。
18岁时，我离开上海前往松江，在太和（Tai Ho）袜厂找到工作，月薪超过20.00美元。
在松江呆了四年后，我回到上海，在法租界蒙托邦边界路（Rue Frontier de Montauban）创办了一家名为“宗泰（Tsung Tai）”的纸箱厂。四年后，由于经济萧条，我的工厂倒闭。我又去法租界董家渡顺成里21号的李順興（Lee Sang Shing）纸箱店为他人做工，在那里受雇一年。
1936年8月7日，我32岁时，因抢劫罪被老闸捕房逮捕，随后被判处3年6个月监禁。
此外，我16岁时曾因盗窃罪被南京路捕房逮捕，并被判处拘留2天

page_data.en:
- 2 -

of age, (judgement being rendered on 29.10.18).
I was last released from Gaol on 9.2.38; and then
lived at 5 Dah Kung Rd, Rue Conty, F.C.
Due to ill health I returned to my native country,
Ningpo; on 9.7.38. In October 1938, I came back to Shanghai
and procured employment in the Zung Tai Ho (〔此处转录不清〕) Carton
Factory, 7 Rue Wants, F.C., with pay of $15.00 per month.
In May of this year I left the above employer owing
to illness.
At 9 a.m. on 18.7.39 I visited my friend, Tsu Hai
Zee (2nd arrested man) (〔此处转录不清〕), at 39 Rue Bluntchli, F.C.
On being requested to seek a job for me, Tsu Hai Zee told
me that there was a vacancy for a boat swain on a certain
steamer, but to secure this position required a sum of
at least $1,600.00 which would be used to canvass a foreigner,
who was the Captain of the steamer, whom a friend of Tsu knew
very well.
Between 1 and 2 p.m. 23.7.39 I met Tsu Hai Zee together
with three unknown persons, in the Fa Tung Tea-Room, Wing On
Co., Nanking Road, when Tsu asked me if the above sum of
money was ready, to which I answered in the affirmative.
One of three unknown persons then urged Tsu to get the money
for the foreigner was waiting for us in Room 434, Oriental
Hotel.
I then went to a friend's home on Kiukiang Road
(No. unknown) to fetch a sum of $1,700.00 which I had loaned
from others two days previously.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

（判决日期为1918年10月29日）。
我最后一次出狱是1938年2月9日；之后居住在法租界孔提埃路大公路5号。
由于健康原因，我于1938年7月9日返回故乡宁波。1938年10月，我回到上海，在法租界万恩路（Rue Wants）7号的宗泰和（Zung Tai Ho）〔此处转录不清〕纸箱厂找到工作，月薪15.00美元。
今年5月，我因病离开了上述雇主。
1939年7月18日上午9点，我去法租界白利南路39号拜访我的朋友周海泉（第二名被捕者）（〔此处转录不清〕）。当我请求他帮我找工作时，周海泉告诉我某艘轮船上有一个水手长的空缺，但要获得这个职位需要至少1,600.00美元，用于打通一位外国人的关系，此人是该轮船的船长，周的一个朋友与他非常熟识。
1939年7月23日下午1点到2点之间，我在南京路永安公司的华通茶室与周海泉及三名陌生人见面，当时周问我上述款项是否准备好，我给予了肯定的回答。三名陌生人中的一人随即催促周去取钱，因为外国人正在东方饭店434房间等我们。
随后我前往九江路（门牌号不详）的一位朋友家，取回我两天前从他人处借来的1,700.00美元。

page_data.en:
Taking with me the above sum of money and accompany-
ing Tsu Hai Zee and two others (i.e. Tung Yih Ming and
Tong Soh Ding (〔此处转录不清〕)), I proceeded to Room 434,
Oriental Hotel, and arrived at about 4 o'clock.
On entering the room I saw a foreigner who, through
an interpreter, asked me if I had brought with me the sum
of money (canvassing fee), and I replied "yes".
On my presenting to the foreigner the $1,700.00,
he took out from his jacket pocket a contract, which he
asked Tsu Hai Zee to sign on the understanding that we
could not repent what we had done. This contract was
duly signed by Tsu Hai Zee. It was during that moment
when a party of police together with some Japanese raided
the room and arrested all of us (four in number). The
reason for my arrest is unknown to me.
Regarding the $1,700.00, $800.00 belongs to Tsu
Hai Zee, and I own the remainder $900.00 which I have
borrowed from my friends.
The above is my true statement.

Signed:
page_data.zh:
我携带上述款项，陪同朱海子（Tsu Hai Zee）及另外两人（即唐一明（Tung Yih Ming）和董索丁（Tong Soh Ding）〔此处转录不清〕），前往东方饭店434号房间，于大约4点钟抵达。
进入房间后，我看见一名外国人，他通过译员问我是否带来了那笔款项（活动经费），我回答“是”。
当我向该外国人出示1,700.00美元时，他从夹克口袋里拿出一份合同，要求朱海子签署，并告知我们不得反悔所作之事。朱海子随即签署了该合同。就在此时，一群警察会同几名日本人突袭了该房间，并将我们所有人（共四人）逮捕。我被捕的原因我不清楚。
关于这1,700.00美元，其中800.00美元属于朱海子，其余900.00美元归我所有，这是我向朋友借来的。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：

续报协助位于桥屋（Bridge House）的日本宪兵队总部，代表日本海军水上警察及浮动的餐厅（Floating Restaurant）行事。

关于日记第3号所述的进一步协助请求，即逮捕名为徐文中（Zee Vung Chung）的一人，此人作为担保人在被扣押的文件上签字，其地址为伯基尔路（Burkill Road）旁的刘孝丰（Lieu Hyoh Fung）〔此处转录不清〕18号。由副警司罗兹（Rhodes）、巡官清水（Shimidzu）、山原（Yamahara）、副督察长齐姆（Zim）、刑事侦探主任206号及本人组成的小组，会同日本宪兵队总部的小牧（Komaki）警佐和日本水上警察的坂本（Sakamoto）警曹长，于1939年7月26日上午10时对上述地址进行了突击搜查。然而，在该处并未发现此人。

对通缉犯徐文中此前居住的房间进行的搜查，未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。

已通知工部局总部和新闸捕房。

关于日记第4号所述的请求，1939年7月26日下午4时，在法国警察的协助下，由巡官山原、清水、副督察长齐姆、刑事侦探主任206号、218号组成的侦探小队，

under the undersigned, were led by the 1st arrested
man, Fong Ah Zeh (方阿才) to the first floor front
room situated in a house No. 66, Rue de Conty, French
Concession. However, the room was found to be vacant
and a chief tenant of the house named Tae Tsung Foh
(戴宗福) stated that this room was vacated for a
considerable time and the arrested man was not known
to him. This fact shows that Fong Ah Zeh is, for some
reason, very reluctant to disclose his proper address.
The 2nd arrested man, Tsu Hai Zee (朱海子),
led the party to his address situated at House 39,
Route Bluntschli, where he occupied the first floor
rear room. A search of this room revealed nothing of
a tangible evidence to this case.
The party returned to C. I. Offices at
4.40 p.m. this inst.
Finger print records show that the 1st
arrested, Fong Ah Zeh, has two previous convictions :-
Larceny, 3 days, 20-10-15.
Highway Robbery
& 7-2-35.
Possession of Arms
Released : 8-2-38.
The 2nd arrested, Tsu Hai Zee, has no
previous convictions.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

在本人带领下，由第一名被捕者方阿才（Fong Ah Zeh）带路，前往法租界康悌路（Rue de Conty）66号房屋的前楼房间。然而，发现该房间空置，该房屋的二房东戴宗福（Tae Tsung Foh）表示，该房间已空置相当长一段时间，他不认识这名被捕者。这一事实表明，方阿才出于某种原因，非常不愿透露其真实住址。
第二名被捕者朱海子（Tsu Hai Zee）带领小组前往其位于白利南路（Route Bluntschli）39号的住址，他居住在该处的后楼房间。对该房间的搜查未发现本案的任何实质性证据。
小组于当日下午4时40分返回刑事调查处办公室。
指纹记录显示，第一名被捕者方阿才有两次前科：
盗窃，监禁3天，1915年10月20日。
持械抢劫
& 1935年2月7日。
非法持有武器
释放日期：1938年2月8日。
第二名被捕者朱海子无前科。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

At 9 a.m. 25-7-39, Sgt. Major Sakamoto of
the Japanese Water Police, accompanied by his informer
Sema, came to C. I. Offices and submitted the informer
for questioning. He gave his name as O. V. de Senna
and claimed to be a Portuguese subject.

Upon being questioned by the undersigned,
Senna fully corroborated the statements of the other
two Chinese informers. In his statement (attached),
which is written by Senna in his own handwriting
(being requested to do so by Sgt. Major Sakamoto), he
states that the seized document, implicating the 2nd
arrested man as a representative of the guerilla unit,
was brought to the room No. 434 of the Oriental Hotel
by the arrested two men. After the document had been
signed by one of the arrested man (the 2nd arrested
admitted to have signed the document as per diary No.2),
Senna passed same to one of the Chinese informers.
When the detectives entered this room, Senna pointed
out the informer who was in possession of the document
at the time. Statements and translation of the two
Chinese informers are attached herewith.

Further interrogation of the two arrested
men are being continued and statements being taken from
them.

M.S.
26/7

D. Kouzmaloff.
D. S. I.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

1939年7月25日上午9时，日本水上警察的坂本（Sakamoto）警曹长在其线人塞马（Sema）的陪同下，来到刑事调查处办公室，并提交该线人接受讯问。他自称O. V. de Senna，并声称是葡萄牙籍臣民。

经本人讯问，森纳（Senna）完全证实了另外两名中国线人的陈述。在他的供词（附后）中，由森纳亲笔书写（应小牧警曹长要求），他指出，牵连第二名被捕者为游击队代表的被扣押文件，是由这两名被捕者带入东方饭店434号房间的。在其中一名被捕者签署文件后（第二名被捕者承认按日记第2号所述签署了文件），森纳将文件交给了一名中国线人。当侦探进入该房间时，森纳指出了当时持有该文件的线人。两名中国线人的供词及译文附后。

对两名被捕者的进一步审讯正在进行中，正在获取他们的供词。

M.S.
27/6

D. Kouzmaloff.
副督察长（D. S. I.）

TUNG YIH MING (唐一鳴), age 26, M/Coal Broker,
residing at No. 365 Peking Road,
Ningpo                                      XX        C.D.C. 206
                                            translated
H. . C. D.              24-7-39             --------  Tsaung Zung Pau

At about 4 or 5 p.m. 10-7-39, Wong Koh Ding (王克亭)
and I were at the Loo Tsung Koh (羅春閣) Teashop, Chekiang
Road, when Zee Vung Chung (徐文中) and two others named Li
(李) and Hwo (華) approached us to discuss regarding the
purchase of firearms, as one named Wong Tuh Chiang (王德昌)
alias Fong Ah Zah (方阿才), who was a relative of Zee Vung
Chung and had just arrived here from his native place, wished
to buy six pistols. I told them that I had no pistols in my
possession, but mentioned that I could introduce to them a
foreigner named Sena, who had pistols for sale. Thereafter
the five of us attended the above teashop daily for the
purpose of discussing the arms deal with the result that
the price for each pistol was settled at $500.00 and that the
foreigner would only agree to this transaction if a certificate
was made out. During the afternoon of 20-7-39 Zee Vung Chung
handed the required certificate to me, and I requested him to
accompany the buyer, Wong Tuh Chong, to the Great Eastern
Tea-room, Yin-Ho-Ka (英華街), on the 22-7-39, when the pistols
would be handed over to him on payment of money. At about
2 p.m. 23-7-39, Wong Koh Ding and I proceeded to the appointed
place where we met Zee Vung Chung, Wong Tuh Chong, Tsu Hai Zee
(周海泉), Li and Hwo, but as the foreigner failed to put in an
appearance, the meeting was postponed to 2 p.m. 24-7-39 and to be
held at the same place. At about 2 p.m. the next day, Wong Koh
Ding and I visited the Tea-room again and met the same five
persons. Wong and I then took the two buyers, Wong Tuh Chong
and Tsu Hai Zee, to Room 434 of the Oriental Hotel, which was
page_data.zh:
唐一明（TUNG YIH MING），26岁，男/煤炭经纪人，
居住于北京路365号，
宁波                                      XX        刑事侦探主任 206号
                                            翻译
H. . C. D.              1939年7月24日             --------  Tsaung Zung Pau

1939年7月10日下午4或5时许，王克亭（Wong Koh Ding）和我在浙江路的罗春阁（Loo Tsung Koh）茶楼，此时徐文中（Zee Vung Chung）和另外两人李（Li）和华（Hwo）走近我们，讨论购买枪支事宜，因为徐文中的亲戚、刚从老家来此的王德昌（Wong Tuh Chiang），又名方阿才（Fong Ah Zah），希望购买六支手枪。我告诉他们我手中没有手枪，但提到我可以向他们介绍一位名叫塞纳（Sena）的外国人，他有手枪出售。此后，我们五人每天光顾上述茶楼，目的是讨论军火交易，结果是每支手枪的价格定为500.00美元，且该外国人同意交易的前提是必须出具一份证明书。1939年7月20日下午，徐文中将所需的证明书交给我，我请他于1939年7月22日陪同买方王德昌前往英华街（Yin-Ho-Ka）的大东茶室，届时付款后手枪将交付给他。1939年7月23日下午2时许，王克亭和我前往约定地点，在那里遇到了徐文中、王德昌、周海泉（Tsu Hai Zee）、李和华，但由于该外国人未出现，会面推迟至1939年7月24日下午2时，地点不变。次日下午2时许，王克亭和我再次访问茶室，见到了同样的五人。随后，我和王带着两名买方王德昌和周海子前往东方饭店434号房间，该房间由

page_data.en:
- 2 -
engaged by the foreigner. The certificate which I handed to
the foreigner on the 20-7-39 was produced and the parties
concerned duly appended their signatures on same.
Subsequently, we were arrested by the Police in this room,

Signed : Tung Yih Ming.

- 2 -
该外国人预订。我于1939年7月20日交给该外国人的证明书被出示，相关各方 duly 在上面签了字。
随后，我们在该房间被警察逮捕，

TUNG YIH MING (唐一鳴), age 28, S/Silk broker,
residing at 356 [?] Road,
Ningpo                                      XX      D.I. Zia Vei Faung
                                            translated  Tsaung Sung au
H. C. B.                24-7-39

At about 5 p.m. 23-7-39, my friend Tung Yih Ming
(唐一鳴) approached me at the Dong Yue Tsung (同興春)
Teashop, Nanking Road, and requested me to meet him at the
Great Eastern Tea-room, Wing On Co., at 11 a.m. the following
day. On the next day I visited this tea-room accordingly
and Tung Yih Ming appeared a few minutes after my arrival.
After waiting for a short while we were joined by two other
persons, i.e. Tsu Hai Dee (朱海德), Fong Ah Zeh (方阿才)
and Lee Vung Chung (李文中), the last mentioned man being a
friend of Tung Yih Ming. We had tea together and presently
I asked Tung why he wanted me to act as an interpreter, to
which he replied that Tsu Hai Zee and Fong Ah Zeh were desirous
of purchasing six Mauser pistols from a foreigner and as he
did not know English himself I was requested to act as their
interpreter. Tsu Hai Zee and Fong Ah Zeh failed to bring the
money for the purchase of these pistols, and consequently they
went away later to fetch same. They returned with the money
at about 5.30 p.m. when Tung Yih Ming and I accompanied them
to Room 434 at the Oriental Hotel, which was said to be
engaged by the foreign arms dealer. On arriving there I was
told by the foreigner to ask Tsu and Fong where they would go
after purchasing the pistols, and they gave their destination
as Wei-an (淮安), Kiangsu. The foreigner then asked them
again, through my interpretation, if there were Japanese troops
in that locality, to which they replied in the negative. The
foreigner further asked them if they had brought the money with
them, whereupon they produced the money and showed it to him.
page_data.zh:
唐一明（TUNG YIH MING），28岁，单身/丝绸经纪人，
居住于[?]路356号，
宁波                                      XX      督察长 Zia Vei Faung
                                            翻译  Tsaung Sung au
H. C. B.                1939年7月24日

1939年7月23日下午5时许，我的朋友唐一明（Tung Yih Ming）在南京路的同兴春（Dong Yue Tsung）茶楼找到我，请我于次日上午11时在永安公司的大东茶室与他见面。次日我依约前往该茶室，唐一明在我到达几分钟后出现。稍等片刻后，又有两人加入，即朱海德（Tsu Hai Dee）、方阿才（Fong Ah Zeh）和李文中（Lee Vung Chung），最后提到的此人是唐一明的朋友。我们一起喝茶，随后我问唐为何要我担任译员，他回答说朱海子和方阿才希望从一名外国人那里购买六支毛瑟手枪，因他自己不懂英语，故请我担任他们的译员。朱海子和方阿才未能带来购买这些手枪的钱款，因此他们随后离开去取钱。他们在下午5时30分左右带着钱回来，此时唐一明和我陪同他们前往东方饭店434号房间，据说该房间由外国军火商预订。到达那里后，外国人让我询问朱和方在购买手枪后将去向何处，他们给出的目的地是江苏淮安（Wei-an）。外国人随后再次通过我的翻译询问该地区是否有日军，他们回答没有。外国人进一步询问他们是否带了钱，于是他们拿出钱款给他看。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

While this was being done Tsu Hai Zee was given a certificate
by the foreigner to append his signature thereon, which the
former complied with. A party of detectives suddenly entered
our room and the four of us were all taken into custody.

Signed by : WONG K.H DING.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

在此过程中，外国人给朱海子一份证明书让他在上面签字，朱照办了。一群侦探突然闯入我们的房间，我们四人全部被拘留。

签名：WONG K.H DING.

At 11.40 a.m. on the 24th July 1939, Sergeant
Major Katoda of the Japanese Gendarmerie, telephoned
to C.l offices, requesting assistance of the S.M.Police
to arrest two male Chinese persons, who were alleged
to be members of a guerilla unit, and to be located
at a certain place in Jessum district. The time for
the raid was stipulated at 2 p.m., same date.

Prior to the assistance being rendered,
Sergeant Major Komaki of the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters, on behalf of Sergt. Major Sakamoto,
who attended the raid with Srgt. Hama of the
Japanese Military River Police, Floating Restaurant,
divulged the following information:-

"That two male Chinese persons named :-
1) Wong Tak Cheong (王德昌) and
2) Zee Wing Chung (徐文忠),
members of the guerilla unit, came to Shanghai
to purchase a quantity of firearms. The first
named supposed to be in possession of a document,

应日本宪兵队总部（百老汇大厦）之请，代表日本水上警察总部（浮动的餐厅）提供协助（逮捕两人）

1939年7月24日上午11时40分，日本宪兵队小头目Katoda致电刑事科办公室，请求上海公共租界工部局警务处协助逮捕两名中国男子，据称此二人为游击队成员，位于杰西姆区（Jessum district）某处。突袭时间定为当日下午2时。

在提供协助之前，日本宪兵队总部的小头目Komaki代表坂本小头目（Sergt. Major Sakamoto），与日本军用水上警察“浮动的餐厅”的Hama警士一同参加了此次突袭，并透露了以下信息：-

“有两名中国男子，名为：-
1) Wong Tak Cheong (王德昌) 和
2) Zee Wing Chung (徐文忠)，
系游击队成员，来上海购买一批枪支。第一名嫌疑人据信持有一份文件，

page_data.en:
2/2.

authorising him to purchase the firearms for
guerilla unit, and he was to be found in
possession of a sum of $1,000.00.
An agent (name not disclosed) employed by
the Japanese Gendarmerie got into contact
with these two men and, on being instructed,
posed as a dealer in firearms. A meeting
between the informer and these two members
of the guerilla unit supposed to take place
in Room 434 of the Oriental Hotel, at 2 p.m.
this inst."

A posse of detectives, comprising of D.S.
Rhodes, D.P.Ses Shimidzu, Yamahara, D.S.I. Zia Vai
Feng, C.D.C.s 206, 212 and the undersigned, in
conjunction with Sergeant Komaki of the Japanese
Gendarmerie Headquarters, Bridge House, and Sergeant
Major Sakamoto and Sergeant Nakao of the Japanese
River Police, Floating Restaurant, carried out a
raid in Room 434 of the Oriental Hotel, Nanking
Road, at 3.30 p.m. 24.7.39.

On entering the room 434 the following
five persons were found present in the room:-
1) Fong Ah Zah (方阿才), 32, Ningpo, S/unemployed,
residing No.7 Rue de
Centy, F.G. (arrested).
2) Tsu Hai Pao (周海寶), alias
page_data.zh:
2/2.

授权其为游击队购买枪支，且据信其随身携带1,000.00美元。
日本宪兵队雇用的一名线人（姓名未披露）与这两人取得联系，并按指示伪装成军火商。线人与这两名游击队成员的会面定于本月2日下午2时在东方饭店434室进行。”

一支由Rhodes副督察、Shimidzu巡官、Yamahara巡官、Zia Vai Feng副督察长、华籍侦探206号、212号及本人组成的侦探小队，会同日本宪兵队总部（百老汇大厦）的Komaki警士，以及日本水上警察“浮动的餐厅”的坂本小头目和Nakao警士，于1939年7月24日下午3时30分对南京路东方饭店434室进行了突袭。

进入434室后，发现室内有以下五人：-
1) Fong Ah Zah (方阿才)，32岁，宁波人，职业/无业，住法租界金神父路7号（被捕）。
2) Tsu Hai Pao (周海寶)，别名

page_data.en:
2/3.

Wong Tah Cheng (王純昌), 30, Yanchow, S/Unemployed,
House 30, Route Blunt-
chelli, P.C. (Arrested)

3) Weng Koh Ding (王一定), Informer.
4) Tung Yih Ming (唐一鳴), " , and
|| 5) Senn, believes to be a Portuguese, informer.

Sergeant Major Sakamoto pointed out the
3rd, 4th and 5th mentioned persons as his informers,
who in turn, pointed out the 1st and 2nd above mentioned
men as the persons who wanted to make a purchase of
firearms for the guerilla unit, whilst the 5th men-
tioned, Senn, produced a document (attached with
translation) which implicates the 2nd mentioned, Tsu
Hai Dee, as a representative of the guerilla unit.

On being searched the first mentioned,
Fung Ah Sah, was found to be in possession of
$1,718.00 in Shanghai currency, 5 papers and 15
photographs. On the person of the second named,
Tsu Hai Dee, alias Wong Tah Cheng, a sum of $101.00
in Shanghai currency, was found. A search of the
room revealed nothing of an incriminating nature.

The arrested two men, Fung Ah Sah and
Tsu Hai Dee, were taken together with the 3rd
and 4th mentioned informers to C.I.D offices for
questioning.
page_data.zh:
2/3.

Wong Tah Cheng (王純昌)，30岁，盐城人，职业/无业，住公共租界Bluntchelli路30号房屋（被捕）

3) Weng Koh Ding (王一定)，线人。
4) Tung Yih Ming (唐一鳴)，同上，及
|| 5) Senn，据信为葡萄牙人，线人。

坂本小头目指出上述第3、4、5人为其线人，而这几名线人反过来指认上述第1和第2人为欲为游击队购买枪支之人；同时，第5人Senn出示了一份文件（附译文），牵连上述第2人Tsu Hai Dee为游击队代表。

经搜查，第一名嫌疑人Fung Ah Sah身上搜得上海货币1,718.00元、5份文件和15张照片。在第二名嫌疑人Tsu Hai Dee（别名Wong Tah Cheng）身上搜得上海货币101.00元。对房间的检查未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。

被捕的两名男子Fung Ah Sah和Tsu Hai Dee，连同上述第3和第4名线人，被带往刑事科办公室接受讯问。

page_data.en:
2/4.

However, on being questioned, the arrested
men, Fong Ah Zah and Tsu Hai Dee, both denied being
members of the Guerilla Unit or intended to make a
purchase of firearms.

Although the 2nd arrested Tsu Hai Dee
admitted to have signed the seized document, yet
pleaded his ignorance of the contents of the same.
He states that the 3rd and 4th mentioned informers
promised to secure a job of sailor through the 5th
mentioned informer, Sema, to whom they had to pay
a fee for procuring the job and to sign the document,
which they understood to be an agreement.

The arrested men stated that the seized
document was brought to the room by the informer
Sema.

The 3rd and 4th mentioned informers, on
being questioned, they aver that the arrested two
men wanted to buy 6 mauser pistols and that they
were acting as brokers for the informer Sema, who
posed as an arm dealer. Statements have been
taken from these two informers, which are now
being translated.

In view of the conflicting evidence existed
in this case as to the origin of the seized document
page_data.zh:
2/4.

然而，经讯问，被捕男子Fong Ah Zah和Tsu Hai Dee均否认是游击队成员或有意购买枪支。

虽然第二名被捕者Tsu Hai Dee承认签署了被扣押的文件，但辩称对该文件内容不知情。他称，上述第3和第4名线人承诺通过第5名线人Sema为他们谋取一份船员工作，他们需为此支付费用并签署该文件，他们理解这是一份协议。

被捕男子称，被扣押的文件是由线人Sema带入房间的。

经讯问，上述第3和第4名线人声称，两名被捕男子欲购买6支毛瑟手枪，而他们则是充当线人Sema的中间人，Sema伪装成军火商。已对这两名线人录取供词，目前正在翻译中。

鉴于本案中关于被扣押文件来源的证据存在矛盾，

page_data.en:

the undersigned requested Sergeant Major Sakamoto
to produce the informer Sena for questioning.
Sergeant Major Sakamoto promised to produce Sena
at 11 a.m. 25.7.39.

Statements are being taken from the arrested
men who are now being detained at the Central Station
cells pending completion of enquiries.

October 30, 1939.

S.M.P. Headquarters,
Shanghai.

Sirs,

I have been instructed to write to you in behalf
of the family of Mr. Wei Ta Chen (衛達成), who was arrested
by the Japanese authorities with the assistance of the
Municipal Police of Central Station on Yu Ya Ching Road
outside Shau Yau Dancing Hall (逍遙舞廳) at about 4 p.m.
on July 24, 1939, and has since been detained.

In April this year, Mr. Wei was appointed Adviser
to the Shanghai Armed Police Constabulary and a photographic
copy of his Certificate of Appointment is attached herewith
for your perusal. If you will be good enough to cause
enquiries to be made you will find that he is a respectable
man and has never had any connection with any improper
organisations.

In order to enable Mr. Wei to be released on
security, it is hoped that you will communicate with the
Japanese authorities with a view to clearing up all
misunderstandings.

Sheng Pei Tung
(Signed & chopped)

MINUTE TO ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER OF POLICE, CRIMINAL INTELLIGENCE BRANCH.

On the two suspects mentioned in this file, being questioned by detectives of C.I., it was learned that the 1st named Wei Yung Tsao (衛永初), holds the office of Aide-de-camp to one Han San Tao (韓三道) alias Han Chiun (韓君), the commander of a pro-Japanese armed force, operating in Tsu Ho Ching (曹河涇), Western Shanghai.

He claims that he met Han Chiun in an opium den off Rue Kratzer during February of this year and after becoming friendly was made Han's Aide-de-Camp.

On being questioned regarding the allegations made against him by the Japanese Authorities, Wei Yung Tsao claims that he has been falsely implicated by Sung Ying Ping (宋英平) the person arrested in Chapel by the Japanese, who is also a follower of Han Chiun and who became jealous over his appointment as Han's Aide-de-camp.

The 2nd named Tsang Ping Ling (張炳林) denies having any political connections and states that at the time of his arrest he was taking shelter from the rain and merely passed a remark on the

WEI YUNG TOOO (衛雲濤)
Shanghai
// S.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung
translated
C.1
25.7.39
/////// Clerk Hau.

My name is Wei Yung Tooo, alias Wei Teh Sung, age
40. native of Shanghai, married and residing at No. 48
Ying Yue Li, Route Kretzer, F.C.

I am employed as Aide-de-Camp to Han San Tao (韓雲濤),
alias Han Chiun (韓均), Chinese commanding officer of the
Si-Tseng ? ( a Japanese subject ) Army, stationed in Zau
Ho Ching, Western District, Shanghai.

I first became acquainted with Han Chiun in February
of this year in an opium den on Route Kretzer, French Con-
cession, where Han was introduced to me by one named Tseu
Hai Tsung (周海宗), a drug addict, in the den.

Since then we have become good friends, and Han
frequently called at my address. One day Han Chiun brought
to my home a Shantung man, (fellow-country man of Han) whom
he introduced me as "Lao Sung". This is the person who led
Japanese to arrest me.

Not long afterwards, I learned that Han Chiun
had been promoted to the rank of Commander-in-chief of
the Armed Police, under Japanese Commander Si-Tseng (?)
in Western district. I also learned that Lao Sung had
endeavoured in vain to procure a position in Han's office;
for this reason Lao Sung and Han Chiun became unfriended.
However, I was at that time appointed by Han Chiun as his
aide-de-camp.

A few days after my appointment, I was approached
by Lao Sung, who requested a loan of money from me, which,
I refused, the refusal incurring thereby Lao Sung's enmity.
page_data.zh:
卫云涛（WEI YUNG TOOO）
上海
// S.S.I. 宋品宗（Soong Ping Tsung）
译
C.1
1939年7月25日
/////// 书记员 Hau.

我叫卫云涛，别名卫德松（Wei Teh Sung），40岁，上海人，已婚，居住在法租界克拉茨路（Route Kretzer）映月里48号。

我受雇担任韩三道（Han San Tao，别名韩均 Han Chiun）的副官，韩是驻扎在上海西区曹河泾（Zau Ho Ching）的Si-Tseng ?（一名日本籍人士）军队的中国指挥官。

今年二月，我在法租界克拉茨路的一家鸦片馆初次结识韩均，当时由一名名叫周海宗（Tseu Hai Tsung）的吸毒者在馆内将我介绍给他。

此后我们成为好友，韩经常到我的住所拜访。一天，韩均带了一名山东人（韩的同乡）到我家，向我介绍他为“老宋”。这就是带领日本人逮捕我的人。

不久后，我得知韩均已被提升为西区日本指挥官Si-Tseng (?) 麾下武装警察的总指挥。我还得知老宋曾试图在韩的办公室谋得一职但未果；因此老宋与韩均关系破裂。然而，我当时被韩均任命为他的副官。

在我任职几天后，老宋找我借钱，我拒绝了，这一拒绝由此招致了老宋的敌意。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Since the date of my appointment I have ordered
for Han Chiun 500 suits of uniform and also introduced
to him, Kying Ding San (金廷山), Compradore of the
Ching Tah (正泰) Foreign Hong, whom he later appointed
the quartermaster of his army.

I have pro-Japanese tendencies, and do not known
or see any reason why the Japanese desired my arrest.

I have occasionally resided in the home of Mr.
Wong, alias Wong Leo Foo, who has a residence in the
Hongkew District, and who, through my recommendation,
was engaged as Adjutant to Han Chiun.

In the evening of 19th, July 1939, I went to
the Great World Amusement Resort and returned home at
12 mid-night, when I was informed by my housemates that
my room had been raided and searched by certain persons,
whom I later ascertained to be Japanese, and therefore
I took no heed about the search of my room.

At about 4 p.m. 24.7.39 I went to Merry Land
Cafe, Yu Ya Ching Road, intending to meet Ah Lai, proprietor
of the above cafe, for the purpose of borrowing money from
the latter.

On failing to meet Ah Lai, I walked out of the
Cafe and was subsequently arrested together with another
male Chinese, who is a stranger to me and I do not know
anything about him.

The above is my true statement.

Signed.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

自从我任职以来，我已为韩均订购了500套制服，并向他介绍了正泰（Ching Tah）洋行的买办金廷山（Kying Ding San），韩后来任命他为军队的军需官。

我有亲日倾向，不知道也不明白日本人为何要逮捕我。

我曾偶尔居住在黄先生（别名黄立夫 Wong Leo Foo）家中，他在虹口区有一处住宅，经我推荐，他被韩均聘为副官。

1939年7月19日晚，我去大世界游乐场，午夜12点回家时，室友告诉我我的房间被一些人搜查过，我后来得知这些人是日本人，因此我对房间被搜查一事并未在意。

1939年7月24日下午4点左右，我去亚亚清路（Yu Ya Ching Road）的Merry Land Cafe，打算见该咖啡馆老板阿莱（Ah Lai），目的是向他借钱。

因未见到阿莱，我走出咖啡馆，随后与另一名我不认识的华籍男子一起被捕，我对他一无所知。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名。

page_data.en:
TSANG PING LING (曾炳靈)
Kading, // C.D.S. 2
translated
C.1 25.7.39 /////// Hsu S.F.

My name is Tsang Ping Ling, alias Tsang Ying,
aged 18 years, native of Kading, a broker, employed
at the Asia Life Insurance Co., and residing with my
parents at the Chiun An (均安) Primary School, off
Ling-ping Road near Yoh Zai Road.

Owing to inconvenience of going to Nanshow district
after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, I
temporarily reside in the home of my god-father, situated
at No.99 Wuting Road, and some time abide in my friend's
place at the Woo Ts (伍子) Hospital on Yanning Road.

At the age of 8 I attended the Yoh Zai (約仔)
Primary School, and after graduation in the above school
I went to study in the Tung Hai (東海) Business Middle
School, which school I left 6 months later, due to the
current hostilities.

About a month ago a friend of mine, named Tang
Ting Chong (鄧定昌), who, well knowing my financial
difficulties and taking pity on me, recommended me to the
Asia Life Insurance Co., where I secured the present position
as a broker.

At approx. 4 p.m. on 24.7.39 I came out of the
Billiard Room in the Chinese Y.M.C.A., Boul. de Montigny,
F.C., and, taking a Route 18 tram-trolley, proceeded to
the intersection of Nanking and Ya Ya Ching Roads, where
I alighted and, on account of it raining very heavily at
the time, I went to take shelter at the Merry Land Cabaret.
About 15 minutes later when I was standing outside the
page_data.zh:
曾炳灵（TSANG PING LING）
嘉定， // C.D.S. 2
译
C.1 1939年7月25日 /////// Hsu S.F.

我叫曾炳灵，别名曾英（Tsang Ying），18岁，嘉定人，经纪人，受雇于亚洲人寿保险公司，与父母居住在约仔路（Yoh Zai Road）附近令平路（Ling-ping Road）旁的均安（Chiun An）小学。

由于中日敌对行动爆发后前往南市（Nanshow）地区不便，我暂时寄居在位于吴亭路（Wuting Road）99号的教父家中，有时也住在延安路（Yanning Road）伍子（Woo Ts）医院的朋友处。

我8岁时进入约仔（Yoh Zai）小学就读，从该校毕业后，我进入东海（Tung Hai）商业中学学习，后因当前战事，六个月后离校。

大约一个月前，我的朋友邓定昌（Tang Ting Chong）深知我的经济困难并同情我，将我推荐到亚洲人寿保险公司，我在那里获得了目前的经纪人职位。

1939年7月24日下午4点左右，我从法租界蒙太尼路（Boul. de Montigny）中华青年会的台球室出来，乘坐18路电车前往南京路与亚亚清路交叉口，下车后因当时雨下得很大，我便去Merry Land Cabaret避雨。大约15分钟后，当我站在上述

page_data.en:
- 2 -

gate of the above cabaret, an unknown male Chinese suddenly
appeared beside me and talked to me about the expected
shower. No sooner had I given a reply to the above
than a party of detectives, accompanied by Japanese,
appeared before us, immediately taking that unknown
person and myself into their custody, the reason for
which is unknown to me.

Signed:
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

歌舞厅门口时，一名陌生的华籍男子突然出现在我身边，与我谈论即将下的阵雨。我刚回答了他，一群由日本人陪同的侦探就出现在我们面前，立即将那名陌生人和我自己拘捕，其原因我不得而知。

签名：

At 3.15 p.m. 3.8.39 Mr. Matsuda, assistant manager
of the N.K.K. Co., called at Crime Branch Headquarters
and as a result of the ensuing interview, it was
ascertained that the statement as made by Tsang Dah Hoo
(張大宏) was correct, i.e. Mr. Matsuda explained
that about one year ago he visited Tsang Wong Kong
(曾旺江) in Zu-Kao Hsien for purpose of opening
an N.K.K. Agency and through the introduction and
recommendation of the Japanese Gendarmerie at that
place, he engaged Tsang Dah Hoo as the N.K.K. Co.
Agent.

In concluding this interview Mr. Matsuda further
explained that since joining the N.K.K. Co. about
one year ago, Tsang Dah Hoo has carried out the duties
required of him in a very efficient and trustworthy
manner, and that as far as the N.K.K. Co. were concerned
they knew of nothing that would be detrimental to his
character.

1939年8月3日下午3:15，N.K.K.公司副经理松田（Matsuda）先生来到刑事侦缉处总部，经过随后的面谈，查明张大宏（Tsang Dah Hoo）所作的陈述是正确的，即松田先生解释说，大约一年前，他为了开设N.K.K.代理处而去朱家角县（Zu-Kao Hsien）拜访曾旺江（Tsang Wong Kong），并通过当地日本宪兵队的介绍和推荐，雇佣张大宏担任N.K.K.公司的代理人。

In the beginning of July 1939, I was informed
by someone at Zah Teong Village (石莊鎮) that Lien 3
(刘9), a loafer in Tsang Vang Keng (張黃港)

I have been't the business agent for the Nishin

I have never collected tax from others, neither have I
signed any receipts to that effect. The manager in either
Tsang Vang Keng or Sing Sang Hong should take responsibilities
for the transporting of cargoes to Shanghai. I have not been
in Tsang Vang Keng since the 2nd Moon (Lunar Calendar) this
year. I know nothing about the transporting of 944 baskets

(翻译    张松藩 (Tsang Sung Fan)
XXXXXXXX

1939年7月初，我接到石莊鎮 (Zah Teong Village) 某人通知，称在距离石莊鎮九里的張黃港 (Tsang Vang Keng) 的一个无业游民刘9 (Lien 3)，因向当地居民勒索钱财而被日本军方当局逮捕；当其家属前往军司令部询问逮捕原因时，被告知他已于前夜从羁押中逃脱。三四天后，刘9的尸体在張黃港附近被发现，并由其子妥善入殓。

我担任日清汽船株式会社 (Nishin Kisen Kaisha) 的业务代理已有一年多，在此期间，我从未向他人收取税款，也未签署过任何此类收据。張黃港或新生港 (Sing Sang Hong) 的经理应对运往上海的货物承担责任。自今年农历二月以来，我未曾去过張黃港。我对将944篮鸡蛋运往上海一事一无所知。

签名：张大虎

page_data.en:
LEE AH SUNG (李大成)
Honan // C.D.C. 164
26.7.39 Hsu

My name is Lee Dah Sung, aged 40 years, native
of Honan, employed as a coolie at the Asia Transportation
Company, and residing at 2 Ching Poh Li, Shense Road.
I went to Room 301, Central Hotel, to meet
Peu Ping Tsung, foreman coolie, for the purpose of
discussing transportation business.
Due to the late hours of the night I slept with
Peu in the above room.
I do not know Tsang Dui Hoo, nor have I any
knowledge of my arrest.
The above is my true statement.

Signed:
page_data.zh:
李大成 (LEE AH SUNG)
河南 // C.D.C. 164
1939年7月26日 徐

我叫李大成，40岁，籍贯河南，受雇于亚洲运输公司 (Asia Transportation Company) 做苦力，居住在申赛路 (Shense Road) 清福里2号。
我去中央饭店301室会见工头苦力潘品仲 (Peu Ping Tsung)，目的是商讨运输业务。
由于夜深，我便与潘在上述房间过夜。
我不认识张大虎 (Tsang Dui Hoo)，也不知道我被捕的原因。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：

A search of this room resulted in the
seizure of the following documents etc. :-

"Four Chinese receipt books pertaining to

"Three invitations to Japanese requesting
their presence at a Chinese dinner
to be held at Mei Ling (眉 齡 )
Sing Song House, Wei Teh Li (衛德里),
on the evening of July 13th, 1939".

"One letter in Chinese addressed to Tsung
Dah Kuo of a personal nature from
a friend".

"Sixteen Chinese visiting cards".

"Eleven Japanese and foreign visiting cards".

"Six papers in Chinese purely of a personal
nature".

"One receipt pertaining to the purchase of
a 'Radio'."

"$10.40 in notes".

"One wallet".

All documents etc., when examined at this
office, were found to contain nothing that would in any
way substantiate the allegations that these men were
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

(3) 林锋 (LING SAI POONG)，22岁，籍贯金波 (Kempo)，单身，“鸡行”经纪人，住法租界新闸新 (Sing Kai Wee) 35号。

(4) 李大成 (LEE DAH ZUNG)，40岁，籍贯罗曼 (Roman)，非裔，苦力工头，住山西路 (Shanse Road) 景奉里22号。

对该房间的搜查导致查获以下文件等物：

“四本属于国际救济协会 (International Relief Society) 的中文收据簿”。

“三份邀请日本人参加定于1939年7月13日晚在眉龄 (Mei Ling) 卫德里 (Wei Teh Li) 歌厅举行的中式晚宴的请柬”。

“一封朋友写给宗达国 (Tsung Dah Kuo) 的私人性质中文信件”。

“十六张中文名片”。

“十一张日文及外国名片”。

“六份纯属私人性质的中文文件”。

“一张购买‘收音机’的收据”。

“纸币10.40美元”。

“一个钱包”。

“一枚德国远东轮船公司 (German Far East S.S. Company) ‘久米丸’ (S.S. Kumi) 轮的徽章”。

所有文件等物在本办公室检查后，发现没有任何内容能证实这些人

page_data.en:
- 3 -

concerned in Guerilla activities, but on the contrary
showed all four to be business men, the first named
being an employee of the Nishin Kisen Kaisha.
On being brought to Station the 1st named
was informed of the allegations made against him by the
Japanese Gendarmerie, which was to the effect that he,
Tsang Dah Hoo, was a subordinate of Tsung Chih Foh
(〔此处转录不清〕), Commander of Chinese Guerillas operating
in the Tungchow area, and in making an emphatic denial
of this he made the attached written statement which in
addition to showing that he was a resident of Japan for
36 years, also to some extent shows the reason for his
arrest.
The remaining three, when questioned, made
written statements showing their associations with the
1st named were and still are purely of a business
nature, also that they knew nothing of what transpired
in the Central Hotel on the afternoon of 26-7-39, when
the two Japanese named Yamada and Sugiura called on
Tsang Dah Hoo.
The facts as outlined in this report and
statements were explained to Sgt. Major Hatsui of the
Japanese Water Police, at whose request these persons
had been arrested and he left Crime Branch Headquarters
at 8.30 a.m. 26-7-39, explaining that he would return
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

参与游击活动，相反，显示这四人均是商人，其中第一名为日清汽船株式会社的雇员。
第一名嫌疑人被带到警局后，被告知其被日本宪兵队指控的内容，即他张大虎是在通州地区活动的中国游击队指挥官宗志佛 (Tsung Chih Foh) 〔此处转录不清〕的下属；他在坚决否认这一指控时，作出了附后的书面陈述，该陈述除表明他在日本居住了36年外，也在一定程度上显示了他被捕的原因。
其余三人在接受讯问时，作出了书面陈述，表明他们与第一名的关系过去和现在都纯粹是商业性质的，并且他们对1939年7月26日下午两名日本人山田 (Yamada) 和杉浦 (Sugiura) 拜访张大虎时在中央饭店发生的事情一无所知。
本报告及陈述中概述的事实已向日本水上警察的初井 (Hatsui) 警佐解释，这些人是应他的要求被捕的；他于1939年7月26日上午8时30分离开刑事科总部，并表示他将返回

page_data.en:
- 4 -

later, after he had made some further enquiries from his
informer, whose name etc. he did not divulge.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

John Campbell
D. S. P.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

稍后回来，在他向其线人（他未透露其姓名等信息）进行进一步查询之后。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

副警务处长

Sir,
At 6.30 p.m. July 25, 1939,Lieutenant Tohida
of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters, Bridge House,
requested,on behalf of the Japanese Military Water Police,
Floating restaurant, that our assistance be rendered
in effecting the arrest of 4 (four) or 5 (five) persons
who are alleged to be members of a guerrilla unit.
According to Lieutenant Tohida, these persons
are to be located at a certain hotel situated on the
east side of Yu Ya Ching Road, and the officer wished

At 7.30 p.m. same date, Sergeant Komaki of the
Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters called at the C.1.
Office,C.B.H.Q., on behalf of Lieutenant Tohida, and
asked for the temporary cancellation of the raid.owing
to the lack of information.
Sergeant Komaki further requested that the raid
be carried out at 5.00 a.m. July 26, 1939,on the same

1939年7月25日。

日本宪兵总部代表日本军用水上警察请求协助。
副警务处长 山原 (Yamahara)

先生，
1939年7月25日下午6时30分，日本宪兵总部（百老汇大厦）的户田 (Tohida) 中尉代表日本军用水上警察（浮式餐厅），请求我方协助逮捕据称为游击队成员的4至5人。
据户田中尉称，这些人位于鱼牙精路 (Yu Ya Ching Road) 东侧的某家旅馆内，该军官希望尽快实施突袭。
同日晚上7时30分，日本宪兵总部的小牧 (Komaki) 警士代表户田中尉来到刑事科总部办公室，因缺乏情报，要求暂时取消突袭行动。
小牧警士进一步要求于1939年7月26日凌晨5时，在罗渣区 (Louza District) 的某地对同一目标实施突袭。

page_data.en:
TUNG TA HU (张大虎), age 50, married,
Su-kao, Koupo                      x       C.D.S. 172
H. . . C. B.          26-7-39      translated      Tsuang Zung Pau

I am in the transportation business and residing
at Room 301 of the Central Hotel, 545 Canton Road.
I am a native of Zah Tsong Village (石莊鄉).
Su-kao Hsien (如皋縣), Kiangsu Province. During my childhood
I studied at a school for four years. At the age of 14, I
was taken by my brother-in-law, Tseu Ts Ching (周子卿), to
Kobe, where I became an apprentice at the Sien Yih (全益)
Native Bank. At the age of 19, I completed my apprenticeship
but still remained in the bank as an assistant. During the
year 1925, Tseu Chia Pau (周家保), the proprietor of the Sien
Yih Native Bank, closed down his business and I therefore lost
my job. Through the introduction of my friend, Yui Shang
Ching (俞秀慶), I became the manager and also a partner in the
Hyeon Yih (源益) Native Bank, in Kobe. I remained there
until April 1937, when I returned to Shanghai with my family.
As it was impossible for me to proceed to Japan after the
outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in July, I decided
to stay in my native place, from where I addressed a letter
to the Hyeon Yih Native Bank in Kobe, giving instructions to
the staff regarding the handling of business affairs. Owing to
the business depression resulting from the Sino-Japanese
hostilities, I wrote to my bank in Kobe during the spring of
1938, advising them to suspend business immediately. I then
stayed at my home at Zah Tsong Village, Su-kao Hsien, until
March 1938, when I was appointed as the chairman of the
Maintenance Association following the Japanese occupation of
this village. I remained in this post till January 1939, when
page_data.zh:
张大虎 (TUNG TA HU)，50岁，已婚，
江苏如皋县石庄乡                      x       C.D.S. 172
H. . . C. B.          1939年7月26日      翻译      庄宗保 (Tsuang Zung Pau)

我从事运输业，居住在广东路545号中央饭店301室。
我籍贯江苏省如皋县石庄乡 (Zah Tsong Village)。童年时我在学校读了四年书。14岁时，我被姐夫周子卿 (Tseu Ts Ching) 带到神户，在全益 (Sien Yih) 钱庄当学徒。19岁时，我出师但仍留在钱庄当助手。1925年间，全益钱庄老板周家保 (Tseu Chia Pau) 停业，因此我失业。经朋友俞秀庆 (Yui Shang Ching) 介绍，我成为神户源益 (Hyeon Yih) 钱庄的经理兼合伙人。我一直留在那里直到1937年4月，随后携家人返回上海。由于7月中日敌对行动爆发后我无法前往日本，我决定留在家乡，并从那里给神户的源益钱庄去信，指示员工处理业务事宜。由于中日敌对行动导致的商业萧条，我在1938年春写信给神户的银行，建议他们立即停业。此后我一直住在如皋县石庄乡的家中，直到1938年3月，在该村被日军占领后，我被任命为维持会主席。我担任此职直到1939年1月，当时

page_data.en:
- 2 -

I tendered my resignation immediately after this Association
had been re-organised and altered to the name of "Zah Tsong
Village Guild". I then operated a concern known as the
Poo Yih (普益) Transportation Co., which, besides undertaking
transportation of goods at Tsang Wang Keng (張黃港) and
Sing Sung Zong (新生港) in Lu-kno lisien, acts as the agent for
the Nishin Kisen Kaisha (Shanghai) at the above two places.
On the 6-7-39, Tai To Ping (戴子賓), the proprietor of Hung
Zung Transportation Co., accompanied by three Japanese named
Sei Dien (小田); Soh Dien (古田) and Dien Dai (田代),
visited my office at Sing Sung Keng and asked me to hand over
all account books etc. relating to the Nishin Kisen Kaisha, to
which I objected. On the 10-7-39 I came to Shanghai and
interviewed Soong Dien (松田), Japanese manager of the Nishin
Kisen Kaisha in Shanghai, who offered mediation in our
dispute by suggesting that Tai To Ping and I should work
together in this business with the addition of two Japanese
and that an addendum be made in the original contract.
I, however, refused to comply with this proposal.
I was subsequently taken into custody this morning.

Signed, Cross-marked & Thumb-printed : TSANG DAH HOO.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

在该协会改组并更名为“石庄乡公会”后，我立即辞职。随后我经营一家名为普益运输公司 (Poo Yih Transportation Co.) 的企业，该公司除了在如皋县的張黃港 (Tsang Wang Keng) 和新生港 (Sing Sung Zong) 承担货物运输外，还在这两个地方担任日清汽船株式会社（上海）的代理。
1939年7月6日，洪众运输公司 (Hung Zung Transportation Co.) 老板戴子宾 (Tai To Ping) 在三名日本人小田 (Sei Dien)、古田 (Soh Dien) 和田代 (Dien Dai) 的陪同下，访问了我在新生港的办事处，要求我移交所有与日清汽船株式会社有关的账簿等物，对此我表示反对。1939年7月10日，我来到上海，会见了日清汽船株式会社上海日方经理松田 (Soong Dien)，他提议通过调解解决我们的纠纷，建议戴子宾和我共同经营此项业务，另加两名日本人，并在原合同中增加补充条款。
然而，我拒绝接受这一提议。
随后我于今晨被拘留。

签名、画押并按手印：张大虎。

page_data.en:
LING SAI POONG (林銳鋒)
Kompo // S.D.C. 184.
3.1. 26.7.39 Hsu.

My name is Ling Sai Poong, aged 22 years, native
of Kompo, single, employed at the Shanghai Hen & Duck
Merchants Union, and residing at No. 37 The French Bund.

I was sent to receive hens and ducks in Sing
Kong and returned to Shanghai on 23.7.39.

During my stay in Sing Kong I was informed
by Chiu Vih Seh (邱維世), employee of the Fu Ching Agency,
that Tsang Dah Hoo (曾大虎) was staying at Room 301,
Central Hotel, Shanghai.

At 10 p.m. 25.7.39, I called on Tsang at the
above room for the purpose of asking him if any ship
sailed for Sing Kong.

Owing to the curfew restrictions being declared
in the late night, I could not return to my shop and
had to stay in the room. Unexpectedly the room was
raided by a party of detectives together with Japanese,
and I was brought to the Station.

The above is my true statement.

Signed : Ling Sai Poong.
page_data.zh:
林锐锋 (LING SAI POONG)
金波 (Kompo) // S.D.C. 184.
1939年7月26日 3.1. 徐。

我叫林锐锋，22岁，籍贯金波，单身，受雇于上海鸡鸭商公会 (Shanghai Hen & Duck Merchants Union)，居住在法大马路 (The French Bund) 37号。

我被派往新港 (Sing Kong) 接收鸡鸭，并于1939年7月23日返回上海。

在新港期间，富成洋行 (Fu Ching Agency) 雇员邱维世 (Chiu Vih Seh) 告诉我，曾大虎 (Tsang Dah Hoo) 住在上海中央饭店301室。

1939年7月25日晚上10点，我到上述房间拜访曾，目的是询问他是否有船开往新港。

由于深夜宣布实行宵禁，我无法返回店铺，只好留在房间里。出乎意料的是，一群侦探会同日本人突袭了该房间，并将我带到警局。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：林锐锋。

page_data.en:
Pang Ping Tsong (潘品仲),
Honan                                C.D.C. 194
C.l,C.B.H.C.        26.7.39       translated          Clark Hsia
                                    /////////

My name is Pang Ping Tsong (潘品仲), age 39,
native of Honan, married, foreman of the Yuen Tong (遠東)
Transportation Company, residing at No.22 Ching Woh Lane,
Shanse Road.

On 19th. July, 1939, I knew that the s.s. "Kang
Teh" of the Poo Yih (普益) Steamship Company arrived
Shanghai. I then went to see one named Tai Tsing (戴清),
chairman of board of directors of the Poo Yih Steamship
Company, to negotiate the transportation of cargoes. I was
introduced to one named Tsang Dah Hoo (張大虎), manager
of the above mentioned company by Tai. Tsang used to open
a room No.501, Central Hotel. Therefore, I usually went
to see him to negotiate some business transactions.

At 10 p.m. 25.7.39, I visited Tsang in the room
No.501, Central Hotel, where I asked him if there is any
business for me. Owing to the restriction of curfew, I had
stayed there. At 4 a.m. 26th. July, 1939, a party of S.M.
Police together with Japanese came to our room and took me
into custody. Later, I was conveyed to the Police Headquarter
This is a true statement.

Signed: Pang Ping Tsong
page_data.zh:
潘品仲 (Pang Ping Tsong)，
河南                                C.D.C. 194
C.l,C.B.H.C.        1939年7月26日       翻译          夏克拉克 (Clark Hsia)
                                    /////////

我叫潘品仲，39岁，籍贯河南，已婚，远东 (Yuen Tong) 运输公司工头，居住在山西路 (Shanse Road) 清和里22号。

1939年7月19日，我得知普益轮船公司 (Poo Yih Steamship Company) 的“康德”号 (Kang Teh) 轮船抵达上海。随后我去见普益轮船公司董事长戴清 (Tai Tsing)，洽谈货物运输事宜。戴将我介绍给上述公司的经理张大虎。张过去常在中央饭店开501室。因此，我通常去那里见他洽谈一些业务交易。

1939年7月25日晚上10点，我在中央饭店501室拜访张，问他是否有业务给我。由于宵禁限制，我便留宿在那里。1939年7月26日凌晨4点，一队公共租界巡捕会同日本人来到我们房间，将我拘留。后来，我被押送至警察总局。
此为真实陈述。

签名：潘品仲

3.

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

Further enquiries were made at 384 Peking
Road on the morning of 29.7.39 and it was ascer-
tained that the office that was raided on the
ground floor of this building had been rented for
the past twelve months by Vung Yu Soo Wu (風雨書屋).
No information could be obtained regarding the
names of the persons who occupied this office.
On information supplied by the Japanese
Consular Police, five packing cases were found in
an alleyway at the back of this office, which con-
tain what appears to be communistic literature.
These five packing cases were removed to C.B.H.Q.
and specimens of the literature submitted to the
Special Branch for perusal. On the morning of
31.7.39 a further examination of the contents of
this office was made together with members of
the Japanese Consular Police and the following
were seized for further investigations:-
A large number of photographs.
A number of books.
One silver ornament, bearing the name of the
accused.
A number of printing blocks.

关于协助日本领事警察一事

1939年7月29日上午，对北京路384号进行了进一步调查，查明该建筑底层遭突击搜查的办公室在过去十二个月内由“风雨书屋”租用。未能获取占用该办公室人员的姓名信息。
根据日本领事警察提供的情报，在该办公室后巷发现了五个包装箱，内装看似共产主义性质的文献。这五个包装箱已被移至刑事处总部，并将文献样本提交给特别处审阅。1939年7月31日上午，会同日本领事警察成员对该办公室内容物进行了进一步检查，并扣押了以下物品以供进一步调查：-
大量照片。
若干书籍。
一件银质饰品，刻有被告姓名。
若干印刷铅块。

The seized books have been submitted to

inserting in a newspaper, but some of them may

The translations of the seized documents

A statement has been taken from the accused,
a copy of which is attached. This statement does
not incriminate the accused in any way.

He was born in Ong Yee Hsien, Pootung.
He received his elementary education at his native
place and later at Kiangsu 2nd Normal School, Nantao.
In 1925 when he was 25 years old he went to Tokyo
and studied art at the Tokyo Art School for 7 years
and at the Tokyo Imperial University for 2 years.
His studies were paid for by the Chinese Government
as he was successful in examinations sponsored by

page_data.en:
Ching Yoh Tsung (金学成)
Pootung                                D.S.I. Pryde
C.1.C.B.11...        31.7.39           Clerk Hsia

My name is Ching Yoh Tsung (金学成), age 35,
native of Pootung.
    I was born in Ong Yee Hsien (奉賢縣), Pootung,
where my father was a teacher in the Ong Yee Primary School.
From the age of 7 years to 13 years I attended the Ong Yee
Primary School. From 13 years to 19 years of age I studied
the Kiangsu 2nd. Normal School, West Gate, Nantuo. I then
obtained a position as a teacher in the 2nd. Shanghai District
Primary School, Yang Ka Doo, Pootung (浦東楊家渡上海縣立第二小學)
and remained there for two years. For the next three years
I studied art in the Central College, Nanking. In 1925, when
I was 25 years of age I went to Tokyo and studied art in the
Tokyo Art School for 7 years. My studies were paid for by the
Chinese Government as I was successful in examinations sponsored
by the Government Educational Bureau. I then entered the
Tokyo Imperial University for two years still studying art.
    Owing to the outbreak of hostilities between Japan
and China my studies had to cease and I returned to Shanghai
in January 1938. I then obtained a position as teacher of the
Japanese language in the Shanghai Law School, 2nd. floor, 384
Peking Road which is a branch of the Shanghai Law School situated
on Route de Boissezon, French Concession. I resigned from this
position in January 1939 as I obtained a position as business
manager of the Hwa Mei Chin Pao (華美晨報), Room 408 Shanghai
Times Building, Avenue Edward VII, at a salary of $100.00
per month, which was later reduced to $60.00 per month. I was
only the business manager and had nothing to do with the
page_data.zh:
金学成 (Ching Yoh Tsung)
浦东                                副督察长 Pryde
C.1.C.B.11...        1939年7月31日           书记员 Hsia

我叫金学成，35岁，籍贯浦东。
    我出生于浦东奉贤县，父亲是奉贤小学的教员。
    7岁至13岁期间，我就读于奉贤小学。13岁至19岁期间，我就读于南市西门的江苏省立第二师范学校。随后，我在浦东杨家渡上海县立第二小学获得教员职位，并在那里工作了两年。接下来的三年，我在南京中央大学学习艺术。1925年，我25岁时前往东京，在东京美术学校学习艺术7年。我的学业费用由中国政府支付，因为我通过了政府教育局主办的考试。随后我进入东京帝国大学继续学习艺术两年。
    由于中日战事爆发，我的学业被迫中断，我于1938年1月返回上海。随后，我在上海法学院获得日语教师职位，该院位于北京路384号二楼，是位于法租界蒲石路（Route de Boissezon）的上海法学院分院。1939年1月我辞去该职务，因为在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）上海时报大厦408室获得了《华美晨报》业务经理的职位，月薪100美元，后减至每月60美元。我只是业务经理，与

page_data.en:
(2)

editorial department, or the policy of this newspaper.
The morning edition of this paper ceased on June
1st. 1939, but I have still continued to work for this firm
collecting outstanding accounts etc.

As my firm ceased to rent the office in the Shanghai
Times Building on July 21, 1939, I moved a filing cabinet,
account books, and old newspaper files to No.384 Peking Road
where I rented office space from one named Tsang Zah Ying
(張者英) for $10.00 per month. I continued to use this
office until arrested. I understood from Tsang Zah Ying that
he was previously employed with the British Publishing Co.
(大英圖書出版公司), Ningpo Road, the manager of which was a
British subject named Mr. Bates (Sanders - Bates). This
company is now closed down. With the exception of the filing
cabinet, newspaper files etc., that I have already mentioned,
all the other property in this office belongs to Tsang Zah
Ying. The packing cases containing books which are stored
in the alleyway outside the office belong to Tsang Zah Ying.
I understood from Tsang Zah Ying that these are actually the
property of the British Publishing Co.

I have never been concerned in any anti-Japanese
activities, neither have any connection with agents of the
Chinese Nationalist Government, and I have no idea why I
should have been arrested.

Signed:- Ching Yeh Tsang.

该报的编辑部或政策无关。
该报的早版于1939年6月1日停刊，但我仍继续为该机构工作，负责催收欠款等事务。

由于我司于1939年7月21日停止租用上海时报大厦的办公室，我将一个文件柜、账簿和旧报纸档案搬至北京路384号，我以每月10美元的价格从名为张者英的人手中租用了办公空间。我一直使用该办公室直至被捕。我从张者英处得知，他此前受雇于宁波路的大英图书出版公司，该公司经理是一位名为贝茨（桑德斯-贝茨）的英国侨民。该公司现已关闭。除我已提及的文件柜、报纸档案等外，该办公室内的其他所有财产均归张者英所有。存放在办公室外巷子里装有书籍的包装箱也属于张者英。我从张者英处了解到，这些实际上是大英图书出版公司的财产。

我从未参与任何反日活动，也与国民党政府特工没有任何联系，我不知道自己为何会被捕。

签名：- Ching Yeh Tsang.

28.7.39 and requested assistance to raid Room 409
of the Tung Yu Trust Co., 384 Peking Road to arrest

of being concerned in guerrilla activities. They
also stated that if this man was arrested he should
be able to lead the raiding party to a certain room
on the ground floor of this building where a quantity
of anti-Japanese literature could be seized.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I.s Fryde and
Soong Ping Tsung, D.S.s Fowler, Sugimoto, D.P.S.
Yamahara, C.D.S. 272, C.D.C.s 184 and 206 and the
stated address raided at 10.45 p.m. In Room 409
the wanted man:-
Ching Yoh Tsung (金学成), 35, Footung,
M/Unemployed, 384 Peking Road
was arrested. His wife, mother-in-law and two
sons were also in the room but as the Consular
Police did not require these persons, they were not
arrested. A search of the room was made and a number
of documents seized, also a number of keys. When

协助日本领事警察

参照日记第1号，日本领事警察的藤田副督察、野田副督察及另外两名警官于1939年7月28日晚上10点30分来到刑事处总部，请求协助突击搜查北京路384号通裕信托公司409室，以逮捕一名涉嫌参与游击活动的名为金学成的人。他们还表示，如果此人被捕，他应能带领突击队员前往该建筑底层的某个房间，那里可以查获大量反日文献。

弗赖德和宋炳宗副督察长、福勒和杉本副督察、山原警佐、华捕272号以及华捕184号和206号提供了协助，并于晚上10点45分对上述地址进行了突击搜查。在409室，目标人物：-
金学成，35岁，浦东，
男/无业，北京路384号
被捕。他的妻子、岳母和两个儿子也在房间内，但由于领事警察不需要这些人，他们未被逮捕。对房间进行了搜查，查获了一些文件以及一些钥匙。当

page_data.en:
2/2

questioned the arrested man admitted having an office
on the ground floor and produced the keys for same.
On this office being visited it was found to be
composed of two rooms containing three desks, filing
cabinets and the usual office furniture. Two packets
of what the Consular Police claim to be anti-Japanese
literature were seized.

As there are a very large amount of account
books, documents, newspapers etc., in these offices,
detectives have been posted there with instructions
to arrest any one who visits there and further
enquiries regarding the contents of these offices
will be made tomorrow.

The arrested man states that he is at present
unemployed but that up to three months ago he was
employed as manager of the Hwa Mei Wan Pao. He
lived in Japan for 10 years and returned to China
in January 1938. He speaks Japanese. He has been
detained in Central Station Cells pending further
enquiries.

H.S.G

G. B. Suple
D.S.I.

经讯问，被捕男子承认在一楼拥有一间办公室，并出示了该办公室的钥匙。
经查访该办公室，发现其由两间房间组成，内有三张办公桌、文件柜及常规办公家具。查获了两包领事警察声称是反日宣传品的刊物。

由于这些办公室内有大量账簿、文件、报纸等物品，已派遣侦探驻守于此，指令逮捕任何前往该处的人员，并将于明日对这些办公室内的物品内容作进一步调查。

被捕男子称目前失业，但三个月前受雇为《华美晚报》（Hwa Mei Wan Pao）经理。他在日本居住了10年，于1938年1月返回中国。他会讲日语。他已被拘押在中央捕房拘留所，以待进一步调查。

TRANSLATION

21st. May.

Dear Mr. Voong Wei,

I arrived in Kobe at 3 p.m. today (21st. May).
At 8 a.m. tomorrow I shall take the train to Tokyo. The
route for our trip is specially prepared by the Ministry
of Railways. I shall ultimately board the s.s. "Shanghai
Maru" on the 14th. of next month to return to Shanghai.
On the 31st. inst. I shall leave Tokyo for Kyoto and in
that case the date for my return to Shanghai will be one
week earlier. If the definite date is affixed, I shall
write you in due course. By that time your assistance
will be requested to notify the telegraph Co. to detail
someone to meet me at the wharf, as the representatives
of the Central China Railway Co. are not familiar with
the local conditions. A duty of $18.00 was levied
on the articles which I had brought with me. I do not
know whether there is anything to be brought back on
my return to Shanghai. Will you please contact with
my Coy. to see if they could make arrangements re the
possibility of being granted free of duty.

Signed: Jien Ming.
page_data.zh:
译文

5月21日。

亲爱的 Voong Wei 先生：

我今天（5月21日）下午3点抵达神户。明天上午8点我将乘火车前往东京。我们的行程路线由铁道省特别安排。我最终将于下个月14日乘坐“上海丸”轮返回上海。本月31日我将离开东京前往京都，那样的话，我返回上海的日期将提前一周。如果确定日期，我会及时写信告知你。届时将请你协助通知电报公司派人到码头接我，因为华中铁道公司的代表不熟悉当地情况。对我随身携带的物品征收了18.00美元的关税。我不知道回上海时是否有东西要带回来。请你与我的公司联系，看看他们能否就免除关税的可能性做出安排。

签名：Jien Ming。

page_data.en:
TRANSLATION

24th May 1939.

Dear Mr. Voong Wei,

I have written to you sometimes.
On 22nd inst. (May 1939) I arrived in Tokyo, Japan
and reside at Room No. 115, the Imperial Hotel.
I am very busy to attend social calling during
these few days. At 4 p.m. today Mr. Tomida,
accompanied me to visit the Ministry of Postal
Affairs and his deputy. I have also visited chief
and sectional chief of the official bureau. The
Ministry of Postal Affairs would invite me to attend
a dinner party but I did not accept his invitation
because I have previous engagement. I will go to
Yokohama on the 27th inst. Siang Keng would return
to Tokyo on 29th and he would go to Zah Tan and Ts
Chu on 30th. On 1st June he would return to Tokyo
again, and three days later he would go to Tsing Too,
Yah Kwei. On the 13th he will take S.S. "Shanghai Maru"
in Nagasaki and he will arrive Shanghai on the 14th.
If there is no delay, he will arrive in Shanghai on
time. Please tell Mr. Foo Dee regarding my visit to
the Ministry of Postal Affairs. Will you please also
inform my family that I am safe.

Signed : Chien Ming

P. S. If Mr. Foo Dee arrive in Tokyo on the 2nd
I would see him and on the 3rd I shall
leave Tokyo.
page_data.zh:
译文

1939年5月24日。

亲爱的 Voong Wei 先生：

我曾多次给你写信。
本月22日（1939年5月）我抵达日本东京，住在帝国酒店115号房间。
这几天我忙于应酬拜访。今天下午4点，富田先生（Mr. Tomida）陪同我拜访了邮政省及其次官。我还拜访了官房长官和科长。邮政省邀请我参加晚宴，但因我已有预约，未接受邀请。我将于本月27日前往横滨。Siang Keng 将于29日返回东京，并于30日前往 Zah Tan 和 Ts Chu。6月1日他将再次返回东京，三天后他将前往青岛（Tsing Too）、Yah Kwei。13日他将在长崎乘坐“上海丸”轮，并于14日抵达上海。如果没有延误，他将按时抵达上海。请告诉 Foo Dee 先生我拜访邮政省的情况。也请告知我的家人我平安无事。

签名：Chien Ming

附言：如果 Foo Dee 先生于2日抵达东京，我会见他，我将于3日离开东京。
