RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Assistance to Japanese Consular Police.

At 1-50 p.m. on 3/8/39, D.P.S. 689 Honda, attached to Central, accompanied by Japanese Consular Police Officer K. Kinbara, came to this station and requested assistance to arrest a male Formosan named Go Min, 38, residing at 633 Yu Ya Ching Road, who was wanted by the Japanese Consular Police for misappropriation.

While above request was being made, Japanese Consular Police Officer I. Asochina, who was waiting outside 633 Yu Ya Ching Road, arrested the wanted man as he was about to enter above address, and brought him to this station.

According to information supplied by D.P.S. Honda, Go Min (accused) was formerly engaged in selling narcotics in partnership with another male Formosan named Ryu Do O (complainant), and in October 1938 the accused absconded from Nanking with $1,500.00, the property of complainant. He was recently traced to Shanghai by complainant, who reported the case to the Japanese Consular Police.

Assistance was rendered by C.D.S. 121 and the undersigned in searching the home of the accused at 633 Yu Ya Ching Road, but nothing of an incriminating nature was found.

协助日本领事警察。

1939年8月3日下午1时50分，隶属中央捕房的日籍副巡官 (D.P.S.) 689号 Honda，在日本领事警察官员 K. Kinbara 陪同下，来到本捕房，请求协助逮捕一名名为 Go Min 的38岁台湾男子，其居住在余姚路633号，因挪用公款被日本领事警察通缉。

在上述请求提出期间，在余姚路633号外等候的日本领事警察官员 I. Asochina，在该通缉犯正要进入上述地址时将其逮捕，并带至本捕房。

根据日籍副巡官 Honda 提供的信息，Go Min（被告）此前与另一名名为 Ryu Do O（原告）的台湾男子合伙贩卖毒品，1938年10月，被告从南京携款1,500.00美元潜逃，该款属原告所有。原告最近在上海追踪到被告，并向日本领事警察报案。

华籍高级侦探 (C.D.S.) 121号和签署人协助搜查了被告在余姚路633号的住所，但未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE

Reference request per attached diary 1;
at 7.30 a.m. August 4, 1939, Sgt. Major Yoshida
attended Crime Branch Headquarters and produced the
attached letter dated April 24, 1939, addressed to a
Mr. Tau San Tseng (陶善〔此处转录不清〕), employed in the
Consolidated Tax Bureau, Kiukiang Road, and also a
name card as evidence of attempted extortion.

Sgt. Major Yoshida explained that Sgt.
Major Katoda and two assistants, all dressed in
Chinese clothing, had taken up positions on Tsapoo
Road, near Lane 427, House 15, Tsapoo Road, the home
of the victim, and were awaiting the Municipal Police
attending.

West Hongkew Station were informed of the
intended visit, as also British Military Headquarters.

A party consisting of D.S.I.'s Fryda and
Seong, D.P.S.'s Yamakawa and Shimizu, C.D.C.'s 206 and
211, and the undersigned left for the scene. On
arrival at North Chekiang Road and Tsapoo Road it was
observed that a party of Police from West Hongkew
Station had arrived there in response to a telephone
call from P./S. Martin (W.R.) on duty at S.S.D.C.,
who had prevented some Japanese in plain clothes, who
page_data.zh:
特务科）。

C.1. 杂项. 130/39   刑事科
                     1939年8月4日.
2

协助日本宪兵队

参照附件日记1中的请求；
1939年8月4日上午7时30分，Yoshida 警曹长来到刑事科总部，出示了一封写于1939年4月24日的附件信件，收件人为陶善〔此处转录不清〕先生，此人受雇于九江路统税局，另有一张名片，作为企图勒索的证据。

Yoshida 警曹长解释说，Katoda 警曹长和两名助手均身着便服，已在乍浦路427弄15号（受害者住所）附近占据位置，等待公共租界警务人员到达。

已通知西虹口巡捕房此次行动，同时也通知了英军司令部。

由副督察 Fryda 和 Seong、特别巡捕 Yamakawa 和 Shimizu、刑事侦探 206号和211号以及署名者组成的小组前往现场。到达浙江北路和乍浦路时，观察到西虹口巡捕房的一队警察已应值班于特别服务分部 (S.S.D.C.) 的马丁巡佐（西区）的电话呼叫到达那里，马丁巡佐阻止了一些便衣日本人进入特别服务分部第一处的院落，这些日本人

page_data.en:
- 2 -

had in custody two male Chinese, from entering the
compound of the 1st S.S.D.C.

It transpired that the Japanese were Sgt.
Major Katoda and his assistants. They had in custody
two male Chinese whom they had arrested at about 7.45
a.m. on Tsepo Road, near Lane 427.

Sgt. Major Katoda explained that whilst
he was awaiting the S.M. Police party, the victim had
pointed out the two males and he had arrested them in
order to prevent them escaping.

Brought to Crime Branch Headquarters the
two Chinese gave their names as :-

(1) ZEE YOH TSUNG (錢越塵), 34, Soochow,
S/Unemployed, 94 South
Chengtu Road.

(2) VEE MING KAU (費鳴皋), 25, Ningpo,
M/Shipping Hong assistant,
residing Lane 253, House
80, Park Road.

Both denied having gone to the victim's
home with the intention of extorting money.

The victim was requested to attend Crime
Branch Headquarters. One named Tsang Zeu Ming (張壽民),
a transportation guard employed by the Consolidated Tax
Bureau, Kiukiang Road, residing Lane 427, House 15,
Tsepo Road, attended. He explained he was acting in
the capacity as representative for one Tau San Tseng,
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

当时正看守着两名中国男性。

经查实，这些日本人是 Katoda 警曹长及其助手。他们看守着两名中国男性，这些人是他们于上午7时45分左右在乍浦路427弄附近逮捕的。

Katoda 警曹长解释说，在他等待公共租界警务人员期间，受害者指认了这两名男性，他为了防止他们逃跑而将其逮捕。

两名中国人被带到刑事科总部后，报出姓名如下：

(1) ZEE YOH TSUNG（錢越塵），34岁，苏州人，
单身/无业，住成都南路94号。

(2) VEE MING KAU（費鳴皋），25岁，宁波人，
男/航运行助理，
住公园路253弄80号。

两人都否认曾意图去受害者家中勒索钱财。

已要求受害者前往刑事科总部。一名名为 Tsang Zeu Ming（張壽民）的人前来，他是九江路统税局的运输警卫，住乍浦路427弄15号。他解释说他作为陶善先生的代表行事，

page_data.en:
- 3 -

No. 7 in the Consolidated Tax Bureau, Kiujiang Road.
The following was as outlined by him :-
On 26-4-39, Tau San Tseng received the
attached letter at his home on Rue Lafayette. In view
of the fact nothing definite was mentioned it was
more or less ignored.
Just prior to 29-5-39, Tau received two
telephone calls at his office, presumably from someone
connected with the sending of the letter. On the
29-5-39, he again received a 'phone call and on this
occasion was told to go himself, or send a
representative, to a food shop on Yu Ya Ching Road,
near Avenue Edward VII, the following morning at
about 8 o'clock.
Tau sent Tsang Zeu Ming as representative.
He went to the appointed place and met a male Chinese
who asked him if he was the representative. He
replied in affirmative. The male then cautioned both
Tau and himself for working with the Japanese and
abruptly demanded money, but did not mention any
amount. Tsang said he would inform Tau of the demand.
He gave the male his home address.
Nothing further transpired until at about
8 a.m. August 3rd when three male Chinese (the male
he had interviewed previously was not one of them)
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

陶善是九江路统税局的第7号人物。
他概述的情况如下：
1939年4月26日，陶善在其霞飞路家中收到附件信件。鉴于信中未提及具体事项，故大致未予理会。
就在1939年5月29日之前，陶善在其办公室接到两个电话，推测来自与寄信有关的人。1939年5月29日，他再次接到一个电话，这次被告知要在第二天早上8点左右，亲自或派代表去爱多亚路附近的虞洽卿路的一家食品店。
陶善派 Tsang Zeu Ming 作为代表。他去了指定地点，遇到一名中国男子，问他是否是代表。他给予肯定回答。该男子随后警告陶善和他本人与日本人合作，并突然索要钱财，但未提及具体金额。Tsang 说他会将这一要求告知陶善。他给了该男子他的家庭住址。
此后未发生其他事情，直到8月3日上午8点左右，三名中国男子（此前与他交谈的那名男子不在其中）

page_data.en:
- 4 -

entered his home and asked if his name was Tsang.
He replied "Yes" and was handed a name card (attached)
and was told they were there on behalf of guerillas.
They asked for money, but did not state the amount
required. He said he would communicate with Tau and
would see them again at 8 o'clock August 4th at his
home.

On going to work he informed Tau of what
had transpired and was later told that several members
of the Japanese Gendarmerie in plain clothes would be
waiting in the vicinity of his home and he was to
inform them should the men return. At about 7.30 a.m.
August 4th, Sgt. Major Katoda called at his home and
introduced himself and then went out onto Tsepo Road.

At about 7.45 a.m. the two arrested males
whom he recognised as having called at his home on the
3rd were seen approaching along Tsepo Road from
North Chekiang Road. He pointed them out to Sgt. Major
Katoda who arrested them.

He identified the two males from among
nine others in an identification parade held at Crime
Branch Headquarters. He also stated that the 1st named
arrest was the man who handed him the name card in his
home on the morning of the 3rd August.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

进入他家，问他的名字是否是 Tsang。
他回答“是”，并被递给一张名片（见附件），并被告知他们是代表游击队而来的。
他们索要钱财，但未说明所需金额。他说他会与陶善联系，并约定于8月4日8点在他家再次见面。

上班后，他将发生的事情告知了陶善，后来被告知几名便衣日本宪兵队员将在他家附近等候，如果那些人回来，他要通知他们。8月4日上午7时30分左右，Katoda 警曹长来到他家，自我介绍，然后走到乍浦路上。

上午7时45分左右，他看到两名被捕男子（他认出他们是3日去过他家的人）从浙江北路沿乍浦路走来。他向 Katoda 警曹长指认了他们，Katoda 随即将其逮捕。

他在刑事科总部举行的列队辨认中，从另外九人中指认出了这两名男子。他还陈述说，第一名被捕者是8月3日上午在他家中递给他名片的那个人。

page_data.en:
- 5 -

A search of the homes of the two males
was made but nothing of an incriminating nature was
unearthed. A Japanese Special Service Section pass
issued to the 1st named on July 28th in Soochow was
found. This permitted him to come to Shanghai on
July 31.

The 1st. named in a statement (copy attached)
admits having visited Tsang's home on behalf of a
guerilla named Wu Ting (  ) who, in turn, was
acting on the instructions of his chief re the
supplying of uniforms for guerilla units on the
borders of Chekiang and Kiangsu provinces. He also
implicates the 2nd. named as knowing the reason of the
visit in spite of the 2nd. named's denials. He denies
having gone with the intention of extorting money
on his own behalf.

The 2nd. named in a statement (copy attached)
states he met the 1st. named on the 2nd. August and
that person invited him to visit the home of Tsang
in Tsepo Road. He admits having accompanied the
1st. named and one other introduced to him as Wong (三)
to the home of Tsang on the 3rd. August and while there
heard Wong ask Tsang for some uniforms. He denies being
a guerilla or knowing the real reason for the visit.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

对这两名男子的住所进行了搜查，但未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。发现了发给第一名男子的一张日本特别服务处通行证，签发于7月28日的苏州。该通行证允许他于7月31日来上海。

第一名男子在一份供词（副本见附件）中承认，他是代表一名名为 Wu Ting（  ）的游击队员前往 Tsang 家的，而 Wu Ting 又是根据其上司关于为江浙边境游击队提供制服的指示行事。他还牵连第二名男子，称尽管第二名男子予以否认，但其知晓来访原因。他否认自己是出于个人目的意图勒索钱财。

第二名男子在一份供词（副本见附件）中称，他于8月2日遇见第一名男子，那人邀请他去乍浦路 Tsang 的家。他承认于8月3日陪同第一名男子和另一名被介绍为 Wong（三）的人去了 Tsang 家，在那里听到 Wong 向 Tsang 索要一些制服。他否认自己是游击队员或知晓来访的真实原因。

Both men have been lodged in the cells at
Central Station.

page_data.en:
TRANSLATION OF A LETTER DATED 26.4.39
ADDRESSED TO MR. TAU

In accordance with the instructions of the
Committee of the Military Affairs of the National
Government, we have established Headquarters at
Vei Kai Chen, San Wo Kong, in Chitung, and have
posted all the detachments separately in Min-Hong, Pootung,
Changzo etc. We have made several desperate battles
against the enemy as have been reported in various
papers in Shanghai already. But our soldiers on
active service are in need of steel helmets, anti-
poison gas masks and medicines. We know that you are
holding an important office in the puppet organization
and have made much profit from it.

Due to the present national crisis, your
activities, are offensive to the statutes of the
country; but, owing to the depression of the market
and the ever-increasing price of goods, we shall
forgive you as you are perhaps compelled to do so
by the high cost of living. Before taking over
your post in the puppet organization, we know that
you were a patriot and hated the enemy. During
this serious period, we sincerely hope that you
will give some consideration about the possible loss
of the country.

As Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek has declared
"one who has money contributes money and one who has
energy, directs energy"; "People and soldiers should
collaborate mutually in order to contest the last
victory", we herewith entreat you to help us with
pecuniary aid so that you can fullfil some of the
duties of civilians. We ask for contributions from
page_data.zh:
1939年4月26日致陶先生信件的译文

遵照国民政府军事委员会的指令，我们已在松江卫家镇三和宫设立总部，并将各分队分别部署在闵行、浦东、常州等地。正如上海各家报纸已报道的那样，我们与敌人进行了多次殊死战斗。但我方现役士兵急需钢盔、防毒面具和药品。我们知道你在伪组织中担任要职，并从中牟取暴利。

鉴于目前的国家危机，你的行为有违国法；但是，由于市场萧条和物价不断上涨，我们将原谅你，因为你可能是被高昂的生活成本所迫。在你担任伪组织职务之前，我们知道你是一位爱国者，痛恨敌人。在这个严峻时期，我们真诚希望你能考虑到国家可能遭受的损失。

正如蒋介石委员长所宣称的，“有钱出钱，有力出力”；“军民合作，争取最后胜利”，我们特此恳请你提供金钱援助，以履行平民的一些义务。我们向他人

page_data.en:
- 2 -

others by voluntary means and not by extortion and
firmly believe that you will donate us the expenses
in the conception of nationalism.
    If we are favored with your aid, we shall
report to our superior of your merits and patriotic
enthusiasm. The destruction of the country will
bring your money into uselessness, and you would
receive the strict punishment from the statutes
of the country when China gains the last victory.
So you should deliberate as to what to do.
    We shall send an aide-de-camp to you for
negotiations after the letter reaches you.

                    Signed:-Zung Nyee
                           Commanding officer.
                    Chopped: Headquarters of the
                             6th Detachment of
                             the 5th Battalion of
                             Chekiang and Kiangsu
                             Border Guerillas.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

自愿募捐，而非勒索，并坚信你会基于民族主义观念向我们捐赠经费。
    如蒙援助，我们将向上级报告你的功绩和爱国热情。国家的毁灭将使你的金钱变得毫无用处，而当中国取得最后胜利时，你将受到国法的严厉惩罚。因此，你应该慎重考虑如何行事。
    信件送达后，我们将派遣副官与你进行谈判。

                    签名:-Zung Nyee
                           指挥官。
                    盖章：江浙边境游击队
                             第五大队第六分队
                             总部。

page_data.en:
Tse Yih Tsung (錢赴塵)
Wu Kung, Kiangsu    U.D.S. 2
Vol, U.B.Ho...    4.8.39    Translated    Clerk Asia
////////

I am a native of Wu Kung, 24 years old, unmarried,
residing in my sister-in-law's residence at 94 South Chengtu
Road. I studied in a primary school in my native place. At
the age of seventeen I graduated from there and entered the
Wu Kung (吳江) Middle School.

Since the outbreak of the hostilities I stopped
my study and came to Shanghai. I am entirely supported by
my old mother. In July, last year, my step-sister recommended
me to an Italian Co. in Nanking. Finally, because of depression
of business the company closed down.

On July 25th. this year (1939) I went to Soochow
and on July 31st. I came from Soochow to Shanghai.

At 3 p.m. August 1st. I went to the French Park and
accidently met two of my friends, Wu Ting (吳鼎) and
Ching Ling (王全林). We talked for a long while and
arranged that we meet one another at 10 a.m. on August 2nd. in
front of the gate of the Great World Amusement Centre, Avenue
Edward VII.

At about 10 a.m. the following day, I met Vee Ming
Hau (費明豪), Wong Ching Ling (王全林) and Wu Ting (吳鼎)
on Avenue Edward VII near the Great World Amusement Resort.
We went to the Tea Room of the Sun Co., Nanking Road to have
some food. On arrival there we were told by Wu that his
superior had written to one named Tau, chief of the Consolidated
Tax Bureau and requested him (Tau) to supply uniforms for the
guerilla units on the borders of Kiangsu and Chekiang Provinces.
This matter was being negotiated with the representative of Tau
page_data.zh:
谢亦宗（錢赴塵）
江苏吴工（Wu Kung）    U.D.S. 2
志愿人员，U.B.Ho...    1939年8月4日    已翻译    亚洲籍文员
////////

我是江苏吴工（Wu Kung）人，24岁，未婚，现居住在我嫂子位于成都南路94号的住所。我在家乡的一所小学读书。十七岁时从该校毕业，随后进入吴工（吴江）中学就读。

自战事爆发以来，我中止学业来到上海。我完全由老母亲供养。去年七月，我的继姐推荐我到南京的一家意大利公司工作。最后，由于生意萧条，该公司倒闭。

今年（1939年）7月25日，我去了苏州，并于7月31日从苏州来到上海。

8月1日下午3点，我去了法国公园，偶然遇到了我的两个朋友，吴鼎（Wu Ting）和王全林（Ching Ling）。我们交谈了很长时间，并约定于8月2日上午10点在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）大世界游乐中心门口见面。

次日上午10点左右，我在爱多亚路靠近大世界游乐场处遇到了费明豪（Vee Ming Hau）、王全林（Wong Ching Ling）和吴鼎（Wu Ting）。我们去了南京路先施公司（Sun Co.）的茶室用餐。到达那里后，吴告诉我们，他的上级给统税局局长陶某写了一封信，请求他（陶）为苏浙边区的游击队提供制服。此事正在与陶的代表

page_data.en:
(2)

named Tsang Sou Ming but without any result. He (Wu) asked
if we (Zee, Yoe and **〔此处转录不清〕**) would dare to visit Tseng at his
home situated at No.15 Yee Shing Lee, Tsepo Road, regarding
the matter of supplying uniforms. We agreed to his suggestion
and promised to meet each other at the corner of Chekiang
and Chefoo Roads at 8 a.m. on the 3rd. August, 1939. We then
returned home.

At 8 a.m. on the 3rd. August, 1939, we three met
at the appointed place and proceeded to Tsang's home on Tsepo
Road. On arrival we interviewed Tseng regarding the matter
of supplying uniforms. He told us that he had taken the
matter up with Tsu and told us to be there again at 8 a.m. the
following day (4th. August, 1939).

On the morning of 4th. August, 1939, Yoe Ming Kau
and I went to Tsang's home and when we arrived at the Yee
Shing Lee off Tsepo Road we were arrested by Japanese.
About 20 minutes later, a party of S.M.Police came to the
scene and brought us to the Police Headquarters.

Signed:- Zee Yoh Tsung
page_data.zh:
(2)

曾寿明（Tsang Sou Ming）进行谈判，但没有任何结果。他（吴）问我们（谢、姚和**〔此处转录不清〕**）是否敢去乍浦路亿盛里15号曾的家中，商谈提供制服的事宜。我们同意了他的建议，并承诺于1939年8月3日上午8点在浙江路与芝罘路的拐角处见面。随后我们各自回家。

1939年8月3日上午8点，我们三人在指定地点见面，并前往乍浦路曾的家中。到达后，我们就提供制服一事采访了曾。他告诉我们，他已与徐（Tsu）交涉过此事，并让我们第二天（1939年8月4日）上午8点再去那里。

1939年8月4日上午，姚明高（Yoe Ming Kau）和我去了曾的家中，当我们到达乍浦路附近的亿盛里时，被日本人逮捕。大约20分钟后，一队工部局警察（S.M.Police）赶到现场，将我们带到警察总局。

签名：谢耀宗（Zee Yoh Tsung）

page_data.en:
Vee Ming Kau (費瑪皋)

Ningpo                                C.D.C. 211
C.l,C.B.H.Q.        4.8.39            translated
                                      //////      Clerk Hsia

My name is Vee Ming Kau, age 25, native of Ningpo,
married, residing in an upstairs room at No. K 80 Zung Shing
Lee, Park Road. I am a parking coolie employed at Mar Ling
(茂林) Shipping Agency, No.14 Sz Teh Lee off Chekiang Road.
    At 2 p.m. on the 31st. July, 28th. year of the
Republic of China (1939) I met one named Zee Yeh Tsung (諸葉宗)
a type-writer merchant, on Rue de Consulat, near Rue Palikao,
French Concession. I nodded to him and continued on my way.
    At about 10 a.m. on the 2nd. August, 1939, I
encountered Zee Yeh Tsung on Yu Ya Ching Road near Avenue
Edward VII. We went to the 3rd. floor of the Sun Co., Nanking
Road to have some food. At same time, he (Zee) told me to
await him at the corner of Chekiang and Chefoo Roads between
7 a.m. and 8 a.m. the following day (3rd. August, 1939) for
the purpose of visiting a friend.
    At about 7 a.m. 3rd. August, 1939, I went there
and noticed Zee and one other named Wong waiting for me at
the corner. We three then proceeded to Lane 427, House 15
Tsepoo Road to visit the occupant in an attic room. I knew
this occupant named Tsang (張) through the introduction
of Wong (王). Later, I heard that Wong requested Tsang
to give him a few sets of uniform. Tsang then told us that
he would give the matter consideration and informed us to be
there the following morning. We then left the premises. Zee
and I were told by Wong that we should meet again at the same
destination between 7 a.m. and 8 a.m. the following day.
    At about 7 a.m. on the 4th. August, 1939, I went
page_data.zh:
费玛皋（Vee Ming Kau）

宁波                                C.D.C. 211
C.l,C.B.H.Q.        1939年8月4日            已翻译
                                      //////      夏姓文员

我叫费玛皋，25岁，宁波人，已婚，居住在派克路（Park Road）众兴里K80号楼上房间。我是受雇于浙江路四德里14号茂林（Mar Ling）轮船代理行的停车苦力。
    中华民国二十八年（1939年）7月31日下午2点，我在法租界领事馆路（Rue de Consulat）靠近贝勒路（Rue Palikao）处遇到一名叫诸叶宗（Zee Yeh Tsung）的打字机商人。我向他点头致意，然后继续赶路。
    1939年8月2日上午10点左右，我在爱多亚路附近的虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）遇到了诸叶宗。我们去了南京路先施公司（Sun Co.）三楼用餐。同时，他（诸）让我第二天（1939年8月3日）早上7点到8点之间在浙江路和芝罘路的拐角处等他，目的是去拜访一位朋友。
    1939年8月3日早上7点左右，我去了那里，注意到诸和另一位姓王的人在那里等我。我们三人随后前往乍浦路427弄15号，去拜访住在阁楼房间里的人。我是通过王（Wong）的介绍认识这位住户张某（Tsang）的。后来，我听说王请求张给他几套制服。张随后告诉我们，他会考虑此事，并让我们第二天早上再去。随后我们离开了该处。王告诉我和诸，我们应该在第二天早上7点到8点之间在同一地点再次见面。
    1939年8月4日早上7点左右，我去了

page_data.en:
(2)

there and met Zoe only whilst Wong failed to keep his promise.
We two then went to Lane 427, House 15 Tsepoo Road. On arrival
at Lane 427 Tsepoo Road, we were apprehended by four Japanese
and a party of Foreign and Chinese detectives, and later we
were conveyed to the Police Headquarters.

Signed: Vee Ming Kau.
page_data.zh:
(2)

那里，只遇到了诸，而王未能履约。我们两人随后前往乍浦路427弄15号。到达乍浦路427弄时，我们被四名日本人以及一队中外侦探逮捕，随后被押送至警察总局。

签名：费玛皋。

ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE H.Q.
RE ATTACHED REPORT, POOTOO RD. MISC. 202/39
(NO ARRESTS OR SEIZURES MADE).

At 11.30 a.m. on the 12th August 1939, Sgt.
Komaki of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters called
at C. I. Offices and requested assistance of the
S. M. Police to visit a second-hand shop on Peking
Road to ascertain sources of the seized aluminium
metal purporting to be parts of a Japanese aeroplane.

The necessary assistance was rendered by
D.P.S. Shimidzu, D.S.I. Wong Lung Wo and the undersigned.

At 11.45 a.m. 12-8-39, the aforementioned
party visited the Tung Fah Ziang (同發祥) Second-hand
Shop at 771 Peking Road, where a shop assistant named
Wong Ping (王彬) produced a Customs pass Reg. No. C.104,
dated June 12, 1939, showing that old aluminium scrap
valued $3,170.00 was imported from Hongkong by the
Zien Hee Kung & Co. (存義公行) and Customs duty being
collected accordingly.

As this shop assistant could not furnish
detectives with full particulars of disposing the
remainder of the imported scrap etc., he was instructed
to inform the proprietor to call at C. I. Offices.

On the following morning, i.e. 13-8-39, Vai
Zang Zung (范長順), proprietor of the Tung Fah Ziang
page_data.zh:
特别处（Special Branch）处长。

总局
刑事科
1939年8月14日

向日本宪兵队总部提供协助
关于附件报告，普陀路杂项 202/39
（未实施逮捕或扣押）。

1939年8月12日上午11点30分，日本宪兵队总部的小牧军曹（Sgt. Komaki）来到刑事调查处办公室，请求工部局警察协助走访北京路的一家旧货店，以查明被扣押铝金属的来源，这些铝金属据称是日本飞机的部件。

清水副巡官（D.P.S. Shimidzu）、黄龙沃副探长（D.S.I. Wong Lung Wo）及本人提供了必要的协助。

1939年8月12日上午11点45分，上述人员走访了位于北京路771号的同发祥（Tung Fah Ziang）旧货店，店内一名叫王彬（Wong Ping）的店员出示了一张海关通行证，注册号C.104，日期为1939年6月12日，显示存义公行（Zien Hee Kung & Co.）从香港进口了价值3,170.00美元的废旧铝屑，并已据此缴纳关税。

由于该店员无法向侦探提供处置剩余进口废屑等的全部详情，他被指示通知店主前往刑事调查处办公室。

次日早晨，即1939年8月13日，同发祥

page_data.en:

Second-hand Shop, came to C. I. Offices and explained
that he had purchased the scrap from Sien Hee Kung
Co. and re-sold the metal to various persons in different
quantities. His statement to this effect was checked
up by an account book which shows that all the scrap
had been sold out to various customers.

P. Konovaloff.
D. S. I.

- 2 -

P. Konovaloff.

ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO JAPANESE CONSULAR
POLICE (NO ARREST OR SEIZURE MADE).

Reference the request made by the Japanese
Consular Police as per diary No.1, the necessary
assistance was rendered by D.S.I.s Crighton, Lieu
Kying Ching, Wong Zung Wo, D.S. Sugimoto, D.P.S.
Yamahara, C.D.S.s 272, 2, C.D.C.s 184, 211 and the
undersigned.

At 11.15 p.m. on the 12th. August, 1939, on
instructions of Supt. Grubb, P.A. to D.C. (Crime),
the aforementioned party, accompanied by D.S.s
Hinomiya and Fujita of the Japanese Consular Police
carried out a raid in a house No.11, lane 233, off
Markham Road.

However from enquiries made amongst the inmates

FURTHER TO QUERY.

With reference to the queries raised
by the J.C.(Crime); the accused has been further
questioned and states as follows:-

He did not proceed to Hongkong to make
his purchases as there is no direct connection
between Liuchow & Hongkong owing to the surround-
ing district of Hongkong being occupied by the
Japanese forces. When the accused first left
Liuchow it was his intention to make his pur-
chases in Nanchow, not Shanghai, and at that
time there was an open road connecting those
two towns.

The accused found he was unable to make
the purchases he required, in Nanchow, so proceed-
ed to Shanghai with the intention of making them
here and shipping them to Liuchow via Nanchow.
Whilst the accused was in Shanghai the Japanese
forces occupied a portion of the Nanchow -
Liuchow Road south of Nanchang in Kiangsi
Province. It therefore became necessary for
him to ship his goods to Hongkong from where
they would have to be transshipped to Liuchow

进一步查询回复。

关于刑事科法官（J.C.(Crime)）提出的查询，被告已被进一步讯问，陈述如下：

他并未前往香港采购，因为由于香港周边地区被日军占领，柳州与香港之间没有直接联系。当被告最初离开柳州时，他打算在南昌而非上海进行采购，当时这两个城镇之间有畅通的道路相连。

被告发现他无法在南昌买到所需的物品，于是前往上海，打算在这里采购并通过南昌运往柳州。当被告在上海期间，日军占领了江西省南昌以南的部分南昌-柳州公路。因此，他不得不将货物运往香港，再从那里

5/2.

via Haiphong, French Indo-China.
Enquiries have been made at the Kyi
Sung Oo (義生和) Shipping Hong which is
situated at 35 Ching Yu Li (靖遠里), Peking
Road and it has been ascertained that they
did ship goods on the accused behalf and
issued the letter in duplicate authorising
the accused to take possession of these goods.
They were shipped aboard the S.S. GHENTVILLE
MANILA on 15.8.39.
The proprietor of this shipping hong
is one named Chen Si Tsoo (陳顯祖) and it
has been established for the past five years.
Prior to the hostilities it was situated in
the Yoong Kyi Li, Suchang Road and appears to
be quite a reputable concern.

H.F.S

经法属印度支那的海防（Haiphong）转运至柳州。
已向位于北京路靖远里35号的义生和（Kyi Sung Oo）轮船行进行调查，经查实，他们确实代表被告装运了货物，并出具了一式两份的信件，授权被告提取这些货物。货物于1939年8月15日装上“根特维尔马尼拉”号轮船（S.S. GHENTVILLE MANILA）。
该轮船行的老板名叫陈显祖（Chen Si Tsoo），该行已成立五年。战前该行位于苏州路永吉里（Yoong Kyi Li），似乎是一家相当信誉良好的商号。

At 11.00 a.m. September 6, 1939 a note (Shan-Ken-Ko No.1018) appended to another note (Wusieh-Keno Ko No.333) were received at C.1.,Crime Branch Headquarters,from Sergeant Komaki of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters,Bridge House.

The note (Wusieh-Ken-Ko No.333) furnishes,in reply to the reference made by Shanghai Gendarmerie Headquarters on Shan-Ken-Ko No.950, information to the effect that the accused,Tseu Tsung Ming (周振民) displayed activities in the capacity of Chief of Aide-de-camp of the Loyal National Salvation Army under the Kiangsu, Chekiang Mobile Committee, and left for Shanghai in April or May 1939.

This information,the note reports,has been obtained from Koo Yeh Shing (顧福興),Chief of bandits,who was arrested by the Wusieh Detachment and is at present being held in their custody.

while the note (Shan-Ken-Ko No.1018) requests, on the basis of information given by Wusieh-Ken-Ko No.333 the handing over to them of Zung Zien(陳泉),alias Tseu Tsung Ming (周振民),alias Tsen Tien Ying (周天英) at an early date.

1939年9月6日上午11时，刑事一处（C.1.）刑事处总部收到来自百老汇大厦日本宪兵队总部小牧（Komaki）军士的一封信函（山宪告第1018号），该信函附于另一封信函（吴宪告第333号）之后。

信函（吴宪告第333号）系回复上海宪兵队总部关于山宪告第950号的查询，提供如下信息：被告周振民曾以江苏、浙江流动委员会下属忠义救国军副官处处长的身份进行活动，并于1939年4月或5月前往上海。

该信函称，此信息是从匪首顾福兴处获得的，顾福兴已被吴淞分队逮捕，目前正由其羁押。

而信函（山宪告第1018号）则基于吴宪告第333号所提供的信息，要求尽早将陈泉（又名周振民，又名周天英）移交给他们。

G.D.I.

and repairs business. That on April 22nd. 1939 he
arrived in Shanghai aboard the s.s. Taiping having
been commissioned by his partners to purchase motor
car accessories etc., in Shanghai and despatch same
to Liuchow. That he did not commence to make these
purchases immediately owing to the fall in the
exchange, and that it was only when he received

his business and return to Liuchow, that he commenced

page_data.en:
Accused.

ZUNG ZIEN (陳泉) alias TSRU TIEN YING (周天引)
alias TSEU HWA (周華)
Zaushing xx D.S.T. Pryde
H. Q. C. B. 18-8-39 Clerk Hsu.

My name is Zung Zien, alias Tseu Tien Ying, alias
Tseu Hwa, age 31 years.
I was born at Zaushing, Chekiang. From the age of
9 to 17 years I was educated in the Yu Tsa (越材) Middle
School. At the age of 18 years I entered the Hangchow
First Middle School, but ceased studies at the age of 19
years owing to the death of my parents. I came to Shanghai
in 1927 and obtained a position as accountant in the Zing
Zi Painting Works (勤業印刷所) situated in an alleyway off
Bubbling Well Road, near Myburgh Road. I remained in this
position for about one year and then returned to Zaushing
and was sick and unemployed.for about 2 years.
In February 1930 I went to Hankow and was employed
as a shop assistant in the Tien Sung (天生) Dispensary.
In April 1931 I went to Nanking and obtained a position as
accountant in the Sun Sun (生生) Dispensary on Tai Bing
Road (太平路). In November 1937 owing to the impending
occupation of Nanking by the Japanese forces, I evacuated
to Changsha along with the staff of the dispensary and we
opened another dispensary business in Changsha. As the
situation in Changsha was uncertain, I, together with the
remainder of the staff of the dispensary, went to Liuchow
(柳州), Kwangsi, where we sold our stock of medicines
and I received approximately $4,000.00 from the proceeds.
I then together with two others named Wu Kwang Lah (吳光樂)
and Za See Tsae (石支社) opened a motor car accessories and
repairs business with a capital of $80,000.00 divided into
page_data.zh:
被告。

陈泉（又名周天引，又名周华）
乍浦 xx D.S.T. Pryde
刑事处总部 1939年8月18日 书记员 Hsu。

我叫陈泉，又名周天引，又名周华，年龄31岁。
我出生于浙江乍浦。9岁至17岁期间，我在越材中学受教育。18岁时进入杭州第一中学，但因父母双亡，19岁时辍学。我于1927年来到上海，在靠近迈尔西爱路的静安寺路一条弄堂里的勤业印刷所获得了一份会计职位。我在此职位上工作了约一年，随后回到乍浦，因病失业约2年。
1930年2月，我前往汉口，在天生药房担任店员。1931年4月，我前往南京，在太平路的生生药房获得了一份会计职位。1937年11月，由于日军即将占领南京，我与药房职员一同撤离至长沙，并在长沙开设了另一家药房业务。由于长沙局势不稳，我与药房其余职员一同前往广西柳州，在那里我们出售了药品库存，我从所得款项中获得了约4,000.00美元。随后，我与另外两名名为吴光乐和石支社的人合伙开办了一家汽车零配件及修理业务，资本为80,000.00美元，分为

page_data.en:
- 2 -

five shares, I taking one share and my two partners taking
two shares each.

In February 1939 I went to Wenchow for the
purpose of buying motor car accessories in connection with my
business and on April 21st left for Shanghai for the same
purpose. I arrived in Shanghai on April 22nd and have
resided in Shanghai ever since. I did not immediately
commence to make purchases in Shanghai owing to the continued
fall in the exchange and it was only when I was pressed by
my partners by cable, to complete my business and return to
Liuchow, that I commenced making purchases. I intended to
return to Liuchow via Hongkong on 19-8-39 and had already
bought the passage tickets.

I have never been concerned in any anti-Japanese
activities, neither have I ever been a soldier. I have no
idea why I should have been arrested, but wish to state that
about a week ago, one of the tea boys at the Dollar Hotel
asked me if I was a representative of the Chinese Army, and
this leads me to believe that my long stay in this hotel must
have aroused suspicions.

If necessary the various firms from whom I have
made purchases in Shanghai can prove I am a proper business
man from Liuchow.

I have never been in Wuchieh in my life so cannot
understand why I should be accused of anti-Japanese activities
there.

Sgd. & Crossmarked : ZUNG ZIEN.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

五股，我持一股，我的两位合伙人各持两股。

1939年2月，我前往温州，目的是为我的业务购买汽车零配件，并于4月21日出于同样目的前往上海。我于4月22日抵达上海，此后一直居住在上海。由于汇率持续下跌，我并未立即开始在上海采购，直到合伙人发电报催促我完成业务并返回柳州后，我才开始采购。我计划于1939年8月19日经香港返回柳州，并已购买了船票。

我从未参与任何反日活动，也从未当过兵。我不知道为何会被捕，但我想声明，大约一周前，美元饭店的一名茶房问我是否是中国军队的代表，这使我相信，我在这家饭店长期停留必然引起了怀疑。

如有必要，我在上海向其采购的各家公司可以证明我是来自柳州的正当商人。

我生平从未去过无锡，因此无法理解为何会被指控在那里从事反日活动。

签名并按手印：陈泉。

TSUNG TIEN GEE 纵天奇
Anhwei
C.P.H.Q. ( C.1 )    17.8.39    // D.S.I. Jong Sung Co.
                               translated
                               //////// Hsu S. F.

My name is Tsung Tien Gee, aged 33 years, native
of Anhwei, married and working with the Japanese Military
Intelligence Service, Pootung.

Formerly I was chief of the Personnel Dept. of
the Soochow - Hangchow Defence Force, which was commanded
by Chu Kuo Bing (诸国屏) under a Japanese named Tan
Fang(?) (楠方), with headquarters at An Loong Chun Hong,
Wusih. The defence force was formed of approximately
2000 men who were all enrolled from the guerilla units.

Tseu Tsung Kong (周振刚); leader of a Guerilla Unit,
composed of over 8000 persons, and assisted by Tseu Tsung
Ming (周振民) who was chief of staff to the former, had
his headquarters at Mei Tsung (梅村), Wusih.

Tseu Tsung Kong intended to surrender to Chu Kuo
Bing and instructed Tseu Tsung Ming to negotiate with
Chu Kuo Bing with this object in view.

Owing to the refusal of Chu Kuo Bing to accept
Tseu's suggestion, the latter finally ordered an attack
on the defence force, which were then stationed at An
Tsoong, Wusih, as a result of which the defence force
was defeated and collapsed. Chu Kuo Bing, therefore,
disbanded his men, and I came to Shanghai and lived
in Pootung.

Later I received a letter from Chu Kuo Bing,
stating that he had been appointed by the Japanese
authorities as officer i/c of the corps to obtain the
surrender of guerillas of Kiangsu, Chekiang & Anhwei provinces
page_data.zh:
〔此处转录不清〕

TSUNG TIEN GEE 纵天奇
安徽
中央捕房总部 ( C.1 )    1939年8月17日    // 副巡官 Jong Sung Co.
                               翻译
                               //////// 徐 S. F.

本人名为纵天奇，33岁，安徽人，已婚，受雇于日本军事情报机关，工作地点在浦东。

此前，我曾担任苏杭防卫队人事部部长，该部队由一名叫 Tan Fang(?) (楠方) 的日本人指挥，诸国屏任指挥官，总部设在无锡安龙春红。该防卫队由约2000人组成，均从游击队中招募而来。

周振刚；一支由8000多人组成的游击队首领，其参谋长为周振民，协助前者工作，总部设在无锡梅村。

周振刚打算向诸国屏投降，并指示周振民以此为目的与诸国屏进行谈判。

由于诸国屏拒绝接受周的建议，后者最终下令攻击当时驻扎在无锡安纵的防卫队，导致防卫队战败并瓦解。因此，诸国屏遣散了部下，我来到上海并居住在浦东。

后来，我收到诸国屏的一封信，称他已被日本当局任命为负责招降江苏、浙江及安徽各省游击队的部队负责人

page_data.en:
- 2 -

On receipt of this letter I proceeded to see
Chu at his home, situated at 12 Hong Keu Foong, Robison
Road.

We later engaged Room 24 in the Mang Chi (梁溪)
Lodging House, where I left at 2 p.m. (date unknown).

At about 5 p.m. (date unknown) Chu Kuo Bing was
murdered outside No. 3 Chekiang Road (South End).

As Tsau Tsung Kong owed Chu a grudge over the
reorganization of guerrillas, the former detailed Tsau
Tsung Ming to come to Shanghai and organize the assassination
of Chu Kuo Bing.

The appointment of Chu's new position as Chief
of the office of obtaining the surrender of guerillas
urged Tsau Tsung Ming to take Chu's life.

Although Chu and I knew the above yet we were
unable to take the necessary precautions against Tsau's
conspiracy to murder Chu.

Through the recommendation of Mr. Yang, (杨)
an interpreter employed by Japanese, I secured a job
in the Japanese Military Intelligence Service in Pootung.

At 8 p.m. on 11.8.39 I observed Tsau Tsung Ming
walking along Yu Ya Ching Road near Peking Road, whereupon
I immediately followed after him and as a result found
him living in Room 219 of the Dollar Hotel, Yu Ya Ching
Road. I then returned Pootung.

Day before yesterday I reported the encounter
of Tsau Tsung Ming to the Japanese Gendarmerie in Hongkew.

The above is my true statement.
Signed:
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

收到此信后，我前往位于罗宾森路虹口坊12号的诸国屏家中见他。

随后，我们租用了梁溪旅馆24号房间，我在下午2点离开（日期不详）。

大约在下午5点（日期不详），诸国屏在浙江路（南端）3号门外被谋杀。

由于周振刚在游击队整编问题上对诸国屏怀恨在心，前者指派周振民来上海策划刺杀诸国屏。

诸国屏被任命为招降游击队办公室主任的新职位，促使周振民决意取诸之性命。

虽然诸和我都知道上述情况，但我们无法采取必要的预防措施来防范周谋杀诸的阴谋。

通过一名受雇于日本人的翻译杨先生推荐，我在浦东的日本军事情报机关找到了一份工作。

1939年8月11日晚上8点，我观察到周振民在北京路附近的亚尔培路上行走，随即我立即跟踪他，结果发现他住在亚尔培路大华饭店219号房间。随后我返回浦东。

前天，我向虹口日本宪兵队报告了遇到周振民的情况。

以上是我的真实陈述。
签名：

page_data.en:

(?) dollars to Fu Sue roh (傅守璞), at Chung Hwa (中華)
Iron Manufacturing Factory, No.? Route Dufour, in order
to clear Fong Yue Ngoh's (方友鶴) loan, and
deposit $10,000.00 in Shanghai. The remainder, you

Awaiting your early reply.
From : Zah sz Lee (石世礼)

2. Is your relative, Tseu (周), in Shanghai? Awaiting

From: Wu Kwong Loh (吳克樂)

3. Is Tseu Hwa (周樺) in Shanghai? Awaiting your speedy

From: Wu Kwong Loh.

4. Come and bring me four hams.
From: Wu.

page_data.en:
Headquarters
C.I. Misc. 137/39 Crime Branch
August 17, 39.
2

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE

Further to Diary No. 1, Sgt. [此处转录不清] Kotoda
and two other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie
came to J.B.H.Q. (C. I.) at 5.30 a.m. on 17-8-39 and
stated they requested assistance to raid Room 219 of
the Dollar Hotel, 39 Yu Ya Ching Road, to arrest one
named Tseu Tsung Ming (周振民), age 34, native of
Chekiang, who was a member of a guerilla unit operating
in the Kusion Area.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I. Pryde,
D.S. Rossington, D.P.S.'s Yamahara and Shimidzu, C.D.S.
40 and C.D.C. 218, and the stated address visited at
5.45 a.m.

The occupant of the room was arrested and
gave his name as :-
ZUNG TIEN (陳泉) alias Tseu Tien Ying
(周天引), age 31, Native of Zaushing.

A search of the room was made and the
following seized :-

13 Cablegrams.
6 name cards.
2 Passenger tickets from Shanghai
to Hongkong, good for S. S.
"Szechuen" sailing on 19-8-39.
2 Inoculation certificates in the
names of Tseu Tien Ying and
TANG TUBONG BAI (陳宗培).
page_data.zh:
总部
刑务处杂项 137/39 罪案组
1939年8月17日。
2

协助日本宪兵队

继日记第1号之后，[此处转录不清] Kotoda 警长及另外两名日本宪兵队成员于1939年8月17日凌晨5点30分来到中央捕房总部 (刑务处)，表示请求协助突袭亚尔培路39号大华饭店219号房间，逮捕一名名为周振民的人，34岁，浙江人，系在库辛地区活动的游击队成员。

普赖德副巡官、罗辛顿副巡官、山原和清水侦探巡佐、40号中国侦探和218号中国侦探提供了协助，并于上午5点45分前往所述地址。

房间住客被捕，并报出姓名为：
ZUNG TIEN (陳泉)，别名周天引，31岁，嘉兴人。

对房间进行了搜查，查获以下物品：

13份电报稿。
6张名片。
2张从上海到香港的船票，适用于1939年8月19日开行的“四川”轮。
2张接种证书，名字分别为周天引和 TANG TUBONG BAI (陳宗培)。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

The following is the searched property of
the accused :-

$500.00 Hongkong currency.
$164.20 Shanghai "
Bank of China Pass Book No. 23684.
Papers.
One chop.
One gold signet ring.
One wrist watch.

The Bank Pass Book shows a credit balance
of $45,000.00 in June 1939 and a balance of $106.00
at the present time.

On return to C.B.H.Q. Sgt. Major Katoda
produced an informer named Wang Tien Gee (汪天奇),
who identified the accused as one known to him as
Tseu Tsung Ming alias Tung Zien, who was previously
employed as the Chief of Staff to Tseu Tsung Keng
(周振剛), who was in charge of the Guerilla Troops
in the Wusieh Area.

The informer states he was previously a
member of these guerillas but deserted from them and
joined up with Chu Koo Ming (諸國屏), who was in
charge of the Japanese sponsored defence force at
Yangchow and Soochow.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

以下是被告的被搜财产：

港币500.00元。
上海币164.20元。
中国银行存折，号码23684。
文件。
印章一枚。
金图章戒指一枚。
手表一只。

银行存折显示1939年6月贷方余额为45,000.00元，目前余额为106.00元。

回到中央捕房总部后，Katoda 警长带来了一名名为汪天奇的线人，该线人指认被告为其所知的周振民，别名 Tung Zien，此前曾受雇于周振剛，担任其参谋长，周振剛负责无锡地区的游击部队。

线人称他此前是这些游击队的成员，但从中逃离，加入了诸國屏领导的队伍，诸國屏负责扬州和苏州地区由日本赞助的防卫队。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

According to the informer, Chu Kuo Bing
was shot dead on Chekiang Road, near Nakhoi Road,
about 5 months ago (Louza F.I.R. 4005/38) and as the
accused was in Shanghai at that time there is good
reason to believe that he was responsible for this
murder as he had previously made threats that he would
kill this man. A statement has been taken from the
informer and is in process of translation.

The murder of Chu Kuo Bing took place on
28-11-38, considerably more than 5 months ago, and
there is nothing to show at the present time that the
accused was in Shanghai then.

The accused denies these allegations and
states he owns a motor accessories business in
Loochow, Kwangsi, and came to Shanghai on business.

Enquiries are being made regarding the
seized documents etc., and a statement will be taken
from the accused when he has been further questioned.

The accused has resided in various rooms of
the Dollar Hotel since 22-4-39.

Sgt. Major Kateda requests that he be supplied
with a police photograph of the accused, in order that
he may forward same to Wusieh.

（签名：Chas. B. Sref?）
D. S. I.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

据线人称，诸国屏大约在5个月前在浙江路靠近纳高伊路的地方被枪杀（老闸捕房报案记录 4005/38），鉴于被告当时在上海，有充分理由相信他对这起谋杀负责，因为他此前曾扬言要杀死此人。已采集线人的供词，目前正在翻译中。

诸国屏被谋杀一案发生在1938年11月28日，距今已超过5个月，目前没有任何证据表明被告当时在上海。

被告否认这些指控，并称他在广西柳州拥有一家汽车配件商店，来上海是为了做生意。

正在对查获的文件等进行调查，待进一步讯问被告后将采集其供词。

被告自1939年4月22日起一直居住在大华饭店的各个房间。

Kateda 警长请求提供被告的警方照片，以便将其发送至无锡。

Wong Wei 王俤
Shanghai xx himself
translated
24-8-39 xxXXXXX Kuh Nei Han

My name is Wong Wei, alias Wong Wei Yeh, alias
Wong Sung Tsien, aged 30, married, and have a daughter, a
native of Shanghai, residing at No. 3, Heng Tuh Li, Lane
509, Chekiang Road.

I am a graduate of The Central Military Academy.
On August 13, 1937, I was appointed the military instructor
of the Railway Military Training Corps and guarded the
North Station at the outbreak of hostilities. Shortly
after, I joined the 88th Division of the Central Army,
and was appointed battalion Commander for defending Za
Wo Dong (石湖荡). After the retreat of the Chinese
army from Shanghai, I went in to the country and organized
the guerrilla corps.

In January this year, I was appointed Vice Commander-
in-Chief and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of The First
Detachment of the Kiangsu and Chekiang Anti-Japanese Self
Defence Force in the 3rd War Area.

Recently I have been introduced by a Japanese
named Chan Yien Shu (長田実), to cooperate with Mr. Keng
Kew (江口中佐), Lieutenant Colonel of the Japanese Special
Service Section, Shanghai and Mr. Sse Ye (矢野少佐), Aid-
de-Camp of the Shanghai Japanese Garrison Headquarters.
They asked me to manage all the affairs relating to the
conservancy of Woosung River and to take the responsibilities
of maintaining peace and order in various Hsiens east of
Soochow. The conditions are not yet agreed upon so I have
not assumed the post. The Japanese also asked me to
page_data.zh:
王俤 上海 xx 本人
翻译
39年8月24日 xxXXXXX 顾内汉（音译）

我叫王俤，别名王文郁，别名王胜泉，30岁，已婚，有一女，上海人，住浙江路509弄恒德里3号。

我是中央军校毕业生。1937年8月13日，我被任命为铁路军事训练团教官，并在战事爆发时守卫北站。不久后，我加入中央军第88师，被任命为营长，负责防守石湖荡。在中国军队从上海撤退后，我进入内地组织了游击队。

今年1月，我被任命为第三战区江苏浙江抗日自卫军第一支队副司令兼司令。

最近，经一名叫长田实（Chan Yien Shu）的日本人介绍，我与日本驻上海特务机关中佐江口（Keng Kew）先生以及上海日本驻屯军司令部少佐副官矢野（Sse Ye）先生进行合作。他们要求我管理所有与吴淞江疏浚有关的事务，并承担维持苏州以东各县治安的责任。由于条件尚未谈妥，我尚未就职。日本人也要求我

page_data.en:
-2-
accept the post of Vice Commander-in-Chief of Woosung
Volunteer Corps but I refused as the rank is too low.
This is the true statement.

Signed by Wong Wei.
page_data.zh:
-2-
接受吴淞义勇队副司令的职务，但我因嫌职位太低而拒绝。
以上陈述属实。

王俤 签字。

协助日本宪兵队总部。

继日记第1号之后。1939年8月23日凌晨2时，日本宪兵队总部的坂本（Sakamoto）警士， accompanied by 另外两名宪兵队员及一名名为周思梅（Tseu S Mei）的囚犯，来到刑事处总部（C. l.），请求协助突袭浙江路599弄3号，逮捕王胜泉（王勝泉），别名王伟（王偉）。据宪兵队羁押的囚犯供称，此人是苏州地区游击队的头目。坂本警士还称，他们预期在该屋内搜获两箱手榴弹。

副督察长 Pryde、Lieu Kyung Ching，督察 Rossington 和 Sugimoto，巡官 Yamahara，华捕探员 115号和华捕警员 62号提供了协助，并于凌晨2时10分突袭了上述地址。在楼上的后间房内，抓获了这名通缉犯，其自报身份如下：
    王伟（王偉），别名王文郁（WONG WEI YOH），
        别名王胜泉（WONG SUNG TSIEN）。
        30岁，上海人。

被告的妻子和孩子也在房内，但未被逮捕。

供复核，附有
一些文件
(23/8)

page_data.en:
- 2 -

The room was searched and the following
seized :-
    Two shell nose cups which appear to
        be detonated.
    One chop.
    A quantity of documents.

When questioned the accused stated that he
is employed by the Japanese as Assistant Commander
of the Peace Preservation Corps at Foosung, but at
the same time he acts as assistant to one named Dong
Ming (唐銘), who is the Chief of Guerilla Troops
at Coochow.

    The accused has been detained in Central Stn.
Cells pending further enquiries.

(批：23/8)

Geo. R. Keppel
D. S. I.

    两个看似已引爆的炮弹引信杯。
    一枚印章。
    大量文件。

经讯问，被告声称受雇于日本人，担任吴淞保安队副司令，但同时他也担任一名叫唐铭（Dong Ming）的人的助手，此人是苏州游击部队的首领。

    被告已被拘留在中央巡捕房牢房，以待进一步调查。

At .30 p.m. on the 23rd August 1939,
reference the request as per diary No. 1, Sergeant
Major Yoshino of the Japanese Gendarmerie Head-
quarters came to C.I office and imparted the
following information re the requested assistance.
"That the Japanese Gendarmerie in Nanking
had arrested a Japanese subject, who,
his name and nature of the case not
divulged, had implicated Ting Tsauh
(丁卓) as the person from whom he
had borrowed a sum of $100.00. The
Nanking Japanese Gendarmerie made a
request to the Gendarmerie Headquarters
in Shanghai to locate Ting Tsauh and
question him with a view to ascertain
the pretext on which the arrested Japanese
subject borrowed the money from Ting Tsauh."
The necessary assistance was rendered by
D.S.I.s Konovaloff, Soong Ping Tsung, D.S. Rhodes
and D.P.S. Shimidzu.

1939年8月23日下午3时30分，
关于日记第1号所载之请求，
日本宪兵司令部吉野军曹长
来到刑事调查处办公室，就所请求的协助
提供了以下信息：
“南京日本宪兵队逮捕了一名日本籍人士，
其姓名及案件性质未予透露，该人供称
丁卓（Ting Tsauh）是借给他
100美元款项的人。
南京日本宪兵队请求上海宪兵司令部
查找丁卓并对其进行讯问，以查明
被捕日本籍人士向丁卓借款的借口。”
刑事调查员科诺瓦洛夫（Konovaloff）、宋秉宗（Soong Ping Tsung）、侦探警司罗兹（Rhodes）及副侦探警司清水（Shimidzu）提供了必要的协助。

At 2.30 p.m. 23.8.39 the aforementioned
party visited the given addresses of Ting Tsauh, at
Room 205, 255 Peking Road, and House, 5, Jinj Myieh
Li off Inza Road Bridge when it was found that
the Room 205 had been vacated by Ting Tsauh two
months ago. At the time of calling at the last
mentioned address Ting Tsauh was also absent, but
a note was left with his wife instructing Ting
Tsauh to call in the C.I offices on the following
morning.

At 9 a.m. on the 24th August 1939 Ting
Tsauh came to C.I offices where he was questioned
by Sergeant Major Yoshino on the subject and was
allowed to go free.

Interrogations of Ting Tsauh show that
nothing of a political nature exist in this case.
He was merely wanted for questioning in order to
verify the veracity of statement of the arrested
Japanese subject in Nanking.

19/-

P. Konovaloff.

D. C. (Special Branch).

H. Q. C. B. 8290/6
August 28, 39.

JAPANESE SUBJECTS KIDNAPPED NEAR KIANGYIN.

D. S. Rhodes D. I. Glover

Sir,

At 11.15 a.m. on August 26th, 1939, Mr. Watanabe, Japanese, employed as an interpreter on the H. I. J. S. Idzumo, came to C.B.H.Q. and requested Police assistance to locate a male Chinese named Tsoong Hai Liang (宗海樑), who, it was believed, was in a position to assist in freeing three male Japanese subjects who are now being held captive by bandits somewhere near Kiangyin.

One of the captive Japanese named Mr. I. Watanabe, aged 29, a resident of No. 10 Eur An Li, North Szechuen Road, is a brother of the applicant.

It was ascertained that the kidnapped Japanese Watanabe and the Chinese Tsoong Hai Liang were associated in some cattle dealing business.

Early in August Watanabe and two Japanese companions proceeded up country to buy cattle, and on August 12th, 1939 were staying at a Chinese hotel near Kiangyin when it was raided by a party of about 80 bandits, who took the Japanese and some Chinese away with them. The news of this raid reached Shanghai, and finally Watanabe heard that one of the victims was his brother.

Before leaving Shanghai Tsoong Hai Liang, who was aware of the intended trip about to be undertaken by Watanabe, had informed him that should such an incident take place, he (Tsoong) should be notified as soon as possible, since he knew some one who was in a position to contact the bandits and thus could secure their release. It was with this object that Police assistance was requested to locate Tsoong Hai Liang.

江阴附近日本籍人士被绑架案。

侦探警司 罗兹 侦探员 格洛弗

先生，

1939年8月26日上午11时15分，受雇于日本海军出云号巡洋舰（H. I. J. S. Idzumo）担任翻译的日本籍人士渡边先生来到罪案分部总部，请求警方协助查找一名名为宗海樑（Tsoong Hai Liang，宗海樑）的中国男性，据信此人能够协助解救三名目前被匪徒扣押在江阴某地的日本籍男子。

被扣人质中的一名日本人名叫I. 渡边，29岁，居住在北四川路欧安里10号，系申请人之兄。

经查，被绑架的日本人渡边与中国人宗海樑在某种牲畜买卖生意中有往来。

8月初，渡边与两名日本同伴前往内地购买牲畜，1939年8月12日，他们住在江阴附近的一家中国旅馆时，遭到约80名匪徒的袭击，日本人及部分中国人被匪徒带走。这一袭击消息传至上海，最终渡边得知受害者之一是其兄长。

在离开上海前，知晓渡边即将出行的宗海樑曾告知他，若发生此类事件，应尽快通知他（宗），因为他认识能够联系匪徒的人，从而可以确保人质获释。正是出于此目的，才请求警方协助查找宗海樑。

D.S.I. Lieu Kyung Ching, D.P.S. Yamahara and the
undersigned, accompanied Watanabe to the Kuo Hwa (國華)
Paper Manufacturing Co., Ltd., Room No. 304, No. 356 Peking
Road, it being known that Tsoong was a partner in that concern.
Enquiries amongst the staff therein elicited that
although he was a partner, he had not visited the premises
for some time past, and his only address known to them was
No. 16 Poo Yuen Li (普益里), Avenue Road.
These premises, however, had been visited earlier
by the Japanese himself, only to find that Tsoong had removed
some time ago.
Efforts to locate other persons who knew of Tsoong's
whereabouts proved of no avail.
One Mr. Zee Chi Sih (徐佳爽), head of the Paper
Coy., stated that Tsoong was not an active partner of the
concern, he having only invested a few thousand dollars
therein. He promised to endeavour to trace the present
whereabouts of Tsoong and would notify the Police on any
information obtained.

the Japanese Consular Police.
The C.P.C., during the enquiry, denied all
knowledge of the robbery in question, except what he
had read in the newspapers and denied being in
possession of a private pistol.
A prisoner brought to C.D.H. (C. I.) as
a witness by the Japanese Consular Police, named :-
WONG KYI LIANG (王向亮), 38, M/Unemployed,
Chauffeur, native of Kempo,
residing in No. 20 Refugee
Camp, Kinghow Road.
was closely questioned by detectives of C. I. and stated
that at 7 a.m. on the 15-8-39, he, accompanied a male
Chinese named Fan (范) to Lane 804, Ferry Road, where

致警务处助理处长

1939年9月8日上午11时30分，日本领事馆警察顾问桥爪（Hashizume）先生请求，
当日下午在中央捕房刑事调查处（C.D.H. (C. I.)）由他进一步讯问华捕2402号。
该请求获准后，华捕2402号于下午2时50分被带至中央捕房刑事调查处，
下午3时10分至5时期间，在日本领事馆警察附属的侦探督察秋冈（Akioka）和远藤（Yendo）及
侦探督察马维丰（Ma Wei Fung）和本人在场的情况下，
由桥爪先生对其进行了严密讯问。
华捕在讯问期间，否认对所述抢劫案有任何了解，
除其在报纸上读到的内容外，并否认持有私人手枪。
一名由日本领事馆警察作为证人带至中央捕房刑事调查处的囚犯，名为：
王向亮（WONG KYI LIANG，王向亮），38岁，男/无业，
司机，金门（Kempo，音译）籍，
居住在昆明路难民收容所20号。
经刑事调查处侦探严密讯问，该人称，
1939年8月15日上午7时，他陪同一名姓范（Fan，范）的中国男子
前往斐伦路804弄，在那里

page_data.en:
2/2

Pan explained he was negotiating the loan of a pistol.
On arrival at the entrance of the lane, he, Wong Kyi
Liang, was requested to remain outside whilst Pan
entered the rear door of the first house in the lane,
and at 8 a.m. returned with a pock-marked faced male
Chinese. After this, all three proceeded to the
Hongkew District.

During the evening of the crime on the
30-8-39 Pan explained to Wong Kyi Liang that the
genuine pistol used had been borrowed from an inmate of
the house visited by them on the 15-8-39, the pistol
having been obtained just prior to the robbery taking
place (7 p.m.).

Wong Kyi Liang was then arrested during the
evening of the 3-9-39 and at about 2 a.m. on the 4-9-39
led a party of Consular Police detectives to No. 15/894
Ferry Road, which was the house believed by him, to have
been visited by Pan on the 15-8-39, all the inmates
including C.P.C. 2402, were scrutinised but without
an identification being made (for full particulars re
illegal search please see Gordon Rd. O.B. entry 5 a.m.
4-9-39).

With a view of checking on the house in
question, Mr. Hashimoto requested and the P.A. to D.C.
Crime gave the necessary permission for the accused Wong
page_data.zh:
2/2

范解释说他正在商借一把手枪。
到达弄堂入口时，王向亮被要求留在外面，
而范进入弄堂内第一栋房屋的后门，
并于上午8时带回一名面部有麻点的中国男子。
此后，三人一同前往虹口区。

在1939年8月30日案发当晚，范向王向亮解释称，
作案使用的真手枪是从他们于1939年8月15日访问的那户房屋的住户处借来的，
该手枪是在抢劫发生前不久（下午7时）取得的。

王向亮随后于1939年9月3日晚被捕，
并于1939年9月4日凌晨2时许，带领一队领事馆警察侦探
前往斐伦路15/894号，据信这是范于1939年8月15日访问过的房屋，
包括华捕2402号在内的所有住户均受到仔细审查，
但未进行指认（关于非法搜查的详细情况，
请参见戈登路值班日志1939年9月4日上午5时的记录）。

为了核实该房屋，桥本（Hashimoto）先生提出请求，
罪案分部助理处长给予了必要许可，允许被告王

page_data.en:
2/3

Kyi Liang to lead detectives of C.B.II.4. (C. 1.) to the
scene.

At 5.10 p.m. a party consisting of D.S.'s
Kioka and Yendo attached to the Japanese Consular
Police, D.P.S.'s Yamahara and Shimidzu, D.C.I. Sia Vai
Faung and the undersigned accompanied the accused to
Ferry and Robison Roads and were then led by him
without hesitation to No. 3/894 Ferry Road.

Here it should be explained that Lane 894
Ferry Road, which is situated on the East side of Ferry
Road, consists of two rows of houses, access to which
can be gained from the roadway by any one of three
lanes, the first door on the north side of the souther-
most lane is the front door of No. 3, the first door on
the north side of the centre lane is the front door of
No. 15, opposite being the rear of No. 3, whilst the
first door of the north side lane is the rear door of
No. 15.

On being questioned as to why he led the
Japanese detectives to the first rear door of the 3rd
lane instead of the centre one, the accused explained
that it was dark at the time of his previous visit, but
on this occasion he was absolutely certain as he re-
cognised a power pole at the entrance of the Lane against
which he rested and further remembered that the Lane in
page_data.zh:
2/3

向亮带领刑事调查二科四股（C.B.II.4. (C. 1.)）的侦探前往现场。

下午5时10分，由隶属于日本领事馆警察的侦探警司秋冈（Kioka）和远藤（Yendo）、
副侦探警司山原（Yamahara）和清水（Shimidzu）、
首席侦探督察谢伟芳（Sia Vai Faung）及本人组成的小组陪同被告
前往斐伦路和罗宾森路，随后由被告毫不犹豫地带领至
斐伦路3/894号。

此处需说明的是，位于斐伦路东侧的斐伦路894弄，
由两排房屋组成，可通过三条弄堂中的任何一条从道路进入，
最南侧弄堂北侧的第一扇门是3号的前门，
中间弄堂北侧的第一扇门是15号的前门，对面是3号的后门，
而北侧弄堂的第一扇门是15号的后门。

当被问及为何带领日本侦探前往第三条弄堂的第一个后门而非中间那个时，
被告解释说，上次访问时天色已黑，
但这次他绝对确定，因为他认出了弄堂入口处的一根电线杆，
他当时曾倚靠在该电线杆上，并且还记得他访问的那条弄堂

page_data.en:
2/4

which he visited was partly occupied by a wooden hut,
whilst the third lane is occupied by a food stall.
    Inquiries in house 3 and vicinity failed
in locating any one answering the description of the
pock-marked faced person.
    From a check of the duty book in O'Neil
Station it was learned that C.P.C. 2402 was on duty
from 7 a.m. to 11 a.m. on the 15-8-39, so could not
have been at home during Fan's visit, and was on duty
from 3 p.m. to 7 p.m. on the 30-8-39, so could not have
handed over a pistol just prior to the robbery, as
stated by Fan.

部分被一个木制棚屋占据，而第三条弄堂则被一个食品摊位占据。
    在3号房屋及周边的查询未能找到任何符合
面部有麻点特征描述的人。
    通过检查奥尼尔捕房的值班记录簿得知，
华捕2402号在1939年8月15日上午7时至11时值班，
因此在范访问期间不可能在家；且在1939年8月30日下午3时至7时值班，
因此不可能如范所述在抢劫发生前不久移交手枪。

J. 罗辛顿（Rossington）

Wong Ki Liang (王廟亮)
Kompo
x D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung
translated Kuh Nei Han

My name is Wong Ki Liang (王廟亮), age 38, a
native of Kompo, married, unemployed, residing in a refugee
camp at No. 28, Kiaochow Road.

At about 3-4 p.m. August 30, 1939, I and Van Yu Wu
(范月湖), went to Lou Ni's (老二) home near Singapore
Road, where I, Van Yu Wu, Ze Sing Dah, Ma Ts (麻子), Lou
Ni and his brother gathered together and negotiated to rob
the Tuh Dah Native Bank, Wuchang Road. Van Yu Wu and
some of them went there immediately after the negotiation
whilst I and Ze Sing Dah went there at about 5 p.m.

When we arrived there Ma Ts took out his pistol
and began to rob the bank. I also took out my imitation
pistol and jointed him. After we stole more than $3000.0.
00 from there we escaped to one of my accomplice's homes
in a certain lane, on Wuchang Road. Each of us has got
one hundred dollars (American Notes) of the spoils.

Next day, Lou Ni and his brother took the rest of
the spoils together with the pistol and an imitation one
to Lou Ni's home, and each got $4500, of the spoils.

At 9 p.m. 3-9-39, I was arrested by the Settlement
Police in a certain small inn near Yu Ya Ching Road, and
I then handed my share to the police.

At 7-8 a.m. August 13, 39, I and Van Yu Wu went to
Ma Ts's home on Ferry Road to see the pistol, but did not
meet Ma Ts or see the pistol.

This is my true statement.

Signed and thumbprinted by Wong Ki Liang.

王庙亮（Wong Ki Liang，王廟亮）
金门（Kompo，音译）
x 刑事调查员 宋秉宗
翻译 顾内汉（Kuh Nei Han，音译）

我叫王庙亮（Wong Ki Liang，王廟亮），38岁，金门（Kompo，音译）人，已婚，无业，居住在胶州路28号的难民收容所。

1939年8月30日下午3-4时许，我和范月湖（Van Yu Wu，范月湖）前往新加坡路附近老二（Lou Ni，音译）的家，在那里，我、范月湖、徐星达（Ze Sing Dah，音译）、麻子（Ma Ts，音译）、老二及其兄弟聚集在一起，商议抢劫武昌路的土大钱庄（Tuh Dah Native Bank，音译）。范月湖和部分人在商议后立即前往那里，而我和徐星达则在下午5时左右到达。

当我们到达那里时，麻子拿出他的手枪开始抢劫钱庄。我也拿出我的仿制手枪加入了他。我们从那里偷走了3000多美元后，逃到了武昌路某弄堂内一名同伙的家中。我们每人分得了一百美元（美钞）赃款。

第二天，老二及其兄弟将其余赃款连同真手枪和一把仿制手枪带到老二的家，每人分得4500美元赃款。

1939年9月3日晚上9时，我在虞洽卿路附近的一家小旅馆被租界警察逮捕，随后我将我分得的赃款交给了警方。

1939年8月13日上午7-8时，我和范月湖前往斐伦路麻子的家看手枪，但未见到麻子，也未看到手枪。

这是我的真实供词。

王庙亮签字并按手印。

Subject Re the functioning of Japanese, in plain-clothes, in Gordon Road District.

Made by D.S. 21 Smith Forwarded by T. E. Mason
Officer i/c.

Sir,

At 2.25 a.m. 4-9-39 a telephone message was received from S.P.C. 3402 (attached to B'well Stn.), through street telephone box No. 2, to the effect that a party of Japanese, in plain-clothes, had just searched his home Lane 904/15 Perry Road.

U.I.S. 153 and the undersigned immediately attended and from enquiries elicited the following:-

At about 7 p.m. 2-9-39 a group of about five Japanese, all wearing foreign style clothing and accompanied by a male Chinese, also wearing foreign style clothing, who acted as interpreter for the party, and one male Chinese of the coolie class wearing blue cotton jacket and pants who was handcuffed, entered the unlocked rear door of Lane 904/17 Perry Road.

Upon entering the party, through the Chinese interpreter, questioned the inmates of the house as to whether there was a musician named Van (范) residing on the premises.

On being informed that the man Van was out and that he had not returned to his 1st floor loft room since the 1-9-39, the Japanese members of the party searched the 1st floor loft that had been occupied by the musician Van.

As far as could be ascertained nothing was seized from the room of the man Van although all boxes etc had been thoroughly ransacked.

After searching the room the party left the premises after informing the inmates that they were 'Police'.

先生：

1939年9月4日凌晨2时25分，通过2号街头电话亭接到隶属于静安寺巡捕房的华捕 3402号的电话留言，称一伙便衣日本人刚刚搜查了他的住所，地址为斐伦路（Perry Road）904弄15号。

印度巡捕 153号与本人立即赶赴现场，经询问获悉以下情况：

1939年9月2日晚7时许，一群约五名日本人，均身着西式服装，由一名同样身着西式服装并担任翻译的中国男子，以及一名身穿蓝布棉袄裤、戴着手铐的苦力阶层中国男子陪同，进入了斐伦路904弄17号未上锁的后门。

进入屋内后，该伙人通过中国翻译询问屋内住户，是否有一名姓范（Van）的音乐家居住在此。

当得知范某外出，且自1939年9月1日以来未曾返回其位于二楼的阁楼房间后，该伙人中的日本成员搜查了音乐家范某曾居住的二楼阁楼。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    Misc. File No. 335/39.

REPORT    Station, ____
Date ____ 19

Subject. ____

Made by. ____    Forwarded by. ____

At about 1.10 a.m. 4-9-39 the same party of Japanese, accompanied by the same interpreter and prisoner, entered the unlocked rear door of Lane 894/15 Ferry Road and, after arousing the inmates, demanded to be shown to the room occupied by a musician.

On being informed by C.P.C. 2402, who was off duty, that there were no musicians residing in the premises the party left, after having written down the number of the C.P.C. from his tunic, which was hanging on the wall of of his room.

After leaving Lane 894/15 Ferry Road the Japanese party proceeded next door and again entered House No.17 of the same lane.

After making enquiries in this house, as to whether or not the man Van had returned and on receiving replies in the negative, the party left the premises via the open rear door and again entered House No.15.

Upon re-entering House No.15 they again made fruit-less enquiries, regarding any musicians residing on the premises and upon gaining no satisfaction, the party left the premises via the rear door at about 2.15 a.m. 4-9-39 without having made any arrests or effecting any seizure.

D.P.S. Tsuji was informed of this occurrence and upon his attending this station he made unsuccessful efforts to learn the identity of the Japanese party who had visited and searched Houses 15 and 17 of Lane 894 Ferry Road. He will, however, continue his enquiries at the Japanese Gendarmerie and Consular Police Headquarters on the 4-9-39.

Sen. Det. 1/o, Officer 1/c, D.D.O."B" and Officer of the Day, U.S.M.C. informed.

1939年9月4日凌晨1时10分许，同一伙日本人，由同一名翻译和囚犯陪同，进入了斐伦路894弄15号未上锁的后门，在唤醒住户后，要求带他们去看一名音乐家居住的房间。

当时休班的华捕 2402号告知他们此处并无音乐家居住，该伙人便离开了，但在离开前记下了挂在房间墙上的华捕制服上的编号。

离开斐伦路894弄15号后，这伙日本人前往隔壁，再次进入了同一条弄堂的17号房屋。

在该房屋内询问范某是否回来后，得到否定答复，该伙人通过敞开的后门离开该处，并再次进入15号房屋。

重新进入15号房屋后，他们再次就是否有音乐家居住在此进行徒劳的询问，在未得到满意结果后，该伙人于1939年9月4日凌晨2时15分左右通过后门离开该处，期间未实施任何逮捕或扣押行动。

已将此事件告知警佐 Tsuji，他赶到本巡捕房后，试图查明访问并搜查斐伦路894弄15号和17号的日本人身份，但未获成功。他将于1939年9月4日继续在日本宪兵队和日本领事馆警察总部进行调查。

已通知高级侦探1/o、主管警官、“B”区副助理总监及美国海军陆战队值班军官。

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Shan-Ken-Ko No. 125 has been received
which states that the two persons, Tsien Pung
(錢鵬) and Wong Tsang Yien (王占一) who
were handed over to the Japanese Gendarmerie
on November 22nd 1939, have been tried and

GENDARMERIE.

Statements taken from the three prisoners
namely:-
1. Wong Tsang Yien (王占一);
2. Tsien Fang (錢),
3. Lieu Kyi Yoong (刘建荣).
are attached herewith.

It will be seen that the 1st. and 2nd.
named have in the past both been concerned in
guerrilla activities, although the method employed
by the Gendarmerie's informers to produce documentary
evidence was done in a manner not compatible with
Police procedure.

The 3rd. named denies having at any time
taken part in guerrilla or anti-Japanese activities
and as only been connected with the former persons
for a short time and then took no part in their
guerrilla activities. Regarding the cloth
badge of appointment which he discarded in the
Police Van enroute to the office of C.B.H.Q., he
admits that just prior to the arrival of the Police
at the Tsung Hwa hotel he snatched same from Woo
Tsung Ming (吳振明) to prevent a quarrel.

名列第三人否认曾参与任何游击或反日活动，并称仅与前两人有短暂联系，且未参与他们的游击活动。关于他在前往刑事科总部办公室的警车上丢弃的委任布质徽章，他承认在警察到达宗华饭店（Tsung Hwa hotel）之前不久，他从吴振明（Woo Tsung Ming）手中夺下该徽章，以防止争吵。

(1)

2nd.
/
Hsuchow
C.I, C.B.H.C.

Wong Tsang Yien
11.11.39

J.S. Rhodes
Clerk Hsin

I wish to make the following statement in connection
with my guerrilla activities, and in corroboration of the
statement made by me to the Japanese Gendarmerie:-

Soon after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in Shanghai in 1937 I was thrown out of employ-
ment and after some months of idleness I decided to join
the regular army.

During October 1938 I definitely made up my mind
to organize a guerrilla unit and in this connection I
approached one named See Tai Uing (徐戴廷), who later
introduced me to Woo Tsung Ling (吴振明) in the Su Loh
teashop, Rue Paul Beau, French Concession. This person I
knew was actively engaged in guerrilla activities.

We agreed to organize a unit which should operate
around the Kompo area and should be composed of men known
as Hung Mun (红帮). The following were elected to serve
as officers:-

Chief of Unit (myself) Wong Tsang Yien (王占一)
Assistant Chief Wu Hai Kwung (吴汉坤)
Chief of 1st.Branch Unit Hsia Pau Chaen (夏保全)
Chief of 2nd.Branch Unit Tsu Tuh Kyi (朱得义)
Secretary & Judge for Court Martial Woo Tsung Ling (吴振明)
Chief of Military Depot See Tai Uing (徐戴廷)
Liaison Officer Ma Sing San (马成山)

Other members were also enlisted as reserves.
page_data.zh:
(1)

第二。
/
徐州
C.I, C.B.H.C.

王占一
1939年11月11日

J.S. Rhodes
书记员 Hsin

我就我的游击活动以及与向日本宪兵队所作陈述相佐证的事项，作出如下声明：

1937年上海中日敌对行动爆发后不久，我失业了，在闲居数月后，我决定加入正规军。

1938年10月期间，我下定决心组织一支游击队，为此我接触了一位名叫徐戴廷（See Tai Uing）的人，他后来在法租界贝当路（Rue Paul Beau）的苏罗茶室将我介绍给吴振明（Woo Tsung Ling）。我知道此人积极参与游击活动。

我们同意组织一支在江湾（Kompo）地区活动的部队，成员由被称为红帮（Hung Mun）的人组成。以下人员被选任为官职：

部队长（本人）王占一（Wong Tsang Yien）
副队长吴汉坤（Wu Hai Kwung）
第一分队长夏保全（Hsia Pau Chaen）
第二分队长朱得义（Tsu Tuh Kyi）
秘书兼军法官吴振明（Woo Tsung Ling）
军需处长徐戴廷（See Tai Uing）
联络官马成山（Ma Sing San）

其他成员也被征召为后备人员。

page_data.en:
(2)

After the above staff had been selected we
decided to enter into negotiations with Chang Yih Ming,
Commander of the Eastern Route Guerrilla Unit Central
Kiangsu and Chekiang Area.

Woo Tsung Ming and Ma Ling San were sent to con-
tact Chang and inform him of our intentions.

Toward the end of September 1939 Woo Tsung Ming
and Ma Ling San returned to Shanghai and informed me that
they had contacted General Chang Yih Ming and that he had
officially appointed me Chief of the unit, which we had
organized and that same was to be known as the 11th. Branch
of the Eastern Route Guerrilla Unit and we were to operate
around the Kompo area. Woo Tsung Ming further added that
I must pay $240.00 to General Chang as a present, to confirm
my appointment. I agreed and handed the money to Woo.

In October 1939, I personally interviewed General
Chang who at that time was in Shanghai staying at the Sing
Sung Wah Lodging House, Rue Krastner, French Concession.

He instructed me and my unit to proceed to Kompo
and there reorganize the Peace Maintenance Corps, and to
train other disorganized units in that area. He issued
to me a badge of appointment.

On 15th. October, 1939, Zee Tai Ding , Tse Tuh
Nyi, Wu Hai Kwang and Woo Tsung Ming proceeded to Ha Ta
(海塌) Yen Chen Hsien to negotiate with the local
authorities there. Woo had in his possession the badge
which Chang had given to me.
page_data.zh:
(2)

在上述职员选定后，我们决定与江浙地区东路游击队司令张逸民（Chang Yih Ming）进行谈判。

吴振明和马灵山（Ma Ling San）(注：前文为马成山)被派去联系张司令，并告知他我们的意图。

1939年9月底，吴振明和马灵山回到上海，告诉我他们已经联系了张逸民将军，张将军正式任命我为我们所组织部队的队长，该部队被称为东路游击队第十一支队，我们将在江湾（Kompo）地区活动。吴振明还补充说，我必须向张将军支付240.00元作为礼物，以确认我的任命。我同意了，并将钱交给了吴。

1939年10月，我亲自拜访了当时住在法租界克拉司纳路（Rue Krastner）新顺华旅馆的张将军。

他指令我和我的部队前往江湾，在那里重组和平维持团，并训练该地区其他散乱的部队。他向我颁发了一枚委任徽章。

1939年10月15日，徐戴廷（Zee Tai Ding）、朱得义（Tse Tuh Nyi）、吴汉光（Wu Hai Kwang）和吴振明前往海塌（Ha Ta）盐城县，与当地当局进行谈判。吴持有张将军给我的那枚徽章。

page_data.en:
(5)

Due to the fact that my wife was ill I did not
accompany the advance party, but a week later I left
Shanghai to join them together with Hsia Pau Chuen.

Arriving at Hu Tu I sent Hsia Pau Chuen ashore
to enquire about the vanguard and later he returned and
reported to me that one of my men named Tsu Tuh Nyi had been
arrested by the local police and executed, and the remainder
had disappeared.

I located Woo Tsung Ming however and stayed with
him one night, the next morning I boarded the ship and
returned to Shanghai intending to report to General Chang
Yih Ming.

However I could not find General Chang and I
commenced hawking vegetables etc. to eke out a living.

I took no further part in guerrilla activities
and did not encounter any of my officers until 6.9.39 when
I met Woo Tsung Ming. After exchanging greeting etc.
Woo invited me to attend the Great Eastern Hotel at 3 p.m.
the same afternoon to have tea with him.

I kept the appointment and took along with me
a friend named Lieu Kyi Yoong (刘建荣).

Arriving at the tea-room of the Great Eastern
Hotel at 3 p.m. I met Tsien Pang (钱鹏) whom I had first
met some time previous, and who I also knew had been in
charge of guerrilla units in Tsengchow.

Later we all adjourned to Room No.815 of the Tsung
Hwa Hotel and there discussed transportation business, Woo
page_data.zh:
(5)

由于我妻子生病，我没有随先遣队同行，但一周后，我与夏宝泉（Hsia Pau Chuen）一同离开上海去与他们汇合。

抵达湖涂（Hu Tu，音译）后，我派夏宝泉上岸打听先遣队的情况，随后他回来向我报告说，我手下的一名叫祖杜尼（Tsu Tuh Nyi，音译）的人被当地警察逮捕并处决，其余人员则下落不明。

我找到了吴宗明（Woo Tsung Ming），并在他那里住了一晚。第二天早上，我登船返回上海，打算向张逸民将军（Chang Yih Ming）汇报。

然而，我未能找到张将军，于是我开始靠贩卖蔬菜等物品维持生计。

此后我不再参与游击活动，直到1939年9月6日遇到吴宗明之前，未再遇见我的任何军官。互相寒暄后，吴邀请我于当天下午3点到东亚大酒店与他喝茶。

我如约前往，并带了一位名叫刘建荣（Lieu Kyi Yoong）的朋友同行。

下午3点到达东亚大酒店的茶室时，我遇到了钱鹏（Tsien Pang），我之前曾见过他，并且知道他曾负责常州地区的游击部队。

page_data.en:
(4)

Tsung Ming claiming that he had 1000 bags of cotton in
Wusih and asked me if I could arrange for a pass to transport
the cotton to Shanghai, since I was employed in a Japanese
transportation company at the time and my job was to arrange
such affairs.

I left the hotel at 8 p.m. and returned home.

At about 9 a.m. 7.9.39 Lieu Kyi Yoong called at
my home and requested me to again attend the Tsung Hwa Hotel
stating that it was the wish of Woo Tsung Ming.

I accompanied Lieu to the hotel and found Tsien
Pang, Woo Tsung Ming and one Ching (陳) there, the latter,
according to Woo Tsung Ming was the owner of the cotton he
wished transporting to Shanghai.

I immediately asked for further details regarding
the transportation of the cotton but Woo said that it would
be discussed further after having had tiffin.

The conversation was general at first, no reference
being made to guerrilla activities until Woo Tsung Ming took
from his person a silk cloth badge of appointment, which
bore my name as chief of a guerrilla unit, and referred
to the appointment of Woo Tsung Ming as chief of the Military
Court under my command.

Here I wish to state that this badge of appointment
is false for during the short time I was engaged in guerrilla
activities I never issued an such appointment to anyone
and the only badge of appointment which I had, was given
to me by Chang Yih Ming when he appointed me chief of the
page_data.zh:
(4)

后来我们都转移到中和饭店815号房间，在那里讨论运输业务，吴宗明声称他在无锡有1000包棉花，问我能否安排通行证将棉花运往上海，因为我当时受雇于一家日本运输公司，我的工作就是处理此类事务。

晚上8点我离开酒店回家。

1939年9月7日上午9点左右，刘建荣来到我家，请求我再次前往中和饭店，称这是吴宗明的意愿。

我陪同刘前往酒店，发现钱鹏、吴宗明和一名姓陈（Ching）的人在那里，据吴宗明说，后者是他希望运往上海的棉花的所有者。

我立即询问关于棉花运输的更多细节，但吴说吃过午饭后再进一步讨论。

起初谈话内容很泛泛，没有提及游击活动，直到吴宗明从身上拿出一块丝绸委任状，上面写着我的名字，任命我为游击队队长，并提及任命吴宗明为我麾下的军事法庭庭长。

在此我要声明，这块委任状是伪造的，因为在我从事游击活动的短暂时间内，我从未向任何人发出过此类委任，我所拥有的唯一委任状是张逸民任命我为

page_data.en:
(5)

11th. Branch Central East Guerrilla Unit.
    This badge of appointment which bore my name
I gave to Woo Tsung Ming when he proceeded to Kompo on
my behalf in October 1938, since which time I have never
seen it, but it is definitely not the one which Woo Tsung
Ming produced in the room of the hotel, and which was
seized by the Police.
    When Woo produced this badge of appointment I
told him that same should be destroyed, I took it from
him and attempted to burn it, but Lieu Kyl Yoong snatched
the cloth from me placed same in his pocket just as Police
arrived and arrested us.
    This is my true statement.

                    Signed:- Wong Tsang Yien
                    王 占 一 十
page_data.zh:
(5)

华东游击队第十一支队队长时发给我的。
    这块写有我名字的委任状，我在1938年10月吴宗明代表我前往甘堡（Kompo，音译）时交给了他，自那以后我再也没见过它，但这绝对不是吴宗明在酒店房间里出示并被警方缴获的那一块。
    当吴出示这块委任状时，我告诉他应该将其销毁，我从他手中拿过委任状试图烧毁它，但刘建荣从我手中抢走布料放入口袋，就在这时警察赶到并将我们逮捕。
    这是我的真实陈述。

                    签名:- 王占一
                    王 占 一 十

page_data.en:
(1)

Tsien Pang
Kampo                                D.S. Rhodes
Col. C.B.H.C.        11.11.59        Clark Hsia

My name is Tsien Pang (錢) alias Tsien Yuin
Chuen (錢芸卅), native of Kampo, unemployed, residing
at No.122 Ying Foo Lee, Rue Buissonet, French Concession
and I wish to state the following in connection with my
guerrilla activities.

At the outbreak of the Sin-Japanese hostilities
in the Shanghai area in 1937 I was compelled to give up
my business and seek the aid of relatives for a living.

In October 1938, I was introduced to Woo Tsung
Ming and from him learned that Toong Jing Ying (鄭本殷),
well known guerrilla leader operating around the Soochow
area was recruiting men.

I decided to join his unit and together with Woo
Tsung Ming and one Lieu Ching Ling (劉全林) proceeded to
Soochow and interviewed Toong.

After a long talk he instructed me and Lieu Ching
Ling to go to Sing An and there organize and train a unit.

Within one month after arriving at Sing An we had
enrolled 300 men, Lieu Ching Ling was made Commander and I was
appointed Chief of Staff. Woo Tsung Ming was made Chief
Secretary and Chief of the Military Court.

We remained inactive in Wusih, but due to lack of
funds we were forced to levy taxes on the residents in order
to maintain our force.

During April 1939, I resigned from the unit and
went to Zangchow, and on the 3rd. June 1939, I came to
Shanghai and went to stay with relatives at 122 Rue Buissonet,
French Concession.
page_data.zh:
(1)

钱鹏
甘堡（Kampo）                                D.S. Rhodes
C.B.H.C. 上校        1959年11月11日        Clark Hsia

我叫钱鹏（Tsien Pang），别名钱芸卅（Tsien Yuin Chuen，音译），甘堡人，无业，居住在法租界蒲石路（Rue Buissonet）英福里122号，现就我的游击活动事宜陈述如下。

1937年上海地区中日敌对行动爆发时，我被迫放弃生意，依靠亲戚接济维持生活。

1938年10月，经人介绍我认识了吴宗明，并从他那里得知，在苏州地区活动的著名游击队领袖郑本殷（Toong Jing Ying）正在招募人员。

我决定加入他的部队，并与吴宗明及刘全林（Lieu Ching Ling）一同前往苏州会见郑。

经过长谈，他指示我和刘全林前往新安（Sing An，音译），在那里组织并训练一支队伍。

抵达新安后一个月内，我们招募了300人，刘全林被任命为指挥官，我被任命为参谋长。吴宗明被任命为秘书长兼军事法庭庭长。

我们在无锡按兵不动，但由于缺乏资金，我们被迫向居民征税以维持部队。

1939年4月，我辞去了部队职务前往常州（Zangchow，音译），1939年6月3日，我来到上海，住在法租界蒲石路122号的亲戚家。

page_data.en:
(2)

On August 22nd. 1939, Woo Tsung Ming came to
my home and explained that he had resigned from the
guerrilla unit and was working in some advertising company.
Later he visited me again and requested me to take
charge of a group of guerrillas in Paoshan and arrange for
them to become members of the Wang Ching wei clique.
This I refused to do, since I had definitely made
up my mind not to take part in any further activities of
such a nature.
Woo then later asked me if I would arrange for 1000
guerrillas then under the Command of one Koo Han Dong (顧漢東)
who were operating in Moh Doh, Soochow to join with the
unit under one Toong Tung Ying.
On September 3rd. 1939, Woo invited me to the
Great Eastern Hotel for the purpose of meeting one named
Ching (陳) who was supposed to be a relative of Koo Han
Dong.
I kept the appointment but Ching did not appear
and I returned home.
Woo continued to visit me at my home and on each
occasion always made reference to the letter he wished me
to write to Toong Tung Ying.
On September 4th. 1939 I met Wong Tsang Yien who
informed me that he was engaged in arranging passes for the
transportation of cargo through the occupied areas. I
first met this person prior to the outbreak of hostilities
when I was operating a shipping company.
page_data.zh:
(2)

1939年8月22日，吴宗明来到我家，解释说他已经从游击队辞职，正在某广告公司工作。后来他又来拜访我，请求我负责宝山的一群游击队员，并安排他们加入汪精卫派系。
我拒绝了这一要求，因为我已下定决心不再参与任何此类性质的活动。
随后吴又问我，是否能安排当时由顾汉东（Koo Han Dong）指挥、在苏州莫都（Moh Doh，音译）活动的1000名游击队员加入童通英（Toong Tung Ying，音译）的部队。
1939年9月3日，吴邀请我到东亚大酒店会见一位姓陈（Ching）的人，据说此人是顾汉东的亲戚。
我如约前往，但陈某没有出现，我便回家了。
吴继续到我家拜访，每次总是提到他希望我写给童通英的信。
1939年9月4日，我遇到了王占一，他告诉我他正忙于安排货物通过占领区的运输通行证。早在敌对行动爆发前我经营航运公司时就初次认识此人。

page_data.en:
(3)

On 1st. September 1959, Woo Tsung Ming again
invited me to have tea at the Great Eastern tea room,
he being desirous that I should meet Ching, the relative
of Koo Man Dong,. I went to the tea room of the Great
Eastern Hotel at about 3 p.m. and found Woo Tsung Ming
already there. When the person Ching failed to put in an
appearance , Woo left for the supposed intention of looking
for him.

He returned about one hour later and stated that
he could not find Ching and further requested me to go to the
Tsung Hwa Hotel.

At the hotel Woo engaged room No.213, again he
requested me to draft a letter to Toong Fung Ying regarding
the guerrillas under Koo Man Dong who were desirous of
joining him (Toong Fung Ying).

Finally I agreed and drafted a letter addressed to
a friend of mine named Kung (孔 ), principal of a school
in Zangchow and requested that he inform Toong Fung Ying,
that Koo Man Dong and his unit were desirous of joining him.
A second letter I wrote to Toong Fung Ying on the same subject
A third letter I wrote to my relatives.

According to Woo Tsung Ming the three letters would
be given to Ching, who would take them to Wusih on the
following day. Later that evening the person Ching arrived
and he posed as a relative of Koo Man Dong, and promised me
$80.00 if the arrangements regarding the amalgamation of the
guerrilla units was a success.
page_data.zh:
(3)

1959年9月1日（原文如此，应为1939年），吴宗明再次邀请我到东亚茶室喝茶，他希望我能见到顾曼东（Koo Man Dong，音译）的亲戚陈某。我于下午3点左右到达东亚大酒店的茶室，发现吴宗明已经在那里。当陈某没有出现时，吴离开说是去找他。

大约一小时后他回来，说找不到陈某，并进一步请求我去中和饭店。

在酒店，吴开了213号房间，再次请求我起草一封给童凤英（Toong Fung Ying，音译）的信，内容是关于顾曼东麾下希望加入他（童凤英）的游击队员。

最后我同意了，并起草了一封信寄给我在常州的一位朋友孔某（Kung），他是一所学校的校长，请他通知童凤英，顾曼东及其部队希望加入。我就同一主题给童凤英写了第二封信。我还给亲戚写了第三封信。

据吴宗明说，这三封信将交给陈某，由他第二天带到无锡。当天晚上，陈某到达，他自称是顾曼东的亲戚，并承诺如果游击队合并事宜成功，将给我80美元。

page_data.en:
(4)

I remained in the room till the night of 6.7.39 and
next morning Koo Tsung Ming, Ching, Wong Tsang Yien, Lieu
Kyi Yoong and one other arrived.

Ching explained that he was unable to take the
letters I had written to Wash and stated that they would
be sent by some other person.

Later during the forenoon Koo Tsung Ming took a
badge of appointment from out of his sock and upon seeing it
Wong Tsang Yien attempted to destroy it.

Lieu Kyi Yoong however took same and put it into
his pocket, shortly afterwards Police arrived and arrested
us. The letters which I had written were found in a draw.

Here I wish to state that the person Ching who had
been posing as a friend of Koo Han Dong, was no other than
a Japanese informer who together with Koo Tsung Ming tricked
me into writing the letters, which were afterwards planted in
the room, in order to enable them to produce documentary
evidence against me.

This is my true statement.

Signed:- Tsien Peng.
錢鵬十
page_data.zh:
(4)

我在房间里一直待到1939年9月6日晚上（原文日期为6.7.39，结合上下文应为9月6日或7日之误，此处照实翻译日期数字），第二天早上，吴宗明（原文误作Koo Tsung Ming）、陈某、王占一、刘建荣和另一人到达。

陈某解释说他无法将我写的信带到无锡（Wash，疑为Wusih无锡之误），并表示将由其他人发送。

后来在上午，吴宗明（原文误作Koo Tsung Ming）从袜子里拿出一块委任状，王占一看到后试图将其销毁。

然而，刘建荣拿走委任状放入口袋，不久后警察赶到并将我们逮捕。我写的信件在一个抽屉里被发现。

在此我要声明，那个冒充顾汉东朋友的陈某，其实是一名日本线人，他与吴宗明（原文误作Koo Tsung Ming）一起诱骗我写下这些信件，随后将信件栽赃在房间里，以便他们能拿出针对我的书面证据。

这是我的真实陈述。

签名:- 钱鹏
錢鵬十

page_data.en:
2nd.
Shangtung
Lieu Kyi Yoong
D.S. Rhodes
Col, C.B.M...
11.11.39
Clerk Hsia

My name is Lieu Kyi Yoong (刘建荣) aged 29,
native of Shantung, residing at 323 Sing Sing Li, Rue Pere
Robert, French concession.

In November, 1937 through the introduction of a
friend I joined the French Municipal Police as constable
No. 954 and was posted to Central Police Station.

On account of sickness I was invalided from the
Force on July 17th. 1939, and for a short time I remained
at home recuperating.

In August 1939, I secured employment with the
Shanghai Chicken & Duck Dealers Association, Rue Massenet
and remained there until the time of my arrest.

Some time during the beginning of this year, 1939,
I first met Wong Tsang Yien (王占一) through the introduction
of my chief tenant named Ma Teh Nyi. (马德义). Later
during the time I was in the Police service I met this
person at Central Station, he often visiting his wife who
was also employed in the Police service. Apart from these
casual meetings I never knew anything more about him and
never visited him at his home.

At about 2 p.m. 6.9.39 I met Wong Tsang Yien and
he invited me to accompany him to the Great Eastern Hotel
where he stated he had an appointment to keep.

I accepted the invitation and upon arriving at the
hotel we went to the tea room where Wong introduced me to
two male Chinese named "Tsien Fang" (钱鹏) and "Woo Tsung
Ming" (吴振明). This was the first time that I had
ever met these people.
page_data.zh:
2nd.
山东
刘建荣
D.S. Rhodes
C.B.M... 上校,
1939年11月11日
书记员 Hsia

我叫刘建荣（Lieu Kyi Yoong），29岁，山东人，居住在法租界贝勒路（Rue Pere Robert，今黄陂南路）新新里323号。

1937年11月，经朋友介绍，我加入法公董局警务处，警号为954，被派往中央巡捕房。

因病，我于1939年7月17日从警队病退，在家休养了一段时间。

1939年8月，我在马思南路（Rue Massenet）的上海鸡鸭同业公会找到工作，并一直工作到被捕之时。

今年（1939年）初的某个时候，经我的主要房客马德义（Ma Teh Nyi）介绍，我初次认识了王占一（Wong Tsang Yien）。后来我在警队服役期间，在中央巡捕房遇到过这个人，他经常去探望也在警队工作的妻子。除了这些偶然的会面，我对他一无所知，也从未去他家拜访过。

1939年9月6日下午2点左右，我遇到王占一，他邀请我陪他去东亚大酒店，他说他有一个约会要赴。

我接受了邀请，到达酒店后，我们去了茶室，王向我介绍了两名中国男子，“钱方”（Tsien Fang，即钱鹏）和“吴振明”（Woo Tsung Ming）。这是我第一次见到这些人。

page_data.en:
(2)

Shortly after Woo Tsung Ming insisted that we all
go to a lodging house where it would be more convenient
to discuss business.

At first I declined since I was not taking any
part in their business talks, but finally they persuaded
me to do so.

We went to room No.213 Tsung Hwa Hotel and there
Woo Tsung Ming, Tsien Pang and Wong Tsang Yien discussed
the question of transportation of 1,000 pieces of cargo
from Moh Doh, Soochow to Shanghai. I heard no reference
made to guerrilla activities. In connection with this
cargo I heard Woo Tsung Ming request Tsien Pang to write
a letter, to whom I do not know, nor did I see him write
it.

Later
From the conversation I learned that Tsien Pang
had been a chief of a guerrilla Unit.

Upon leaving the hotel I was invited to attend
again the next day for a tiffin party.

On 7.9.39 I and Wong Tsang Yien arrived at the
hotel and found Tsien Pang and his wife already there.
Woo Tsung Ming arrived later closely followed by one named
Ching (陳).

The conversation was again in connection with the
1000 pieces of cargo.

Later Woo Tsung Ming took from under his sock
a silk cloth and showed same to Wong Tsang Yien saying
that it was the appointment he had given him sometime ago.
page_data.zh:
(2)

不久后，吴振明坚持要我们都去一家旅馆，说那里谈生意更方便。

起初我拒绝了，因为我不参与他们的商务谈判，但最终他们说服了我。

我们去了中和饭店213号房间，在那里，吴振明、钱鹏和王占一讨论了从苏州莫都（Moh Doh，音译）运输1000件货物到上海的问题。我没有听到任何提及游击活动的内容。关于这批货物，我听到吴振明请求钱鹏写一封信，收信人是谁我不知道，我也没看他写。

后来
从谈话中我得知钱鹏曾是一支游击队的队长。

离开酒店时，我被邀请第二天再来参加午宴。

1939年9月7日，我和王占一到达酒店，发现钱鹏和他的妻子已经在那里。吴振明稍后到达，紧随其后的是一名姓陈（Ching）的人。

谈话内容再次与那1000件货物有关。

后来，吴振明从袜子下面拿出一块丝绸布料，展示给王占一看，说这是他不久前发给王的委任状。

page_data.en:
(3)

Wong became angered, a quarrel ensued and I took
the cloth from Woo and placed same in my pocket, not knowing
the nature of it.
Food was then ordered and shortly afterwards Police
arrived and we were placed under arrest.
Previous to the meeting in the Tsung Hwa Hotel
I had no knowledge that Wong Tsang Yien had been connected
with guerrillas.
I have never taken any part in any guerrille or
anti-Japanese activities and the only reason I took possession
of the cloth badge of appointment was to prevent a quarrell
and out of curiosity.
This is my ture statement.

Signed:- Lieu Kyi Yong.

刘建荣十
page_data.zh:
(3)

王变得愤怒起来，随之发生争吵，我从吴手中拿过布料放入口袋，并不知道其性质。
随后点了食物，不久后警察赶到，我们将被逮捕。
在中和饭店会面之前，我不知道王占一与游击队有任何关联。
我从未参与任何游击或反日活动，我占有那块丝绸委任状的唯一原因是为了阻止争吵以及出于好奇。
这是我的真实陈述。

签名:- 刘建荣

刘建荣十

D. C. (Special Branch).

Headquarters

10-11-39

10

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO THE JAPANESE GENDARMERIE

Translations of statements taken from the prison-
ers by the Japanese Gendarmerie are attached herewith,
together with a request for handing over.
The three prisoners have been further questioned
regarding these statements and they admit same are true
in most part.
Wong Tsang Yien(王占一) and Tsien Pang(錢朋)
it will be seen have in the past both taken an active
part in guerrilla activities.
Lieu Kyi Yoong(劉建榮) however appears to have
only been connected with the two former persons a few days
prior to their arrest than only overheard their conversa-
tions regarding guerrilla activities. He has not taken
part himself in their guerrilla activities.
Regarding the cloth badge he admits that he took
same from the Wong Tsang Yien out of curiosity.

（批：S.S. ... 10/11）

（签名）
D. S. 114.

D. C.（特科）。

1939年11月10日

Col.Misc.146/39

10

关于进一步协助日本宪兵队事宜

随函附上由日本宪兵队从囚犯处获取的供词译文，以及移交请求。
就这些供词对三名囚犯进行了进一步讯问，他们承认供词大部分属实。
可以看出，王占一（Wong Tsang Yien）和錢朋（Tsien Pang）过去都曾积极参与游击活动。
然而，劉建榮（Lieu Kyi Yoong）似乎仅在逮捕前几天与前两人有联系，且只是偶然听到了他们关于游击活动的谈话。他本人并未参与他们的游击活动。
关于布质徽章，他承认是出于好奇从王占一处拿走的。

（批注：S.S ____ 10/11）

（签名）
D. S. 114.
