page_data.en:
TRANSLATION

Ref. Shan-Ken-Ko No. 1112.
Shanghai Detachment,
Japanese Gendarmerie.
October 9, 1939.

Major E. M. Bourne,
Commissioner of Police,
S.M.P./I.M.C.

Sir,

With reference to Wong Tsang Yien (王占一)
and Tsien Pang (錢鵬), who were arrested with the
assistance of your Police Force at Room 213 of Tzeng Hwa
Hotel, Szechow Road, on October 7, 1939 and a request for
whose handing over was already filed by us, we have not
been given the custody of these two accused yet.

I, therefore, take the pleasure to request
you that these two accused be handed over to us at your
earliest convenience on verification of the following
points :-

(1). That Wong Tsang Yien alias Wong Tsung Tien
(王震天) was the commander of the 11th Company, Eastern
Route Guerilla, Central Area (中央東路游擊隊十一隊長) in
November 1938, was evident from the silk cloth badge.
According to the statement of Wong Tsang Yien he was
employed by the Nakatsu Yoko, a Japanese concern, in
August 1938 and after resignation from this firm he obtained
a position of the manager of the Okada Yoko.

From enquiries made by our Police in connection
with Nakatsu Yoko and Okada Yoko, it was learnt that he
was in the employment of the Shing Kong (新港) Branch of
the Nakatsu Yoko in April or May 1939 for about one month
and from the middle part of June 1939 he became concerned
with the Okada Yoko and engaged in the interior trades with
office at Tsang Wang Kong (張黃港) for about one month,
page_data.zh:
译文

参考号：山检考第1112号。
日本宪兵队上海分队。
1939年10月9日。

E. M. Bourne 少校，
警务处处长，
上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 上海公共租界工部局。

先生：

关于王占一（Wong Tsang Yien）和錢鵬（Tsien Pang），二人于1939年10月7日在四川路振华饭店（Tzeng Hwa Hotel）213室由贵警队协助逮捕，我方此前已提出移交请求，但至今尚未接管这两名被告。

因此，谨请阁下在核实以下几点后，尽早将这两名被告移交我方：

(1). 从丝绸布质徽章可以明显看出，王占一，又名王震天（Wong Tsung Tien），曾在1938年11月担任中央东路游击队十一队长。根据王占一的供词，他于1938年8月受雇于日本商社中津洋行（Nakatsu Yoko），从该行辞职后，在冈田洋行（Okada Yoko）获得经理职位。

经我方警方就中津洋行和冈田洋行进行调查，获悉他于1939年4月或5月在中津洋行新港（Shing Kong）分行任职约一个月，并从1939年6月中旬开始与冈田洋行有关联，在张黄港（Tsang Wang Kong）设有办事处，从事内地贸易约一个月，

page_data.en:

but he has nothing to do with these two firms at present.
This indicates that he made a false statement
on the questioning of the S.M.P. and judging from this
point we can infer the rest of his statement made at the
S.M.P.
(2). It has been definitely ascertained that Telen
Pang was the Chief of Staff of Jung Fung Ying (鄧本殷),
Commander of a guerilla unit operating in Zangchow and
Soochow area.
The documents etc. seized at the time of his
arrest shows that he is still maintaining connection with
Jung Fung Ying.
In view of the above, I believe that statements
of persons concerned are sufficient to substantiate the
corpus delicti of the two accused being guerillas, although
they claim as if the allegation made against them was
concocted by the informers.
Statements taken from the managers of the
Nakatsu and Okada Companies are attached herewith.

I am, Sir,
Yours faithfully,

Shopped : Major-General S. Miura.
Officer-in-Command.

但他目前与这两家公司已无关系。
这表明他在接受上海公共租界工部局警务处讯问时作了虚假陈述，据此我们可以推断他在警务处所作其余供词的情况。
(2). 已确切查明，Telen Pang（译注：此处原文拼写可能有误，结合上下文应指錢鵬/Tsien Pang）是邓本殷（Jung Fung Ying）的参谋长，邓本殷是在常州和苏州地区活动的一支游击队的指挥官。
在他被捕时查获的文件等显示，他仍与邓本殷保持联系。
鉴于上述情况，我认为相关人员的供词足以证实两名被告作为游击队员的犯罪事实成立，尽管他们声称针对他们的指控是由线人捏造的。
随函附上从中津公司和冈田公司经理处获取的供词。

此致，

敬礼，

on the condition that "Hereafter trade with the interior be
engaged upon the amalgamation of myself, Lieu Tsong Liang
and Wong Tsang Yien, and the permission of business be
obtained by myself from the Authorities, and that fifteen

上述人员于1939年9月28日在日本宪兵队总部作出如下陈述。
我于去年1月16日从日本来到上海。自今年2月以来，我一直从事上海与高邮（Kompo）张黄港（Chang Wong Kong）之间的百货贸易。我想大约是今年4月，一名叫刘忠良（Lieu Tsong Liang）的中国男子，42岁，扬州人，是我雇佣的一名女佣的丈夫，向我建议说他认识一名叫王占一（Wong Tsang Yien）的中国男子，此人居住在法租界，精通贸易，在华人社群中是一位知名人物。因此，如果我能与他（王）合作，我在生意上就能获得更多利润。随后，通过刘的介绍，我在东方饭店（Grand Hotel）会见了王，此后我又见过他两三次。最后，我在法租界一处中国车库的三楼会见了王，王就住在那里。我与王达成协议，条件是“今后由我、刘忠良和王占三人联合开展内地贸易，由我负责从当局获得营业许可，并将收益的百分之十五

native of Japanese taken by me Second Sub-Lieutenant K. toda

at Jap. Gend. Hdqs. on the 2.10.39 and interpreted by ____________________

The abovementioned person made the following
statement at the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters on
2.10.39.

I came to Shanghai from Japan on the latter part
of December 1937. During April this year, my company newly
established a branch at Sing Kong, Kompo, when the branch
employed one male Chinese, named Wong Tsang Yien ( 王 藏 仁 ),
through introduction of Tsu ( 朱 ), interpreter of my shop,
but he was of bad disposition, being a loafer. Therefore,
I dismissed him after one month from his employment.
After this I heard he had been making malicious propaganda
in connection with my shop. I do not know as to wether or
not Wong had connection with guerrilla unit.
With regard to Fong Ching Sung ( 豐 金 松 ), I had
connection on business with him for a short period when
a branch was established at Shing Kong ( 新 江 ), Kompo, during
April this year, but I had no employment connection with
him. Fong has never frequented my shop since I dismissed
Wong.

I heard that Wong Tsang Yien had connection with
Okada Co. after the dismissal.
I do not know where or how he is at present.
I have nothing else to state
The above statement is true.

Tatsuo Matsumoto
(signed & chopped).

以下是松本达雄（T M tsumoto，译注：原文名字拼写不完整，根据签名应为Tatsuo Matsumoto）先生的陈述，36岁，中津公司（Nakatsu Co）业主，居住在北四川路139号。
籍贯日本，由日本宪兵队总部二等少尉 K. toda 于1939年10月2日在日本宪兵队总部进行讯问，并由___翻译。

上述人员于1939年10月2日在日本宪兵队总部作出如下陈述。

我于1937年12月下旬从日本来到上海。今年4月，我的公司在高邮新江（Sing Kong，译注：前文作Shing Kong，此处可能指同一地点或新江镇）新设了一家分行，当时分行通过本店翻译朱（Tsu）的介绍，雇佣了一名叫王藏仁（Wong Tsang Yien，译注：中文名与之前王占一不同，可能是别名或记录差异）的中国男子，但他品行不端，是个游手好闲之徒。因此，我在雇佣他一个月后将其解雇。
此后，我听说他一直在散布有关我店铺的恶意宣传。我不知道王是否与游击队有联系。
关于丰金松（Fong Ching Sung，译注：前文作Feng Ming Sung/豐金声，此处作豐金松，可能存在记录差异），今年4月在高邮新江（Shing Kong）设立分行期间，我曾与他有过短暂的商务往来，但我与他没有雇佣关系。自从我解雇王以来，丰从未光顾过我的店铺。

我听说王占一在被解雇后与冈田公司（Okada Co.）有联系。
我不知道他目前的下落或状况。
我别无其他陈述。
以上陈述属实。

松本达雄（Tatsuo Matsumoto）
（签名并盖章）。

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE
GENDARMERIE.

The three suspects in custody namely:-
1) WONG TSANG YIEN (王占一), alias
WONG TSUNG TIEN (王宏天);
2) TSIEN PANG (錢鵬), alias
TSIEN YUIN CHEU (錢瀛洲);

have been closely interrogated regarding their

4/1

关于进一步协助日本宪兵队事宜。

在押的三名嫌疑人，即：
1) 王占一（WONG TSANG YIEN），又名王宏天（WONG TSUNG TIEN，译注：前文作王震天）；
2) 錢鵬（TSIEN PANG），又名錢瀛洲（TSIEN YUIN CHEU）；
3) 刘建荣（LIEU KYI YONG）

就其涉嫌的游击活动及其与日本宪兵队线人的联系受到了严密讯问，结果显示，逮捕时在房间内发现的书面证据是由线人放置在那里的，以充实案件证据。

王占一，又名王震天（Wong Tsung Tien），受雇于冈田公司（Okada Co.），这是一家日资运输企业，办事处位于高邮（Kompe，译注：前文作Kompo/Kompe）张黄港（Chang Wong Kong）。

他否认曾与游击队有任何联系，并解释说，他是受日本线人吴阿东（Woo Auh Deong，音译）邀请前往振华饭店（Tsung Ho hotel）213室的，吴让他相信此次访问的目的是讨论业务。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特科）
（批注：Ruy）
（批注：28/9）

page_data.en:
4/2

He has known this informer for some time and also
knows Tsien Pang, and Lieu Kyl Yoong, the latter
person accompanied him to the hotel room at his
request.

He further added that this informer Woo
Au Doong (吴鹤東) is also known as Woo Tsung Ming
(吴振明) (Statement No.1 attached).

Tsien Pang, alias Tsien Yuin Cheu, admits
that he has been a member of a guerrilla unit, but
claims that he severed connections with them during
February, 1939 since which time he has not interested
himself in any such work.

He has been carefully interrogated and has
fully explained how the evidence in the form of two
letters which he wrote, were placed in the room
by the informers just prior to the police party
entering.

He stated that this informer who gave his
name to the Police as Woo Au Doong is known to him as
Woo Tsung Ming and that in October, 1938, they both
organized a guerrilla unit in the Soochow and Zangchow
area under the direction of one Toong Pung Ying(本殷).
Tsien Pang was appointed Chief of Staff and the informer
Woo was made Chief Secretary and Chief of the Military
Court.
page_data.zh:
4/2

他认识这名线人已有段时间，也认识钱邦（Tsien Pang）和刘桂荣（Lieu Kyl Yoong），后者是应他的要求陪同他前往酒店房间的。

他还补充说，这名线人吴鹤东（Woo Au Doong）又名吴振明（Woo Tsung Ming）（见附件陈述书第1号）。

钱邦，别名钱云洲（Tsien Yuin Cheu），承认他曾是游击队的一员，但声称他于1939年2月与他们断绝了联系，自那时起便不再参与任何此类活动。

经过仔细审讯，他充分解释了两封由他书写的信件作为证据，是如何在警方进入房间之前不久被线人放入房间内的。

他表示，这名向警方自称吴鹤东的线人，他所知为吴振明；1938年10月，他们两人在董本殷（Toong Pung Ying）的指挥下，在苏州和常州地区组织了一支游击队。钱邦被任命为参谋长，线人吴则被任命为秘书长兼军事法庭庭长。

page_data.en:
4/3

In February, 1939, Tsien Pang left the
unit and ceased to have any further connection with
guerrillas, later he came to Shanghai taking up his
residence with relatives at No.122 Rue Boissonet,
French Concession.

On September 5th. 1939, Woo Au Doong alias
Woo Tsung Ming met him and invited both him and his
wife to have tea at the Dah Tung (大東) tea room the
same afternoon.

The appointment was kept and during the
conversation which ensued Woo mentioned that he had
forsaken the guerrilla unit and was working for some
advertising business. He also suggested to Tsien Pang
that he join the Wang Ching Wei (汪精衛) group.

Later this informer concocted a story of
how he had a friend whose relative was desirous of
joining Toong Pung Ying's unit, and in this connection
suggested that Tsien Pang write a letter to a school
principle in Wusih who was in a position to arrange
a meeting between Toong Pung Ying and Koo Nan Dong
(顧乃同) the relative. Tsien Pang would not
write the letter he being suspicious of this informer
and intimated same to him, whereupon he gave him
photographs of himself and also his visiting card as
proof his sincerity.
page_data.zh:
4/3

1939年2月，钱邦离开该部队，不再与游击队有任何联系，随后他来到上海，居住在法租界布西尼路（Rue Boissonet）122号的亲戚家中。

1939年9月5日，吴鹤东（又名吴振明）与他见面，并邀请他和他的妻子于当天下午去大东茶室喝茶。

双方如约赴会，在随后的谈话中，吴提到他已脱离游击队，正从事某种广告业务。他还建议钱邦加入汪精卫集团。

后来，这名线人编造了一个故事，称他有一位朋友，其亲属希望加入董本殷的部队，并借此建议钱邦给无锡的一位校长写一封信，该校长的地位能够安排董本殷与该亲属顾乃同（Koo Nan Dong）会面。钱邦因怀疑这名线人而不愿写信，并向他暗示了这一点，于是线人将自己的照片和名片交给他，以证明自己的诚意。

page_data.en:
4/4

Before leaving the Dah Tung tea room it was
arranged that Woo should bring his friend Ching (陳)
along too.

On the afternoon of 6.9.39 Tsien Pang and
his wife kept the appointment at the tea room, Woo
was present, but Ching was absent, and Woo explained
that he would arrive later.

After further conversation Tsien Pang
agreed to write the letter, and they arranged that they
go to a room in a lodging house to do so.

Note paper was purchased on the way by
the informer and they proceeded to room No.213 Tsung
Ho Hotel, Foochow Road, where he (informer) explained
what he wished Tsien Pang to write (Letter No.1).

A second letter written by Tsien Pang was
also done at the request of Woo and the contents are
as directed by him (Letter No.2).

A third letter deals with family affairs
only (Letter No.3).

Continuing Tsien Pang added that before
writing the letters he and the informer Woo had agreed
that both should sign their names to same and later
when he reminded Woo of his promise he explained that
he would affix his chop to them later.
page_data.zh:
4/4

在离开大东茶室之前，双方约定吴也应将他的朋友陈（Ching）带来。

1939年9月6日下午，钱邦及其妻子如约前往茶室，吴在场，但陈缺席，吴解释说他会稍后到达。

经过进一步交谈，钱邦同意写信，他们商定去一家旅馆的房间进行书写。

信纸由线人在途中购买，他们随前往福州路振华旅社（Tsung Ho Hotel）213号房间，在那里他（线人）说明了希望钱邦书写的内容（信件第1号）。

钱邦书写的第二封信也是应吴的要求所作，内容均按吴的指示撰写（信件第2号）。

第三封信仅涉及家庭事务（信件第3号）。

钱邦接着补充说，在写信之前，他和线人吴曾约定两人都在信上签名，后来当他提醒吴履行承诺时，吴解释说他会稍后在信上盖章。

page_data.en:
4/5

Shortly after having completed the letter
writing the person Ching arrived was shown the letters
and expressed satisfaction with them, then he left
the room stating that he would mail the letters at
once and took them away.

It was later agreed that Tsien Lung and
his wife spend the night in room 213, since Woo had
to go out for the night on business.

Tsien agreed and his wife was called from
the Dah Tung tea room after which Woo left explaining
that he would affix his chop to the letters written
by Tsien and taken away by Ching, and would return
the following morning.

The following morning 7.9.39, Woo and
Ching arrived and soon after Wong Tsang Yien, and
Lieu Kyi Yoong and others came to the room all of
whom were arrested at 11.45 a.m.

The letters written the previous night
by Tsien Pang and which were taken away by Ching to
mail, were found in a drawer of a dressing table.
None bore the chop of Woo, the informer.

Here it should be mentioned that the
person Ching who assisted Woo to prepare the case
for the Japanese, is named Lieu Tuk Ming (刘德明),
alias Lieu Ching San (刘景山), who is also a
page_data.zh:
4/5

写完信后不久，陈到达，查看了信件并表示满意，随后他离开房间，声称将立即寄出信件并将信带走。

事后商定，由于吴当晚需外出办事，钱邦及其妻子将在213房间过夜。

钱邦表示同意，并从大东茶室叫来了他的妻子，随后吴离开，解释说他将把章盖在钱邦书写并由陈带走的信件上，并于次日早晨返回。

次日早晨，即1939年9月7日，吴和陈到达，不久后黄藏炎（Wong Tsang Yien）、刘桂荣（Lieu Kyi Yoong）等人也来到房间，所有人于上午11点45分被捕。

钱邦前夜书写并由陈带走准备邮寄的信件，在梳妆台的抽屉里被发现。这些信件上均未盖有线人吴的印章。

此处应提及，协助吴为日本人构陷此案的名叫陈的人，实名为刘德明（Lieu Tuk Ming），别名刘景山（Lieu Ching San），他也是一名

page_data.en:
4/8

Japanese informer, and it was upon the information
evidence produced by these two men that the arrests
were made.

Lieu Kyl Yoong, ex C.P.C. No.954, dismissed
from the French Police about the middle of July 1939,
denies being concerned in guerrilla activities. He
explains that it was Wong Tsang Yien, who invited
him to the room wherein he was arrested. Regarding
the cloth badge pertaining to the appointment of one
to a position of guerrilla officer, Lieu admits that
he did have same, but obtained possession of it in
the following manner.

At 11.45 a.m. 7.9.39, when the Police party
entered the room wherein the arrests were made , the
informer Woo Au Doong, alias Woo Tsung Ming placed
the cloth into the pocket of Lieu Kyl Yoong, and
since he did not realize the significance of same,
he did not pay any more attention to it until on the
way to the Police Station when he realized that it
may be incriminating evidence, consequently he attempted
to dispose of it.

Tsau Kwang Tsai (趙廣才), since
released, and Wong Tsang Yien both claim that they
saw the cloth badge handed to Lieu Kyl Yoong.
page_data.zh:
4/8

日本线人，逮捕行动正是基于这两人提供的情报证据进行的。

刘桂荣（Lieu Kyl Yoong），前法租界巡捕房编号954号巡捕，于1939年7月中旬被法国警察开除，他否认参与游击活动。他解释说，是黄藏炎邀请他进入那个他被捕的房间的。关于那块委任某人为游击队军官的布质徽章，刘承认他确实持有过，但是通过以下方式获得的。

1939年9月7日上午11点45分，当警方进入实施逮捕的房间时，线人吴鹤东（又名吴振明）将这块布放进了刘桂荣的口袋里，由于他当时未意识到其重要性，因此未加注意，直到在前往警察局的路上，他才意识到这可能是定罪证据，因而试图将其丢弃。

赵广才（Tsau Kwang Tsai，目前已获释）和黄藏炎均声称，他们看到这块布质徽章被递给刘桂荣。

page_data.en:
4/7

The only persons who saw him discard same
whilst in the Police van were the Japanese informers
dispite the fact that both Japanese and Chinese
detectives were present, no mention was made of
this exhibit until the informers were interrogated.
Further it should be noted that this cloth
badge bears the name of Woo Tsung Ming, the informer,
and refers to his appointment as Chief of the Military
Court, 11th. Detachment of the Central East Route
Guerrilla Unit.
This confirms the statement made by Tsien
Peng that Woo Tsung Ming did perform this duty.
Enquiries have been made at the Tsung Ho
Hotel and it has been ascertained that room No. 213
was engaged by this informer Woo on 6.9.39 at 10.30 a.m.
and he signed his name in the book as Chien Chuin
(錢均).
Room boy Dee Tsu Hai (杜九海) identified
Woo at the time of arrest as the person who engaged
the room.
Tsien Tsoo Sz (錢周氏) has brought to
this office one photograph of the informer, Woo, which
she claims is one he gave to her husband at their
first meeting in the Dah Tung tea room on 5.9.39.
page_data.zh:
4/7

尽管当时既有日本侦探也有中国侦探在场，但在警车上目睹他丢弃该物品的只有日本线人，直到审讯线人时，才提及这一物证。此外，值得注意的是，这块布质徽章上印有线人吴振明的名字，并注明他被任命为华中东路游击队第11支队军事法庭庭长。这证实了钱鹏所述吴振明确实履行此职的说法。经向振华旅社查询，查明该线人吴于1939年9月6日上午10点30分预订了213号房间，并在登记簿上签名为钱均（Chien Chuin）。侍应生杜九海（Dee Tsu Hai）在逮捕时指认吴即为预订房间之人。钱周氏（Tsien Tsoo Sz）向本局提交了一张线人吴的照片，她称这是1939年9月5日他们在大东茶室初次见面时吴给她丈夫的。

page_data.en:
4/8

Lieu Tuh Ming (刘德明), and Woo Au Boong (吴雅東),
Li a Foo Tsung Ming (吴振明), Japanese informers,
both deny the statements made by the three suspects.
No evidence has been found to show that
either Wong Tsang Yion or Lieu Kyi Young are members
of any guerrilla unit, the cloth badge allegedly
discarded by the latter is extremely doubtful and
under the circumstances cannot be accepted as
evidence against Lieu.
Tsien Peng has freely admitted having had
connections with guerrillas, but the two letters
seized are very doubtful evidence.
From the foregoing enquiries it shows that
this is an unsatisfactory case and points to the fact
that the two agents employed by the Japanese acted
as agents provocateurs and planted the evidence to
prove their case either to secure a reward or curry
favour with their employers.
Statements attached.

13/9
C. Ruard
D.S. 114.
page_data.zh:
4/8

刘德明（Lieu Tuh Ming）和吴雅东（Woo Au Boong，即吴振明 Li a Foo Tsung Ming），均为日本线人，两人都否认三名嫌疑人的陈述。未发现任何证据表明黄藏炎或刘桂荣是任何游击队的成员，后者据称丢弃的布质徽章极具疑点，在此情况下不能作为指控刘的证据。钱鹏 freely admitted（自由承认）曾与游击队有联系，但查获的两封信作为证据非常可疑。从上述调查来看，这是一起证据不足的案件，且表明这两名受雇于日本的代理人充当了挑衅者（agents provocateurs），为了获取报酬或讨好雇主而栽赃证据以坐实其罪名。附陈述书。

9月13日
C. Ruard
D.S. 114.

page_data.en:
Hsuchow
C.J.H. . .
1.9.39
(王占一)
S.I. Lieu Kying Ching
translated
Hsu S. P.

My name is Wong Tsang Yie, aged 37 years,
native of Hsuchow, Manager of the Okada & Co., a
Japanese Concern, and residing at No. 1 An Ling Li,
near Jeu Rosi near Rue de Marche, F.C.

I came to Shanghai at the age 22 years,

In August of last year I was employed as a
transport escort of the Nakai & Co., the owner being
a Japanese named Matsumoto. Whilst being engaged
in the above coy. I used to travell between Shanghai
and Nanziang.

In March of this year the Nakai & Co. was removed
to Sing Kong, Kompo and I was assigned to act as a canvasser
for business of the coy.

Some time during April or May 1939, I resigned
this position the successor of which is my teacher named
Foong Kying Sung (丰金声)

After my resignation from the above coy. I
procured another employment as manager of the Okada & Co.
The proprietor of the Okada & Co. is a Japanese named
Mr. Tsunee Okada with whom I have signed a contract.
This coy. has its office at Chang Wong Kong (張黃港),
Kompo, and deals in transportation of cotton, leather,
pigs and other sundry goods between Kompo and Shanghai.

I came to Shanghai together with Mr. Tsunee Okada
in Aug. of this year.

In the evening of Aug. 20th. I, in company with
Messrs. Tsunee Okada, and Yoshimura and two others
page_data.zh:
徐州
C.J.H. . .
1939年9月1日
(王占一)
特别调查员 刘景清（Lieu Kying Ching）
翻译
徐 S. P.

我叫黄藏炎（Wong Tsang Yie），37岁，徐州人，冈田商会（Okada & Co.，一家日本公司）经理，居住于法租界马浪路（Rue de Marche）附近巨籁达路（Jeu Rosi）安岭里1号。

我22岁时来到上海，

去年八月，我被中井商会（Nakai & Co.）雇佣为运输押运员，老板是一位名叫松本（Matsumoto）的日本人。在该公司任职期间，我经常往返于上海和南翔之间。

今年三月，中井商会迁至公兴（Sing Kong, Kompo），我被指派担任该公司的业务推销员。

1939年4月或5月间，我辞去了该职位，继任者是我的老师丰金声（Foong Kying Sung）。

从上述公司辞职后，我另谋得一份工作，担任冈田商会经理。冈田商会的业主是一位名叫冈田常吉（Tsunee Okada）的日本人，我已与他签订合同。该公司办公室位于公兴张黄港（Chang Wong Kong, Kompo），经营公兴与上海之间的棉花、皮革、生猪及其他杂货运送业务。

今年八月，我与冈田常吉先生一同来到上海。

8月20日晚，我与冈田常吉先生、吉村（Yoshimura）先生及另外两名

page_data.en:
names unknown (also Japanese), had supper in "Is Mei Lou"
(致真樓) Restaurant, Foochow Road. After supper I
went to "Tsung Ho" (振華) Lodging House, and engaged
a room, number unknown, for the purpose of discussing
business.

Unless being called out on business I always
stayed at home.

At 10.30 a.m. 7.9.38 while walking along Foochow
Road together with Tsau Kwang Tsai (趙廣才), one of
my co-workers, I encountered Woo Tsung Ming (吳振明)
and Tsien Pang (錢) outside the Tsung Ho lodging
house. At the request of Woo Tsung Ming we went to Room
15 of the above said lodging house where Woo Tsung Ming
told me that he had 1000 bundles of cotton which he intended
to be transported to Kompo. Shortly afterwards the room
wherein we stayed was suddenly raided by a Police party
and I was consequently arrested.

The above is my true statement.
page_data.zh:
姓名不详的日本人（亦为日本人），在福州路“致真楼”餐厅共进晚餐。晚餐后，我前往“振华”旅社（Tsung Ho Lodging House），预订了一个房间（号码不详），以便商讨业务。

除非因公务被叫出，否则我总是待在家里。

1938年9月7日上午10点30分，我与同事之一赵广才（Tsau Kwang Tsai）沿福州路行走时，在振华旅社外遇到了吴振明（Woo Tsung Ming）和钱邦（Tsien Pang）。应吴振明的要求，我们前往上述旅社的15号房间，吴振明告诉我他有1000包棉花打算运往公兴。不久之后，我们所在的房间突然遭到警方突袭，我因此被捕。

以上是我的真实陈述。

page_data.en:
TSIEN PENG (錢鵬)
Taichow, Kampo                                D.S. Rhodes
C.B.H. . Col        12/9/39                    Clerk No.10

My name is Tsien Peng (錢鵬), alias Tsien Yuin
Chou (錢雲洲); aged 44, native of Taichow, Kampo, married,
unemployed, residing at No.122 Rue Boissonet, French Con-
cession.

At the age of 11 years I studied at home under a
priv. te teacher and continued until I was sixteen years of
age. From then until eighteen I remained at home and
assisted my father who at that time owned an oil shop, then
I went to Nanking and enlisted in the 33rd. Regiment of the
Nationalist Army which was then commanded by Tse Shu Tsung
(徐紹曾).

I remained with the regiment in Nanking for two
years and was then transferred to the Military Academy in
Paoting (保定).

After about six months in Paoting I went to Canton
hoping to enter a military school there, but despite the
fact that I was in possession of a certificate from Paoting
certifying that I had graduated from that academy, I was
unable to enter the army in the position I was desirous of
obtaining, and since I did not intend to enter the Army as a
ranker, For a period of three years I, with the assistance
given by friends moved from place to place around South China
seeking employment, but without result.

At the end of that time I was successful in securing
a position as chief of the Taichow Cigarette and Wine Tax
Bureau, and remained thereat for about five years, at the
end of which time I came to Shanghai and obtained a job as
page_data.zh:
钱鹏（TSIEN PENG）
泰州，公兴                                D.S. Rhodes
C.B.H. . Col        1939年9月12日                    10号文员

我叫钱鹏（Tsien Peng），别名钱云洲（Tsien Yuin Chou）；44岁，泰州（公兴）人，已婚，无业，居住于法租界布西尼路122号。

11岁时，我在家中跟随私人教师学习，直至16岁。从那时起到18岁，我留在家中协助父亲，当时父亲拥有一家油店，随后我前往南京，加入了由徐绍曾（Tse Shu Tsung）指挥的国民革命军第33团。

我在南京的该团服役两年，随后被调往保定军校。

在保定大约六个月后，我前往广州，希望能进入那里的军事学校，但尽管我持有保定颁发的毕业证书，证明我从该军校毕业，我却无法以期望的职位入伍，由于我不打算以普通士兵身份入伍，在随后的三年里，我在朋友的帮助下，在中国南方各地辗转求职，但毫无结果。

在那段时间结束时，我成功谋得泰州烟酒税务局局长的职位，并在那里任职约五年，期满后我来到上海，获得了一份

page_data.en:
(2)

a w teleman with the King Shing Steamship Co.
After two years this steamship company ceased to
exist, consequently I became unemployed.
At the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in 1932, I met General Tsung Ying Dei (陳印潭), who was
then in Nantao in charge of the 3rd. Division of the 60th.
Army. I offered my services to the Army and since I had made
friends with him when I was in the military academy in Baoting,
he appointed me as his aide-de-camp.
I stayed with General Tsung Ying Dei and his army
in Nantao until the conclusion of hostilities when we moved
to Haimen, where the 60th. Army was disbanded. At this time
I was asked to go to Fukien to a branch of the army there, but
I refused and returned to Shanghai as a civilian.
The same year (1932) I with nine others rented a
plot of land and a house in Nantao and attempted to organize
a shipping company, but due to a very long delay in obtaining
the necessary permission from the Ministry of Communications
the venture was a failure.
In October, 1938, a friend of mine named Lieu Ching
Ling (刘金林) introduced me to one Woo Tsung Ming (吴振明),
alias Woo Auh Doong (吴鹤東) and from him I learned that
he was a friend of one Toong Fung Xing (鄧本殷), a well
known guerrilla unit commander around the Soochow area.
During the following two days we met frequently and
decided to interview Toong Fung Xing and offer our services as
guerrillas.
page_data.zh:
(2)

我是 King Shing 轮船公司的一名电报员。两年后，该轮船公司停业，因此我失业了。
1932年中日敌对行动爆发时，我遇到了陈印潭将军（General Tsung Ying Dei），他当时在南市负责第六十军第三师。我向该部队效力，由于我在保定军校时与他结为好友，他任命我为其副官。
我与陈印潭将军及其部队留在南市，直到敌对行动结束，随后我们移驻海门，第六十军在此解散。当时有人请我去福建加入那里的陆军分支，但我拒绝了，并以平民身份返回上海。
同年（1932年），我与另外九人在南市租了一块地皮和一栋房屋，试图组建一家航运公司，但由于从交通部获得必要许可的过程拖延太久，这项 venture 以失败告终。
1938年10月，我的一位名叫刘金林（Lieu Ching Ling）的朋友将我介绍给吴振明（Woo Tsung Ming），又名吴鹤東（Woo Auh Doong）。从他那里我得知，他是苏州地区一位著名的游击队指挥官鄧本殷（Toong Fung Xing）的朋友。在接下来的两天里，我们经常见面，并决定去拜访鄧本殷，主动提出作为游击队员为其效力。

page_data.en:
(3)

Toward the end of October, 1938, we three went
to Dong-keu (蕩口), Soochow, and there met Toong Lung
Ying, and after a lengthy conversation he suggested that
we go to Sing-an (新安) and Tsau Chi (焦溪) districts
Changchow area and there form a guerrilla unit, we all agreed.

About a month later, we had recruited about 300
men and all were sent to Wusih where Toong Lung Ying came
and addressed the men on their duties and rates of pay etc.

Lieu Ching Ling was made Commander of the unit, I
was made Chief of Staff, and Woo Tsung Ming, alias Woo Auh
Doong was appointed Chief Secretary and Chief of the Military
Court.

Toong Lung Ying ordered that we were to remain
in Sing-an and train the unit.

About February, 1939, Toong's unit was dispersed
by the Japanese Army and he (Toong) came to Sing-an and thence
a few days later he proceeded to Shanghai, address not known.

We remained inactive at Sing-an for about a month
and since we had not heard from Toong or received any money
from him to pay the members of the unit, we levied taxes on
the people in the surrounding areas to support the unit.

The people paid at first but later they became
angered at this continued taxing, and since I did not agree
with oppressing the people in this manner I resigned from
the unit about the middle of April, 1939, and went to Dong-
keu, Changchow, the home of my father-in-law where I stayed
for two months, then on 3.7.39, I and my wife came to
page_data.zh:
(3)

1938年10月底，我们三人前往苏州的蕩口（Dong-keu），在那里见到了 Toong Lung Ying。经过长时间的交谈，他建议我们去常州地区的新安（Sing-an）和焦溪（Tsau Chi）区组建一支游击队，我们都同意了。

大约一个月后，我们招募了约300人，并将所有人送往无锡。Toong Lung Ying 来到那里，向士兵们训话，讲解他们的职责和薪饷等事宜。

刘金林被任命为部队指挥官，我被任命为参谋长，吴振明（又名吴鹤東）被任命为主席秘书兼军事法庭庭长。

Toong Lung Ying 命令我们留在新安训练部队。

1939年2月左右，Toong 的部队被日军击溃，他（Toong）来到新安，几天后便前往上海，地址不详。

我们在新安无所事事地待了大约一个月，由于没有收到 Toong 的消息，也没有从他那里得到钱来支付部队成员的薪饷，我们便向周边地区的百姓征税以维持部队运作。

起初百姓们缴纳了税款，但后来他们对这种持续的征税感到愤怒。由于我不同意以这种方式压迫百姓，我于1939年4月中旬左右从部队辞职，前往常州蕩口，住在我岳父家，在那里待了两个月。然后，1939年7月3日，我和妻子来到

page_data.en:
(4)

Shanghai and after staying one night in a small lodging
house moved to No.122 Rue Boissonet, French Concession,
the home of relatives.
I was not successful in obtaining employment and
was forced to seek the aid of relatives and pawn various
articles of clothing etc. in order to live.
One evening about the beginning of September, 1939
whilst walking on the road in the French Concession, I met
Tong Tsang Tien (王占一), who I first became acquainted
with some years ago when he operated a food shop on Rue de
Consulate. We talked for some time and during the conversa-
tion Tong mentioned that he had learned from Woo Tsung Ming
that I was in Shanghai.
He also mentioned that he was working for a
Japanese owned transportation company, and that if I could
get any business for him I would receive a commission.
On 5.9.39 at 10 a.m. Woo Tsung Ming, who had
arrived in Shanghai some weeks earlier, came to my home and
invited me to have tea at the Dah Tung tea room at 3 p.m.
the same day.
My wife and I kept the appointment and upon arrival
found Woo waiting for us.
During the general conversation, which ensued Woo
Tsung Ming stated that he had left the guerrilla unit entirely
and was now doing some advertising business. He asked if I
intended to return to guerrilla work and when I replied that
I had definitely finished, he suggested that I join the Wang
page_data.zh:
(4)

上海，在一家小旅馆住了一晚后，搬到了法租界白赛蒙路（Rue Boissonet）122号亲戚家中。
我未能找到工作，被迫寻求亲戚的帮助，并典当各种衣物等物品以维持生计。
1939年9月初的一个晚上，我在法租界的路上行走时，遇到了王占一（Tong Tsang Tien）。几年前他在领事馆路（Rue de Consulate）经营一家食品店时，我就认识了他。我们交谈了一会儿，谈话中王提到他从吴振明那里得知我在上海。
他还提到他在一家日资运输公司工作，如果我能帮他拉到生意，我会收到佣金。
1939年9月5日上午10点，几周前已抵达上海的吴振明来到我家，邀请我当天下午3点在“大同”茶室喝茶。
我和妻子如约前往，到达时发现吴正在等我们。
在随后的泛泛交谈中，吴振明表示他已完全离开游击队，现在从事一些广告业务。他问我是否打算重返游击工作，当我回答说我已彻底结束时，他建议我加入汪

page_data.en:
(5)

Ching Wei (汪精衛) clique, this I told him I would never
do.

Woo Tsung Ming further told me that he had a friend
named Ching (陳 ) who was related to one named Koo Nan
Dong (顧乃同 ); a commander of guerrilla unit in Moh-
Doh (木), Soochow, and who was desirous of joining Toong
Pung Ying's unit, in this respect he asked me to write a
letter to a school principle in Sush, who is a friend of
mine requesting him to write to Toong Pung Ying and by this
means arrange for Koo Nan Dong to meet Toong Pung Ying.

The school teacher is known to Toong Pung Ying
and was in a position to arrange a meeting between the two unit
commanders.

Woo Tsung Ming added that if I would agree he would
arrange for the letter to be sent to Sush.

At the time I would not agree to write the letter
since I had no further interest in guerrilla activities,
therefore Woo suggested that we meet again the next day when
Ching, the relative of Koo Nan Dong would also be present.

At about 4.30 p.m. on 6.9.39 I again went to the
Dah Tung tea room and met Woo, when I asked why the person
Ching was not present, he replied that Ching was busy and
would come later.

He then suggested that we go to a hotel and write
the letter. This time I agreed to write the letter and
forthwith we proceeded to room No.213 Tsung Ho (振華) hotel,
Foochow Road.
page_data.zh:
(5)

精衛（Wang Ching Wei）派系，我告诉他我绝不会这样做。

吴振明还告诉我，他有一位姓陈（Ching）的朋友，与顾乃同（Koo Nan Dong）有亲属关系；顾乃同是苏州木渎（Moh-Doh）地区的一支游击队指挥官，希望加入 Toong Pung Ying 的部队。在这方面，他请求我写一封信给我在苏州的一位朋友——一位校长，请他写信给 Toong Pung Ying，以此安排顾乃同与 Toong Pung Ying 会面。

这位学校老师认识 Toong Pung Ying，并有能力安排两位指挥官会面。

吴振明补充说，如果我同意，他会安排将信寄往苏州。

当时我不愿意写这封信，因为我对游击活动已不再感兴趣，因此吴建议我们第二天再见面，届时顾乃同的亲属陈某也会在场。

1939年9月6日下午4点30分左右，我再次来到“大同”茶室见到吴，当我问为什么陈某不在场时，他回答说陈某很忙，稍后会来。

随后他建议我们去一家旅馆写信。这次我同意写信，于是我们立即前往福州路的振华（Tsung Ho）旅馆213房间。

page_data.en:
(6)

Woo, who purchased note paper whilst enroute to the
hotel, obtained a pen from the room boy and I wrote to my
friend Cheng (陳), as directed by Woo.

A second letter I wrote to Tsong Ping Ying and
in explanation of this I wish to state that this is as
dictated by Woo Tsang ing. That part of the letter referring
to 1000 articles, means that 1000 guerrillas are at Hoh -doh,
Soochow.

Woo further offered me $50.00 if, when a reply was
received, I would go to Tsong Ping Ying to arrange for Soo
Min Dong to join his unit. This I refused to do. Although
I signed my name to the letters, it had previously been
agreed between us that we both would sign, but Woo at the
time refused stating that he would affix his chop thereto
later.

A third letter I wrote to my father-in-law and
deals only with family affairs.

At about 6 p.m. Cheng arrived and Woo handed the
three letters to him and he, after reading same replied that
he would have to leave at once to mail them, and he left the
room. At the same time Woo explained that since it was
rather late I should stay and have dinner with him in the
room and he suggested that he call my wife who was waiting
in the Dah Tung tea room, to join us.

However, at this juncture I reminded Woo of his
promise to affix his chop to the letters I had written and
he said that first he would call my wife and then would meet
page_data.zh:
(6)

吴在去旅馆的路上买了信纸，从侍者那里拿来一支钢笔，我按照吴的指示给我的朋友陈（Cheng）写了信。

我写的第二封信是给 Tsong Ping Ying 的，对此我需要说明，这是由 Woo Tsang ing 口授的。信中提到的“1000件物品”，是指苏州木渎（Hoh-doh）有1000名游击队员。

吴还提出，如果收到回信后我去见 Tsong Ping Ying 并安排 Soo Min Dong 加入他的部队，他将给我50美元。我拒绝这样做。虽然我在信上签了名，但我们之前曾约定两人共同签名，但吴当时拒绝了，声称他稍后会盖上他的印章。

我写的第三封信是给我岳父的，只涉及家庭事务。

下午6点左右，陈（Cheng）到达，吴将三封信交给他。他读完后回答说必须立刻离开去寄信，随即离开了房间。同时吴解释说，因为时间较晚，我应该留下来和他一起在房间里吃晚饭，并建议他把在“大同”茶室等候的妻子叫来加入我们。

然而，在此刻我提醒吴他曾承诺在我写的信上盖章，他说他会先叫我妻子，然后在信件离开上海之前与

page_data.en:
(7)

Ching before the letters left Shanghai. About half an hour
later Woo returned with my wife and after having partaken
of a meal Woo stated that he would go out and drop the
letters and invited my wife and myself to stay the night
in the room, because Ching had arranged a dinner party for
us the next day.

Next morning, 7.9.59, Woo Tsung Ming and Ching
arrived and soon after Wong Tsang Yien and Lieu Kyi Yoong
(刘建荣) also came to the room. At this time I had
never met Lieu Ching Yoong before and Wong introduced him to
me as his friend.

Wong explained that Woo had invited him to come
to the room to discuss some business affairs.

After a short time Wong and Lieu prepared to leave,
but Woo told them to wait a little longer since he had
ordered a table of food.

At 11.15 a.m. before the food had arrived Police
entered the room and as they did so I saw Woo place a rolled
piece of cloth into Lieu Ching Yoong's pocket.

I omitted to mention that on the afternoon of the
5.9.59 whilst in the Dah Tung tea room Woo Tsung Ming gave
me three photographs of himself and two visiting cards.

This is my true statement.

Signed: Tsien Pang
page_data.zh:
(7)

陈（Ching）见面。大约半小时后，吴带着我的妻子回来。用餐完毕后，吴表示他要出去寄信，并邀请我和妻子在房间里过夜，因为陈已为我们安排了第二天的晚宴。

第二天早上，1939年9月7日，吴振明和陈到达。不久后，王占一（Wong Tsang Yien）和刘建荣（Lieu Kyi Yoong）也来到房间。当时我以前从未见过刘建荣，王将他作为朋友介绍给我。

王解释说，吴邀请他来房间讨论一些商业事务。

过了一会儿，王和刘准备离开，但吴让他们再等一会儿，因为他已经点了一桌饭菜。

上午11点15分，饭菜尚未送到，警察进入房间。就在他们进入时，我看到吴将一卷布塞进刘建荣的口袋里。

我漏提了一点，1939年9月5日下午，在“大同”茶室时，吴振明给了我三张他自己的照片和两张名片。

这是我的真实陈述。

签名：钱邦（Tsien Pang）

page_data.en:
Lieu Kyi Yoong (劉建榮)
Shantung                                      C.D.C. 184
                                               translated
Col, C.B.H.Q.          7.9.39                  xxxxxx      Clerk Hsia

My name is Lieu Kyi Yoong, age 29, native of Shantung,
married, residing at No.323 Sing Sing Lee, Point Pere Robert,
French Concession. I am an inspector of the Duck & Chicken
Dealers' Federation, Nantao, Shanghai.

During May, 1935 (24th. year of the Republic of China)
I came to Shanghai and obtained a job as coolie in the Wu
Kung Shing (吳順興) Iron Works, Point Road, Hongkew, through
the recommendation of my brother. About 5 months later, I was
working in a Cotton Weaving Factory in Yangtsepoo district,
and then lost my employment.

At the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities, the
French Police enrolled men for police service, so I went
there and passed the examination. During November, 1937
(26th. year of the Republic of China), I was appointed as a
Chinese policeman No.964 at Lokawei Police Station.

On 17th. July, 1939 (28th. year of the Republic
of China), I was dismissed by the French Police because of
sickness and absence from duty. I then remained at home.
I became acquainted with one named Wong Tsang Yien (王占一),
a friend of my chief tenant Mah Teh Hyi (馬德義), because
he always came to my house for amusement. Later, I secured
a position as inspector of the Duck & Chicken Dealers'
Federation, Nantao, Shanghai (上海南市鸡鸭联合会).

On the morning of 7th. September, 1939, I started
out to visit some friends at the Carlton Theatre, Park Road,
but on arriving on Fooshow Road, met Wong Tsang Yien, who
requested me to go with him to see a friend at room 213 of the
page_data.zh:
刘建荣（Lieu Kyi Yoong）
山东                                      C.D.C. 184
                                               已翻译
上校，中央局总部          1939年9月7日                  xxxxxx      夏书记员

我叫刘建荣，29岁，山东人，已婚，居住在法租界贝当路（Point Pere Robert）新新里323号。我是上海南市鸡鸭联合会的稽查员。

1935年5月（民国二十四年），我来到上海，通过哥哥的介绍，在虹口百老汇路（Point Road）的吴顺兴（Wu Kung Shing）铁工厂找到了一份苦力的工作。大约5个月后，我在杨树浦区的一家棉织厂工作，随后失业。

中日敌对行动爆发时，法国警察招募警员，我便前去报考并通过考试。1937年11月（民国二十六年），我被任命为卢家湾警察署的第964号华捕。

1939年7月17日（民国二十八年），我因病缺勤被法国警察开除。此后我一直待在家里。我认识了王占一（Wong Tsang Yien），他是我的二房东马德义（Mah Teh Hyi）的朋友，因为他常来我家消遣。后来，我获得了上海南市鸡鸭联合会稽查员的职位。

1939年9月7日上午，我出发去派克路卡尔登大戏院拜访几位朋友，但在到达福州路时，遇到了王占一，他请求我跟他一起去见一位朋友，地点在

page_data.en:
2
...ng to lodging house. e went there and noticed Tsien
Yuin Cheu and his wife in room 213 of the above mentioned
lodging house. A few minutes later one named ... 漢
came in, I was introduced to him by Tsien Yuin Cheu.
e then had a conversation, and two hours later a party
of ... Police and Japanese entered to search the room.
the Police entered the room too suddenly handed to
me a piece of silk cloth which was rolled into ball,
and which I put into my pocket. At that time I asked
him what was it, I was told by him not to mind, or be
afraid. In the police van, I threw the white cloth
away (inside the van), but I did not know the contents
of the same. I also do not know why I should have been
arrested.
This is a true statement.
page_data.zh:
2
……某旅馆。我们去了那里，发现钱云周（Tsien Yuin Cheu）和他的妻子在上述旅馆的213房间。几分钟后，一个名叫……漢的人进来，钱云周将我介绍给他。
随后我们进行了交谈，两小时后，一群……警察和日本人进入房间进行搜查。
警察进入房间时太突然，[某人]递给我一块卷成球的丝绸布料，我把它放进了口袋。当时我问他这是什么，他告诉我别在意，也别害怕。在警车里，我把那块白布扔掉了（在车内），但我不知道里面的内容。我也不知道自己为何被捕。
这是一份真实的陈述。

page_data.en:
Tseu Kweng Tsai 赵廣才
Tungchow
C.I.M.O.(C.1)    7.9.39    C.J.S. 2.
translated
Hsu S. F.

My name is Tseu Kweng Tsai, age 25, native of
Tungchow, E/employee of the Okada & Co.(a Japanese concern),
and residing at 1 A: Ling Li, Route de Zikawei, French
Concession.

I came to Shanghai at the age of 15 and had since
been employed at the Tai Kong (泰康) Canned Goods Factory,
where I left owing to lower pay after a long service of
10 years. After my resignation from the above factory
some-time in April of this year I was introduced by Wong
Tsang Yien (王占一), a friend of mine, to the Okada & Co.
in Chang Wong Kong, Kempo, where I later procured a position
as transport escort, travelling between Chang Wong Kong and
Shing Kong (新港).

A week ago Wong Tsang Yien and I came to Shanghai
consignment of
with/cotton on board S.S. "Kaston" (?) (a German ship),
and arrived at Shanghai at about 3 p.m. 25.8.39. We
landed at No. 13 Pontoon, The Bund. On reaching shore,
I went home in French Town.

At approximately 10 a.m. on 7.9.39 Wong Tsang
Yien called at my home and informed me that he was going
to meet some friends at the Tsung Ho (振華) Lodging House,
Foochow Road, with the object of discussing transportation
of cotton. I went with Wong to Tsung Ho lodging house by
a tram car and on arrival we went to Room 213.

About 10 minutes after our arrival at the room,
a party of Police raided the room and brought me to
Station. The reason for my arrest is entirely unknown to me.

The above is my true statement.
Signed:
page_data.zh:
赵廣才 (Tseu Kweng Tsai)
通州
C.I.M.O.(C.1)    1939年9月7日    C.J.S. 2.
已译
徐 S. F.

本人名为赵廣才，现年25岁，籍贯通州，系冈田商会（一家日本商号）雇员，居住于法租界徐家汇路安邻里1号。

本人15岁时来到上海，此后受雇于泰康罐头食品厂，因服务十年后薪资降低而离职。今年四月某时从上述工厂辞职后，经友人王占一介绍，进入位于虹口张华浜的冈田商会工作，随后谋得运输押运员一职，往返于张华浜与新港之间。

一周前，本人与王占一同乘德国轮船“Kaston”号（音译）运载棉花抵沪，于1939年8月25日下午3时许抵达上海。我们在外滩第13号浮码头登岸。上岸后，本人返回法租界家中。

1939年9月7日上午10时许，王占一到访本人住所，告知他要去福州路振华旅馆会见几位朋友，商讨棉花运输事宜。本人随王乘电车前往振华旅馆，到达后进入213房间。

我们进入房间约十分钟后，一批警察突袭该房间并将本人带至警局。本人对被捕原因完全不知情。

以上陈述属实。
签名：

page_data.en:
Tsien Tsoo Sz (錢周氏)
Taichow                                      C.J.C. 184
                                             translated
C.l, C.B.H.Q.        7.9.39                  xxxxxx      Clerk Hsia

My name is Tsien Tsoo Sz, age 32, native of
Taichow, married, residing at No.122 Rue Boissonet,
French Concession.
             On the 17th. August, 1939, my husband and I came
to Shanghai and stayed with my sister-in-law for 21 days,
because my husband could not obtain any employment whilst
in the country (Taichow). Later, my husband secured a job
as waiter in the Slaughter House in Hongkew through the
introduction of one named Tsu (朱), son-in-law of my
husband's nephew. He returned home daily. It was not
convenient for us to stay with my relatives, so my husband
took me out for amusement and opened a room in the Tsung
Ho (振華) Lodging House, Foochow Road on 6th. September, 193
On the morning of 7th. September, 1939, a party
of 5 or 6 persons visited my husband in the room, but I
could not understand what they were talking about. At about
12 noon, I was arrested by S.M.Police, and I have no idea
why should I have been arrested.
             This is a true statement.

                                     Signed: Tsien Tsoo Sz.
page_data.zh:
錢周氏 (Tsien Tsoo Sz)
泰州                                      C.J.C. 184
                                             已译
C.l, C.B.H.Q.        1939年9月7日                  xxxxxx      书记员 Hsia

本人名为錢周氏，现年32岁，籍贯泰州，已婚，居住于法租界蒲石路122号。
             1939年8月17日，本人与丈夫来到上海，在嫂嫂家借住21天，因为丈夫在乡下（泰州）未能找到工作。后来，丈夫通过其侄女婿一位姓朱的人介绍，在虹口屠宰场谋得侍者一职。他每日回家。由于借住亲戚家不便，丈夫带我外出娱乐，并于1939年9月6日在福州路振华旅馆开房住宿。
             1939年9月7日上午，有五、六人进入房间看望我丈夫，但我听不懂他们在谈论什么。中午12时许，我被公共租界工部局警务处逮捕，我不明白为何会被捕。
             此陈述属实。

                                     签名：錢周氏

page_data.en:
Wong Tai Sz (王戴氏)
Zengchow                                C.J.C. 184
C.l, C.B.H.Q.        7.9.39             translated   Clerk Hsia
                                          xxxxxx

My name is Wong Tai Sz, age 34, native of Zengchow,
married, residing at No.1 Er Ling Lee (安鄰里) off Rue
du Marche, French Concession.
      During November, 1937 (26th. year of the Republic
of China), I lived together with one named Wong Tsang Yien(王
占一). At the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities,
my husband lost his employment, therefore he returned to
Zengchow with me. We stayed in country about four months.
      During January, 1939 (28th. year of the Republic
of China), my husband came to Shanghai and visited his
"Shi Sang" (先生) named Voong Ching Zung (馮景順) and
asked for a job. Later, he obtained a position in the
Nakai Transportation Co. (中井洋行) in Sing Kong (新港)
through the introduction of Voong. Two or three months
later, he secured a situation as sub-manager of the Okada
& Co., a transportation company, which co-operated by Voong
Ching Zung and Japanese.
      During June, 1939, I received a letter from my
husband requesting me to come to Shanghai. On 6th. June,
1939, I came to Shanghai and stayed with my relatives for
two months, and later I removed to No.1 Er Ling Lee, Rue
du Marche, French Concession.
      On the morning of 7th. September, 1939, my husband
and I visited a friend in Tsung Ho (振華) Lodging House
regarding transportation of cotton. At about 12 noon, I
was arrested by S.M.Police and I have no knowledge why should
I have been arrested.
      This is a true statement.
                        Signed: Wong Tai Sz
page_data.zh:
王戴氏 (Wong Tai Sz)
常州                                C.J.C. 184
C.l, C.B.H.Q.        1939年9月7日             已译   书记员 Hsia
                                          xxxxxx

本人名为王戴氏，现年34岁，籍贯常州，已婚，居住于法租界麦赛尔蒂罗路安邻里1号。
      1937年11月（中华民国二十六年），我与一名叫王占一的人共同生活。中日战事爆发后，丈夫失业，因此他带我返回常州。我们在乡下停留了约四个月。
      1939年1月（中华民国二十八年），丈夫来到上海，拜访他的“先生”馮景順并求职。后来，通过馮的介绍，他在新港的中井洋行获得职位。两三个月后，他在冈田商会谋得副经理一职，这是一家由馮景順与日本人合作经营的运输公司。
      1939年6月，我收到丈夫来信，要求我来上海。1939年6月6日，我来到上海，在亲戚家住了两个月，随后搬至法租界麦赛尔蒂罗路安邻里1号。
      1939年9月7日上午，我与丈夫前往振华旅馆拜访一位朋友，商讨棉花运输事宜。中午12时许，我被公共租界工部局警务处逮捕，我不明白为何会被捕。
      此陈述属实。
                        签名：王戴氏

Joo Tsu Hai (朱祖海) 9
sushing C.D.C. 184
C.B.H.Q.(C.1) 12.9.39 translated Hsu S. P.

My name is Joo Tsu Hai, age 56, native of Sushing,
employed at the Tsung Ho (宗和) Lodging House, Lane 538/5
Foochow Road, as a tea-boy.

At 10.30 a.m. on 6.9.39 a male Chinese, led by
an accountant of the lodging house, came to engaged
Room 213. The man paid $3.00 and gave his name as
"Chien Chuin" (钱春). Shortly afterwards he left
the room.

About an hour later another male Chinese accompanied
by a female Chinese called at Room 213, (this male Chinese
same
was not the/man who had engaged Room 213). Both the male
and female Chinese passed the night in the aforementioned
room.

At a few minutes past 11 a.m. 7.9.39 Room 213
was raided and searched by a Police party, who also
questioned me regarding the man who engaged the room.
In reply I informed the Police officers that the person
who had engaged Room 213 was of short build, thin face,
and wearing white silk long gown. I further identified
and pointed out to the Police this short man who was one
of the persons arrested by Police Detectives.

The above is my true statement.

Signed:
page_data.zh:
朱祖海 (Joo Tsu Hai) 9
苏州 C.D.C. 184
C.B.H.Q.(C.1) 1939年9月12日 已译 徐 S. P.

本人名为朱祖海，现年56岁，籍贯苏州，受雇于福州路538弄5号宗和旅馆，职务为茶房。

1939年9月6日上午10时30分，一名中国男子在旅馆账房的带领下前来预订213房间。该男子支付了3.00美元，自称“钱春”。不久后他离开了房间。

约一小时后，另一名中国男子陪同一名中国女子来到213房间（这名中国男子并非之前预订213房间的那位）。这一男一女在上述房间过夜。

1939年9月7日上午11时刚过，一批警察突袭并搜查了213房间，并就预订房间的男子向我问话。作为回答，我告知警官，预订213房间的人身材矮小，瘦脸，身穿白色丝绸长衫。我还向警方指认并指出这名矮个子男子，他是被警探逮捕的人员之一。

以上陈述属实。

签名：

page_data.en:
C.1.M1 c.146/39.
HEADQUARTERS
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Sept. 7, 39.

2.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE

At 9.30 a.m. on September 7th 1939 the
Japanese Gendarmerie requested S.M.Police
assistance to raid certain premises on Foochow
Road where it was alleged that three male
Chinese members of a guerrilla unit were
residing.

According to later verbal information
supplied the three persons they wished to arrest
were active members of guerrilla units, and
present in Shanghai to purchase arms.

Assistance was rendered by D.S. Fowler,
D.S. Sugimoto, D.F.C. Yamahara, D.S.I. Lieu
Ching Ching, C.D.S. 2, C.D.C.s 184 and 212
and the undersigned, and at 11.45 a.m. 7.9.39
a raid was made on room No. 213 Tsung Ho (旅華)
Hotel, Lane 363 No. 5 Foochow Road and the
following persons who were present therein,
were arrested.

1) WONG TSANG YIH (王占一) 35, alias
WONG TSUNG TIEN (王震天), Hankow,
S/sub-manager removal contractor, No.
1 An Ling Li, Zeh Jin Road, F.C.
page_data.zh:
C.1.M1 c.146/39.
总部
上海公共租界工部局警务处
1939年9月7日。

2.

协助日本宪兵队

1939年9月7日上午9时30分，日本宪兵队请求公共租界工部局警务处协助，突袭福州路某处所，据称有三名中国男子游击队成员居住于此。

根据后来提供的口头信息，他们希望逮捕的三人是游击队的活跃成员，目前在上海购买武器。

福勒侦探长、杉本侦探长、山原副侦探长、刘正清一级副侦探长、第二刑事侦缉股、第184和212刑事侦缉组以及签署人提供了协助，并于1939年9月7日上午11时45分突袭了福州路363弄5号振华旅馆（旅華）213房间，逮捕了当时在场的以下人员。

1) 王占一 (WONG TSANG YIH)，35岁，别名王震天 (WONG TSUNG TIEN)，汉口人，搬迁承包商副经理，居住于法租界扎金路安邻里1号。

page_data.en:
2/2.

2) TSIEH P NG ( 钱鹏, alias
TSIEH YUIN CHUU (钱瑜玠), 52, Honpo, /un-
employed, M.F.A.

3) LIU LI YI YOONG (刘建荣), 29, Shangtung,
M/unemployed, No.323 Sing Sing Li, Rue
Pere Robert.

4) TSAU KIANG TAI (赵广才), 25, Tungchow,
M/assistant, residing No. 1 An Ling Li,
Zah Jau Road.

5) TSUI TSOU SZ (崔周氏), 52, Hsuchow,
F/female, N. F. A.

6) WONG TAI SZ (王戴氏), 34, Changchow,
S/female, An Ling Li, Zah Jau Road.

7) LIEU TUH MING (刘德明), 25, alias
LIEU CHING SAN (刘景山), Nanking, M/Japanese
informer, No. 4 Yoong Oen Li, Avenue du Roi
Albert.

8) WOO AU DOENG (吴鹤东), 33, Shanghai, M/Japanese
second, No. 4 Yoong Oen Li, Avenue du Roi Albert.

A search of the room was made and three letters,
property of the 2nd named, were found.
page_data.zh:
2/2.

2) 钱鹏 (TSIEH P NG)，别名钱瑜玠 (TSIEH YUIN CHUU)，52岁， Honpo (音译) 人，失业，无固定住址。

3) 刘建荣 (LIU LI YI YOONG)，29岁，山东人，失业，居住于祁齐路星星里323号。

4) 赵广才 (TSAU KIANG TAI)，25岁，通州人，男/助理，居住于扎侯路安邻里1号。

5) 崔周氏 (TSUI TSOU SZ)，52岁，徐州人，女，无固定住址。

6) 王戴氏 (WONG TAI SZ)，34岁，常州人，女，居住于扎侯路安邻里。

7) 刘德明 (LIEU TUH MING)，25岁，别名刘景山 (LIEU CHING SAN)，南京人，男/日本线人，居住于亚尔培路永恩里4号。

8) 吴鹤东 (WOO AU DOENG)，33岁，上海人，男/日本二等线人，居住于亚尔培路永恩里4号。

对房间进行了搜查，发现了属于第二名嫌疑人的三封信件。

page_data.en:
2/3.

At C.B.H.Q.s Sub Lieutenant Aetoda
pointed out the following three persons who had
been mentioned as being guerrillas.
1. WONG TUNG YUN (王占一) alias
WONG TUNG TIN (王震天)
2. TSUN PANG (津 鵬) alias
T IEN YU CHU (錢瀛洲)
3. LIEU KYI YOONG (刘建荣).
and requested that they be detained, the remainder
he added could be released.

However, it was ascertained that the
information regarding the above three persons
had been given to the Japanese Gendarmerie by
the 7th and 8th named, therefore it was considered
necessary to question them first as to the authenticity
of the information.

Statements have been taken and it will
be seen that they both implicate the 1st and
2nd named, whilst the 3rd named is supposed to
have been seen by them to discard a silk cloth
badge which refers to the appointment of one
Woo Tsung Ming (吴振明) into a guerrilla unit.

In regards to the throwing away of this
cloth badge, Lieu Kyi Yoong finally admitted that he
page_data.zh:
2/3.

在刑事科总部，加藤少尉指出了以下三名被提及为游击队员的人：
1. 王占一 (WONG TUNG YUN)，别名王震天 (WONG TUNG TIN)
2. 津鵬 (TSUN PANG)，别名錢瀛洲 (T IEN YU CHU)
3. 刘建荣 (LIEU KYI YOONG)。
并要求拘留他们，他补充说其余人可以释放。

然而，经查实，关于上述三人的情报是由第七和第八名嫌疑人提供给日本宪兵队的，因此认为有必要先向他们询问情报的真实性。

已录取供词，可见两人均牵连第一和第二名嫌疑人，而据称他们看到第三名嫌疑人丢弃了一枚丝绸布质徽章，该徽章涉及任命吴振明加入游击队一事。

关于丢弃这枚布质徽章一事，刘建荣最终承认他

page_data.en:
2/4.

did discard s me, but avers that it was given to
him at about 11 a.m. 7.9.39 by the Japanese
employed second Woo Au Doong.

Questioned further Lieu claims that he
did not look at the cloth when it was given to
him, and Woo had explained that the Police were
about to search the hotel and he did not wish
to be found in possession of it.

Tsau Kwang Tsai and Tong Tseng Yien also
claim that they saw the cloth badge handed to
Lieu by Woo.

Woo Au Doong denies that he ever had
the cloth badge, but a doubt exists as to which
of the two men is telling the truth, and considering
the fact that the two informers appear to have been
the only ones who saw Lieu discard the badge in
the Police van despite the fact that Chinese and
Japanese detectives were present, the veracity
of their account of this exhibit is extremely
doubtful.

Detectives were not notified that the cloth
badge existed until the informer was being questioned.

The following is the verbal evidence put
forward against the three men:-
page_data.zh:
2/4.

确实丢弃了某物，但声称该物是日本雇佣的二等线人吴鹤东于1939年9月7日上午11时许交给他的。

经进一步讯问，刘声称当东西交给他时他并未查看，吴解释说警察即将搜查旅馆，他不希望被发现持有该物。

赵广才和王占一也声称他们看到吴将布质徽章交给刘。

吴鹤东否认他曾持有该布质徽章，但对于这两人中谁在说实话存在疑点，考虑到两名线人似乎是唯一看到刘在警车上丢弃徽章的人，尽管当时有中日警探在场，他们关于这一物证的证词真实性极值得怀疑。

直到讯问线人时，警探们才得知布质徽章的存在。

以下是针对这三名男子提出的口头证据：-

page_data.en:
2/5.

Wong Tsang Yien, Commander of the Western
Route Guerrilla Unit of the Central Army, and
present in Shanghai to detect the military situation.
Tsien Pang, formerly chief aide-de-camp
of the 19th Route Army, now chief of staff
attached to 2nd Route, of the newly organized
4th Army, came to Shanghai to purchase military
supplies and to enlist recruits.
Lieu Kyi Yoong, Chief of th Section of
Guerrilla Unit, operating in San Soo Pong, Tsungming.
All three men deny being in any way connected
with guerrillas, Wong Tsang Yien is employed by
Okada & Co., a Japanese transportation Co., and
claims that he went to the room in the hotel to
meet Tsien Pang, who is unemployed at present, he
having arrived in Shanghai about three weeks ago
from Kampo.
Lieu Kyi Yoong is unemployed and states
that he was dismissed from the French Police Force
about one month ago.
Regarding the three letters found in the room
Tsien Pang admits that he wrote them but did so at
the request of Woo An Poong, who he alleges took
them away with him and thus he cannot explain how
they returned to the room. Further he cannot explain
page_data.zh:
2/5.

中央军西路游击队指挥官王占一（Wong Tsang Yien），现于上海侦察军情。
钱鹏（Tsien Pang），原第十九路军首席副官，现任新组建的第四军第二路参谋长，来沪采购军需物资并招募新兵。
刘建萍（Lieu Kyi Yoong），游击队某科科长，在崇明三双浜（San Soo Pong）活动。
三人均否认与游击队有任何关联。王占一受雇于日本运输公司冈田商会（Okada & Co.），声称他去旅馆房间是为了会见目前失业的钱鹏，钱鹏约三周前从江浦（Kampo）抵达上海。
刘建萍处于失业状态，并称他约一个月前被法国巡捕房解职。
关于在房间内发现的三封信件，钱鹏承认是他所写，但称是应吴鹤东（Woo An Poong）之请求而写，据称吴将信带走，因此他无法解释信件为何又回到房间。此外，他无法解释

page_data.en:
2/6.

why when writing letters for some one else, he
signed his own and fictitious names to them.
He further claims that the person mentioned as
Woo Tsung Ming 's none other than Woo u Doong,
and that the allegations made against him are
without foundation, having been made by Woo in
order to please the Japanese and claim reward.
The three men Wong Tsang Yien, Tsien Ping,
and Lieu Kyl Yoong, are at the request of the
Japanese being detained, whilst the remainder
were released upon completion of enquiries.
Enquiries proceeding.
Statements are in course of preparation.

M.S.
8/9

C. Thomas.
D. S. 114.
page_data.zh:
2/6.

为何在替他人写信时，却签上自己的名字和虚构的名字。
他还声称，信中提到的吴宗明（Woo Tsung Ming）无非就是吴鹤东（Woo u Doong），针对他的指控毫无根据，是吴为了取悦日本人并索取赏金而捏造的。
应日方要求，王占一、钱鹏和刘建萍三人被拘留，其余人员在调查结束后获释。
调查正在进行中。
供词正在整理中。

M.S.
8/9

C. Thomas.
D. S. 114.

page_data.en:
Lieu Ching San (刘景山) alias Lieu Tuh Ming
D.S. Fowler
Nanking, 86
12 Noon          7.9.39          D.S.I. Lieu Kying Ching.

My name is Lieu Ching San alias Lieu Tuh Ming,
residing No. 4 Yoong An Li Avenue Du Roi Albert.
I am an informer of Japanese Gendarmerie and
have worked for about 4 months for them.
I was introduced to the Gendarmerie by one
named Tsang Hyi Kwang (東經光), who at present is
in Nanking.
On 6.9.39 Woo Au Doong (吳鶴東) informed me
that one named Wong Tsang Yien (王占一) alias Wong
Tsung Tiep (王震天) had arrived in Shanghai from
Kompo on 26.8.39 and had met Woo Au Doong and told
him that he was in Shanghai for the purpose of recruiting
men for guerilla units. Wong Tseng Yien had met another
named Tsien Pang (錢鵬) who had arrived from Wusih
with his wife Tsien Teoo Sz (錢周氏) about 1.9.39.
Tsien Pang is also a guerilla, being second in Command
to Toong Pung Ying (童本殷) who is the leader of
guerillas in and around Wusih.
I informed the Japanese Gendarmerie of the
foregoing and they said they would take the necessary
action. They asked for proof and I told them I had
seen two letters written by Wong Tsang Yien to Toong
Pung Ying.
Wong Tsang Yien had told me he had opened
room No. 215 in the "Tsung Ho (振華) Lodging House"
No. 5 Lane 656 Foochow Road and was staying there with
his wife and Tsien Pang.
page_data.zh:
刘景山（Lieu Ching San），又名刘德明（Lieu Tuh Ming）
D.S. Fowler
南京，86号
中午12点          1939年9月7日          D.S.I. 刘景清（Lieu Kying Ching）。

我叫刘景山，又名刘德明，住阿尔贝特国王大道（Avenue Du Roi Albert）永安里4号。
我是日本宪兵队的线人，已为他们工作约4个月。
我是由一名叫张经光（Tsang Hyi Kwang）的人介绍给宪兵队的，他目前在南京。
1939年9月6日，吴鹤东（Woo Au Doong）通知我，一个叫王占一（Wong Tsang Yien），又名王震天（Wong Tsung Tiep）的人，已于1939年8月26日从江浦（Kompo）抵达上海，并会见了吴鹤东，告诉他来上海的目的是为游击队招募人员。王占一会见了另一个叫钱鹏（Tsien Pang）的人，钱鹏与其妻钱周氏（Tsien Teoo Sz）于1939年9月1日左右从无锡抵达。
钱鹏也是游击队员，是童本殷（Toong Pung Ying）的副手，童本殷是无锡及周边地区游击队的头目。
我将上述情况报告了日本宪兵队，他们说将采取必要行动。他们要求提供证据，我告诉他们我曾见过王占一写给童本殷的两封信。
王占一告诉我，他在福州路656弄5号振华旅社（"Tsung Ho (振華) Lodging House"）开了215号房间，并与妻子及钱鹏同住在那里。

page_data.en:
I was told to be present in the lodging house
before 12 noon on the 7.9.49 when the band would visit
home with assistance of Municipal Police.

I and Joo An Doong went to the lodging house
at about 11 a.m. and there met Tsien Pang and his wife
Tsien Tsoo Sz, Jong Chang Yien and his sweet heart and
Jong Ai Sz (王戴氏), friend Lieu Kyi Yoong (刘建萍)
who is a member of the French Police, No. 954. Also
present was Tsau Kwang Tsui 赵廣材

I know that Tsien Pang and Jong Tsang Yien are
proper guerillas.

On the way to the station in a van I saw one
named Lieu Kyi Oong (刘建萍) hide a piece of silk on
which were Chinese characters near the seat on which
he was sitting.

Signed:
page_data.zh:
我被告知要在1949年9月7日中午12点前到达该旅社，届时警队将在市警察局的协助下进行搜查。

我和朱安东（Joo An Doong）于上午11点左右到达旅社，在那里遇到了钱鹏及其妻钱左氏（Tsien Tsoo Sz，原文如此，前文为钱周氏）、钟占一（Jong Chang Yien）及其女友、王戴氏（Jong Ai Sz，原文姓氏为Jong，中文名注为王戴氏）、朋友刘建萍（Lieu Kyi Yoong），他是法国巡捕房第954号巡捕。在场的还有赵广材（Tsau Kwang Tsui）。

我知道钱鹏和钟占一是真正的游击队员。

在乘坐面包车前往警局的途中，我看见一个叫刘建萍（Lieu Kyi Oong）的人将一块写有汉字的丝绸藏在他座位附近。

签名：

page_data.en:
Woo Au Doong
D.S. Fowler
Shanghai 33
12 noon 7-9-39 Lieu Kying Ching.

My name is Woo Au Doong (吴鹤东), residing No. 4
Yoong An Li off Avenue Du Roi Albert.

I am a "Second" of Lieu Ching San who resides same
address.

On 3-9-39 I met one named Wong Tsang Yien (王震天)
alias Wong Tsung Tien (王震天); outside the Great World
Amusement Centre, Avenue Edward VII. I have known him for
about one year. I also know he is a guerilla.

Wong Tsang Yien (王震天), told me he had arrived
in Shanghai with his wife Wong Tai Se (王震氏) from
Kiangsu on 26-8-39 and was looking for Tsien Pang (钱鹏鸣);
a guerilla, to organise a number of other guerillas.

He told me that if I located Tsien Pang (whom I
knew) I was to go to the Dah Tung restaurant in the Great
Eastern Hotel and meet him there.

I went to the Dah Tung Restaurant on the 6-9-39
and there met Wong Tsang Yien and a little later met Tsien
Pang who arrived on his own.

Tsien Pang and I went to the Tsung Ho (振華) lodg-
ing House No8 Lane 656 Yeechow Road where Tsien Pang opened
room No. 213. Whilst in the room I saw Tsien Pang write
two letters addressed to Tsong Pung Ting (鄧本殷), a well-
known guerilla in Wush.

I later informed Lieu Ching San, for whom I work
of what had transpired and he told me he would inform the
Japanese Gendarmerie.

He later informed me we were to visit room 213 of
page_data.zh:
吴鹤东（Woo Au Doong）
D.S. Fowler
上海，33号
中午12点 1939年9月7日 刘景清（Lieu Kying Ching）。

我叫吴鹤东，住阿尔贝特国王大道旁永安里4号。

我是刘景山的“副手”，刘景山住在同一地址。

1939年9月3日，我在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）大世界游乐中心外遇见了一个叫王震天（Wong Tsang Yien），又名王震天（Wong Tsung Tien）的人。我认识他大约一年了。我也知道他是游击队员。

王震天告诉我，他和妻子王震氏（Wong Tai Se）于1939年8月26日从江苏抵达上海，正在寻找游击队员钱鹏（Tsien Pang），以组织其他游击队员。

他告诉我，如果我找到钱鹏（我认识他），就去汇中饭店（Great Eastern Hotel）的大通餐厅（Dah Tung restaurant）与他见面。

1939年9月6日，我去了大通餐厅，在那里见到了王占一，稍后又见到了独自前来的钱鹏。

钱鹏和我去了宜昌路（Yeechow Road，原文如此，前文为福州路）656弄8号振华旅社，钱鹏在那里开了213号房间。在房间里，我看见钱鹏写了两封给邓本殷（Tsong Pung Ting，原文如此，前文为童本殷）的信，邓是无锡著名的游击队员。

后来我将发生的情况告知了我为之工作的刘景山，他告诉我会通知日本宪兵队。

他后来通知我，我们要去振华旅社的213号房间，

page_data.en:
- 2 -

the Tsung Ho lodging house on the morning of 7-9-39 where
Municipal Police would arrive together with Gendarmerie.
On the way to the station in a van I saw one named
Lieu Kyi Oong (刘建荣), hide a piece of silk on which were
Chinese characters near his seat.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

在乘坐面包车前往警局的途中，我看见一个叫刘建荣（Lieu Kyi Oong，原文如此，前文为刘建萍）的人将一块写有汉字的丝绸藏在他座位附近。

page_data.en:
Translation of a letter addressed to
Dung Fung Ying by Zien Bang

6th Sept. 1939.

Dear Mr. Dung,

I have received more than 1,000
articles of goods from Moh Doh, Soochow. I am
not the only one in Shanghai, as Mr. Woo Tsung
Ming also helped to settle the matter at Ching
Ling's place. I am not telling any lies. These
are the real facts.

Bearer is hereby detailed to send
you this letter, and a reply is awaited from you
as to when we can come to your place so that you
may judge the case yourself.

Yours faithfully,

ZIEN RANG (Sgd. & Chopped)
page_data.zh:
钱鹏（Zien Bang，原文如此）致邓本殷（Dung Fung Ying，原文如此）信函译文

1939年9月6日。

尊敬的邓先生：

我已从苏州莫笃（Moh Doh，音译）收到一千多件货物。在上海并非只有我一人，吴宗明先生也在青灵（Ching Ling，音译）处协助解决了此事。我没有说谎。这些都是事实。

特派专人将此信送达给您，期待您的回复，告知我们何时可以前往您的住处，以便您亲自裁决此案。

此致
敬礼，

钱邦（ZIEN RANG，签名并盖章）

page_data.en:
Translation of a letter addressed to
Tsien Yuin Tseu to his father-in-law

6th Sept. 1939.

Dear Father-in-law,
I have arrived here safely from
Zangchow. I have succeeded in obtaining a job as
an accountant in a sugar hong at a monthly wage of
$30.00. It is rather difficult to find a suitable
job in Shanghai with so many people living here.
I shall not write you again until next month.
My wife makes a living by packing sugar for thirty
or forty cents per day.

Yours obediently,

Tsien Yuin Tseu (Sgd.)
page_data.zh:
钱元子（Tsien Yuin Tseu，音译）致岳父信函译文

1939年9月6日。

尊敬的岳父大人：
我已从常州（Zangchow，音译）安全抵达此地。我成功在一家糖行找到了一份会计工作，月薪30.00美元。在上海这么多人居住的情况下，很难找到合适的工作。
下个月之前我不会再给您写信。
我的妻子靠打包糖为生，每天收入三十或四十美分。

愚婿，

钱元子（签名）

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY WATER POLICE
THROUGH JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Reference request for assistance per diary 1;
a party of S.M. Police consisting of D.S.I.'s Pryde
and Lieu, D.S. Fowler and Shimoto, D.P.S. Yamahara,
C.D.S.40, C.D.C. 206 and 211 rendered assistance to
Sgt. Major Yoshino of the Gendarmerie who, in turn,
was giving assistance to Sgt. Major Sakamoto of the
Military Water Police.

At 10 p.m. September 8, 1939, the combined
parties visited No. 66 Stone Bridge Road for the pur-
pose of arresting two alleged well-known guerillas
named 1, Ding Dah Yue (丁大裕) and 2, Ding Hyien an
(丁易山)。

Both males were absent at the time. The wife
of the 1st. named wanted man stated her husband had
gone out early on the morning of the 8-9-39 and had
not returned . She pointed to the informer of the
Military Water Police named Wong Ying (王英) 27,
Ningpo, married, residing 126 Pakhoi Road and stated
he had called at the house during the morning and
again at about 4 p.m. asking for her husband. She
had told him her husband had gone out and not returned.

(bad) 8/9.

2

通过日本宪兵队向日本海军水上警察提供协助。

参照日记1中的协助请求；由特别巡官普赖德（Pryde）和刘（Lieu）、巡官福勒（Fowler）和Shimoto、副巡官山原（Yamahara）、华籍探员40号、华籍巡长206号和211号组成的市警察局小组，向宪兵队曹长吉野（Yoshino）提供了协助，而吉野曹长转而向海军水上警察曹长坂本（Sakamoto）提供协助。

1939年9月8日晚上10点，联合小组前往石桥路66号，目的是逮捕两名据称是著名游击队员的男子，分别是1. 丁大裕（Ding Dah Yue）和2. 丁易山（Ding Hyien an）。

当时两名男子均不在家。第一名通缉犯的妻子称，她的丈夫于1939年9月8日一早外出，尚未返回。她指认了海军水上警察的线人王英（Wong Ying），27岁，宁波人，已婚，住北河南路126号，并称他当天上午和下午4点左右曾到家中寻找她的丈夫。她告诉他丈夫外出了，尚未回来。

（字迹不清）8/9.

page_data.en:
- 2 -

He then wrote some thing on paper and left. The informer
admitted this.

The whereabouts of the 2nd named wanted male
was not made the subject of such thorough enquiries as
that of the first named.

A search of the upstairs front and back room
resulted in the following being found and handed to
the undersigned for safe-keeping pending handing over
to the Military Water Police.

3 Japanese passes to travel inland.
3 photographs.
1 inoculation certificate.
1 vaccination certificate.
All the above are in the name of Ding Dah Yue
(丁大佑).

The U.S.M.C. and Sinsa Station were informed
of the visit.

（批：5/9）

G.W. Fowler
D.S.S. 389.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

随后他在纸上写了些东西便离开了。线人承认了这一点。

对第二名通缉男子的下落并未像对第一名那样进行彻底调查。

对楼上前后房间的搜查结果发现了以下物品，并交给下述签署人保管，待移交给海军水上警察。

3张内地通行证。
3张照片。
1张接种证书。
1张疫苗证书。
以上所有物品均以丁大佑（Ding Dah Yue，中文名用字与前文略有不同）的名义登记。

已通知美国海军陆战队（U.S.M.C.，原文如此，疑为笔误或特定指代）和新闸捕房此次行动。

（批注：5/9）

G.W. Fowler
D.S.S. 389.

A MEMORANDUM REQUESTED BY THE JAPANESE GENDARMERIE HEADQUARTERS.

C.D.I. Nakamura

Sir,

I beg to report that at 4.30 p.m. September 7,
1939, Sergeant-Major Yoshino of the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters called on C.I. Office and requested our
assistance to arrest two male Chinese alleged to be a
commander of guerillas and his follower respectively,
at a certain place situated near Stone Bridge, Singa District.
Sergeant-Major Yoshino wishes that the raid be
carried out between 9.30 and 10 p.m. September 7, 1939.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

which resulted in his death.
This crime took place on the streets of

1939年10月5日下午，日本宪兵队的冈本（Okamoto）警曹长来到罪案组总部，随行有一名中国女子，名为 Tseu Tse **〔此处转录不清〕** (        )
该女子称，第一被告张燦荣（Chang Tsui Yoong）与其他数人一起，用铁条袭击了她的丈夫朱祖生（Tseu Choh Sung），导致其死亡。
这起犯罪发生在1937年农历十一月十五日（1937年12月17日）的无锡街头。死者妻子称她当时在场并目睹了犯罪过程。
在罪案组总部进行了一次列队辨认，证人（Tseu Tse **〔此处转录不清〕**）立即指认第一被告张燦荣（Chang Tsai Yoong）为袭击其丈夫的人员之一。
第一被告已接受讯问，并否认参与此罪行。他承认认识死者，两人是同乡，并称是从他人处得知此人被谋杀，但不知晓犯罪的具体情况。
他称这名女证人对他怀恨在心，因为

（印：特科 339）
（批：S. E. C 4/10）

page_data.en:
4/2.

him a grudge because he denounced her husband
to the Public Safety Bureau in Wusih for the
murder of one named Tsu Sing Nun (朱星南) in
June 1937. That Tseu Choh Sung (the deceased)
was arrested for this crime, but released because
of the hostilities.

A statement has been taken from the
accused and a translation is attached.

〔此处为手写签名及缩写 D. S. I.〕

他在1937年6月向无锡公安局举报了她的丈夫谋杀一名叫朱星南（Tsu Sing Nun）的人。朱祖生（死者）因此罪被捕，但因战事爆发而被释放。

已获取被告的供词，译文附后。

〔此处为手写签名及缩写 D. S. I.〕

page_data.en:
further
Chang Tsai Yoong ( 張燦榮 ).
x D.S.I. Ma Vui Faung
translated Fun Mei Han
6-10-39

At 4 p.m. of 5-10-39, the wife of the late Tsu Choh
Sung ( 朱菊生 ) came to K.C.D. and identified me as the
murderer of her husband. Actually I know nothing whatsoever
about this crime, but wish to point out the following:-
About 18 years ago, Tsu Sing Nan ( 朱星南 ), son of
Tsu Bei Kung ( 朱培根 ) (deceased Tsu Choh Sung's elder Brother),
became my adopted son owing to some Chinese superstition
that he could not be brought up under his father's care. In
the beginning of June 1937, Tsu Sing Nan incurred the enmity
of his uncle Tsu Choh Sung(deceased) as the result of a
dispute in the allotment of estates. A few days later, Tsu
Choh Sung killed his nephew Tsu Sing Nan with a pair of
scissors. I then reported this case to the Public Safety
Bureau in Wusieh together with the latter's parents. Tsu
Choh Sung was finally arrested by the Public Safety Bureau
and was handed to the court for trial. After the Sino-Japanese
hostilities broke out in Shanghai, he was released and stayed
at his home. I, however, do not know how he was released.
Following the retreat of the Chinese Army from Wusieh, I
heard that Tsu Choh Sung was murdered, but I don't know who
killed him.
This is my true statement.

Signed and thumbprinted: Chang Tsai Yoong.
page_data.zh:
续
张燦荣（Chang Tsai Yoong）。
x D.S.I. Ma Vui Faung
翻译 Fun Mei Han
1939年10月6日

1939年10月5日下午4时，已故朱菊生（Tsu Choh Sung）的妻子来到刑侦探访部（K.C.D.），指认我是杀害她丈夫的凶手。实际上我对这起犯罪一无所知，但愿指出以下几点：
大约18年前，朱培根（Tsu Bei Kung）（已故朱祖生的兄长）之子朱星南（Tsu Sing Nan），因某种中国迷信说法认为他不能在父亲抚养下长大，而成为我的养子。1937年6月初，朱星南因遗产分配纠纷与其叔父朱祖生（已故）结怨。几天后，朱祖生用一把剪刀杀死了他的侄子朱星南。随后，我与朱星南的父母一同将此案报告给无锡公安局。朱祖生最终被公安局逮捕，并移送法院审判。上海中日敌对行动爆发后，他被释放并居家。然而，我不知道他是如何被释放的。
在中国军队从无锡撤退后，我听说朱祖生被谋杀，但我不知道是谁杀了他。
这是我的真实陈述。

签名并按手印：张燦荣。

CHINA BRANCH
SEPT. 18, 39.

The seized documents have been perused
by the Special Branch and it has been found that
none of them are of an incriminating nature; an
explanation of these documents is attached.
Statements have been taken from the
three arrested persons and translations of
same are forwarded herewith. The gist of these
statements follows:-
The 1st accused Chang Tsai Yoong states he is
age 49 and a native of Wusih. That he was educated
at his native place and has worked there ever since
as a pork butcher and farmer and previously was
the master of the Zou Loo (長樂) Teashop there,
but this is now closed down. That he has visited
Shanghai on many occasions in the past for the
purpose of visiting friends etc. That on this
occasion he came to Shanghai for the purpose of
placing his son (the 2nd accused) in the Loo Chung
(綠鐘) Middle School, Gordon Road.
That one of the letters seized is from another
son who is at present in Chengtu, but he does not
know in what capacity this son is employed there.
That this son disappeared at the beginning of
hostilities and he has not seen him since.

1939年9月18日。

特科已查阅缴获的文件，发现其中没有任何具有定罪性质的内容；对这些文件的解释附后。
已获取三名被捕人员的供词，译文随函附上。这些供词的要点如下：
第一被告张燦荣称，他49岁，无锡人。他在家乡受教育，此后一直在那里做猪肉屠夫和农民，以前曾是当地长乐（Zou Loo）茶馆的老板，但该茶馆现已关闭。他过去曾多次来上海拜访朋友等。这次来上海的目的是为了送他的儿子（第二被告）进入戈登路绿钟（Loo Chung）中学就读。
他说，缴获的信件中有一封来自另一个目前身在成都的儿子，但他不知道这个儿子在成都从事什么工作。他说这个儿子在敌对行动开始时失踪，此后便未再见过面。

page_data.en:
3/

He further states that he has not been concerned
in Anti-Japanese activities of any nature.

The 2nd accused Chang Tuh Ming states he is age
16 years and the son of the 1st accused. That in
January 1939 he came to Shanghai and studied at
the Sung Ya (新亞) Middle School, Rue Lafayette.
That in July 1939 his father (the 1st accused) came
to Shanghai with the intention of placing him in the
Loo Chung Middle School, Gordon Road.

The 3rd accused, Dong Yeeng Fah states he is
aged 30 years and a native of Wusih. That he was
educated in his native place and came to Shanghai
at the age of 15 years and became an apprentice
in the Zang Shing Restaurant, N. Szechuen Road.
That he had to evacuate from there at the commence-
ment of hostilities and made a living by operating
a macaroni stall. In November 1938 he obtained a
job as tea-boy in the Sing Ziang Lodging House,
82 Rue Galle, the master of this establishment
being one named Lieu Zan Kun (樓長根). That
the lodging house closed down in April 1939 and he
then went to live with the master of same at 9 Rue
Amiral Bayle.

That on Aug. 25th 1939 he left Shanghai to
page_data.zh:
3/

他进一步声明，他从未参与任何性质的反日活动。

第二被告张德明（Chang Tuh Ming）称，他16岁，是第一被告的儿子。1939年1月他来上海，在霞飞路新亚（Sung Ya）中学读书。1939年7月，他的父亲（第一被告）来上海，打算将他送入戈登路绿钟中学。

第三被告董永发（Dong Yeeng Fah）称，他30岁，无锡人。他在家乡受教育，15岁时来到上海，在北四川路臧兴餐厅（Zang Shing Restaurant）当学徒。敌对行动开始时他不得不从那里撤离，靠经营一个意大利面摊位谋生。1938年11月，他在加利路82号新江旅馆（Sing Ziang Lodging House）找到一份茶房的工作，该旅馆老板名叫楼长根（Lieu Zan Kun）。该旅馆于1939年4月关闭，随后他便去贝勒路（Rue Amiral Bayle）9号与老板同住。

1939年8月25日他离开上海去

page_data.en:
3/3

visit his native place, as his daughter was ill,
and returned to Shanghai on Sept. 8th 1939.

At 10 p.m. on 9.9.39 he went to Room 30
of the Liang Kyl Lodging House to see a lawyer named
Ziang Ding An (〔此处转录不清〕) in connection with his
master's business. This lawyer was supposed to
ramble in this room together with the 1st accused.
As the lawyer did not turn up, he remained there
for the night and was arrested at 5 a.m. on the
morning of 10.9.39.

The master named Lieu Zau Kun, has been
called to C.B.H.Q. and corroborates the statement
of the 3rd accused in that he sent this man to
Room 30 of the Liang Kyl Lodging House, to see
the lawyer in question.

No further evidence against the three
arrested persons has been received from the
Japanese Gendarmerie by this office up to the
present.

〔此处为手写签名〕
D. S. I.
page_data.zh:
3/3

探望家乡，因为他的女儿生病了，并于1939年9月8日返回上海。

1939年9月9日晚上10点，他去良吉旅馆（Liang Kyl Lodging House）30号房间见一位名叫江定安（Ziang Ding An，〔此处转录不清〕）的律师，处理他老板的事务。据说这位律师会和第一被告一起在这个房间里闲谈。由于律师没有出现，他在那里过夜，并于1939年9月10日凌晨5点被捕。

老板楼长根（Lieu Zau Kun）已被传唤至罪案组总部，并证实了第三被告的供词，即是他派这个人去良吉旅馆30号房间见上述律师。

截至目前，本办公室尚未从日本宪兵队收到针对这三名被捕人员的更多证据。

〔此处为手写签名〕
D. S. I.

page_data.en:
Chang Tsia Yoong (張燦榮)
Susieh
No. 30, Liang Chi Lodging House
translated by Tsi Han
XXXXXX

My name is Chang Tsia Yoong (張燦榮); age 49,
married, a native of Susieh, residing at Room 30 of the
Liang Chi Lodging House, No. 144, Hoopah Road.

When I was 7 years old, I studied at a certain school.
At the age of 13, I finished my study and acted as an hawker
in my native country. At the age of 17, I became as an
apprentice for three years in the Foong Kung Butchery in
San Mlo (雙廟), Susieh. After having completed my apprentice-
ship when I was 20 years old, the proprietor of the Butchery
transferred the shop to me by paying him 100 dollars. I
then became the proprietor of the butchery. I have also
been the master of the San Loo Tea Shop in my native country,
but now the tea shop has closed down.

I used to come to Shanghai for purchasing or visiting
my relatives and friends. I have no profession in Shanghai.
I came to Shanghai this time for the purpose of accompanying
my son to enter the Loo Chung Middle School, Gordon Road.
My son intended to board at the school, but he has no luggage
at present so he is living with me in the Liang Chi Lodging
House. The accused named Tang Yoong Fah is one of my fellow
country men. He knew that I resided at the Room 30 of the
Liang Chi Lodging House so he used to come to my room for
gossipping or playing. Yesterday night he remained in my
room by curfew so was also arrested by the detectives. I
don't know why he should be arrested. I have never been
concerned in any crime, neither have I been concerned in
Anti-Japanese activities of any kind.
page_data.zh:
张燦荣（Chang Tsia Yoong）
无锡
湖北路144号良吉旅馆30号
由 Tsi Han 翻译
XXXXXX

我叫张燦荣（Chang Tsia Yoong）；49岁，已婚，无锡人，现住湖北路144号良吉旅馆30号。

我7岁时在某学校读书。13岁时完成学业，在家乡做小贩。17岁时，我在无锡双庙（San Mlo）的丰公肉铺（Foong Kung Butchery）当了三年学徒。20岁完成学徒期后，我付给店主100美元，盘下了这家店铺。随后我成为了肉铺老板。我也曾在家乡做过三乐（San Loo）茶馆的老板，但现在茶馆已经关闭。

我过去常来上海购物或探亲访友。我在上海没有职业。这次来上海是为了陪同儿子进入戈登路绿钟中学就读。我儿子打算住校，但目前没有行李，所以和我住在良吉旅馆。被告唐永发（Tang Yoong Fah，音译）是我的同乡。他知道我住在良吉旅馆30号房间，所以常来我房间聊天或玩耍。昨晚他因宵禁留在我房间，因此也被探员逮捕。我不知道他为何被捕。我从未参与任何犯罪，也从未参与任何性质的反日活动。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

The seized letter was written by my 2nd son named
Chang Tuh Tsing who disappeared during the outbreak of
hostilities in Shanghai on August 13, 1939. I now know that
he is in Chengtu, Szechuan by receiving the only one letter
of him since his disappearance. But I don't know how he
is employed in Chengtu.
This is my true statement.

Signed and thumbprinted by Chang Tsin Young.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

缴获的信件是我第二个儿子张德清（Chang Tuh Tsing，音译）写的，他在1939年8月13日上海敌对行动爆发期间失踪。自从他失踪后，我只收到过他一封信，由此得知他现在四川成都。但我不知道他在成都做什么工作。
这是我的真实陈述。

张燦荣（Chang Tsin Young，音译）签名并按手印。

page_data.en:
Chang Tuh Ming (張德明):
Wusieh                                                                 DeSol. Tia Vai Faung
                                                                             translated Kuh Mei Han

My name is Chang Tuh Ming (張德明), aged 16, a
native of Wusieh. My father is a proprietor of the Foong
Teng Butchery in San Mio (雙廟), Wusieh. I lived with
my parents in my native country.

At the age of 7, I studied at a certain school,
and at the age of 14, I stopped my study as the hostilities
broke out in Shanghai on August 13, 1937. I then assisted
my father in farming.

In January, 1939, I came to Shanghai with a fellow
country man of mine and resided at one of my relative's
homes, No. 350, Sinza Road. Shortly after, I entered the
Sing Ya Middle School, Rue Lafayette, F.C.

Toward the end of July, 1939, my father came to
Shanghai from my native country and resided at Room 30 of
the Liang Chi Lodging House, No. 144, Ssepeh Road. I then
went there and lived together with my father.

On September 4th, 1939, I took the entrance examina-
tion of the Leo Chung Middle School, Gordon Road, and every
night I still went to the Liang Chi Lodging House and lived
with my father. At about 5 a.m. on 10-9-39, I and my father
were arrested by detectives of the Settlement Police. I have
never been concerned in any crime, neither have I been con-
cerned in Anti-Japanese activities of any kind.

This is my true statement.

Signed and thumbprinted by Chang Tuh Ming.
page_data.zh:
张德明（Chang Tuh Ming）：
无锡                                                                 DeSol. Tia Vai Faung
                                                                             翻译 Kuh Mei Han

我叫张德明（Chang Tuh Ming），16岁，无锡人。我父亲是无锡双庙（San Mio）丰泰肉铺（Foong Teng Butchery）的老板。我和父母住在家乡。

7岁时，我在某学校读书，14岁时，因1937年8月13日上海爆发敌对行动而辍学。随后我协助父亲务农。

1939年1月，我和一位同乡来到上海，住在新闸路350号的一位亲戚家。不久后，我进入法租界霞飞路新亚中学就读。

1939年7月底，我父亲从家乡来到上海，住在新闸路（Ssepeh Road，注：原文此处拼写可能有误，通常Ssepeh指四牌楼或类似，但结合上下文及前文湖北路，此处可能指代不明或为另一地址，按音译保留或参照前文逻辑，前文为Hoopah/Hupeh即湖北路，此处Ssepeh可能为OCR错误或不同路名，暂按音译或保留原意，但在历史语境中Ssepeh Rd常指四牌楼路，然前文明确为湖北路144号良吉旅馆，此处可能存在档案记录不一致，依原文翻译）144号良吉旅馆30号房间。随后我去那里和父亲同住。

1939年9月4日，我参加了戈登路绿钟中学的入学考试，每晚我仍去良吉旅馆和父亲同住。1939年9月10日凌晨5点左右，我和父亲被租界警察局的探员逮捕。我从未参与任何犯罪，也从未参与任何性质的反日活动。

这是我的真实陈述。

张德明签名并按手印。

page_data.en:
Dong Yoong Fah (唐榮法)。
x D.S.I. Zia Vai Faung
translated
xxxxxx Kuh Nei Han

I am named Dong Yoong Fah (唐榮法), aged 30, a native of Wusieh, married, residing in the Shing Zian Lodging House on Rue Galle near Rue Engene Bard, F.C., and employed as a tea boy there.

When I was eight years old, I studied at a certain primary school in my native country. At the age of 14, I finished school and assisted my father in farming. At the age of 15, I came to Shanghai and acted as an apprentice in the Zang Shing Restaurant in front of Guang Ta Li, North Szechuen Road. After having completed my apprenticeship, I remained in this employment with pay of nearly 20 dollars per mensem. On January 28, 1932, the restaurant was compelled to stop business as the Sino-Japanese Hostilities broke out in Shanghai. I then went to live with my master in the Foo Shing Yuen Restaurant, Canton Rd. for 4 months. After the hostilities, I returned to the Zang Shing Restaurant with my master.

At the outbreak of hostilities on August 13, 1937, I went to my master's home, No. 23, Route Alfred Magy, F.C., and resided there. In January, 1938, I acted as a macaroni stall keeper on the entrance of Chentao Road, near Burkill Rd. In November 1938, I obtained employment as a tea boy in the Shing Zian Lodging House and in April 1939, the house stopped its business as the homeowner intended to reconstruct the premises. I then resided with my master named Lieu Tan Kun, at No. 9, Rue Bayle, F.C.

On August 25, 1939, a fellow country man of mine
page_data.zh:
唐榮法 (Dong Yoong Fah)。
x 副督察 Zia Vai Faung
翻译
xxxxxx Kuh Nei Han

本人名为唐榮法 (Dong Yoong Fah)，现年30岁，籍贯无锡，已婚，居住于法租界恩利巴路 (Rue Engene Bard) 附近加利路 (Rue Galle) 的兴贤旅馆 (Shing Zian Lodging House)，受雇为该处茶房。

本人八岁时，在家乡某小学读书。十四岁时毕业，协助父亲务农。十五岁时来到上海，在北四川路广达里前的张兴酒家 (Zang Shing Restaurant) 当学徒。学徒期满后，继续在该处受雇，月薪约二十元。1932年1月28日，因上海爆发中日战事，该酒家被迫停业。随后本人随店主前往广东路的福兴园酒家 (Foo Shing Yuen Restaurant) 居住了四个月。战事结束后，本人随店主返回张兴酒家。

1937年8月13日战事爆发时，本人前往店主位于法租界马吉路 (Route Alfred Magy) 23号的家中居住。1938年1月，本人在伯基路 (Burkill Rd.) 附近的陈陶路 (Chentao Road) 路口经营面食摊。1938年11月，本人在兴贤旅馆受雇担任茶房；1939年4月，因房东意图重建房屋，该旅馆停止营业。随后本人与名为刘坦坤 (Lieu Tan Kun) 的店主一同居住在法租界贝勒路 (Rue Bayle) 9号。

1939年8月25日，一位同乡

page_data.en:
- 2 -

come to Shanghai telling me that my daughter was very ill
so I returned to my country immediately. I stayed in the
country for 16 days and on September 8, I came back to
Shanghai and still lived with my master.

At 10 p.m. on 9-9-39, I went to Room 30 of the Liang
Chi Rodging House to see a lawyer named Tien Ding An in
connection with the business of my master. This lawyer used
to visit this room for the purpose of gambling. As he did
not arrive there by curfew I remained in this room for the
night. At 5 a.m. on 10-9-39, I was arrested. I have never
been concerned in any crime, neither have I been concerned
in Anti-Japanese activities of any kind.

This is my true statement.

Signed and thumbprinted by Deng Yeong Fah.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

来到上海，告知本人女儿病重，
因此本人立即返回家乡。本人在
家乡停留了16天，于9月8日回到
上海，仍与店主同住。

1939年9月9日晚上10点，本人前
往良记旅馆 (Liang Chi Rodging House) 30
号房间，因店主事务去见一位名为丁定安
(Tien Ding An) 的律师。该律师常来此房间
进行赌博活动。因宵禁前他未到达，本人
便在此房间过夜。1939年9月10日凌晨5
点，本人被捕。本人从未参与任何犯罪活
动，也未参与任何形式的反日活动。

此为本人真实陈述。

邓永发 (Deng Yeong Fah) 签名并按指印。

C.1.Misc.154/39.
HEADQUARTERS
CRIME BRANCH
SEPT. 10, 39

2.

Further to Diary No. 1. At 5 a.m. 10.9.39
Sgt. Major Yoshino of Japanese Gendarmerie Head-
quarters came to C.B.H.Q. accompanied by Sgt. Major
Sakamoto and two other members of the Japanese
Gendarmerie Water Police and requested assistance
to raid Room 30 of the Liang Kyi (梁記) Lodging
House, 144 Rupeh Road to arrest two male Chinese,
one named Tsang Tsai Yung (张燦雲); the other
name unknown, on suspicion of being concerned in
guerrilla activities.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I.s
Pryde and Zia Wen Faung, D.S.s Rossington
and Sugimoto, D.P.C. Yamahara, C.D.C.s 211
and 212 and the stated address visited at
5.15 a.m. Five persons were found in the room,
three of whom were placed under arrest at the
request of the Japanese Gendarmerie, the remaining
two were not arrested. The names and particulars
of the arrested persons follow:-

1st : Tsang Tsai Yoong (张燦雲)✓, 49, Wusih,
M/Pork Shop master, Wusih.
2nd : Tsang Tuh Ming (张德明)✓, 16, Wusih,
S/Student, son of 1st accused.

C.1.Misc.154/39.
总部
刑事科
1939年9月10日

2.

续日记第1号。1939年9月10日凌晨5点，
日本宪兵队总部的吉野 (Yoshino) 警曹长
在坂本 (Sakamoto) 警曹长及另外两名日本
宪兵队水上警察成员的陪同下，来到刑事
科总部，请求协助突袭湖北路144号良记
(梁記) 旅馆30号房间，逮捕两名中国男
子，一名名为张燦雲 (Tsang Tsai Yung)；
另一名姓名不详，涉嫌参与游击活动。

副督察 Pryde 和 Zia Wen Faung、侦
探 Rossington 和 Sugimoto、侦探警长
Yamahara、刑事侦探科员 211 号和 212
号提供了协助，并于凌晨5点15分抵达上
述地址。房间内发现五人，其中三人应日
本宪兵队要求被逮捕，其余两人未被逮捕。
被捕者姓名及详情如下：-

第一名：张燦雲 (Tsang Tsai Yoong)✓，49岁，无锡，
男/猪肉店店主，无锡。
第二名：张德明 (Tsang Tuh Ming)✓，16岁，无锡，
学生/第一被告之子。

page_data.en:
2/2.

3rd : Dong Yoong Fah (唐荣法); 30 Wusih,
M/lodging house accountant,
Rue Galle, French Concession.

A search of the room was made and the
following seized : -
3 letters.
One spare envelope.
One small account book.
Japanese passes belonging to the 1st, 2nd & 3rd
accused.
One Japanese pass in the name of Lieu Yoong
Fung (吕荣顺).

The 1st accused states he arrived in
Shanghai about one month ago to arrange about
the education of his son, the 2nd accused, and
has lived in the Liang Kyi Lodging House since
arrival.

The 3rd accused states he visited this
address to see his friend, the 1st accused.

Sgt. Major Sakamoto states he will produce
further evidence tomorrow. All three accused have
been detained in Cent. cells, pending further
enquiries being made and the seized documents
translated.

Geo. R. Rufolo
D. S. I

第三名：唐荣法 (Dong Yoong Fah)；30岁，无锡，
男/旅馆会计，
法租界加利路。

对房间进行了搜查，查获以下物品：-
3封信件。
1个备用信封。
1本小账簿。
属于第一、第二及第三被告的日本通行证。
1张名为吕荣顺 (Lieu Yoong Fung) 的日本通行证。

第一被告称，他约一个月前抵达上海，
是为了安排其子（即第二被告）的教育问
题，自抵达后一直居住在良记旅馆。

第三被告称，他访问此地址是为了看
望他的朋友，即第一被告。

坂本 (Sakamoto) 警曹长表示，他将于
明日提供更多证据。三名被告均被羁押在
中央监狱牢房，以待进一步调查及翻译缴
获的文件。

Geo. R. Rufolo
副督察
